They establish neither a universal unique native fold, universal spontaneous folding, a complete energy-landscape mechanism nor experimentally validated SOMA process-level ancestry.

nodes.name: Finite protein hydration and ionic-microenvironment source scope
nodes.shortDescription: Resolve original card 3.31 to the source BPTI supercooled water-relaxation measurement, fitted quantities and conditional heterogeneous-hydration interpretation. Local dynamic perturbation is supported within that model/preparation. Ionic distributions, universal long-range solvent order, electrostatic organization and hydration-caused binding/catalytic/stability effects are excluded from the selected evidence scope.

nodes.name: Protein modification and functional readout boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Distinguish post-synthesis substrate conjugate accumulation, an engineered genetic fusion, targeting, initiation and later functional/degradation outcomes. An accumulating ubiquitin-associated band is not an isolated modification rate or a universal reversible protein-control mechanism.

nodes.name: Scoped ubiquitination and protein-modification evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The reused lysate control reports ubiquitinated-form accumulation for full and shortened N-end-rule DHFR constructs at similar source rates and extents. This is a finite protein-modification readout; it does not make every modification fast, reversible, site-resolved or sufficient for degradation.

nodes.name: Prepared2-methylimidazole activated RNA species
nodes.shortDescription: The source prepares monophosphorylated RNA monomers/oligomers and converts their5-prime phosphates to2-methylimidazolides using supplied laboratory reagents, then purifies products chromatographically. Its worked AGC example is checked by negative-mode electrospray MS and UV-based concentration estimation. These prepared stocks are supplied to the extension assays; their continuing reactivation is not part of those reactions.

nodes.name: Separate matched and mismatched RNA monomer-addition assays
nodes.shortDescription: The source combines the same RNA primer and activated AGC helper with four short templates differing at the next copying position, and separately assays each of the four2-methylimidazole activated canonical monomers. Denaturing-gel primer conversion gives apparent kobs for16template/monomer combinations. Retain the Figure2/3caption versus Methods monomer-concentration discrepancy and the unreported unique reaction temperature.

nodes.name: Activated versus unactivated downstream helper in RNA extension
nodes.shortDescription: Use the source prepared RNA primer/template with activated G monomer and compare no downstream helper against AGC bearing5-prime OH, phosphate or2-methylimidazole activation. The selected Figure1 reaction is buffered with CHES pH9 and magnesium; gel fluorescence measures remaining primer over time and the source fits pseudo-first-order kobs. The differing template arrangements and monomer/oligomer reactions remain labelled rather than treated as one identical binding geometry.

nodes.name: Helper-assisted short mixed-monomer RNA extension
nodes.shortDescription: The source assays a prepared short RNA template with a simultaneous mixture of activated A,G,C and2-thiouridine monomers,plus selected activated helper trimers. It compares absent versus added helper sets and follows denaturing-gel extension lengths over time. Preserve the differing Figure4caption and Methods preparation descriptions rather than pool them into a corrected protocol.

nodes.name: External pH and trapped-phosphorylation readout definitions
nodes.shortDescription: The Racker proton readout is calibrated external-medium pH. Its phosphorylation readout is radiolabelled glucose-6-phosphate formed through a hexokinase trap, with ATP supplied initially. These report different responses; neither alone is a direct measurement of a complete membrane gradient or an accumulating free ATP pool.

nodes.name: Bounded modern-vesicle chemiosmotic interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: The separate proton-response and phosphorylation controls support the authors’ finite chemiosmotic energy-transduction interpretation in reconstituted protein-containing vesicles. They do not identify an altered intrinsic reaction equilibrium constant or demonstrate protein-free primordial coupling.

nodes.name: Prepared protein-containing phosphorylation-reporter context
nodes.shortDescription: The source assayed illuminated vesicles containing purple membrane, mitochondrial membrane proteins and coupling factors using phosphate radiolabelling and hexokinase trapping; omission and inhibition controls were compared with the complete preparation.

nodes.name: Light-dependent trapped-phosphorylation response
nodes.shortDescription: The complete illuminated preparation produced a higher phosphorylation-reporter signal than darkness. Coupling-factor omission or rutamycin reduced the signal; purple-membrane omission or uncoupler addition abolished detectable reporter formation in the reported comparison.

nodes.name: Prepared purple-membrane vesicle pH-response context
nodes.shortDescription: The source reconstituted purple membrane in phospholipid vesicles and recorded external pH during light/dark changes with acid-pulse calibration and transport-disrupting controls.

nodes.name: Light-dependent external-pH response of reconstituted vesicles
nodes.shortDescription: Illumination raised external pH in the reconstituted purple-membrane vesicles, and darkness reversed the response. Transport-disrupting controls suppressed it. The authors interpret this as inward proton translocation opposed by passive leakage.

nodes.name: Reaction Gibbs energy and standard equilibrium conventions
nodes.shortDescription: Definitions of reaction Gibbs energy, reaction quotient and equilibrium constant under a specified reaction equation and reference state.

nodes.name: Bounded glutathione-linked redox recovery interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Together the source characterization and intracellular trajectories support a bounded glutathione-linked oxidation/reduction interpretation for the sampled HeLa region. The data distinguish reversible sensor response and finite recovery without identifying a universal redox potential, cofactor-regeneration flux or specific feedback mechanism.

nodes.name: DNA partition and RNA synthesis scope
nodes.shortDescription: Selected bacterial isotope-transfer and heat-subunit observations support qualified semiconservative DNA partition; separate E. coli enzyme-fraction experiments support supplied-DNA-dependent RNA-product synthesis and bulk composition. These finite results retain copying and expression while leaving complete sequence fidelity, regulated end-to-end machinery and universal inherited continuity outside the admitted measurements.

nodes.name: Finite RNA serial amplification
nodes.shortDescription: The source paired RNA products increase with logistic-shaped batch growth that levels as substrates deplete. Six five-hour incubations with 4 percent carryover and fresh substrate sustain amplification for 30 hours; the source reports cumulative dilution-corrected amplification greater than 10^8 for each enzyme. This finite observation supports replenishment-dependent cross-catalysis, with no observed infinite duration or complete resource autonomy.

nodes.name: Global RNA conformation proxies and cleavage-response parameters
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected hammerhead assays, an ensemble FRET response is a dye-geometry-dependent proxy for a global helical arrangement. A metal concentration midpoint and Hill coefficient summarize the fitted titration; they are not automatically microscopic ion dissociation constants, bound-ion stoichiometries, folding rate constants or atomic structures. Separately, a substrate-cleaved progress curve defines an apparent first-order response. In Boots 2008 the source explicitly defines kobs as an approach-to-equilibrium rate equal to cleavage plus ligation rates, rather than kcat or isolated chemical cleavage.

nodes.name: Reciprocal RNA catalyst production
nodes.shortDescription: The selected R3C-derived RNA enzymes each catalyze ligation of two supplied oligoribonucleotide substrates to produce the reciprocal enzyme. The source paired amplification vessel contains no protein catalyst; this supports a particular cross-catalytic RNA organization rather than a universal protein-first reaction network.

nodes.name: Prepared worm dual-GFP reporter context
nodes.shortDescription: The source compared muscle nuclear GFP-LacZ and mitochondrial GFP fluorescence in the supplied reporter strain after target-related or control dsRNA introduction, with separate injected-animal and progeny observations.

nodes.name: Finite target-related dual-GFP fluorescence response
nodes.shortDescription: In the dual-reporter preparation, gfp-related dsRNA reduced both fluorescent reporters, whereas lacZ-related dsRNA preferentially reduced the nuclear GFP-LacZ reporter while mitochondrial GFP was largely retained. The unc-22 control did not produce the same fluorescence pattern. The response included incomplete and mosaic effects.

nodes.name: Prepared worm mex-3 transcript-staining context
nodes.shortDescription: The source compared endogenous mex-3 in situ hybridization staining in early embryos from parents given target-related purified antisense or duplex RNA, using uninjected and no-probe controls to interpret the staining signal.

nodes.name: Reduced detectable mex-3 transcript signal
nodes.shortDescription: Early embryos from the mex-3 duplex-RNA preparation had no detectable endogenous mex-3 hybridization signal in the source comparison, whereas the purified antisense preparation retained substantial signal. This supports reduced detectable transcript abundance under the source assay conditions.

nodes.name: Prepared worm single-strand/duplex phenotype context
nodes.shortDescription: The source introduced qualitatively characterized single-strand or complementary RNA preparations into adult worms and compared selected movement, developmental and progeny phenotypes; purified-duplex activity and source sequence controls were examined.

nodes.name: Finite dsRNA-associated worm phenotypes
nodes.shortDescription: For selected targets, complementary double-stranded RNA preparations produced stronger interference phenotypes than the purified individual strands in the source comparisons. Activity persisted in purified duplex material and was observed in finite progeny cohorts as well as selected injected-animal readouts.

nodes.name: Source-specific RNA-interference readout convention
nodes.shortDescription: For this acquisition, RNA interference denotes the source-specific effects of introduced double-stranded RNA in prepared C. elegans. Phenotype, reporter fluorescence and in situ transcript staining are separate readouts. They do not by definition identify a modern small-RNA/protein-complex pathway or a universal non-coding-RNA regulatory architecture.

nodes.name: Bounded introduced-dsRNA interference interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: The selected source comparisons support introduced-dsRNA-associated, sequence-related functional interference in prepared C. elegans, with a separate mex-3 observation of reduced detectable transcript. The evidence does not resolve the molecular silencing mechanism or establish the full non-coding-RNA, translation, chromatin, reversibility and adaptive-regulation claims of original card 23.

nodes.name: Separate RNase reoxidation and functional readouts
nodes.shortDescription: During the selected oxidation, sulfhydryl content and optical rotation change before substantial catalytic activity appears. The paper reports near-restoration of native physical properties and RNA activity, while synthetic-substrate activity in the oxidation mixture is variable, generally 60-70% of native; possible inhibition was not investigated. The lag prevents identifying total disulfide formation or one physical proxy with immediate formation of active native molecules.

nodes.name: Tentative RNase disulfide-reshuffling interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: The authors exclude their one-by-one native-molecule mechanism using the lagged functional readout and tentatively favor initially nonnative disulfide pairings followed by interchange toward active RNase. Thermodynamic selection is an interpretation of this preparation, with alternative mechanisms not all rigorously excluded; no measured global free-energy minimum or universal one-sequence/one-fold law follows.

nodes.name: Protocol-dependent recovery of Rubisco catalytic activity
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 1A reports apparent activity-recovery rate constants about 0.015/min for solution plus BSA,0.08/min for GroEL/GroES/ATP and 0.14/min for SR1/GroES/ATP. Omitting BSA leaves low solution recovery, while the chaperonin protocols recover activity with or without BSA. These are source bulk activity curves after the specified quench/release/dimerization steps, not an atomic structural determination or a universal folding rate.

nodes.name: Controlled Rubisco refolding-protocol comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The source compares the same80 nM denatured Rubisco input at 15 C in solution with or without BSA and with GroEL/GroES/ATP or SR1/GroES/ATP, retaining the stated aliquot/quench and SR1 release/dimerization operations. This is a controlled combined protocol intervention, not an isolated ATP-hydrolysis experiment.

nodes.name: Rubisco solution association during activity recovery
nodes.shortDescription: Refolding Rubisco plus BSA scatters light, whereas native Rubisco plus BSA and BSA alone give negligible scattering. Source35S-Rubisco gel filtration at 10,75 and 140 min shows intermediate-sized, void-volume and native-dimer-sized fractions changing with time. The source interprets part of native recovery as reversal of intermolecular association while other material accumulates in the void peak.

nodes.name: CETCH 1.0 combined-operation context
nodes.shortDescription: For the source CETCH 1.0 combined-operation test, enzymes, cofactors and ferrocenium are present from the start; added propionyl-CoA initiates conversion and NaH13CO3 supplies labeled inorganic carbon. The main text reports ferrocenium limited to 0.1 mM because higher concentrations precipitated other assay enzymes. Full protocol, sampling duration, calibration and controls remain unread; this preparation is separate from stepwise addition and CETCH 5.4.

nodes.name: CETCH 1.0 stepwise-addition context
nodes.shortDescription: The CETCH 1.0 main-text stepwise preparation starts from chemically supplied propionyl-CoA, cofactors and bicarbonate-containing buffer. Propionyl-CoA carboxylase is added first, followed by eleven other enzymes; ferrocenium is added with methylsuccinyl-CoA dehydrogenase. HPLC-MS is the reported intermediate readout. Only this described order and input boundary is reconstructed; complete conditions and duration remain unknown.

nodes.name: CETCH finite isotope/product context
nodes.shortDescription: CETCH 5.4 supplied in vitro enzyme network and source Figure 2 assay: initiate from supplied propionyl-CoA with NaH13CO3 and externally supplied cofactors/regeneration/protection resources. Follow six CoA intermediates and their fractional isotope labeling over 90 minutes; couple glyoxylate output to malate synthase and externally added acetyl-CoA. Source final volume is 0.52 ml with 2.3 mg/ml core cycle proteins plus 0.8 mg/ml auxiliary proteins. Full buffer, temperature, enzyme concentrations/calibration and supplemental controls remain unread and are not invented.

nodes.name: Finite selective proteasome-degradation source scope
nodes.shortDescription: Resolve original card 3.36 to defined tag, tail and folded-domain manipulations in the source lysate assays. Efficient substrate band loss depends on the tested initiation context and can stop at a stabilized domain. These finite results qualify selective degradation, while universal misfolding recognition, native-protein exclusion, toxic-aggregate removal, amino-acid recovery and persistent system fidelity are excluded from this evidence scope.

nodes.name: Conditional sequence/fold/function scope
nodes.shortDescription: The reused lymphotactin study links named WT/engineered constructs, condition-sensitive NMR folds and distinct calcium/heparin responses. This supports a bounded sequence/structure/function association with environment and partners explicit; neither unique-fold determinism nor selective inheritance follows.

nodes.name: Sequence, conformation and function boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Distinguish polymer sequence, environment-conditioned conformations, source structural models and functional response assays. A construct comparison can change both sequence and conformation; inherited sequence, catalytic persistence and selective amplification require their own measurements.

nodes.name: Finite mixed-monomer nonenzymatic RNA chain extension
nodes.shortDescription: Figure4shows finite multi-step primer extension in the helper-containing mixed-monomer preparation,including products extended by four nucleotides,where the corresponding helper-absent lane shows little extension. This is source-specific qualitative chain growth,without a repaired exact yield/time value,all-sequence fidelity or autonomous replication claim.

nodes.name: Biochemical signal-response boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Distinguish a supplied biochemical pathway preparation, input-dependent molecular activation, downstream enzyme response and any separate electrical readout. One local response does not identify an entire network or a universal transfer gain.

nodes.name: Scoped transducin/PDE signal transduction
nodes.shortDescription: The existing Fung preparation supports a finite light-dependent transducin/PDE biochemical response. This is a local signal-transduction example; network topology, universal amplification and adaptive control are separate unmeasured claims.

nodes.name: Alpha-lytic protease activity, spectroscopy and conditional rate context
nodes.shortDescription: Study alpha-lytic protease I-to-N conversion in 10 mM potassium acetate, pH 5, at 4 and 25 C using sensitive activity detection after pepsin removal of I and calibration to native enzyme. Measure WT activity loss at 0.98 M guanidinium-HCl and use inactive S195A for broader denaturant-dependent fluorescence/CD unfolding measurements and extrapolation. Analyze Pro-catalyzed folding separately at 4 C in 20 mM potassium phosphate, pH 7.2, with Pro:I at least 15:1, fitting fast pre-equilibrium plus a slow folding step. CD urea titration and a separate calorimetric cycle have their stated baselines and temperatures.

nodes.name: Conditional supplied lipid-membrane account
nodes.shortDescription: Joint source chemistry, optical and morphology evidence supports phospholipid production with reorganization/expansion of an already supplied membrane population under selected preparations. The R18 increase precedes chemical conversion and morphology preparations differ, so the account does not identify an isolated synthesis-to-area effect, first boundary origin, controlled permeability or self-maintaining cell.

nodes.name: Finite supplied phosphatidic-acid production
nodes.shortDescription: In the declared SI Figure S3 source preparation, internal-standard-normalized LC-MS signals show oleic-acid loss and PA product accumulation during the supplied three-enzyme reaction in pre-existing liposomes. This supports finite phospholipid chemical production; absolute conversion yields, species response/uncertainty and resource autonomy are not independently reconstructed.

nodes.name: Conditional T4 residue and reaction-channel interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Activity/product observations for T4 mutants and localized structural comparisons support a proposed T26H double-displacement mechanism involving Glu11 proton donation and a His26 covalent intermediate. E11H/T26H has no detected halo activity while D20C/T26H retains qualitative activity. The source discusses competing structural or electronic explanations for preference toward transglycosylation; the catalytic trajectory remains an interpretation.

nodes.name: Prepared T4 lysozyme product-selection assay
nodes.shortDescription: Incubate cysteine-free pseudo-WT-derived T26H T4 lysozyme with an E.coli cell-wall-derived peptide tetrasaccharide containing one reduced terminal NAM unit. For the higher-substrate experiment use80 micromolar substrate,0.5 micromolar enzyme,20 mM sodium acetate pH 5.0,0 C and 60 min. Resolve products by reversed-phase HPLC and assign masses by electrospray MS; maintain the source distinct lower-substrate5-min comparisons and qualitative halo assay as separate observations.

nodes.name: Finite T26H longer-glycan product formation
nodes.shortDescription: The source 80 micromolar substrate T26H reaction yields higher-mass glycan products assigned as trimer and tetramer, with a tentative pentamer, and an estimated transglycosylation-to-hydrolysis product ratio about 10:1 after60 min. The lower-substrate inherited comparison gives different anomeric product assignments for WT* and T26H. These data support preparation-dependent product selection without supplying an initial-rate enhancement.

nodes.name: Activation, copying-rate and fidelity distinction
nodes.shortDescription: In these selected reactions, an activated nucleotide is a supplied chemically modified substrate with a leaving group. Separate downstream activated oligomers can accelerate primer extension under the source comparison. Define kobs as the source pseudo-first-order primer-loss fit, and fN as the matched-addition rate divided by the sum of matched and mismatched rates on that template in the declared separate-assay convention. Neither fN nor its mean is an independently measured all-context copying accuracy or a genome-replication result.

nodes.name: Kinetic template discrimination and informational-inheritance boundary
nodes.shortDescription: The selected RNA experiment shows matched additions faster than mismatched additions under defined separate assays. It supports finite template-dependent kinetic discrimination;source-derived fidelity averages and error-threshold interpretations remain conditional rather than all-context pairing rules,stable-association energetics or demonstrated inherited information.

nodes.name: Finite template-dependent match/mismatch rate discrimination
nodes.shortDescription: The source table reports matched U-on-A,A-on-U,G-on-C andC-on-G kobs central values1,6,26 and44per hour respectively; the G-on-U mismatch is0.3per hour,about5%of the matched A-on-U response. Other mismatches are slower but nonzero. The source averages its separate-assay discrimination fractions to report98%,with no claim here of universal or mixed-pool copying fidelity.

nodes.name: Cell-free RNA-dependent polypeptide scope
nodes.shortDescription: The selected supplied-polyU cell-free E. coli experiment supports RNA-dependent phenylalanine incorporation and a product with several poly-L-phenylalanine properties. It retains finite template-associated polypeptide production without attributing a complete codon/adaptor/frame/translocation/fidelity mechanism or recursive functional-protein production to this source.

nodes.name: Lymphotactin NMR, engineered-variant and heparin-control context
nodes.shortDescription: Use recombinant human lymphotactin for NMR, including Ltn(2-93), and native-N-terminal functional constructs with the source stated methionine substitutions, plus engineered CC3 and W55D variants. Acquire NMR in 20 mM sodium phosphate, pH 6.0, 90% H2O/10% D2O; vary temperature and NaCl as specified. Infer Ltn40 structure at 40 C without added NaCl using chemical shifts, NOEs, isotope-filtered intermonomer contacts and restrained refinement. Compare XCR1-expressing HEK293-cell calcium responses normalized to carbachol, heparin chromatography/titration and WT versus CC3 responses with and without heparin.

nodes.name: Supplied-amphiphile vesicle assembly and enclosure
nodes.shortDescription: Prepared supplied-amphiphile vesicles enclose fluorescent aqueous material; confocal images support multilamellar membrane organization before and after the source growth/division operation.

nodes.name: Osmotic vesicle competition and population-inference boundary
nodes.shortDescription: For the tRNA competition arms, Table 1 reports approximately 21% area gain in the swollen labelled preparation and 23% area loss in the low-osmolarity labelled preparation; source-fitted response rates are about 0.1 per minute. This is finite differential membrane-area growth under an imposed osmolyte contrast, without a measured heritable genotype-frequency change.

nodes.name: Finite vesicle encapsulation and reaction-compatibility scope
nodes.shortDescription: Prepared lipid vesicles retain supplied short oligonucleotides; a separately prepared encapsulated DNA primer-template supports externally fed modified-nucleotide extension, and another vesicle study partitions supplied short RNA into daughters. This preserves positive confinement and reaction compatibility while leaving general catalyst/network intensification, genotype-phenotype coupling and coacervate alternatives outside the admitted result.

nodes.name: Two supplied-lipid growth and shear-associated division cycles
nodes.shortDescription: After the first feed the source FRET response corresponds to approximately 3.7-fold membrane-area growth by approximately 25 minutes, with thread-like shape formation. A second feed produces another area-growth response; microscopy follows division after applied agitation in the cycle experiment.

nodes.name: Fed vesicle growth, external fission and heredity boundary
nodes.shortDescription: The selected oleate experiments couple externally supplied membrane growth to shapes that divide under applied fluid agitation, and a separate cargo preparation retains and partitions short supplied RNA. This is positive finite growth/division and cargo redistribution, with supplied feed and force explicit; internally synthesized membranes, replenished genomes, accurate nonrandom segregation and autonomous reproduction are not demonstrated.

nodes.name: Activation- and preparation-dependent nucleotide permeation
nodes.shortDescription: The selected membrane shows little AMP/ADP/ATP leakage over 24 hours without magnesium; AMP and ADP can permeate slowly with magnesium. Singly charged phosphorimidazolide-activated nucleotides cross more readily, with source-reported equilibration half-time approximately 12 hours under the approximately 100 nm conditions.

nodes.name: Finite dA10 retention in vesicles
nodes.shortDescription: Figure S6 shows approximately 100% vesicle-associated fluorescent dA10 over the displayed 24-hour window in the source assay. This supports finite polymer retention alongside separate small-solute permeability observations.

nodes.name: Passive vesicle permeability and physiological-control boundary
nodes.shortDescription: The selected prepared fatty-acid membranes pass different small solutes at composition- and nucleotide-dependent rates while retaining a separate supplied oligonucleotide over its finite assay. These observations support selective passive exchange in model membranes; they do not establish active control, maintained metabolism or universal import/export requirements.

nodes.name: Composition-dependent ribose permeation
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected Table S1 comparison, ribose permeability is reported as 24 for myristoleate and 87 for 2:1 myristoleate:monomyristolein, in units 10^-8 cm/s. Other composition/solute comparisons show conditional variation rather than a universal permeability constant.

nodes.name: Finite short-RNA partition into daughter vesicles
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports approximately sixfold more detectable RNA-containing oleate vesicles after one fed/agitated division operation, with only trace RNA leakage; extrusion releases much more RNA in the separate comparison. Retained short cargo is partitioned into daughter compartments without demonstrated RNA replication.

nodes.name: External-feed copying of an encapsulated homopolymer segment
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected fatty-acid vesicles, gel products extend substantially by 3 hours and full-length product accumulates through 24 hours after externally supplied activated monomer. POPC vesicles show no detectable corresponding extension in the source assay. This demonstrates finite transport/retention/chemistry compatibility, not a completed genome-replication cycle.

nodes.name: Original card 3.10: bounded Viral Assembly and Maturation
nodes.shortDescription: Original card 3.10 remains an unresolved assembly-to-maturation/infectious-competence hypothesis. None of the selected optical, mature-structure or isolated-receptor observations is a measured post-assembly maturation trajectory or a matched competence transition.

nodes.name: Original card 3.16: bounded Mechanisms of Viral Infection
nodes.shortDescription: Original card 3.16 remains an unresolved full-infection-program hypothesis in this review. Separate structural association, genome density and cell-free assembly are not a single host-entering, replicating, expressing and propagating system; host takeover and coordinated timing are not acquired.

nodes.name: Original card 3.29: bounded Structural Organization of Viral Genomes
nodes.shortDescription: The canonical scope for original card 3.29 is source-specific ordered RNA density and asymmetric RNA-capsid spatial correspondence in MS2. Complete sequence assignment, packaging-signal functions, selective encapsidation, regulatory timing, replication/expression and whole-lifecycle coupling remain unestablished by the structure.

nodes.name: Original card 3.30: bounded Mechanisms of Viral Entry into Cells
nodes.shortDescription: Original card 3.30 remains an unresolved complete-cellular-entry hypothesis. Isolated-pilus association is a finite separate observation and does not establish boundary crossing, intracellular delivery, irreversibility, tropism, entry efficiency or replication initiation.

nodes.name: Original card 3.35: bounded Viral Reprogramming of the Transcription–Translation Apparatus
nodes.shortDescription: Original card 3.35 remains an unsupported host-expression-reprogramming hypothesis within the selected evidence. No actual host transcription/translation comparison, polymerase/ribosome redirection, host shutoff or preferential viral production was acquired; structural contacts do not establish downward causal control.

nodes.name: Original card 3.9: bounded Self-Organization of Viral Capsids
nodes.shortDescription: The canonical scope for original card 3.9 is finite cell-free MS2 assembly-associated optical dynamics, with approximate signal-to-protein interpretation and separately reported morphology. Free-energy minima, microscopic interface rules, universal cooperativity, shell protection and emergence remain unestablished.

nodes.name: Prepared yeast sugar-perturbation pH context
nodes.shortDescription: The source measured standard-curve-converted pHluorin ratios after glucose removal and readdition, comparing yeast wild type with sugar-sensing deletions and selected rescue constructs over time and at declared response times.

nodes.name: Glucose-dependent intracellular-pH regulation in yeast
nodes.shortDescription: Yeast pH recovery depended on glucose availability. Under limiting glucose, selected sugar-sensing deletions yielded less acidification than wild type, whereas loss of Snf1 yielded more. Combined pathway perturbations and Gpa2 rescue comparisons support a regulated, preparation-specific intracellular-pH response.

nodes.name: DNA-cage enzyme characterization context
nodes.shortDescription: The source prepared DNA half/full cages with nominal internal dimensions20by20by17 nm and designed small pores, carrying supplied Aspergillus niger GOx or horseradish HRP through oligonucleotide attachment. Assembly/purification is checked by agarose gel and negatively stained TEM. Dye-labeled enzyme/cage colocalization and normalized Cy3 photobleaching are assessed separately on immobilized samples in the source room-temperature TIRF preparation. Concentrations use A260 and conjugate absorbance/labeling estimates. These characterization preparations are distinct from the bulk activity wells; no universal exact pair occupancy is assumed.

nodes.name: GOx-HRP cage comparison activity context
nodes.shortDescription: For source Figure 3 and SI Figure 12, compare nominal1 nM GOx/HRP enzyme or enzyme-DNA-cage preparations with 1 mM glucose and 2 mM ABTS in 1xTBS, pH7.5; the source bulk Methods specify1 mM MgCl2. Monitor increasing absorbance at 410 nm. The panel includes a co-caged GOx/HRP pair, a mixture of separately full-caged enzymes, a mixture of separate half-cages, free enzymes with an empty cage and free enzymes without cage. SI Figure 12 includes fresh, same-thermal-program and substrate-background controls. Figure 3 reports SD of at least three replicates. Complete base TBS salt composition and an exact common active-enzyme population are not supplied/reconstructed; source concentration/normalization conventions are retained.

nodes.name: Externally fed oleate membrane growth and applied-agitation cycles
nodes.shortDescription: The source labels prepared approximately 4 micrometre multilamellar oleate membranes with a donor/acceptor FRET pair in bicine pH 8.5 at room temperature. Two externally supplied micelle-feed rounds are followed with FRET and separate microscopy, with externally applied agitation between growth rounds. Retain this membrane-area acquisition apart from RNA-cargo and glycine volume-recovery assays.

nodes.name: Prepared multilamellar oleate vesicle enclosure and imaging
nodes.shortDescription: The source makes aqueous oleate vesicles from supplied oleic-acid film in buffered solution, and selects approximately 4 micrometre multilamellar compartments. HPTS reports enclosed aqueous space in epifluorescence; a separate membrane-labelled confocal preparation resolves lamellar structure. The main oleate imaging regime is room temperature and sodium bicine pH 8.5. Subsequent micelle feeding is a separate experimental input.

nodes.name: Short supplied RNA partition during fed vesicle division
nodes.shortDescription: The source encapsulates supplied fluorescent A10 RNA in approximately 4 micrometre multilamellar oleate vesicles in bicine pH 8.5. Following externally supplied oleate-micelle growth and applied agitation, fluorescence microscopy counts RNA-bearing daughter compartments; filtrate fluorescence measures release, with intact and detergent-lysed reference signals. The selected result is Figure 3A-D oleate, not the separate decanoate mixture.

nodes.name: Acute IL-1alpha-associated neutrophil recruitment
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports less peritoneal recruitment after Il1a-deficient donor lysates and reduced rIL-1alpha-induced recruitment in Cxcr2-deficient recipients. This supplies a bounded local coordination outcome, without establishing a necessary developmental stage before organism-scale immunity.

nodes.name: Age/CMV-associated circulating T-cell composition
nodes.shortDescription: In the reported cross-sectional cohort, age is associated with absolute naive-CD8 loss even among CMV-negative people, while memory-subset patterns differ with CMV status. Subset counts, antibody titers and individual cellular function are distinct; an expanded memory compartment does not establish universal exhausted function.

nodes.name: TRAIL execution-switch analysis context
nodes.shortDescription: Expose HeLa cells to TRAIL under the source sensitization conditions and compare RNAi/overexpression perturbations. Track caspase substrate cleavage and mitochondrial permeabilization; compare observations with the fitted EARM ODE model.

nodes.name: TRAIL execution-switch analysis perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare TRAIL response with specified Bcl-2-family/caspase-network perturbations.

nodes.name: TRAIL execution-switch analysis response
nodes.shortDescription: Execution readouts show variable delay followed by rapid switching; protein perturbations and modeling constrain how upstream signaling, mitochondrial gating and inhibitor balance shape that behavior.

nodes.name: Unresolved transfer of AMPK/autophagy regulation
nodes.shortDescription: Opposite autophagy outcomes in the Kim2011 and Nwadike2018 preparations require matched nutrient, serum, cell-background, time and flux comparisons before a common causal rule can be assigned.

nodes.name: Apoptotic execution and reversibility boundary definition
nodes.shortDescription: Molecules do not have autonomous survival goals. A whole-cell commitment label is not an extra intervention. Execution signs do not universally preclude recovery, and local viability/repair capability was not exhaustively measured before death.

nodes.name: Apoptotic execution and reversibility boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Apoptotic execution is represented by molecular network perturbations, mitochondrial/caspase dynamics, response heterogeneity and a separate inducer-washout recovery counterexample.

nodes.name: Arrest and inflammatory secretion are separable
nodes.shortDescription: p16-induced arrest produces little IL-6 in this preparation, while damaged cycling/p53-impaired cells can secrete IL-6. ATM depletion reduces damage-associated IL-6/IL-8 without eliminating the reported RAS-associated arrest phenotype. Thus an inflammatory secretome is neither identical to arrest nor guaranteed by every senescence route.

nodes.name: Unidentified cause of ATP heterogeneity
nodes.shortDescription: The source proposes variation in enzyme content as a possible cause of ATP heterogeneity but does not establish that mechanism. Similar ATP/ADP ratios across cells remain possible even when ATP concentrations differ.

nodes.name: ATP reporter calibration and interference boundary
nodes.shortDescription: The source QUEEN controls reduce growth-rate-dependent bias relative to the tested FRET reporters, while residual in-vivo/in-vitro differences require correction. Acidified cells below the reported pH-insensitive range can bias QUEEN-2m estimates.

nodes.name: Autophagy, selective turnover and flux scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: LC3/puncta are not alone completed flux. Chaperone participation, mTOR input and prokaryotic organization are not universal prerequisites for every degradation pathway. Direct atom-level recycling and every cargo-recognition mechanism remain unmeasured.

nodes.name: Autophagy, selective turnover and flux scope
nodes.shortDescription: Autophagy is represented by regulated initiation, lysosomal degradation/flux constraints and a selective mitochondrial-turnover preparation, with markers, cargo elimination and molecular reuse distinguished.

nodes.name: Bacterial electrochemical state is dynamic and condition-dependent
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports whole-cell PROPS flashes with stable intracellular pH within its stated control precision, supporting transient depolarization. Respiration interruption and uncoupling replace blinking with sustained bright PROPS response; illumination changes blinking frequency and duration.

nodes.name: bajwa2016-cmv-peptide-polyfunction: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare CMV-positive UK young (26, age 19-35) and older (69, age 60-85) participants with a separately selected 22-person oldest-old Italian group. Stimulate PBMCs with pools covering 19 CMV proteins; use DMSO negative and SEB positive controls, overnight incubation and flow readouts CD107/CD154/IL-2/TNF/IFNgamma. Background-subtracted Boolean subsets feed a declared linear-weight polyfunctionality index; multiple-comparison corrections and responder eligibility restrict comparisons. Oldest-old prose/table age-range discrepancy remains unresolved.

nodes.name: barber2006-lcmv-inhibitory-blockade: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare adult C57BL/6 Armstrong-resolved versus clone-13 chronic infection and defined CD4-depleted chronic preparations. Administer 200 micrograms anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-1, isotype or anti-CTLA-4 intraperitoneally every third day. Main intact-CD4 blockade spans days 23-37; the separate helpless assay starts after at least 40 days and lasts two weeks. Tetramers, peptide-induced cytokines, BrdU/Ki67/CFSE, CD107, chromium release and viral titers assess cell number, proliferation, effector output and viral burden separately. PD-L1-knockout chronic-infection survival is a distinct genotype comparison.

nodes.name: Basal Cytokine Production and Cytokine Signaling Baseline: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: A basal cytokine condition is reconstructed by tonic IFNbeta-linked maintenance of STAT1 in existing mouse fibroblast cultures and conditional later IFNgamma responsiveness. Production, receptor competence, downstream protein availability and finite antiviral readouts are separated. This is not a universal quasi-stationary inflammatory set point, an absolute secretion threshold or a baseline that requires inflammasome activation, senescence, SASP or microbial translocation.

nodes.name: basisty2020-secretome-contexts: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Culture the declared primary cells at 37 degrees C, 10 percent CO2 and 3 percent O2. Compare 10-Gy irradiated cells after 10 days with mock/quiescent controls, inducible RAS fibroblasts after 4 or 7 days, and atazanavir fibroblasts after 9 or 14 days. Collect 24-hour serum-free conditioned medium; ultracentrifugation separates soluble and small-EV-enriched fractions. DIA-MS relative protein abundance is normalized to cell number, with source replicate counts and FDR-corrected q < 0.05. Viability assays address gross death-related contamination; they do not establish active export mechanism for every protein.

nodes.name: Synthetic yeast reporter-state follow-up during colony growth preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Follow induced source ABY001 on- and off-cells on agarose containing the same inducer. Inspect colony descendants by fluorescence; retain the source Figure 5 caption times of 16 h for the illustrated off-derived colony and 22 h for the on-derived colony separately from the main prose 16 h description.

nodes.name: Synthetic yeast expression architectures and finite response distributions preparation
nodes.shortDescription: In source S. cerevisiae derivatives cultured in synthetic dropout medium at 30 C, compare source-designated constitutive rtTA and positive-autoregulatory circuits, with chromosomal GFP reporters or direct rtTA-GFP fusion. Vary inducer and gene dosage; examine fluorescence 6-12 h after induction. Keep promoter, reporter placement and copy-number variants distinct.

nodes.name: Signal and receptor dependence of engineered yeast ER export preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Follow source fluorescent cargo released from ER aggregates by ligand in modified S. cerevisiae at approximately 23 C. Compare absent/APVNTT/APVNTA export-signal variants and ERV29 versus erv29 deletion, retaining the engineered pdr1/pdr3 and vps10 background. Quantify perinuclear ER fluorescence and endoglycosidase-sensitive mobility.

nodes.name: Cargo persistence during changing yeast Golgi identity preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Track individual source yeast Golgi cisternae by three-color 4D confocal microscopy after release of engineered fluorescent cargo, using early Vrg4 and late Sec7 markers. The ordinary maturation observations are kept separate from nocodazole-treated daughter-cell FRAP experiments.

nodes.name: AP-1 and glycosylation contrasts in Golgi cargo recovery preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use source nocodazole-treated yeast mothers and daughters. After cargo release, bleach daughter cargo fluorescence while preserving resident Golgi markers and follow recovery at maturation; compare AP-1 Apl4 deletion or nonglycosylated reporter with the designated controls.

nodes.name: Secreted cargo detection in rich medium and boundary effects preparation
nodes.shortDescription: After ligand-triggered cargo release, compare cell-associated and medium fractions from source engineered yeast in rich glucose medium by immunoblotting; contrast the source minimal-medium observation, where cell-wall/periplasm retention and fluorescence quenching are relevant.

nodes.name: Cell-state causal attribution boundary
nodes.shortDescription: A coarse-grained cell-state description may organize physical rate dependence, but an independently identifiable higher-level causal effect requires specified interventions, mediators, alternatives and aggregation assumptions.

nodes.name: Heterogeneous ATP concentration within one culture
nodes.shortDescription: The source estimates an asymmetric ATP distribution with mean 1.54 mM and standard deviation 1.22 mM in its selected culture. These are population distribution statistics after source correction, not universal cellular values or uncertainty of a common ATP concentration.

nodes.name: Bacterial voltage dynamics, mechanical response and dye efflux
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct the cellular electrochemical property through source optical voltage/pH controls, a separate tethered-motor preparation and dye-efflux observations. Separate voltage, concentration gradients, proton-motive force, ATP metabolism and mechanistic transport attribution; retain illumination and preparation boundaries.

nodes.name: Cellular energy observations and their integration limits
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct cellular energy transformation through calibrated ATP heterogeneity and separate bacterial electrical/motor responses. Distinguish concentration, flux, ATP/ADP ratio, voltage, pH and mechanical work; no single scalar or merged cross-publication cell supplies the complete metabolic regime.

nodes.name: Cellular signaling and response scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: A cell-wide interpretation is a synthesis over defined assays, not proof of complete integrated control, cellular understanding, adaptation optimality or a universal eukaryotic/prokaryotic prerequisite.

nodes.name: Cellular signaling and response scope
nodes.shortDescription: Cellular signaling is reconstructed as stimulus-dependent molecular/cellular response in bacterial, yeast and mammalian preparations, with timing, amplification, attenuation and feedback measured separately.

nodes.name: Cellular specialization and state scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: Shared lineage/genetic background does not prove complete sequence identity; lentiviral conversion explicitly changes the construct context. Persistent identity, epigenetic inheritance, metabolic specialization and signaling responsiveness require distinct endpoint evidence.

nodes.name: Cellular specialization and state scope
nodes.shortDescription: Natural embryonic lineage expression separation and engineered fibroblast-to-neuron functional conversion provide different evidence for cellular state diversification.

nodes.name: Lineage-specific reduced organelle genome inventories
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports 979356 bp and 867 protein-coding sequences for P. longichromatophora, and 977190 bp and 863 protein-coding sequences for P. micropora NZ27. Protein-coding counts differ from total annotated genes; these are organism-specific sequence/annotation results.

nodes.name: Proposed Golgi-mediated import remains a mechanistic hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Transit motifs, predicted helices and processing patterns motivate the source Golgi/AP-1 trafficking model, but do not directly demonstrate the complete route. Processing peptidase identity and translocation across the inner chromatophore membrane remain unknown.

nodes.name: Genomic complement is distinct from measured metabolic exchange
nodes.shortDescription: Comparative annotation retains photosynthesis-related functions while identifying loss/incompleteness of several biosynthetic pathways in chromatophores. This supports a source inference of host dependence, without directly measuring each metabolite flux or host rescue pathway.

nodes.name: Processed nuclear-encoded proteins in chromatophore preparations
nodes.shortDescription: The source identifies N-termini for 132 chromatophore-encoded and 76 nucleus-encoded proteins. Of 37 nuclear proteins carrying the source transit-peptide annotation, thirty show processing in a common region; most retain the second transit-peptide part.

nodes.name: Scoped chronic CD8 functional constraint
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports sustained PD-1 expression and impaired tested antigen-specific CD8 functions in chronic clone-13 compared with resolved Armstrong infection. These contrasts identify an experimental infection-associated regime, not chronological aging or all adaptive immune incapacity.

nodes.name: Contact coordination and aggregate scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: An engineered aggregate is not a universal evolutionary prototissue stage. No gap-junction conductance, general neighbor synchronization, complete tissue function or universal two-cell critical number is measured.

nodes.name: Contact coordination and aggregate scope
nodes.shortDescription: Cell contact, engineered juxtacrine induction, differential adhesion and multicellular spatial sorting are separated from natural lineage signaling and from physiological tissue differentiation.

nodes.name: Cell-cycle, arrest and death scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: Cell-cycle regulation and apoptosis are not one obligatory process shared by every cell. Neither prokaryotic ancestry, allostery in every control step nor a universal irreversible termination threshold is derived from these experiments.

nodes.name: Cell-cycle, arrest and death scope
nodes.shortDescription: Proliferation/quiescence control, cell-free mitotic switching, DNA-damage-dependent arrest and receptor-mediated apoptotic execution are distinct processes that can interact in particular cells.

nodes.name: Organelle-specific spatial organization in cultured cells
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct cell-scale spatial organization as finite ER/mitochondrion/endosome localization and movement under specified microtubule-state perturbations. Distinguish persistent optical overlap and preferential routes from permanent anchoring, universal cell geometry, inherited spatial structure and an independently established downward causal law.

nodes.name: Unresolved transfer from localization to global downward control
nodes.shortDescription: The observed organelle preferences and drug responses do not uniquely determine a cell-scale downward causal law, molecular-signaling efficiency, division inheritance, or the causal role of each contact in lipid/calcium exchange.

nodes.name: Innate Immune Pattern Recognition and Damage-Associated Inflammatory Signaling: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: Damage-associated inflammatory signaling is reconstructed by defined mouse necrotic-lysate/mesothelial and peritoneal experiments. Donor IL-1alpha, recipient IL-1R/MyD88, secreted CXCL1 and downstream recruitment are distinguished. Endogenous damage cues need not act through TLR2/4 or inflammasome components in this preparation; no universal homeostatic-disturbance threshold, senescence requirement or gut-translocation prerequisite is admitted.

nodes.name: Repair-pathway readout depends on selection and template design
nodes.shortDescription: The source detects different target-alteration fractions according to transfected-cell selection, donor availability, guide clone and assay. A donor that removes probe/primer sites makes repair products disappear from that particular assay; intact target signal does not independently count every break.

nodes.name: Repair fractions retain their assay interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: For the source selected F8-S2 conditions, the adjacent-probe analysis assigns approximately 43% of the inferred break outcomes to donor-associated HDR. This is a source inference dependent on probe design and normalization, not a universal cellular HDR probability or guaranteed restoration of native sequence.

nodes.name: Tested dynab/dynamin coexpression contrast
nodes.shortDescription: In the measured HeLa transferrin assay, dynab and dynamin isoform coexpression alter intracellular uptake relative to the named controls.

nodes.name: Cargo persists while Golgi marker identity changes
nodes.shortDescription: Individual source cisternae lose early Vrg4, acquire late Sec7 and subsequently lose Sec7 over approximately three minutes, while cargo remains visible through maturation. Functional compartment organization does not require immutable molecular membership.

nodes.name: EGF uptake is less affected than transferrin uptake
nodes.shortDescription: In the source low-EGF assay, dynab has only a minor effect on EGF internalization and does not show the transferrin-receptor redistribution pattern. The response of one endocytic cargo is insufficient to describe all uptake.

nodes.name: eigenbrod2008-mesothelial-lysate: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: C57BL/6-background primary mesothelial cells and macrophage controls receive five-freeze-thaw macrophage extracts (1:10) or liver homogenate (1:100), typically for 6 hours. Compare donor Il1a deletion and recipient Il1r/MyD88/Tlr2-Tlr4/Asc/caspase-1 deletions, plus IL-1 receptor antagonist at 500 ng/ml. Read cell-free CXCL1/IL-6 ELISA and NF-kappaB/MAPK immunoblots; triplicate wells are distinguished from independent experiments.

nodes.name: eigenbrod2008-peritoneal-recruitment: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Inject extracts corresponding to 1.5 x 10^7 necrotic WT or Il1a-deficient dendritic cells per mouse; analyze lavage at 6 hours. A separate rIL-1alpha challenge (0.05 ng/g body weight) compares WT and Cxcr2-deficient recipients. Gr-1 flow cytometry with cytospin verification quantifies neutrophil recruitment, with saline and genotype controls.

nodes.name: Historical organelle integration is inferred from extant comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: The source comparative sequences and phylogeny support cyanobacterial affinity and reductive evolution of Paulinella chromatophores. Reconstructed ancestral inventories, early rapid loss and later slower loss are historical inferences, not a witnessed transformation or automatically repeatable construction protocol.

nodes.name: Extant organelle integration and inferred endosymbiotic history
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct endosymbiotic organization through contemporary Paulinella chromatophore protein processing and comparative genome evidence. Distinguish extant host/organelle coordination, annotated functional dependence, historical reconstruction and proposed import mechanisms; do not turn evolutionary origin into a repeatable universal construction recipe.

nodes.name: Unresolved universal route of organelle construction
nodes.shortDescription: These chromatophore comparisons do not establish a single mandatory sequence for all mitochondria, plastids and cellular compartments. Exact extinct donor, host state, universal event order, inheritance control and sufficient construction conditions remain outside the reviewed evidence.

nodes.name: Tested export-signal and Erv29 conditions
nodes.shortDescription: For the supplied engineered yeast cargo, the APV signal/Erv29 comparison changes measured ER-exit kinetics, while the glycosylation-site variant retains rapid exit.

nodes.name: Microtubule curvature is not the unique ER-sliding requirement
nodes.shortDescription: After source hyperacetylation treatment, sliding also occurs on straighter microtubules. Untreated curvature/acetylation association therefore does not identify geometric curvature as a universal prerequisite for sliding.

nodes.name: Persistent optical contacts during dynamic reorganization
nodes.shortDescription: The source live imaging shows ER-mitochondrial and ER-endosomal overlaps persisting during movement. This supports dynamic spatial organization within the optical observation window, not permanent anchoring or proof of all molecular contacts.

nodes.name: Signal-specific ER export in a defined reporter preparation
nodes.shortDescription: The APV-containing signal accelerates source reporter ER exit to a reported approximately 7.5 min half-time; removing Erv29 returns slow bulk-flow-like exit. Eliminating the glycosylation signal does not remove rapid ER exit, separating receptor-linked export from glycosylation.

nodes.name: Inhibitor-associated increase in ER sliding
nodes.shortDescription: The source TSA comparison increases sliding events approximately two- to fourfold by sixty minutes in four tested cells, while tip-associated events do not increase. A tubacin comparison gives a similar qualitative response, strengthening the connection to HDAC6-linked state.

nodes.name: Distinct spatial routes of ER remodeling
nodes.shortDescription: The source distinguishes ER sliding along existing microtubule shafts from tip-attachment-complex extension. Sliding is faster and persists longer during nocodazole treatment, while tip-associated events cease earlier; neither observation alone identifies the complete molecular motor linkage.

nodes.name: Selective exchange and dynamic eukaryotic compartments
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct compartmentalization as preparation-specific selective exchange and dynamic organelle identity in living yeast, with complementary cultured-cell spatial observations. Separate nuclear-pore transport, ER export, Golgi maturation and organelle contact from origin, universal organelle stability and complete cellular coordination.

nodes.name: HDAC-inhibitor treatment and ER-sliding response preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Measure source COS-7 ER sliding before and after TSA, with a separate tubacin comparison. Immunofluorescence/immunoblot report increased tubulin acetylation, while matched live-imaging windows count sliding and STIM1-marked tip-associated events in defined peripheral regions.

nodes.name: ER sliding and tip-associated extension on distinct microtubules preparation
nodes.shortDescription: In cultured COS-7 cells imaged at 37 C, compare ER-marker/tubulin live images with the separate STIM1 tip-associated readout. Use source peripheral regions and pre/post-nocodazole windows; sliding and tip-attachment events have distinct operational definitions.

nodes.name: Organelle-specific localization and ER contact patterns preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use separate source COS-7 preparations labeled for ER plus mitochondria or ER plus Rab5-positive early endosomes. Combine live imaging and retrospective tubulin/acetylation staining in cell peripheries; the organelle comparisons are not one simultaneous same-cell acquisition.

nodes.name: Matched-source EGF uptake with dynab and dynamin expression variants preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the source HeLa expression variants in the separate low-EGF fluorescent uptake assay, followed by acid removal of surface ligand and EGFR immunofluorescence. Do not equate the different ligand concentration, receptor or cells with the transferrin experiment.

nodes.name: HeLa clathrin-pit lifetime with and without dynab preparation
nodes.shortDescription: In source HeLa cells, compare tagged clathrin with EGFP control or dynab using live TIRF imaging. The embedded Figure 4 supplement 1 pools 234 and 236 events, respectively, from four experiments with one to five cells per experiment.

nodes.name: Dynab/dynamin-dependent transferrin uptake in HeLa cells preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare source HeLa cells expressing dynab alone, dynamin-1 or dynamin-2 alone, corresponding coexpressions and nontransfected controls. Measure fluorescent transferrin after the 30 min uptake interval and acid removal of surface ligand; use intracellular image intensity and separate transferrin-receptor immunofluorescence.

nodes.name: Satellite-cell redox and chromatin response context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare vehicle and Trolox-treated geriatric satellite cells using ROS/autophagy-associated measurements, INK4a-locus H2A-ubiquitination ChIP, p16 expression and finite proliferation/regeneration readouts. The ChIP comparison uses a 48-hour treatment.

nodes.name: Satellite-cell redox and chromatin response perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the source-defined antioxidant treatment to the geriatric preparation.

nodes.name: Satellite-cell redox and chromatin response response
nodes.shortDescription: Trolox treatment changes redox-associated, autophagy and p16/chromatin readouts and improves reported geriatric satellite-cell function, constraining a source-proposed ROS–INK4a connection.

nodes.name: Geriatric satellite-cell rescue context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare young and geriatric satellite cells using bafilomycin-controlled LC3 reporters. For rescue, pretreat geriatric cells for 48 hours with rapamycin or supply LV-Atg7, then transplant labeled cells into pre-injured recipient muscle and assess the source 4/28-day endpoints.

nodes.name: Geriatric satellite-cell rescue perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Pretreat geriatric donor cells with rapamycin or the separately defined Atg7-expression intervention.

nodes.name: Geriatric satellite-cell rescue response
nodes.shortDescription: Restoring autophagy-related activity improves source-reported proliferative/regenerative behavior of geriatric satellite cells in these finite assays; this response differs from rapamycin-treated arrested fibroblasts and Atg7-null cells.

nodes.name: Satellite-cell Atg7 loss context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare Atg7-floxed control and Pax7-Cre/Pax7-CreER satellite-cell deletion preparations. The inducible comparison measures markers after tamoxifen and satellite-cell pool size at 30 days; injury/regeneration assays are distinct source endpoints.

nodes.name: Satellite-cell Atg7 loss perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Delete Atg7 in the specified Pax7-expressing satellite-cell preparation.

nodes.name: Satellite-cell Atg7 loss response
nodes.shortDescription: Atg7 loss in young satellite-cell preparations is associated with premature senescence-related phenotypes and reduced cell-pool/regenerative function; rapamycin does not rescue the reported Atg7-null regenerative failure.

nodes.name: Expression distribution depends on regulatory architecture
nodes.shortDescription: The source constitutive-activator circuits give graded unimodal responses, whereas the positive-feedback variants produce separated low/high GFP populations over tested induction conditions. Reporter placement and gene dosage change peak separation and the fractions in each state.

nodes.name: Bimodality does not identify a universal bistable mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: The source mathematical model offers bistability as an interpretation of the synthetic positive-feedback data; its kinetics/noise assumptions and illustrative cooperativity are not independently fitted here. Positive feedback need not give binary behavior for all parameter regimes.

nodes.name: Finite induced-state persistence and reversal
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected autoregulatory preparation, the source reports stable population fractions during its 6-12 h examination interval; removing the inducer causes expression to decay toward uninduced levels. The observation does not establish irreversible cell identity.

nodes.name: Observed expression transitions during growth
nodes.shortDescription: Initially low-expression cells can produce mixed low/high colonies under continued induction, while the illustrated high-expression lineage retains detectable reporter expression. The source reports slower growth of high-expressing cells, but the inconsistent image times prevent a new precise relative division-rate estimate.

nodes.name: Conditional gene-expression response in synthetic yeast circuits
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct gene regulation through source-designated synthetic yeast expression architectures, finite reporter-state persistence and lineage follow-up. Preserve experimental bimodality, model interpretation, reporter limitations and source inconsistencies; do not generalize to every natural regulatory layer or irreversible cell fate.

nodes.name: Tested genetic-complement intervention
nodes.shortDescription: In the existing JCVI-syn3.0 genome, the source seven-gene addition/deletion comparison changes the morphological phenotype, while single-cluster addition is insufficient.

nodes.name: Targeted DNA-repair readouts and genome-maintenance limits
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct DNA repair with the source human-cell targeted-break assay, distinguishing repair-product detection, selection, donor-template effects and inferred pathway fractions. Retain broad lesion surveillance, endogenous fidelity, checkpoint/chromatin coordination and cell-fate control as separate unresolved coverage obligations.

nodes.name: Unresolved extension from a targeted assay to genome stability
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed targeted-break assays do not establish total endogenous lesion repair, replication-error correction, chromatin-state control, checkpoint coordination, apoptosis selection or faithful genome inheritance over many generations. Those broader claims require separate lesion- and lineage-specific studies.

nodes.name: AP-1 and glycosylation affect a specific cargo-recovery route
nodes.shortDescription: The source control cisternae recover cargo fluorescence around the early-to-late transition; AP-1 disruption or removal of the reporter glycosylation site largely eliminates the recovery and transient increase, while Golgi maturation remains observed.

nodes.name: Cargo fluorescence changes during the maturation transition
nodes.shortDescription: Across 19 aligned source maturation events, cargo fluorescence transiently increases by approximately 70% during the early-to-late transition. This intensity result motivates an exchange interpretation but is not by itself direct counting of transported molecules.

nodes.name: Tested AP-1 and cargo-modification conditions
nodes.shortDescription: In the source nocodazole/FRAP preparation, AP-1 disruption or loss of reporter glycosylation suppresses the measured cargo recovery at the maturation transition.

nodes.name: Unresolved molecular packaging mechanism of soluble cargo
nodes.shortDescription: The source proposes that glycosylated soluble cargo can accompany transmembrane glycosylation enzymes in AP-1 carriers. The actual cargo-enzyme binding and individual recycling carriers were not directly established by this source readout.

nodes.name: gough2010-fibroblast-tonic-priming: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Primary or 3T3-immortalized matched MEFs are cultured in DMEM with 5 percent FBS and 2 mM glutamine. Conditioned medium is prepared over 3 days and transferred for 16-24 hours. c-Jun deficiency, IFNAR deficiency, type-I-IFN/IFNAR-blocking antibodies, IFNbeta RNAi and STAT1 add-back distinguish production, receptor response and downstream competence. Read STAT1 mRNA/protein, IFNgamma-induced GAS binding/transcription and EMCV protection. Figure 7 gives a 24-hour viral assay but Methods gives 16 hours; timing is unresolved.

nodes.name: Yeast nutrient-conditioned acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Collect chemostat cultures under source-defined nutrient limitations and growth rates. Measure extracellular exchange, metabolite abundance and enzyme/protein abundance; distinguish these inputs from subsequently constrained internal flux estimates.

nodes.name: Yeast nutrient-conditioned acquisition perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Change the supplied limiting nutrient and controlled culture growth conditions.

nodes.name: Yeast nutrient-conditioned acquisition response
nodes.shortDescription: Nutrient-limited chemostat conditions yield different measured metabolite/protein profiles and extracellular rates, supplying inputs for the separate source flux/kinetic inference.

nodes.name: Nutrient-dependent metabolic-rate inference context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare controlled nutrient-limited chemostats using metabolite/protein abundance measurements, external rates and constrained metabolic flux analysis. SIMMER compares kinetic forms; selected predicted inhibitors receive separate biochemical tests.

nodes.name: Nutrient-dependent metabolic-rate inference perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Change the limiting nutrient and compare source-inferred flux and candidate kinetic regulation.

nodes.name: Nutrient-dependent metabolic-rate inference response
nodes.shortDescription: Substrate and metabolite levels account for substantial flux variation across the tested conditions; selected allosteric inhibition is biochemically supported, whereas broader rate-control assignments depend on model and available measurements.

nodes.name: Source HDAC-inhibitor intervention
nodes.shortDescription: Under the declared COS-7 treatment and imaging conditions, TSA and the separate tubacin comparison increase measured ER sliding with increased acetylation-associated signal.

nodes.name: Unresolved molecular implementation of osmotic integration
nodes.shortDescription: The source infers effective integral feedback and constrains its location, but the complete molecular realization of the integrating reactions remains unidentified in this reconstruction.

nodes.name: Homeostasis and stress-response scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: No unique fixed viable envelope, simultaneous stabilization of all variables, universally beneficial stress response or general recovery guarantee is measured. Redox and every ion-specific mechanism remain separate evidence obligations.

nodes.name: Homeostasis and stress-response scope
nodes.shortDescription: Homeostasis is represented by named regulated variables and finite recovery responses: osmotic signaling/volume, cytosolic pH, heat-shock feedback and nutrient-dependent quality-control responses.

nodes.name: Bounded human-exposure/ex-vivo recovery
nodes.shortDescription: The human endotoxemia/ex-vivo preparation supports modifiability of selected measured monocyte outputs after a controlled acute exposure. It does not equate a culture recovery intervention with in-vivo therapeutic efficacy or reconstruct the full human progenitor memory compartment.

nodes.name: Cellular Mechanisms of Immune Response: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: Cellular immune response is reconstructed as a family of existing mammalian-cell recognition/signaling/effector preparations, not a single universal cellular arising. Necrotic donor IL-1alpha and recipient IL-1R/MyD88-dependent secretion, primed NLRP3 cytokine processing and acute local recruitment are distinct admitted cases. None establishes that prokaryotic cell organization or antigen-antibody recognition is necessary for every cellular defense, or that these modern mechanisms arose before organism-scale immune systems.

nodes.name: Inflammasome Activation and IL-1-family Signaling: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: Inflammasome activation is reconstructed as tested canonical WT NLRP3 activation in already LPS-primed mouse BMDMs, with ASC/caspase-1/IL-1beta outputs, ionic manipulation and explicit AIM2/activating-mutant controls. Priming, assembly-associated readouts, processing and secretion are not interchangeable. The tested K-dependent route is not every inflammasome or IL-1-family pathway; sterile IL-1alpha/mesothelial signaling provides a separately observed non-ASC/non-caspase-1-dependent case.

nodes.name: Cytoskeleton-associated ER movement and organelle-specific routes
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct intracellular transport through separate COS-7 ER movement modes, source intervention responses and organelle localization. Distinguish movement, track association, physical contact, motor identity, delivery function and cell-scale organization rather than treating cytoskeleton as one universal routing cause.

nodes.name: joncker2010-mhc-environment-reset: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Transfer WT or beta2-microglobulin-deficient splenocytes, typically into recipients irradiated with 6 Gy 4-5 hours earlier; an MHC-I-positive NK-deficient host enables upward-reset comparison. Each recipient receives 10^8 splenocytes containing about 2.5-3.5 x 10^6 NK cells. Measure donor-gated receptor-triggered intracellular IFNgamma at about 10 days, and separately test deficient-target graft rejection. CFSE-undivided donor cells address mature-cell resetting without proliferation; source unirradiated and chimera comparisons have distinct conditions.

nodes.name: AMPK/mTOR–Ulk1 coupling context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare glucose starvation, AMPK perturbation, Rheb/mTORC1 activity and Ulk1 mutants using immunoprecipitation, phosphosite blots, in-vitro kinase assays and source autophagy readouts.

nodes.name: AMPK/mTOR–Ulk1 coupling perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Change AMPK/mTOR activity or Ulk1 phosphorylation context under defined nutrient conditions.

nodes.name: AMPK/mTOR–Ulk1 coupling response
nodes.shortDescription: The source supports AMPK-dependent Ulk1 activation and mTORC1-dependent inhibition of Ulk1–AMPK coupling in its preparations; glucose versus amino-acid starvation can use different AMPK dependencies.

nodes.name: Yeast heat-feedback disruption context
nodes.shortDescription: Shift yeast from 25 to 39 degrees C and follow an HSE-YFP reporter. Compare wild type with Hsf1-independent Hsp70 expression, Hsf1 CE2 variants, biochemical binding assays and Hsp104 aggregation readouts.

nodes.name: Yeast heat-feedback disruption perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Disconnect Hsf1-to-Hsp70 transcriptional feedback or alter CE2-mediated Hsp70 binding.

nodes.name: Yeast heat-feedback disruption response
nodes.shortDescription: Disconnecting inducible Hsp70 expression prolongs Hsf1 reporter activation; Hsp70-binding-site perturbations tune response deactivation. Reporter persistence and aggregate clearance can dissociate.

nodes.name: Cationic dye loss accompanying bacterial voltage transients preparation
nodes.shortDescription: In the source TMRM-loaded E. coli imaging preparation, record dye intensity with PROPS; retain the separate no-PROPS dim-illumination control. Treat cell loading, illumination and loss from the fluorescent intracellular pool as assay boundaries.

nodes.name: Tethered bacterial motor response during optical depolarization preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the separate source JY29 strain tethered to a coverslip by a flagellum, and record body rotation together with PROPS. Preserve this preparation rather than transferring its strain identity to all optical or ATP assays.

nodes.name: Optical voltage dynamics and pH controls in supplied E. coli preparation
nodes.shortDescription: In the source PROPS-expressing E. coli preparation under an agarose pad and minimal medium, compare optical voltage responses with coexpressed cytoplasmic pHluorin and metabolic/illumination perturbations. Calibration is based on induced transmembrane voltage; full strain/preparation details are in the unread supplement.

nodes.name: Corrected senescence-assay controls
nodes.shortDescription: The 2021 correction fixes original Figure 6 control labels and separates drug schedules from DMSO-treated shRNA depletion.

nodes.name: SASP–arrest separation context
nodes.shortDescription: After irradiation or oncogenic-RAS senescence induction, compare rapamycin with vehicle using cell number, DNA synthesis and colony-formation readouts over the source recovery windows. Corrected Figure 6e panels have GFP shRNA; Figure 6g depletion comparisons have DMSO. These are distinct controls, not a combined drug/shRNA intervention.

nodes.name: SASP–arrest separation perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Keep the senescence induction context while changing rapamycin exposure.

nodes.name: SASP–arrest separation response
nodes.shortDescription: Rapamycin does not reverse established irradiation-associated growth arrest in these primary cells, although some senescence-associated phenotypes are reduced.

nodes.name: mTOR-sensitive SASP output context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare rapamycin- and vehicle-treated senescent fibroblasts using cytokine assays, polysome profiling and NF-kappaB/IL1 signaling measurements; add recombinant IL1A as a bypass/rescue test.

nodes.name: mTOR-sensitive SASP output perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Inhibit mTORC1 pharmacologically and compare the IL1A bypass condition.

nodes.name: mTOR-sensitive SASP output response
nodes.shortDescription: Rapamycin selectively reduces inflammatory output and IL1A translation; exogenous IL1A restores IL6 secretion in the tested rapamycin-treated senescent preparation.

nodes.name: Phylogenomic and ancestral reconstruction of chromatophore evolution preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Analyze source chromatophore/cyanobacterial/plastid ortholog comparisons, keeping the 406-gene cyanobacterial/chromatophore tree distinct from the twenty-gene forty-genome Fig. 2 analysis. Infer gene-family ancestors by parsimony and dates through the source externally calibrated molecular clock.

nodes.name: New chromatophore genome sequences and retained cellular functions preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Keep newly sequenced Paulinella longichromatophora and P. micropora NZ27 chromatophore genomes distinct from three previously deposited comparator genomes. Assemble and annotate source sequence data; the source species differ in collection, genome preparation and sequencing platform.

nodes.name: Stimulus-dependent macrophage activation spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: Across the declared human stimulation panel, transcriptional relationships extend beyond a single M1/M2 axis. The spectrum is a source-derived representation of measured expression, not a count of immutable natural cell types or an experimentally established dominant scalar regulatory bias.

nodes.name: Expression network and tissue-function boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Correlation/WGCNA modules identify stimulus-associated programs; inferred connections remain analytical associations. Persistent tissue repair, regulatory function, hysteresis and trained history require their own preparations and cannot be read directly from this network geometry.

nodes.name: Macrophage Polarization and Local Myeloid Regulatory Bias: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: Macrophage activation is reconstructed as source-defined human monocyte-derived culture programs under multiple inputs, with a spectrum rather than a compulsory M1/M2 binary. Transcriptomic geometry, selected functional checks and separate trained-history experiments are distinguished. A persistent dominant scalar bias, all resident/recruited cell origins, fixed tissue-repair/regulatory roles and causal links read from a coexpression graph are not admitted without matched source evidence.

nodes.name: Secreted cargo detection depends on the external collection boundary
nodes.shortDescription: The source reporter is detected in rich medium by approximately ten minutes and more prominently at twenty minutes. No medium signal was detected in the separate minimal-medium experiment, despite evidence for periplasmic reporter accumulation; absence from collected medium is not equivalent to absence of secretion.
