nodes.name: Enclosure without detected cytoplasmic reporter
nodes.shortDescription: Selected RGD6 vesicles have membrane staining and exclude external fluorescent dextran yet lack detectable constitutive mCherry. Enclosure alone therefore does not establish possession of the source cytoplasmic reporter or a complete self-maintaining cell.

nodes.name: Dark-adapted single-rod current and incremental background response preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Dark-adapt mice for at least 15 hours; suction-electrode recordings from single rods in perfused retinal pieces at 35-37 C, pH 7.4. Calibrated 500 nm 10 ms flashes; dim responses at most 20 percent of maximum. Estimate mean single-photon response by mean-variance scaling from at least 30 flashes; 520 nm steady backgrounds are applied about one minute before incremental flashes.

nodes.name: Dark-adapted single-rod current and incremental background response response
nodes.shortDescription: GCAP knockout yields larger, slower dim-flash responses; GCAP2-only expression does not restore the early fast recovery even when maximal homogenate activity is restored. Bright-background incremental sensitivity falls sooner, while non-GCAP adaptation remains.

nodes.name: Dark-adapted single-rod current and incremental background response scope
nodes.shortDescription: This assay retains its own preparation, observable and inference boundary; a separate biochemical or cell-current result is not the same acquisition.

nodes.name: Retinal homogenate and rod-outer-segment guanylate cyclase assays preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Pool four dark-adapted retinas per genotype for homogenate assays; separately assay rod-outer-segment extracts. Compare low calcium (at most 50 nM) with 2 micromolar calcium, GCAP2 transgene and recombinant GCAP1 addition. Three experiments at least in duplicate are reported.

nodes.name: Retinal homogenate and rod-outer-segment guanylate cyclase assays response
nodes.shortDescription: Knockout removes detectable calcium dependence of GC activity, rather than removing the GC enzyme or all basal activity; GCAP2 transgene restores maximal homogenate activity and added recombinant GCAP1 restores calcium responsiveness in separate extracts.

nodes.name: Retinal homogenate and rod-outer-segment guanylate cyclase assays scope
nodes.shortDescription: This assay retains its own preparation, observable and inference boundary; a separate biochemical or cell-current result is not the same acquisition.

nodes.name: GCAP1/2 knockout and transgenic GCAP2 expression validation preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Target both GCAP genes in 129SV/C57BL6-derived mice and compare retinal transcript/protein expression with wild-type, heterozygous and bovine GCAP2 transgenic genotypes.

nodes.name: GCAP1/2 knockout and transgenic GCAP2 expression validation response
nodes.shortDescription: Double knockout removes detectable GCAP1/2 expression; transgenic GCAP2 is expressed at about twice endogenous GCAP2, so downstream rescue is not a dose-matched single-variable control.

nodes.name: GCAP1/2 knockout and transgenic GCAP2 expression validation scope
nodes.shortDescription: This assay retains its own preparation, observable and inference boundary; a separate biochemical or cell-current result is not the same acquisition.

nodes.name: Mesothelial IL-1R/MyD88 inflammatory output
nodes.shortDescription: Recipient Il1r or MyD88 deficiency and IL-1 receptor antagonist impair lysate-induced CXCL1/signaling. Tlr2/Tlr4-, Asc- and caspase-1-deficient mesothelial cells retain the reported response; microbial agonist controls distinguish the tested pathways.

nodes.name: Genomic context changes the FtsZ-cluster requirement
nodes.shortDescription: JCVI-syn3A retains nearly normal morphology after deletion of the ftsZ-containing cluster, despite that cluster being required in the tested syn3.0+126 context. The observed requirement is conditional on genomic and expression context, not a universal seven-gene minimum for life.

nodes.name: Joint gene-complement morphology response
nodes.shortDescription: Adding seven source genes together restores a nearly normal morphology in the JCVI-syn3.0 background; the ftsZ-containing cluster alone does not. Within the tested syn3.0+126 background, removing any of the seven returns pleomorphism.

nodes.name: Unresolved division mechanism in minimized cells
nodes.shortDescription: The physical roles of several genes, force transduction, membrane accumulation and precise scission mechanisms remain unresolved in this review; filament propagation does not establish a universal autonomous cellular construction mechanism.

nodes.name: Propagation with heterogeneous morphology
nodes.shortDescription: In the source microfluidic setting, JCVI-syn3.0 and RGD6 propagate as irregular, branching or pearled cellular forms, whereas JCVI-syn1.0 is predominantly small and round. Growth and shape change are not equated with complete daughter-cell scission.

nodes.name: mitroulis2018-day28-transplant: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Isolate LT-HSCs from beta-glucan- or PBS-treated male mouse donors 28 days after the declared 1-mg systemic priming. Transfer 50 sorted donor LT-HSCs plus 2 x 10^5 congenic carrier cells per recipient into lethally 9-Gy-irradiated B6/SJL recipients. Measure donor-derived blood lineages and overall donor chimerism at week 12. This transplantation is a distinct preparation from early pool expansion and inhibitor assays.

nodes.name: mitroulis2018-progenitor-training: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Male 9-11-week C57BL/6 mice receive a single intraperitoneal 1-mg Trametes-versicolor beta-glucan-peptide injection in 200 microliters PBS, with PBS control. Flow-defined progenitors are assessed at days 1, 7 and 28. Defined IL-1 receptor antagonist, GM-CSF blockade and metabolic inhibitors probe early expansion, without isolating every cell-intrinsic step. These timed pool/inhibitor acquisitions are kept distinct from the separately recorded sorted-cell transplantation.

nodes.name: Transient microbial-priming history
nodes.shortDescription: Initial beta-glucan and LPS exposures yield different day-6 macrophage-like response programs: beta-glucan enhances tested subsequent cytokine responses, while LPS can tolerize them. Repeated or sustained stimulation is therefore not required in this particular induction design and need not monotonically increase reactivity.

nodes.name: Nutrient–mTOR, autophagy and senescence scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: Nutrient classes, cell backgrounds, serum and observation times change the autophagy outcome. Rapamycin-sensitive SASP does not demonstrate rejuvenation, recovery of division or a universal maintenance-versus-growth decision variable.

nodes.name: Nutrient–mTOR, autophagy and senescence scope
nodes.shortDescription: mTOR/AMPK regulation of Ulk1/autophagy and mTOR-sensitive senescent secretion are distinct preparation-specific regulatory processes; senescence growth arrest is an independent endpoint.

nodes.name: munoz2013-primed-bmdm-ion-gating: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare WT, Nlrp3-deficient, Asc-deficient and Nlrp3-R258W BMDMs after LPS priming with tested pore-forming/particulate agonists or low-K medium. Isosmotic NaCl/KCl/choline substitution controls ionic composition at 300 mOsm. Read IL-1beta by ELISA, caspase-1 processing/ASC oligomerization by immunoblot and intracellular ions by ICP-OES; ion measurements in deficient cells limit secondary pyroptotic leakage. Timing is assay-specific: rapid gramicidin tests include 15-30 minutes, particulate challenges include 2 hours, AIM2/R258W comparisons include 4 hours and ROS perturbation controls include 6 hours; complete preparation protocol remains partly supplemental.

nodes.name: Yeast ramp and feedback constraint context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare step and ramp osmotic inputs, altered PBS2 expression and Hog1 kinase/protein-production perturbations using the source flow-chamber readouts.

nodes.name: Yeast ramp and feedback constraint perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Change the temporal waveform or feedback activity rather than treating adaptation as a constant trait.

nodes.name: Yeast ramp and feedback constraint response
nodes.shortDescription: Ramp inputs do not show the same perfect adaptation as steps. The source constrains an effective integrating feedback mechanism involving Hog1-dependent glycerol synthesis without uniquely identifying every molecular reaction.

nodes.name: Yeast step osmoadaptation context
nodes.shortDescription: Log-phase Hog1-YFP yeast, with the Sln1 branch isolated by SHO1 deletion, receives osmolyte steps in a flow chamber. Phase contrast, nuclear Hog1 fluorescence and glycerol assays constrain volume and signaling dynamics.

nodes.name: Yeast step osmoadaptation perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Apply a hyperosmotic step while retaining the defined growth medium and observation boundary.

nodes.name: Yeast step osmoadaptation response
nodes.shortDescription: Hog1 nuclear enrichment returns near its pre-step level while glycerol accumulates and volume-growth behavior recovers in the assayed step-input range.

nodes.name: Parkin-associated mitochondrial turnover context
nodes.shortDescription: Use CCCP depolarization, Parkin localization and mitochondrial markers; distinguish endogenous recruitment assays from ectopic-Parkin HeLa/MEF elimination assays. Compare ATG5-deficient and lysosomal/autophagy-inhibitor conditions.

nodes.name: Parkin-associated mitochondrial turnover perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Depolarize mitochondria and compare Parkin/autophagy competence within the stated preparations.

nodes.name: Parkin-associated mitochondrial turnover response
nodes.shortDescription: Parkin is recruited to impaired mitochondria, and source ectopic-Parkin preparations show autophagy-dependent mitochondrial elimination constrained by ATG5 and inhibitor controls.

nodes.name: Necrotic donor IL-1alpha input
nodes.shortDescription: WT necrotic macrophage/liver extracts induce mesothelial CXCL1; Il1a-deficient donor extracts show greatly reduced activity. The perturbation identifies a contribution of donor IL-1alpha, not direct binding of all damage molecules to a generic pattern receptor.

nodes.name: Altered MHC environment and donor-cell controls
nodes.shortDescription: Transferred mature WT NK cells become less receptor-responsive in MHC-I-deficient hosts, while deficient-origin cells gain responsiveness in the specified MHC-I-positive recipient comparison. The environment and recipient controls differ by direction; the source retains unresolved stromal/other-cell contributions.

nodes.name: Plastic mature NK responsiveness and scoped rejection
nodes.shortDescription: Changes occur among donor NK cells that have not divided, arguing against replacement by newly differentiated NK cells as the sole explanation. Downward-reset preparations also show impaired deficient-target graft rejection. This is a conditional capacity, not a fixed immune safety margin or a guarantee that reduced self-MHC always triggers elimination.

nodes.name: NK-Mediated Immune Surveillance Capacity: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: NK capacity is reconstructed as conditional mature-cell receptor responsiveness and separately assayed deficient-target rejection in mouse transfer preparations. Existing NK cells can reset upward/downward under a changed MHC environment without division; loss of self-MHC therefore does not guarantee elimination. This supports plastic source-bound competence, not a fixed persistent safety margin, lifetime prevention probability, universal antigen-independent history or complete tumor/viral surveillance mechanism.

nodes.name: Scoped NLRP3 assembly and IL-1beta output
nodes.shortDescription: The tested WT pathway links K depletion with ASC oligomerization, caspase-1 processing and IL-1beta release. The AIM2 polydAdT control and activating Nlrp3-R258W mutant do not share the same K requirement. ROS/mitochondrial perturbation, large-pore formation and Na influx are not universal necessary components in these assays.

nodes.name: Primed macrophage low-potassium condition
nodes.shortDescription: In primed WT BMDMs, low-K medium alone produces NLRP3-dependent IL-1beta release, while raising extracellular K inhibits the tested canonical agonist responses. Isosmotic substitutions and inflammasome-deficient ion measurements constrain osmolarity and secondary lysis alternatives.

nodes.name: novakovic2016-culture-recovery: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Healthy-donor purified monocytes receive LPS (10-100 ng/ml) or beta-glucan (5 micrograms/ml) for 24 hours, washout and five days of culture in RPMI/10 percent human serum. Rechallenge with LPS and assay TNF/IL-6 release after 24 hours; separate early RNA/chromatin responses are not substituted for secretion. A defined post-LPS beta-glucan recovery exposure tests reversibility, with untreated, tolerant and trained culture comparators.

nodes.name: novakovic2016-endotoxemia-exvivo: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Twelve healthy nonsmoking volunteers receive an intravenous 2-ng/kg E. coli O:113 reference LPS bolus. Obtain blood before and 4 hours afterward, isolate monocytes and apply culture or beta-glucan ex vivo; then challenge ex vivo with LPS (10 ng/ml) and measure TNF/IL-6 by ELISA. This linked in-vivo/ex-vivo preparation remains distinct from the standard donor culture.

nodes.name: Geometry-dependent normalization of exchange measurements
nodes.shortDescription: The source normalizes passive exchange through a compartmental Fick-law model using nuclear/cytoplasmic volumes and estimated pore numbers. Size-dependent exchange is an inferred permeability under these assumptions, not direct counting of individual nuclear-pore crossings.

nodes.name: Gradual nuclear-pore permeability rather than a hard cutoff
nodes.shortDescription: The measured reporter-size series shows progressively slower passive exchange without a sharp mass cutoff. Source normalized time constants are 15 +/- 1.4 s for 27 kDa GFP and 413 +/- 92 s for the 67 kDa reporter, with source 95% confidence intervals.

nodes.name: Nutrient-specific autophagy-flux boundary context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare amino-acid withdrawal, glucose withdrawal and combined withdrawal under explicit serum conditions, including 2-hour and longer observations. Use bafilomycin-sensitive LC3, tandem fluorescent LC3, early autophagosome markers and lysosomal-acidification assays.

nodes.name: Nutrient-specific autophagy-flux boundary perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Change the nutrient combination or activate AMPK with source-defined pharmacology.

nodes.name: Nutrient-specific autophagy-flux boundary response
nodes.shortDescription: Amino-acid starvation stimulates robust autophagic readouts in these preparations, while glucose withdrawal and AMPK activation can suppress initiation and lysosomal activation; LC3-II accumulation alone can reflect restricted flux.

nodes.name: Nuclear and chromatophore protein processing in isolated chromatophores preparation
nodes.shortDescription: In Paulinella chromatophora CCAC0185, prepare chromatophore lysates from three independent cultures and enrich protein N-termini by HUNTER for LC-MS/MS. Assign peptides with source transcriptome/chromatophore reference sequences, keeping detected protein processing distinct from bioinformatic transit-motif prediction.

nodes.name: Natural early lineage segregation context
nodes.shortDescription: Collect ICM cells from E3.25-E4.5 mouse embryos, perform single-cell amplification/qPCR and microarray profiling, and compare staged wild-type with Fgf4-null embryos. The main wild-type microarray map contains 66 selected single cells.

nodes.name: Natural early lineage segregation perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare staged embryos and Fgf4-null versus wild-type ICM profiles.

nodes.name: Natural early lineage segregation response
nodes.shortDescription: Lineage expression separation emerges progressively, while Fgf4-null profiles show impaired EPI/PrE segregation relative to wild type; initial expression variability and later signal reinforcement are distinguished.

nodes.name: Preserved older CMV response and cohort-limited oldest-old contrast
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports similar aggregate CMV-specific polyfunctionality in young and usual older UK participants, with protein specificity/response size influencing results. Lower index in the separate oldest-old Italian sample qualifies a universal age-decline narrative; no isolated age mechanism, guaranteed better protection or physiological necessity of every measured function follows.

nodes.name: Track preference depends on organelle identity
nodes.shortDescription: In the source untreated samples, 77% of 57 mitochondria from ten cells colocalize with acetylated microtubules. Only 14% of 426 early endosomes from five cells show that colocalization, despite frequent ER association. The denominators and distinct preparations are retained.

nodes.name: Yeast cytosolic-pH regulation context
nodes.shortDescription: Use pHluorin fluorescence with the source calibration, buffered medium and growth measurements. Compare batch growth, medium exchange, deletion mutants and PMA1-related perturbations.

nodes.name: Yeast cytosolic-pH regulation perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Change culture environment or pH-regulatory genotype and measure pH with growth.

nodes.name: Yeast cytosolic-pH regulation response
nodes.shortDescription: Cytosolic pH varies with extracellular and growth conditions, and perturbation analyses support a contribution of pH to growth regulation rather than an invariant pH set point.

nodes.name: Conditional blockade response and damage trade-off
nodes.shortDescription: Anti-PD-L1 treatment increases tested chronic T-cell proliferation/effector responses and reduces viral burden relative to controls, including in a separately defined CD4-depleted preparation. Anti-CTLA-4 does not reproduce the reported benefit. Constitutive PD-L1 absence during clone-13 infection leads to immunopathologic death, so increased immune activity is not universally beneficial.

nodes.name: Genome-context-dependent restoration of minimized-cell morphology preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare source gene-addition and deletion derivatives of JCVI-syn3.0 and JCVI-syn3A in supplied SP4 medium, using bulk optical area distributions, representative microscopy and microfluidic morphology. Keep ectopic addition to syn3.0 distinct from deletion in the larger syn3A background.

nodes.name: Minimized mycoplasma propagation and membrane-bounded cellular forms preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare JCVI-syn1.0, JCVI-syn3.0 and RGD6 in supplied serum-containing SP4 medium. Bulk-culture morphology and shear-sheltered microfluidic time-lapse imaging are distinct measurements; overnight imaging at 37 C lasts approximately 10-16 h. mCherry labels cytoplasm, nucleoid dyes label DNA and membrane/dextran labels delimit selected cellular forms.

nodes.name: DDR-dependent secretory subset
nodes.shortDescription: ATM, NBS1 and CHK2 depletion reduce initiation/maintenance of the tested damage-associated cytokine response. ATM depletion changes a subset rather than all detected SASP factors; cytokine output, chromatin lesions and proliferation remain distinct observables.

nodes.name: Phototransduction cascade: observable boundaries
nodes.shortDescription: The original card is reconstructed through distinct source-bound preparations; full end-to-end transfer remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Complete phototransduction transfer: unresolved
nodes.shortDescription: A complete gain/noise and membrane-voltage transfer function has not been established by the admitted preparations.

nodes.name: Pit lifetime and successful cargo uptake are different observables
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports no significant change in clathrin-pit lifetime under its dynab/control comparison, while its separate transferrin experiment detects impaired internalization. Unchanged pit timing is therefore insufficient to certify unperturbed cargo transport.

nodes.name: Egg-extract Cdc2 hysteresis context
nodes.shortDescription: Use cycloheximide-treated Xenopus egg extracts and recombinant nondegradable delta65-cyclin B1. Compare Cdc2 kinase activation at controlled cyclin concentrations and different prior mitotic/interphase states.

nodes.name: Egg-extract Cdc2 hysteresis perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Vary supplied nondegradable cyclin and initial extract state.

nodes.name: Egg-extract Cdc2 hysteresis response
nodes.shortDescription: Cdc2 activity exhibits different activation and inactivation thresholds with preparation history, consistent with bistability and hysteresis in the tested extract system.

nodes.name: Untracked post-Golgi delivery steps
nodes.shortDescription: The source follows cargo departure from late Golgi but could not track post-Golgi carriers or their final fusion at the plasma membrane. Detailed targeting, docking, fusion and release mechanisms remain unestablished by this acquisition.

nodes.name: Prokaryotic organization in a supplied minimal-cell model
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct prokaryotic organization through existing genomically minimized mycoplasmas: separate membrane enclosure, population propagation, complete scission, reporter expression and genotype-dependent morphology. These supplied living-cell observations do not demonstrate origin, universal minimality or simultaneous closure of every cellular function.

nodes.name: Protein modification has a separate measured response
nodes.shortDescription: The source APVNTT cargo shows an endoglycosidase-H-sensitive mobility difference relative to its nonglycosylated variant. This supports N-linked modification of the chosen reporter, not exhaustive maturation or folding of all exported proteins.

nodes.name: Source-specific targeting, modification, recycling and secretion
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct the secretory pathway using distinguishable source observations in engineered yeast: signal/receptor-dependent ER exit, glycosylation, Golgi marker maturation, AP-1/glycosylation-dependent recovery and cargo collection outside the cell. Preserve the untracked late-carrier/fusion steps and the hypothetical soluble-cargo packaging mechanism.

nodes.name: DNA-damage signaling dynamics context
nodes.shortDescription: After gamma irradiation, compare naturally pulsed p53 with a source-designed sequence of Nutlin-3 additions sustaining p53. Follow fluorescence and target-gene expression; the Figure 4 single-cell FISH comparison fixes pulsed cells at 21 hours and sustained cells at 12 hours to compare similar cumulative p53. The Figure 3 later proliferation/arrest assays instead use three-day signaling schedules followed by recovery.

nodes.name: DNA-damage signaling dynamics perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Use timed MDM2 inhibition to change p53 waveform while retaining the damage comparison.

nodes.name: DNA-damage signaling dynamics response
nodes.shortDescription: Changing p53 dynamics after the same irradiation stimulus changes downstream expression; the source three-day schedules also change later proliferation/arrest distributions. Separately, the Figure 4 equal-cumulative-p53 comparison measures higher CDKN1A/PML expression with sustained signaling at 12 hours than with pulsed signaling at 21 hours; it does not directly compare later cell fate at matched cumulative exposure.

nodes.name: Regulatory architecture and dynamics scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: A drawn motif alone does not establish its dynamic function. These local/mesoscopic network studies do not reconstruct one complete cell-wide controller, every coupling strength or a universal robustness theorem.

nodes.name: Tested regulatory-architecture contrast
nodes.shortDescription: Within the tested engineered yeast circuit family, replacing source-designated constitutive activator expression with positive autoregulation changes the single-cell reporter response distribution.

nodes.name: Regulatory architecture and dynamics scope
nodes.shortDescription: Regulatory networks are represented by preparation-specific feedback, switching, input waveform and response constraints across Hsp70, Hog1, CDK2, apoptosis, transcription-factor and metabolic assays.

nodes.name: rodier2009-conditioned-medium-invasion: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Collect 24-hour serum-free conditioned media from presenescent or irradiated HCA2 cells with control or ATM-targeting shRNA. Apply medium to modified Boyden/Matrigel invasion chambers containing T47D cells for 16-24 hours. Compare serum-free/presenescent medium, senescent control medium, ATM-depleted medium and recombinant IL-6 restoration to the control measured concentration (3 ng/ml). Count cells on the underside of the filter.

nodes.name: rodier2009-fibroblast-arrest-secretion: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: HCA2 human foreskin fibroblasts are cultured in DMEM/10 percent FBS at ambient oxygen. Compare 0.5 and 10 Gy X-rays, p16 expression, telomerase, p53 suppression and DDR-protein depletion; related primary fibroblast strains provide additional comparisons. BrdU labeling over 24 hours, 53BP1/gammaH2AX immunofluorescence and cell-number-normalized IL-6/IL-8 ELISA separate DNA synthesis, persistent damage and secretion. Main contrasts follow the corrected Figure 1a dose assignment; high-dose cytokine secretion develops over days, rather than the initial acute DDR.

nodes.name: saeed2014-monocyte-history: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Purify human circulating monocytes by depletion of T/B/NK cells; culture in human-serum-containing medium. Prime during the first 24 hours with beta-glucan, LPS or medium, then continue differentiation without the initial stimulus. Rechallenge day-6 macrophage-like cells for 24 hours and measure cytokines by ELISA; parallel RNA-seq/histone/accessibility profiling compares cells at collection and after culture. Figure 1B pools at least ten donors across four experiments; complete supplemental preparation details remain unread.

nodes.name: Conditioned-medium perturbation and IL-6 restoration
nodes.shortDescription: Matched donor ATM depletion and IL-6 add-back alter the activity of fibroblast conditioned medium; the medium is an experimentally transferred mixture, not a universal fixed SASP composition.

nodes.name: Scoped paracrine invasion outcome
nodes.shortDescription: T47D filter invasion is enhanced by irradiated-control conditioned medium, reduced with ATM-depleted donor medium and largely restored by added IL-6. This is a measured non-local response in the declared preparation, separate from senescence in the recipient cell or human aging disease.

nodes.name: Context-dependent soluble and EV protein output
nodes.shortDescription: The source's soluble/EV proteomic comparisons show shared and distinct protein changes across tested senescence inducers, cell types and collection times. Detection in a fraction is not proof of a unique vesicle class or secretion route, and protein abundance is not interchangeable with mRNA abundance.

nodes.name: Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: SASP is reconstructed as preparation-dependent soluble/EV-enriched protein output and specific paracrine effects, separate from proliferation arrest. Human fibroblast DDR perturbations, a controlled medium/IL-6 restoration invasion assay and a multi-context secretome atlas provide distinct evidence. Neither all listed mediators in every senescent cell nor a necessary progression to chronic inflammation/aging dysregulation, complete secretory mechanism or a universal tissue-remodeling threshold is admitted.

nodes.name: SASP composition and causal boundary
nodes.shortDescription: The atlas supports a heterogeneous measured protein output, not a rule that every senescent cell secretes every cytokine/protease/vesicle/metabolite, nor that any detected factor uniquely identifies senescence or necessarily produces chronic inflammation.

nodes.name: Persistent damage-associated fibroblast arrest
nodes.shortDescription: The source distinguishes transient 0.5-Gy DDR from 10-Gy-associated persistent foci and a senescent arrest phenotype. BrdU, damage markers and experimental context jointly identify the case; no single marker or arbitrary damage threshold defines every senescent cell.

nodes.name: Cellular Senescence as a Stress Outcome: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: Cellular senescence is reconstructed through declared human-fibroblast damage/arrest and perturbation comparisons, with independent DNA synthesis, DDR and secretory readouts. Durable stress-associated arrest differs from a transient checkpoint and from secretory output; it is not absolutely irreversible under all genetic interventions. Neither every senescence-inducing mechanism nor metabolic/epigenetic rewiring, organismal aging, tumor protection or a necessary mTOR/autophagy pathway is established by this case alone.

nodes.name: Cellular sensing and adaptation scope definition
nodes.shortDescription: A sensory pathway can also change behavior, as in chemotaxis; excluding behavioral action is an editorial boundary, not a biological law. No universal optimization, toxin-sensing mechanism or perfect adaptation to arbitrary inputs is established.

nodes.name: Cellular sensing and adaptation scope
nodes.shortDescription: Sensing is represented by ligand-dependent bacterial pathway activity, yeast osmotic response and stress/nutrient-response signaling, with adaptation distinguished from initial detection and later viability.

nodes.name: Bacterial chemotaxis FRET context
nodes.shortDescription: Engineered CheY-YFP/CheZ-CFP E. coli strains are attached to coverslips in flowing pH-7 tethering medium. Attractant/repellent steps and receptor methylation mutants are compared by emission-ratio FRET.

nodes.name: Bacterial chemotaxis FRET perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Change attractant/repellent concentration and compare receptor-modification backgrounds.

nodes.name: Bacterial chemotaxis FRET response
nodes.shortDescription: Ligand changes alter the pathway FRET signal, and response sensitivity depends on receptor modification and CheB background; signal amplification is conditional on the assayed bacterial circuit.

nodes.name: TRAIL sister-cell variability context
nodes.shortDescription: Follow sister cells expressing caspase/MOMP reporters after uniform TRAIL exposure; compare division-to-treatment interval, protein-synthesis inhibition and Bid overexpression with adopted model predictions.

nodes.name: TRAIL sister-cell variability perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare related and unrelated cells and perturb protein production or Bid level.

nodes.name: TRAIL sister-cell variability response
nodes.shortDescription: Closely related cells initially have more similar response times than unrelated cells, but this resemblance decays; protein-state variability and history matter even within clonal populations.

nodes.name: CDK2 proliferation–quiescence bifurcation context
nodes.shortDescription: Track asynchronous MCF10A cells with DHB-Venus and nuclear markers through mitosis and the next cycle. Compare mitogen withdrawal, p21 loss/induction and S-phase-associated reporter/immunofluorescence measurements.

nodes.name: CDK2 proliferation–quiescence bifurcation perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Alter p21 or mitogen availability and follow individual subsequent CDK2 trajectories.

nodes.name: CDK2 proliferation–quiescence bifurcation response
nodes.shortDescription: Cells diverge after mitosis into rising-CDK2 cycling trajectories or low-CDK2 transient quiescence; mitogen history and p21 perturbation change the observed trajectory distribution.

nodes.name: STAT1-dependent later cytokine competence
nodes.shortDescription: STAT1 re-expression in IFNAR1-deficient MEFs rescues tested IFNgamma GAS-binding/gene responses and improves protection against EMCV-associated cytopathic loss. Basal cytokine signaling is therefore represented by this regulated IFNbeta/STAT1 case, without requiring prior inflammasome activation.

nodes.name: Cell-state dependence of local biochemical rates definition
nodes.shortDescription: The cell-state description summarizes physically realized variables. The assays do not establish an additional irreducible downward force, coordinated purpose, universal metabolic-cycle necessity or causation from a global state label alone.

nodes.name: Cell-state dependence of local biochemical rates
nodes.shortDescription: Metabolite availability, pH, kinase state and compartment-associated signaling can condition biochemical activity and inferred pathway flux in specified cellular preparations.

nodes.name: Recovery after apoptotic signs context
nodes.shortDescription: Expose primary mouse liver cells to 4.5 percent ethanol for the main same-cell 2.5-hour imaging experiment, remove inducer and follow the same cells. The 5-hour population experiment is a distinct comparison; no HeLa caspase result is transferred to these cells.

nodes.name: Recovery after apoptotic signs perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Remove the defined apoptotic inducer and observe the same previously responding cells.

nodes.name: Recovery after apoptotic signs response
nodes.shortDescription: Primary liver cells exhibiting apoptotic morphology and mitochondrial fragmentation can recover those appearances after ethanol removal in the source same-cell experiment.

nodes.name: HeLa execution-reporter washout context
nodes.shortDescription: Follow HeLa cells expressing the NES-DEVD-YFP-NLS reporter through 4.3 percent ethanol exposure and washout. The Results describe Figure 1G same-cell imaging after 3 hours of exposure, with morphological recovery within 2 hours; Figure 1H population quantification and the default Methods specify 5 hours of exposure and a 2-hour recovery. Keep these acquisition histories distinct; the population fractions do not quantify the exact imaged cells.

nodes.name: HeLa execution-reporter washout perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Wash out ethanol after the defined reporter-positive response.

nodes.name: HeLa execution-reporter washout response
nodes.shortDescription: Previously responding HeLa cells can recover morphology after caspase-biosensor activation and inducer washout in this defined preparation.

nodes.name: Constrained T-Cell Function under Chronic Stimulation and Age-Shifted Immunity: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: T-cell constraint is reconstructed as distinct mouse chronic-LCMV inhibitory-pathway interventions, human cross-sectional age/CMV subset observations and human ex-vivo CMV functional comparisons. These are not one universal exhaustion/aging process. PD-L1 blockade improves selected chronic functions but constitutive pathway absence can damage the host; usual older UK donors retain tested CMV polyfunctionality. Blood composition, cellular function, response thresholds and clinical protection remain distinct.

nodes.name: Passive nucleocytoplasmic exchange of a yeast reporter-size series preparation
nodes.shortDescription: In living wild-type yeast, compare six GFP-Protein A reporter variants of approximately 27-67 kDa. Bleach cytoplasm and fit nuclear fluorescence equilibration using measured cell/nuclear geometry and an assumed NPC surface density; the source reports 236 wild-type single-cell measurements across the series.

nodes.name: Synthetic contact-induced sorting context
nodes.shortDescription: Mix L929 sender cells bearing CD19 with synNotch receiver cells that induce E-cadherin/GFP, then follow fluorescence and spatial sorting. Reciprocal ligand circuits form a separate three-layer program.

nodes.name: Synthetic contact-induced sorting perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Provide the specified synthetic sender–receiver contact and cadherin-output circuit.

nodes.name: Synthetic contact-induced sorting response
nodes.shortDescription: Engineered contact signaling coupled to cadherin expression yields spatial sorting and sequential multicellular structures; no-Ecad and DAPT comparisons are reported controls for this circuit.

nodes.name: Tolerant output is not complete transcriptional silence
nodes.shortDescription: LPS-tolerized macrophages retain substantial transcription/chromatin responses to re-exposure while selected cytokine outputs are reduced. In particular, IL6 transcript induction need not coincide with released IL-6 protein; an apparent weak output is not absence of every internal response.

nodes.name: Source-specific partial recovery after beta-glucan
nodes.shortDescription: A later beta-glucan exposure partially restores selected tolerized cytokine/program responses and associated chromatin activity. This provides a history-dependent and modifiable state comparison, not proof of a single universal inflammatory set point or an irreversible innate memory state.

nodes.name: Tonic IFNbeta-dependent priming input
nodes.shortDescription: Wild-type conditioned medium restores STAT1 expression in c-Jun-deficient MEFs; IFN/IFNAR neutralization and donor IFNbeta knockdown reduce this activity. IFNAR-deficient recipients fail to use that conditioned-medium signal, distinguishing ligand production from response competence.

nodes.name: Trained Immunity and Innate Memory Reprogramming: reviewed scope
nodes.shortDescription: Trained immunity is reconstructed as finite history-dependent responses in human peripheral monocyte cultures, modifiable tolerance/recovery including a linked human endotoxemia/ex-vivo preparation, and a separate mouse systemic-progenitor/transplant case. Initial exposure can enhance or diminish later output; one short priming exposure can suffice in the declared designs. Response amplitudes, chromatin associations, progenitor lineage bias and actual stimulus thresholds are distinguished. No universal lower threshold, irreversible memory, common histone mechanism or organism-scale inflammatory hysteresis law is admitted.

nodes.name: Finite transferred progenitor lineage bias
nodes.shortDescription: LT-HSCs isolated 28 days after priming produce a higher myeloid proportion in the defined congenic recipients at week 12 than control-origin cells, without a reported difference in total donor chimerism. This supports persistent preparation-associated lineage bias, not identification of one obligatory epigenetic mark or universal autonomous cellular memory.

nodes.name: Systemically primed progenitor changes
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports timed changes in mouse hematopoietic/myeloid progenitor pools after beta-glucan versus PBS. IL-1 receptor, GM-CSF and metabolic perturbations reduce selected expansion readouts; different time points need not change every HSC population in the same direction.

nodes.name: Finite trained and tolerant recall output
nodes.shortDescription: After the intervening culture period, rechallenge cytokines differ with prior exposure and accompany distinct transcript/histone/accessibility profiles. The experiment measures response amplitudes and program associations, not a complete stimulus-dose threshold curve, thermodynamic hysteresis loop or unique epigenetic storage mechanism.

nodes.name: Cargo uptake depends on probe and dynamin context
nodes.shortDescription: Dynab alone or coexpressed with dynamin-2 markedly reduces source transferrin internalization and redistributes detectable receptor toward the cell surface; coexpression with dynamin-1 preserves uptake relative to the tested dynamin-overexpression controls.

nodes.name: Cargo-specific endocytosis and separately observed secretion
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct uptake and secretion as distinct cellular operations: cargo/isoform-dependent HeLa internalization, clathrin-event timing and engineered yeast release to medium. Keep receptor uptake, intracellular routing, periplasm retention and final fusion mechanisms separate.

nodes.name: Factor-induced neuronal specialization context
nodes.shortDescription: Introduce doxycycline-inducible neuronal-factor lentiviruses into mouse fibroblasts, screen factor combinations and assay neuronal markers, morphology and whole-cell electrophysiology. Functional synapse tests include source-defined co-cultures.

nodes.name: Factor-induced neuronal specialization perturbation
nodes.shortDescription: Supply the defined neuronal transcription factors and culture protocol.

nodes.name: Factor-induced neuronal specialization response
nodes.shortDescription: Defined transcription-factor combinations can generate cells with neuronal functional readouts from fibroblast cultures; marker expression and electrical function are distinct measured endpoints.

nodes.name: Dye loss and electrical transients coincide
nodes.shortDescription: Source PROPS flashes coincide with abrupt TMRM fluorescence loss; stepwise dye loss also occurs without the PROPS plasmid under dim illumination. This supports a real source phenomenon beyond dependence on PROPS expression, without identifying a unique transport mechanism.

nodes.name: Electrically regulated efflux remains mechanistically unresolved
nodes.shortDescription: The source proposes voltage-regulated cationic efflux and discusses lowered thermodynamic barriers during depolarization. The data do not uniquely distinguish a particular active efflux system, changing permeability, passive redistribution or their combination.

nodes.name: Motor slowdown coincides with the electrical transient
nodes.shortDescription: In the source tethered-cell experiment, PROPS flashes coincide with slowed or stopped rotation. Together with the separate stable-pH observation this supports electrical depolarization and reduced proton-motive drive, without resolving the molecular trigger.

nodes.name: Electrical potential is distinct from pH and full electrochemical driving force
nodes.shortDescription: The source separates voltage-sensitive and pH-sensitive signals. Membrane voltage alone is not a measured concentration gradient for every solute, a complete proton-motive-force budget or a globally constant cellular state.

nodes.name: wertheimer2014-age-cmv-blood: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Study 391 healthy community-dwelling adults aged 21-101 years: 152 CMV-seronegative and 239 CMV-seropositive participants recruited in Oregon, Arizona and Texas. Use CMV IgG ELISA, fresh blood/PBMC flow phenotyping and complete blood counts to distinguish relative subset frequencies from absolute numbers; stratify age and CMV status. Individuals are sampled cross-sectionally, not randomized to age/infection or followed through their own aging trajectory.

nodes.name: xue2014-human-macrophage-stimuli: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Differentiate purified blood monocytes with GM-CSF or M-CSF for 72 hours and compare 28 subsequent stimulation conditions involving microbial-receptor ligands, cytokines and metabolic cues. Profile expression on Illumina arrays with normalized sample relationships, correlation clustering and WGCNA; the main analysis uses a declared 72-hour macrophage set. The source also performs selected protein/functional checks, but complete stimulus doses and detailed protocols remain in unread supplements.

nodes.name: xue2014-network-analysis: acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: The source applies normalized expression similarity, correlation-network layout, hierarchical clustering and WGCNA to the measured donor-culture panel. The 3D spectrum uses selected sample coordinates and cluster mean vectors; WGCNA modules summarize coexpression. This is a source-reported analysis with declared input measurements, not an independently replayed raw-array pipeline or direct molecular interaction acquisition.

nodes.name: QUEEN reporter response and calibration controls preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare purified QUEEN variants and reporter-expressing E. coli, keeping cell-suspension/luciferase calibration and continuous-culture growth controls separate. QUEEN-2m optical ratios depend on ATP and calibration; high-affinity and ATP-insensitive QUEEN variants estimate measurement effects. pHluorin supplies a separate cellular pH control.

nodes.name: ATP concentration heterogeneity in a supplied bacterial culture preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Observe QUEEN-2m-expressing E. coli from glucose-limited aerated continuous culture at 25 C, immobilized under the source agarose film. Convert single-cell 405/480 excitation ratios to estimated ATP using the source calibration and noise correction; images are single observations per cell, not ATP time courses.

nodes.name: Readout-dependent repair estimates at an engineered human-cell DNA break preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare source HEK293T F8-S2 nuclease-exposed populations with control backbone or donor template, retaining two guide clones and unselected versus approximately two-week drug-selected pools. Assess genomic PCR products by melting curves and cut-site/adjacent-site TaqMan probes with control and beta-actin normalization.

nodes.name: Anisotropy hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed directional criterion whose specific derivation and observables remain unresolved in the reviewed foundation paper.

nodes.name: Carrier promotion contract
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed transition from persistent collective organization to a new state space and admissible operations, tested by a forward abstraction map.

nodes.name: Dispersion parameter m²
nodes.shortDescription: Under the declared case convention ∂²tΨ−∂²xΨ+m²Ψ=0, m²=ω²−k². Reconcile the source action and operator together before using this as a general rule.

nodes.name: Selection among eligible candidates
nodes.shortDescription: A comparison operation on an explicit cohort using a defined functional; retain ties and report sensitivity. Selection is distinct from physical generation.

nodes.name: Compensation relation
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed balance relation between primitive distinctions; a measurable functional remains open.

nodes.name: CRT carrier class — no admitted instance
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed localized persistent carrier, admitted only after every declared objecthood gate passes. The existing expanded case admits none.

nodes.name: Perturbation test candidate
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed perturbation protocol. Perturbative persistence motivates testing but does not establish directional mechanisms.

nodes.name: Directional gradient hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A retained proposal requiring a defined state variable, domain, gradient operator and source-specific derivation.

nodes.name: Discrete scale hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A discrete admissible spectrum is an open hypothesis. E=ℏω and p=ℏk do not force continuous parameters to become discrete.

nodes.name: Distinguishability
nodes.shortDescription: A declared criterion for distinguishing configurations; its domain and equivalence relation remain to be operationalized.

nodes.name: Ensemble carrier class
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed collection of admitted CRT carriers with a specified coupling and demonstrated collective persistence; no such input cohort exists in the current case.

nodes.name: Ensemble action family
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed coupling functional for admitted carriers. Nonzero coupling alone does not establish a stable collective regime.

nodes.name: Promoted carrier class
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed effective carrier with a tested state map, dynamics and intervention interface. No effective next-level dynamics have been derived here.

nodes.name: Assumed hyperbolic analytic frame
nodes.shortDescription: An indefinite bilinear frame within the selected two-direction quadratic model class. The assumptions are explicit and not derived from unrestricted absence of structure.

nodes.name: Integrated density Γ
nodes.shortDescription: Γ=∫ρ dμ on a declared support with measure and normalization. Conservation and finiteness require separate conditions.

nodes.name: Local density ρ
nodes.shortDescription: For a declared complex field, ρ(x)=|Ψ(x)|². This nonnegative quantity alone does not establish localization or irreducible closure.

nodes.name: Nonlinear action family
nodes.shortDescription: A candidate interaction model requiring explicit independent fields, constraints and boundedness analysis. Tested completions have not supplied an object-qualified CRT.

nodes.name: Admissibility context Ω
nodes.shortDescription: The author’s foundational possibility context. It is neither an observed material substrate nor a measured physical field in this release.

nodes.name: Oscillatory mode class
nodes.shortDescription: Candidate solutions under a declared wave operator, domain and boundary conditions. Equation satisfaction is separate from objecthood.

nodes.name: Premetric frame
nodes.shortDescription: A formal context for primitive distinctions before a metric is introduced. Kept separate from an assumed analytic metric.

nodes.name: Quadratic action family
nodes.shortDescription: An assumed quadratic derivative action. The source operator sign must be reconciled, and stationarity does not certify a minimum.

nodes.name: Sequential distinction
nodes.shortDescription: A primitive ordering direction. Identifying it with measured physical time requires an additional model.

nodes.name: Spatial distinction
nodes.shortDescription: A primitive direction of separability. Physical distance and dimension are not supplied by this definition.

nodes.name: Synchronization observable
nodes.shortDescription: A collective observable requiring specified variables, phase convention and tolerance. Agreement alone is not a promoted carrier.

nodes.name: Transport bias hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A retained proposed effect requiring a transport model and evidence of the stated bias.

nodes.name: Triad candidate configuration class
nodes.shortDescription: A class of joint three-mode candidates passing a declared resonance and closure surrogate. Passing this stage does not establish localized objecthood.

nodes.name: Triadic admission predicate
nodes.shortDescription: A proposed joint closure test for three modes. Simple-cycle minimality is conditional on the chosen graph class.

nodes.name: Trial field domain
nodes.shortDescription: The declared class of complex trial fields on which an action and density can be defined before any solution passes admission tests.

nodes.name: Unique neural accumulator hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: The selected behavioral and neural findings do not uniquely identify a LIP-local accumulator as the necessary implementation of all decision making.

nodes.name: Event cascades in jointly activated acute slices
nodes.shortDescription: Acute rat slices under combined NMDA and D1-agonist exposure exhibit sampled event cascades; these are distinct from the culture records.

nodes.name: A1 agonist does not rescue D1-neuron receptor loss
nodes.shortDescription: In Extended Data Figure 8h, CPA co-treatment did not prevent the increased D1-challenge seizure susceptibility of Adora1 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice. Rescue in CD39-deletion mice cannot be transferred to a preparation lacking the relevant neuronal receptor.

nodes.name: D1 challenge after D1-neuron A1-receptor deletion
nodes.shortDescription: Adora1 floxed mice crossed to Drd1a-Cre versus controls, challenged with 5 mg/kg SKF81297.

nodes.name: D1-challenge seizure incidence after neuronal A1 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 4k source counts report seizures in 5/6 Adora1 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice versus 2/12 controls after D1 agonist. This receptor deletion differs from microglial CD39 deletion.

nodes.name: Unified affective property hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A single system-wide evaluative property does not follow from a projection-specific exploration assay; its representation and relation to conscious feeling remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Astrocyte calcium under alpha1B blockade
nodes.shortDescription: Cyclazosin treatment reduced the L-MO radial astrocyte calcium response evoked by NE-MO stimulation. Pharmacology supports alpha1B receptor involvement without proving exclusive astrocyte-specific action.

nodes.name: Genotype whole-cell capacitance null
nodes.shortDescription: The reported whole-cell capacitance comparison did not differ significantly between Arf6 genotypes. This supports the specified current-density comparison without demonstrating equal cell function or membrane lipid abundance.

nodes.name: Control-cell PIP2 current null
nodes.shortDescription: No significant Kir-current change was reported after bath diC16-PIP2 in Arf6fl/fl control cells. This null is separate from the current increase in knockdown cells and is not an equivalence test.

nodes.name: Arf6 genotype with subsequent barium
nodes.shortDescription: Ten Arf6fl/fl and nine Arf6iECKD mice; pre/post 100 micromolar cortical barium laser-Doppler responses, distinct from the PIP2 cohort.

nodes.name: Whisker perfusion after partial Arf6 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Arf6 knockdown mice had lower untreated whisker-evoked perfusion responses than littermate controls in the reported comparison. Subsequent barium reduced both responses, with a smaller reported barium-sensitive fraction in knockdown mice; no exact fraction is calibrated.

nodes.name: Kir current after partial endothelial Arf6 loss
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary endothelial cells from inducible Arf6 knockdown mice had lower barium-sensitive Kir current density than littermate controls. Partial endothelial knockdown is distinct from complete or capillary-restricted deletion.

nodes.name: Arf6 genotype and isolated cEC currents
nodes.shortDescription: Tamoxifen-treated Arf6iECKD and Arf6fl/fl littermates; conventional patch clamp with 60 mM external potassium and barium subtraction.

nodes.name: Microvessel ATP-depletion comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: Separate 0.1 mM GTPgammaS/PBS and 3 micromolar NAV-2729/DMSO comparisons; four to seven male mice and vehicle-normalized assay batches.

nodes.name: Microvessel kinase-activity proxy
nodes.shortDescription: GTPgammaS reduced residual ATP and NAV-2729 increased it relative to their separate vehicle controls in the supplemented microvessel lysate assay. The inverse readout supports altered kinase activity, not direct endothelial membrane PIP2 measurement.

nodes.name: Upstream dilation under NAV-2729
nodes.shortDescription: NAV-2729 reduced upstream arteriole dilation to focal capillary potassium in the ex vivo preparation relative to vehicle. Diameter is the observed endpoint; conducted voltage is inferred rather than directly recorded in this assay.

nodes.name: NAV and concurrent PIP2 during whisker flow recording
nodes.shortDescription: Anesthetized laser Doppler with manual whisker stimulation; twenty-minute 3 micromolar cortical NAV exposure, separate vehicle and NAV plus 0.5 mg/kg intravenous diC16-PIP2 groups.

nodes.name: Whisker perfusion under NAV and concurrent PIP2
nodes.shortDescription: Cortical NAV-2729 reduced whisker-evoked relative perfusion. Concurrent intravenous diC16-PIP2 preserved a larger response relative to NAV alone, but did not restore the higher vehicle-treated response. Groups and pre/post comparisons remain distinct.

nodes.name: NAV-associated Kir current decline and protection
nodes.shortDescription: Pipette NAV-2729 caused a time-dependent reduction of capillary endothelial Kir currents relative to vehicle. Bath diC16-PIP2 present before recording preserved much of the current during NAV exposure; it was not a sequential rescue after current loss in the same cell.

nodes.name: NAV-2729 in potassium-stimulated CaPA
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary 10 mM potassium for ten seconds; 0.1-1 micromolar NAV in the bath, with pressure-induced and U46619-preconstricted preparations pooled.

nodes.name: NAV-2729 with pre-recording PIP2 supplementation
nodes.shortDescription: Three micromolar NAV in the pipette, with or without 10 micromolar bath diC16-PIP2 preincubated for twenty minutes; sixteen-minute whole-cell recording with repeated voltage ramps.

nodes.name: Exclusive Arf6-PIP2 vascular mechanism
nodes.shortDescription: The genetic, pharmacological and supplementation results constrain a PIP2-dependent interpretation. Direct lipid measurements and selective tests of alternative Arf6 pathways are needed to establish exclusive mediation or a general disease-restoring mechanism.

nodes.name: PIP2 supplementation in a separate Arf6 cohort
nodes.shortDescription: Eight Arf6fl/fl and seven Arf6iECKD mice, each measured before and after 0.5 mg/kg intravenous diC16-PIP2.

nodes.name: Perfusion response after PIP2 in Arf6 knockdown
nodes.shortDescription: Intravenous diC16-PIP2 increased the whisker-evoked perfusion response in Arf6 knockdown mice in a separate cohort. The nonsignificant treated-genotype contrast does not establish complete equivalence or restoration of every vascular function.

nodes.name: Kir current after PIP2 in Arf6 knockdown cells
nodes.shortDescription: Bath diC16-PIP2 increased the measured Kir current in capillary endothelial cells from Arf6 knockdown mice relative to untreated knockdown cells. The result supports a supplementation effect without direct measurement of endogenous lipid concentration.

nodes.name: PIP2 supplementation in Arf6 knockdown cECs
nodes.shortDescription: Separate isolated-cell treatment conditions with 10 micromolar bath diC16-PIP2 before patch recording; cells nested within three mice per condition.

nodes.name: Resting tone null under NAV
nodes.shortDescription: The ex vivo comparison reports no significant resting-tone change under the tested NAV-2729 concentrations. Conflicting tone normalization and pooled preconstriction conditions prevent numerical interpretation as exact preserved contractility.

nodes.name: Vehicle-associated perfusion increase
nodes.shortDescription: The Figure 4c vehicle group showed increased whisker-evoked perfusion after treatment relative to its own baseline. Vehicle is therefore not an inert zero-change comparator in this experiment.

nodes.name: Free-swimming controls after astrocyte ablation
nodes.shortDescription: No significant change in free-swimming frequency or velocity was reported after the selected astrocyte ablation. This control differs from the restrained fictive-passivity assay and does not establish full equivalence.

nodes.name: Passivity after astrocyte ablation
nodes.shortDescription: Partial two-photon ablation of hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced time in futility-induced passivity in selected larval zebrafish; it did not abolish all passive behavior.

nodes.name: Swim output after astrocyte GPCR activation
nodes.shortDescription: Light activation of gfap-driven Opto-alpha1-AR in hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced fictive swim power relative to controls.

nodes.name: Passivity after TRPV1 activation
nodes.shortDescription: Capsaicin treatment of fish expressing rat TRPV1 sparsely in radial astrocytes increased passive time in closed loop; transgene-negative and saline controls did not show the same effect.

nodes.name: Stimulus-linked glutamate sensor response
nodes.shortDescription: In the DG slice imaging assay, astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion reduced CNO-evoked glutamate-sensor responses. Responses were detected in a subset of tested astrocytes; exact population proportions remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion during glutamate imaging
nodes.shortDescription: In the DG slice imaging assay, astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion reduced CNO-evoked glutamate-sensor responses. Responses were detected in a subset of tested astrocytes; exact population proportions remain unresolved.

nodes.name: Paired DG field potentiation
nodes.shortDescription: Theta-burst LTP was lower in DG synaptic fields near recombined VGLUT1-deficient astrocytes than in neighboring unrecombined fields. Figure 3 source data contains 16 paired normalized measurements; this does not establish universal astrocyte necessity for LTP.

nodes.name: Sparse astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion in DG
nodes.shortDescription: Theta-burst LTP was lower in DG synaptic fields near recombined VGLUT1-deficient astrocytes than in neighboring unrecombined fields. Figure 3 source data contains 16 paired normalized measurements; this does not establish universal astrocyte necessity for LTP.

nodes.name: AVAR calcium response
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVER activation produced increased downstream AVAR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).

nodes.name: AVDR calcium response
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVJR activation produced increased downstream AVDR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).

nodes.name: AVER stimulation protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Targeted two-photon activation of AVER during population calcium imaging in the Randi WT-background preparation.

nodes.name: AVJR stimulation protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Targeted two-photon activation of AVJR during population calcium imaging in the Randi WT-background preparation.

nodes.name: Nonrunning affect-assay comparisons
nodes.shortDescription: The reported nonrunning open-field and forced-swim comparisons did not show significant treatment effects on the named outcomes. Novelty-suppressed-feeding reporting contains conflicting significance statements. These tests do not establish equivalent affective states or clinical antidepressant efficacy.

nodes.name: Bicuculline field-LTP comparison
nodes.shortDescription: At eight weeks, field LTP recorded with 10 micromolar bicuculline did not differ significantly between treatment groups. These separate slices do not establish equal single-neuron plasticity or a matched within-cell reversal of the no-bicuculline effect.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and retained BrdU labels
nodes.shortDescription: The day-56 dentate assay found more retained BrdU-labeled cells after the Bax manipulation: reported means 3004 versus 11113, three mice per group. BrdU was given on days 9-18; only a subset expressed NeuN, so the total is not a count of mature functional neurons.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and retained BrdU labels assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; BrdU 150 milligrams per kilogram daily on days 9-18, terminal dentate counting on day 56.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and context discrimination
nodes.shortDescription: In the nine-day similar-context task, male NCff mice given tamoxifen had higher discrimination ratios than vehicle controls (11 versus nine mice; reported treatment P=0.023). This supports a task-specific behavioral effect; it does not directly measure neural pattern separation or general memory improvement.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and context discrimination assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; male-only testing eight weeks later, shock-associated A and similar nonshock B, nine days, ratio (A-B)/(A+B). Figure 2c and Methods disagree on context order; the per-animal schedule remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Single-trial context comparison
nodes.shortDescription: NCff groups showed no significant difference in next-day freezing in the trained context or in the very different context C (14 mice per group). Separate Cre-negative controls address tamoxifen exposure. This null does not negate the distinct similar-context discrimination result.

nodes.name: Neuron-count mediation hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: An increase in surviving dentate neurons is a candidate mediator of the Bax manipulation’s task-specific effects. Nestin-lineage breadth, altered cell properties and other cohort differences require selective mediation and rescue tests before neuron count alone becomes a causal construction rule.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and DCX population
nodes.shortDescription: Eight weeks after tamoxifen, NCff mice had more dentate DCX-positive cells and more DCX-positive cells with tertiary dendrites than vehicle controls (three mice per group). This is a marker-population response to the Bax manipulation, not a direct neuron birth-rate measurement.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and DCX population assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; day-56 dentate DCX immunohistochemistry and separate total/tertiary-dendrite counts.

nodes.name: Four-week DCX comparison
nodes.shortDescription: At four weeks, the total DCX-positive population comparison was nonsignificant; the tertiary-dendrite subset was reported at P=0.05, with four mice per group. The eight-week increase cannot be assigned unchanged to this earlier assay.

nodes.name: Discrimination protocol variants
nodes.shortDescription: Two supplementary contextual-discrimination variants report treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06, with interactions or selected day-specific differences. Their schedules and contrasts differ from the main task; they do not constitute uniformly significant treatment main effects.

nodes.name: Task-specific learning and retention nulls
nodes.shortDescription: Named recognition, water-maze, active-avoidance, extinction and memory-clearance endpoints showed no significant treatment benefit in their separate cohorts. These are not equivalence findings or evidence that all behavior is unchanged; novel-object habituation locomotor responses included a significant interaction.

nodes.name: Bax proliferation-marker nulls
nodes.shortDescription: Reported Ki67 proliferation-marker comparisons were nonsignificant at four and eight weeks after tamoxifen (four and five mice per group, respectively). These samples do not establish an exactly unchanged birth rate or make survival the only possible mediator.

nodes.name: Running comparison-specific nulls
nodes.shortDescription: In running-housed mice, reported light-dark, novelty-suppressed-feeding and forced-swim comparisons were nonsignificant in ten vehicle and eleven treated mice. The separate home-cage activity sample used seven per group and was also nonsignificant; open-field exploration is a different result.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and exploration during running
nodes.shortDescription: In the running-housed comparison, tamoxifen-treated NCff mice showed greater open-field path length, rearing and center exploration than vehicle controls (11 versus ten mice). Changed locomotion prevents an isolated anxiety interpretation and does not establish a human therapeutic effect.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and exploration during running assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; shared-cage wheel access from five weeks after treatment; Figure 4 shows behavioral testing on days 64-84, with ten vehicle and eleven treated mice.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and dentate field LTP
nodes.shortDescription: At eight weeks, the Bax manipulation increased the weak-tetanus dentate field-LTP response without bicuculline (reported treatment P=0.039). This population assay does not identify the contribution of each birthdated neuron or prove a complete cell-number mediation route.

nodes.name: Bax manipulation and dentate field LTP assay
nodes.shortDescription: NCff mice, tamoxifen 2 milligrams intraperitoneally daily for five days versus equal-volume vehicle, beginning at at least eight weeks; eight-week medial-perforant-path field recordings, four one-second 100-Hz trains spaced 15 seconds apart, without bicuculline; eight slices/six controls and eleven slices/seven treated mice.

nodes.name: Alternate bracketing mismatch
nodes.shortDescription: For Alternate, post-experimental brackets in the pooled 42-person sample do not significantly correlate with the proposed language parse (reported r=0.08, P=0.77). Participants favor repeated AB pairs rather than the model-predicted series of alternations.

nodes.name: Binary sequence bracketing agreement
nodes.shortDescription: Post-experimental visual bracketing agrees with the proposed language for nine of ten templates in the reported group correlations. Seven shared templates pool the 23 fMRI and 19 MEG participants; three fMRI-only templates use 23 participants.

nodes.name: Binary description model comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Among twelve reported models, combining LoT-chunk cost with first-order transition surprise has the lowest reported AIC for sensitivity and correct-response time. The comparison comprises six complexity measures, each with and without surprise, using participant random intercepts.

nodes.name: Binary sequence violation detection
nodes.shortDescription: In the 23-person fMRI behavioral sample, all tested template/violation-position conditions have above-chance detection. Across the ten template means, sensitivity decreases with assigned description cost (reported R squared 0.95), while correct-response time increases (R squared 0.85).

nodes.name: Binary sound detection task
nodes.shortDescription: Twenty-three adults detect single-tone violations in ten 16-tone templates during fMRI. Tones last 50 ms with 250 ms SOA. Each template and its swapped A/B version has ten habituation sequences and eighteen test sequences, six containing a violation; button responses are required during test blocks. Twenty mini-sessions span five runs. Post-experimental visual bracketing allows repeated auditory re-exposure.

nodes.name: Binary deviant fMRI association
nodes.shortDescription: BOLD responses to all deviants decrease with assigned complexity across a broad network, and all nine selected task ROIs have a negative linear complexity effect. A small medial superior frontal region has the opposite whole-brain association.

nodes.name: Binary habituation fMRI association
nodes.shortDescription: In the 22-person imaging sample, habituation BOLD responses covary positively with assigned description cost in a broad frontal, parietal, temporal and cerebellar network. All nine selected task ROIs have a positive linear effect; seven have a negative quadratic term, with right precentral and right superior temporal regions as exceptions.

nodes.name: Detected-deviant fMRI controls
nodes.shortDescription: Restricting the fMRI model to correctly detected deviants retains a narrower negative complexity map. Four of nine task ROIs retain corrected negative effects: bilateral superior temporal cortex, left intraparietal sulcus and right cerebellar lobule VIII; the other five do not reach the stated corrected threshold.

nodes.name: Binary task and functional localizer
nodes.shortDescription: In the same imaging sample, all seven independently localized mathematics ROIs show positive habituation complexity effects, while four show negative deviant effects. Most language ROIs have weak or absent positive modulation, but left IFG pars opercularis shows positive habituation and negative deviant effects, and posterior STS shows a negative deviant effect.

nodes.name: Binary standard-trial fMRI association
nodes.shortDescription: For standard test items, positive complexity associations occupy a narrower parietal, precentral and cerebellar network than during habituation, alongside negative associations in other regions.

nodes.name: Binary violation decoder readout
nodes.shortDescription: A classifier trained on standard versus deviant MEG item epochs across the seven templates shows stronger violation readout for simpler sequences. The reported average decision-vector contrast and temporal-generalization analysis are nonsignificant for Shrinking and Complex, while the five simpler templates show significant violation readout.

nodes.name: Binary sequence evoked field power
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate 19-person MEG sample, evoked global field power has a positive complexity association during habituation (reported 108-208 ms), no significant standard-item association, and negative deviant associations (116-300 and 312-560 ms).

nodes.name: Position-specific binary violation signals
nodes.shortDescription: Despite nonsignificant average temporal-generalization results for Shrinking and Complex, Figure 8 reports significant violation signals at position 15 for both; their other tested positions are nonsignificant. Pairs&Alt.1 also shows context-dependent responses inconsistent with the tested first-order transition account alone.

nodes.name: Binary MEG transition-statistics controls
nodes.shortDescription: Sensor regressions report complexity-related clusters in habituation, standard and deviant trials after the specified controls for current/next repetition or alternation and first-order transition surprise. The transition observer uses a decaying history of approximately 100 observations.

nodes.name: Binary sequence description language
nodes.shortDescription: The study describes A/B sequences using stay (+0), switch (b), repetition, variation and nested composition. Its LoT-chunk model forbids descriptions that split a contiguous run of identical items. Figure 1 assigns costs 4, 6, 6, 6, 12, 15, 16, 18, 21 and 28 to its ten selected templates. These are grammar-dependent description scores, not measured bits, neural counts or a physical minimum.

nodes.name: Direct BLA somatic activation
nodes.shortDescription: Somatic ChR2 illumination in the high-stress comparison; distinguish this recruitment from the CeA terminal field.

nodes.name: BLA terminal activation in CeA
nodes.shortDescription: Unilateral ChR2 terminal illumination in the high-stress cohort; 20 Hz, 5 ms pulses; off/on/off exploration assays.

nodes.name: BLA-to-CeA terminal inhibition
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral eNpHR3.0 terminal illumination with continuous amber light in a separate low-stress cohort.

nodes.name: RGC-input engulfment after C3 loss
nodes.shortDescription: P5 microglia in C3 knockout mice engulfed less labeled RGC input than WT littermate controls. The developmental knockout does not isolate microglial C3 production or an exclusive complement pathway.

nodes.name: Developmental C3 loss in the engulfment assay
nodes.shortDescription: Whole-animal C3 knockout versus WT littermates, CTB tracing at P4 and microglial volume reconstruction in P5 dLGN.

nodes.name: CA1 plasticity under astrocytic Gq stimulation
nodes.shortDescription: In the reviewed SC-CA1 slice assays, MrgA1 agonist or endothelin stimulation of astrocytic Gq pathways produced calcium elevations without significant modulation of the reported transmission, PTP or LTP readouts.

nodes.name: CA1 plasticity in IP3R2 knockout slices
nodes.shortDescription: IP3R2 knockout and WT littermate slices showed no significant difference in the reported SC-CA1 PPF, PTP and LTP assays; this is a pathway- and preparation-scoped null result.

nodes.name: NMDA-sensitive CA1 potentiation induction
nodes.shortDescription: DL-APV prevents potentiation induction at doses that spare basal evoked field responses in the reported assay.

nodes.name: Pro-inflammatory cytokines after Calca-cre activation
nodes.shortDescription: Calca-cre nodose hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta after LPS. IL-10 did not differ significantly and is represented separately; this population does not inherit the TRPA1-associated three-analyte profile.

nodes.name: Calca-cre nodose activation with LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry with CNO; eleven treated and nine control mice, with two-hour cytokine sampling.

nodes.name: IL-10 null after Calca-cre nodose activation
nodes.shortDescription: The Calca-cre nodose hM3Dq versus mCherry comparison reported no significant circulating IL-10 difference after LPS (P=0.88), despite reduced IL-6 and IL-1beta. This is not an equivalence test or the TRPA1 IL-10 effect.

nodes.name: Upstream dilation after capillary potassium
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium dilated the attached upstream arteriole ex vivo. Barium treatment and endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion suppressed this response in the specified comparisons.

nodes.name: Feed arteriole dilation in vivo
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary 10 mM potassium increased upstream feed-arteriole diameter in the in vivo paired comparison. This does not imply that the stimulated capillary itself dilated.

nodes.name: Capillary stimulation with upstream diameter imaging
nodes.shortDescription: Acute anesthetized cranial window; eight paired upstream-diameter experiments in seven mice.

nodes.name: Focal capillary potassium and RBC passage
nodes.shortDescription: Anesthetized cranial-window line scans; 200-300 ms pressure ejection, paired baseline and peak flux. Wild type eleven mice, knockout nine and barium-treated wild type six.

nodes.name: High-potassium capillary response boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Capillary 25 or 60 mM potassium failed to sustain the upstream dilation elicited by 10 mM potassium in the same ex vivo dose comparison. Transient traces and the stimulated vessel segment constrain interpretation.

nodes.name: Stimulated capillary diameter null
nodes.shortDescription: No significant local capillary diameter change was detected after focal potassium in eighteen capillaries from seven mice. The measured sites lacked pericytes according to the Discussion; this is not a general test of pericyte control.

nodes.name: Capillary potassium in pressurized CaPA
nodes.shortDescription: Forty mmHg CaPA, focal capillary stimulation and upstream diameter; six wild-type preparations from six mice and five knockout preparations from five mice, with 30 micromolar bath barium in wild type.

nodes.name: Control-ejection flux and velocity nulls
nodes.shortDescription: Pressure ejection of 3 mM potassium aCSF did not significantly change RBC flux or velocity in the six-mouse paired control. This bounds the injection artifact under that protocol, without proving equivalence.

nodes.name: Capillary RBC flux after focal potassium
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased peak RBC flux in wild-type mice. The response was attenuated in endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 knockout and barium-treated wild-type groups; flux counts RBC passages per second.

nodes.name: Capillary RBC velocity after focal potassium
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased RBC velocity in the wild-type comparison; no significant increase was detected in the knockout or barium-treated comparisons. Velocity was measured in the peak-flux bin and is distinct from flux.

nodes.name: Upstream smooth-muscle hyperpolarization
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary 10 mM potassium hyperpolarized upstream arteriolar smooth muscle in the isolated CaPA recording. This is a direct voltage measurement at the sampled upstream cell, not along every intervening endothelial contact.

nodes.name: Potassium-evoked RBC flux under TTX
nodes.shortDescription: Focal capillary potassium still increased RBC flux under cortical tetrodotoxin, while whisker-evoked flux was suppressed in the separate control comparison. Ejected potassium bypasses the physiological release step.

nodes.name: Capillary potassium after sodium-channel blockade
