nodes.shortDescription: Microglia contained more labeled RGC input from the TTX-treated eye than from the vehicle eye in the selected P5 dLGN regions. This supports activity-dependent selection without identifying the exact synapse-tagging sequence.

nodes.name: Retinal TTX in the engulfment assay
nodes.shortDescription: P4 CX3CR1/EGFP mice: 0.5 micromolar TTX in the left eye and saline in the right, followed 4-5 h later by distinct CTB tracers; selected dLGN regions analyzed at P5.

nodes.name: Vagal input labeling from Dbh-cre cNST
nodes.shortDescription: The reported monosynaptic retrograde labeling co-localizes with Calca or Trpa1 transcripts in nodose neurons, supporting an anatomical input interpretation. Conflicting reporter and quantitative caption labels remain unresolved; no numerical tracing fraction or functional coupling weight is assigned.

nodes.name: Reduced cNST calcium after vagotomy
nodes.shortDescription: The separately vagotomized group showed lower LPS-evoked cNST calcium-response area than intact animals. The published figure reports an approximately 80% reduction with residual signal; it does not demonstrate complete elimination of every immune-to-brain route.

nodes.name: Subdiaphragmatic vagotomy and LPS
nodes.shortDescription: Bilateral vagal transection with two weeks of recovery, compared with the intact LPS photometry group; six mice per group.

nodes.name: Cytokine nulls after Vgat-cre cNST activation
nodes.shortDescription: The specified Vgat-cre cNST activation experiment reported nonsignificant IL-6, IL-1beta and IL-10 differences after LPS, with four treated and five control mice. This does not establish that all inhibitory neurons are irrelevant to immune regulation.

nodes.name: Analysis-dependent regional detection times
nodes.shortDescription: With the main 100 ms smoothing procedure, conventional-band contrasts are reported at 120-310 ms for AI beta, 180-320 ms for ACC beta, 370-470 ms for amygdala beta, and 60-340 plus 380-470 ms for IFG high gamma.

nodes.name: Classifier performance after ordered feature removal
nodes.shortDescription: The paper reports 76.28 percent classification accuracy using thirteen pooled features. Removing any one feature retains above-chance decoding; sequentially removing the eight highest-weight features leaves reported accuracy 49.78 percent with P=0.617. The saved removal array ends at 49.775 percent.

nodes.name: Proposed neurodynamic organization of pain empathy
nodes.shortDescription: Tan et al. propose a multi-region neurodynamic account linking early IFG activity, regional low-frequency changes and cross-region coupling during vicarious pain perception. Its interpretation as a necessary or minimal empathy architecture remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Cross-region phase-amplitude associations
nodes.shortDescription: Painful pictures produce reported increases in coupling between IFG high-gamma amplitude and selected beta phases in ACC, AI and amygdala, with an additional AI alpha-phase cluster. The main analysis uses 219 ACC-IFG, 459 AI-IFG and 254 amygdala-IFG channel pairs.

nodes.name: Frequency-specific interregional power correlations
nodes.shortDescription: The main analysis reports reduced ACC-AI beta power correlation at 25-32 Hz and AI-amygdala correlation at 18-24 Hz. ACC-amygdala correlation increases at 18-22 Hz and decreases at 25-30 Hz.

nodes.name: Distinct pain, unpleasantness and empathy ratings
nodes.shortDescription: In the sixteen-rater subset, stronger empathy ratings associate with lower ACC alpha and AI low-frequency power differences. Perceived pain and own unpleasantness have distinct associations: AI coefficients are negative for perceived pain and positive for own unpleasantness; the ACC unpleasantness association is nonsignificant.

nodes.name: Picture-related regional iEEG power contrasts
nodes.shortDescription: Painful versus neutral hand pictures elicit reported AI low-frequency power decreases, ACC alpha decreases and beta increases, amygdala beta decreases and IFG high-gamma increases. The main sample contains 297 channels across four overlapping regional patient subsets.

nodes.name: Directional transfer-entropy associations
nodes.shortDescription: The reported beta-power transfer-entropy analysis finds lower ACC-AI values during painful pictures and a direction-by-condition interaction for AI-amygdala. The latter includes an amygdala-to-AI decrease, while AI-to-amygdala has P=0.629. ACC-amygdala effects depend on the beta frequency range.

nodes.name: VIP manipulation and RGL cycle-marker nulls
nodes.shortDescription: The tested five-day VIP-interneuron activation and inhibition comparisons show no significant change in the RGL EdU/MCM2 endpoints. The selected slice controls do not establish that VIP neurons never affect RGLs through other routes or conditions.

nodes.name: Exploratory interareal amplitude-connectivity results
nodes.shortDescription: Exploratory amplitude-based connectivity after removal of the evoked response showed brief content-selective effects differing from the phase-consistency result.

nodes.name: Stimulus-duration neural readouts
nodes.shortDescription: Some posterior iEEG responses track stimulus duration; the preregistered prefrontal onset-and-offset profile was not detected in the reported analysis.

nodes.name: Suprathreshold visual feature decoding
nodes.shortDescription: Suprathreshold feature decoding differs by cortical region, feature and recording modality; category decoding and orientation decoding are not interchangeable.

nodes.name: Visual reliability and height-conflict protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Two-interval height discrimination; aligned stereo and PHANToM haptic stimuli; randomized visual noise and small cue discrepancies; no feedback.

nodes.name: Prespecified interareal phase-consistency results
nodes.shortDescription: The preregistered phase-consistency readout did not support either theory's specified gamma/beta connectivity prediction under the reported analysis.

nodes.name: Learned selective-updating hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Dopamine-dependent gating and reinforcement are proposed to admit task-relevant context into maintained representations and learn when updating is useful. This sketches a possible mechanism for adaptable control; it does not demonstrate a measured closed feedback loop or an exclusive dopamine mediator.

nodes.name: Functional requirements of guided control
nodes.shortDescription: Within Miller and Cohen's theory, guided control requires task-relevant bias, maintenance robust to distraction with selective updating, access to diverse task information and plasticity for learning new goals and means. These requirements define what a candidate model must demonstrate.

nodes.name: Selected macaque visual-memory preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Two macaques supplied 145 prescreened task-responsive PF units from 264 screened units during visual delayed matching. Standard and ABBA task experience differs between animals; ABBA repeats an irrelevant nonmatch while preserving the sample as the final target.

nodes.name: Post-pulse category evidence across task relevance
nodes.shortDescription: In the separate six-person Experiment 3, unattended-category decoding exceeds chance after the first cue, when the item can still matter. After the second cue, when that item is dropped, the corresponding decoding result is nonsignificant.

nodes.name: Category decoding after targeted TMS
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 2, unattended-category EEG decoding transiently exceeds chance after TMS. Targeted and nontargeted category conditions both show reported above-chance evidence; the data do not by themselves demonstrate an exclusive target-specific storage site.

nodes.name: Distinct episodic-buffer hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A limited temporary store binding information across modalities and long-term memory is proposed as an episodic buffer. A distinct store versus activated long-term memory remains a mechanistic alternative, and functional binding does not identify a physical buffer or establish consciousness.

nodes.name: Priority-dependent category evidence in fMRI
nodes.shortDescription: In Experiment 1, fMRI category evidence follows the cued item. Evidence for the unattended category approaches absent-category levels and can return after a priority switch. This reports a category-level BOLD readout.

nodes.name: Global evoked metrics do not separate attention states
nodes.shortDescription: Supplementary Figure S6 and Table S1 report no significant attention-state main effects or interactions for significant current density, significant current scatter and perturbational complexity in the category-targeted TMS-EEG preparation.

nodes.name: Latent synaptic storage hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: A latent synaptic trace is one proposed account of information that remains potentially accessible when current category decoding is weak. Category-context reinstatement, weak active codes and distributed or dynamic carriers remain alternatives to a uniquely silent synaptic store.

nodes.name: Unattended-item lure errors across TMS groups
nodes.shortDescription: Experiment 4 reports more first-probe unattended-item false alarms in the TMS group than the separate no-TMS group. The corresponding second-probe comparison is nonsignificant. The effect concerns recognition behavior, not EEG recovery of a particular memory item.

nodes.name: Multicomponent working-memory vocabulary
nodes.shortDescription: Baddeley distinguishes phonological storage and rehearsal, visuospatial storage, attentional control by a central executive and a proposed episodic buffer. These are functional model components, not disjoint cell populations or a one-to-one anatomical partition.

nodes.name: Continuous diversity of PF delay profiles
nodes.shortDescription: PF delay activity includes increasing, decreasing and flatter temporal profiles. Within-interval and across-interval indices vary continuously; the illustrated profiles do not establish separate biological cell classes.

nodes.name: PF sample selectivity between distractors
nodes.shortDescription: Forty selected PF units show sample-dependent delay firing; best/worst selectivity reappears between intervening test stimuli. Stimulus-evoked activity interrupts delay firing. Reported six-way classification averages 20.8% against 16.7% chance after excluding the first delay.

nodes.name: PFC guided-activation hypothesis
nodes.shortDescription: Maintained prefrontal goal and rule representations are proposed to bias processing in other systems. Control is modulatory: the stimulus-to-response path need not pass through PFC, and modeled inhibition can arise through local competition rather than a direct inhibitory PFC command.

nodes.name: PF and IT delay readouts under interference
nodes.shortDescription: Selected PF units preserve a best/worst sample difference across the tested blank intervals, while the selected IT average in Figure 7 distinguishes samples only in the interval used for ranking. IT match responses can still carry prior-sample information after intervening stimuli.

nodes.name: PF enhancement for the remembered match
nodes.shortDescription: Excitatory PF responses can be enhanced for the sample-matching test while repeated irrelevant nonmatches do not produce the same enhancement profile. Enhancement begins before the bar release in the reported response traces.

nodes.name: PF suppression for matching and irrelevant repeats
nodes.shortDescription: A separate response pattern suppresses firing for the remembered match and for a repeated irrelevant nonmatch. Repetition suppression and match enhancement therefore have different selectivity in the ABBA task.

nodes.name: Pooled recognition comparison without a TMS main effect
nodes.shortDescription: Supplementary Figure S4 reports no significant TMS main effect on recognition accuracy in a pooled comparison of twelve TMS participants and twenty-four no-TMS participants; probe and switching demands affect accuracy.

nodes.name: Working-memory task construct
nodes.shortDescription: Working memory denotes temporary retention and use of information during a specified task. A graph instance must identify the material, delay, distraction, required transformation and behavioral readout; storage span, processing demands and executive control are distinct measurements.

nodes.name: Bulk absorption coefficient
nodes.shortDescription: A length-reciprocal coefficient, distinguished from dimensionless flux fractions and from a microscopic carrier count.

nodes.name: Directional reflectance distribution
nodes.shortDescription: A radiometric density under stated geometry and ray-optics assumptions, distinct from a reflected flux fraction.

nodes.name: Measured transmission of IR windows
nodes.shortDescription: Transmitted-light measurements for the stated window samples; not a general channel operator or a complete field reconstruction.

nodes.name: IR sample and measurement boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Incident beam, specified sample and integrating-sphere collection protocol; not an additional generating physical entity.

nodes.name: Measured response of specular IR samples
nodes.shortDescription: Aggregate reflected-light response in the specified Hanssen preparation; no complete directional scattering law is inferred.

nodes.name: Reported pure-water absorption spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: A publication-scoped absorption observation with an explicit unresolved precision dispute.

nodes.name: Conditional atomic-reference calibration
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the quoted external 199Hg atomic frequency-per-field magnitude and multiply it by the corrected PSI ratio; preserve its shielded-proton-in-water reference chain and the distinct alternative calibration direction.

nodes.name: Adopted mercury atomic reference
nodes.shortDescription: For the absolute conversion, Afach Equation 2 adopts gamma_Hg/(2*pi)=7.590118(13) MHz/T from an external Hg-to-shielded-proton-in-water calibration and reference value. This is a quoted input, not a new PSI measurement of that absolute reference.

nodes.name: Conditional neutron frequency-per-field magnitude
nodes.shortDescription: Multiplying the corrected PSI ratio by the adopted Hg atomic reference gives the published |gamma_n|/(2*pi)=29.164705(55) MHz/T. The absolute scale therefore depends on the external reference as well as the measured ratio.

nodes.name: PSI neutron/mercury precession preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Store polarized UCN and 199Hg atoms together, fit neutron Ramsey fringes against the optically read mercury frequency, and correct the selected field-up/down data for unequal field sampling and frequency shifts.

nodes.name: Corrected neutron/mercury ratio
nodes.shortDescription: The selected PSI analysis reports the positive neutron/199Hg frequency-ratio magnitude 3.8424574(30), or 0.78 ppm relative uncertainty, after the stated corrections. The final uncertainty is the larger of the field-up and field-down errors.

nodes.name: Replayed AlphaGamma calibration arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: The printed thesis inputs give a weighted activity of 23545.129016... per second and uncorrelated uncertainty 4.421378... per second. The body common-error convention gives 6.99106... per second total uncertainty; the Appendix B fraction gives 4.45442... . Displayed-input rounding permits values rounding to the reported mean. The 2018 printed activity quotient is 23540.204... per second, inconsistent with the reported center even under display rounding; Equation 12-derived target corrections agree only within their quoted uncertainty.

nodes.name: Printed AlphaGamma arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Evaluate the ideal rate-transfer identity, printed thesis source-activity combination and rounding envelope, 2018 printed activity quotient and Equation 12-derived target corrections, retaining conflicting source conventions.

nodes.name: Absolute neutron count-rate transfer
nodes.shortDescription: In the ideal AlphaGamma transfer, a calibrated alpha source fixes Omega_AG=r_Pu,AG/R_Pu. A thin boron target transfers that calibration to the gamma response, giving R_n=r_gamma,thick*r_alpha,thin/(r_gamma,thin*Omega_AG) for the totally absorbing target.

nodes.name: Conditional AlScN transverse piezoelectric sign reversal
nodes.shortDescription: For the source Al0.64Sc0.36N thin-film direct bending preparation, the effective transverse coefficient e31,f changes from-2.90 C/m^2 as deposited to+2.76 C/m^2 after the stated one-minute room-temperature polarization reversal. This gives a finite electromechanical sign-control example in the switched film; it is not a longitudinal d33 coefficient or an unconstrained bulk-crystal constant.

nodes.name: Prepared AlScN switching with polarity-sensitive controls
nodes.shortDescription: The source AlScN series reports field-reversible polarization responses for its prepared x=0.27-0.43 films. At x=0.36 the combination of switched/as-deposited polarity-selective etching, transverse piezoelectric sign reversal and switching/non-switching pulse controls supports the source ferroelectric classification beyond a P-E loop alone. With the capacitor short-circuited between2 ms read pulses, the source finds no resolved loss attributable to back-switching over the tested interval up to10^5 s, while non-switching charge is not exactly zero.

nodes.name: Isolated water-dimer geometry and DLPNO-CCSD(T)/LED model context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the isolated neutral-water-dimer Conf1 geometry optimized at RI-MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ, including harmonic frequencies/ZPE at that level. Compute TightPNO DLPNO-CCSD(T) energies with frozen O1s cores, localized occupied/virtual orbitals, counterpoise BSSE correction and augmented triple/quadruple-zeta extrapolation. Compare LED energy components with the same paper DFT-SAPT partition under its stated basis and asymptotic-functional conventions.

nodes.name: Directional surface-radiometry and inverse-identification boundary
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected uniform-sample radiometry, distinguish specular reflected/incident flux ratio, directional BRDF f_r in sr^-1, dimensionless reflectance factor R=pi*f_r and directional-hemispherical reflectance integrated over outgoing directions at fixed incidence. In ROSI under-illumination, f_r equals the corrected reflected/incident flux ratio divided by the effective projected solid angle Omega_prime=(A/D^2)*C_f*C_e*cos(theta_r). Geometry, incident polarization, wavelength and illuminated position are part of the declared observable.

nodes.name: Scoped conjugation and benzene energetic/magnetic criteria
nodes.shortDescription: Aromatic-system description is retained through named finite criteria: the existing neutral-benzene VB state lowers the source model energy relative to its one-Kekule-function reference, while a separate GIAO-SCF calculation gives a specified ring-center magnetic shielding probe for benzene with a saturated control. Conjugation is broader than cyclic aromaticity. These model results do not establish universal electron-count thresholds, all-response equivalence or a new physical stage beyond resonance.

nodes.name: Asymptotic freedom in the perturbative domain
nodes.shortDescription: When b0>0, the zero-coupling fixed point is ultraviolet attractive for sufficiently small positive coupling. At fixed flavor number, the one-loop solution alpha_s(mu_R^2)=1/[b0 ln(mu_R^2/Lambda^2)] tends to zero as mu_R grows without bound.

nodes.name: ATLAS 2011-2012 search acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the ATLAS pp data at 7 TeV in 2011 and 8 TeV in April-June 2012, with channel luminosities 4.6-4.8 and 5.8-5.9 fb^-1. Apply channel-specific lepton/photon triggers, object reconstruction, isolation, jet and missing-momentum selections.

nodes.name: ATLAS historical neutral-boson mass fit
nodes.shortDescription: Using the four-lepton and diphoton channels with independently varying signal strengths, ATLAS reports a mass of 126.0 +/-0.4 statistical +/-0.4 systematic GeV for the new particle. This is the original 2012 fit result.

nodes.name: ATLAS historical combined excess and strength
nodes.shortDescription: The full published combination reports local significance 5.9 standard deviations (p0=1.7e-9), and global significance about 5.1 (p0=1.7e-7) over 110-600 GeV. At mH=126 GeV the fitted common signal strength relative to the Standard Model is 1.4 +/-0.3.

nodes.name: ATLAS selected diphoton candidates
nodes.shortDescription: The selected diphoton samples contain 23788 candidates at 7 TeV and 35251 at 8 TeV in 100-160 GeV, divided into ten categories per energy. Figure 4 shows inclusive and model-weighted views with fitted background residuals of these same samples.

nodes.name: ATLAS selected four-lepton candidates
nodes.shortDescription: The reanalysed 7 TeV and new 8 TeV four-lepton selections give the Figure 2 invariant-mass spectrum. In the Table 3 window 120-130 GeV, the reported observed counts are 6 four-muon, 5 mixed-electron/muon and 2 four-electron candidates; modeled signal and backgrounds are separate.

nodes.name: ATLAS 2012 limited Higgs compatibility
nodes.shortDescription: The reported channels support a new neutral boson compatible with the Standard Model Higgs production/decay hypothesis. Diphoton observation disfavors spin one; the paper explicitly requires more information to determine the particle nature in detail.

nodes.name: ATLAS original likelihood and combination
nodes.shortDescription: Profile the stated signal/background likelihood with correlated nuisance parameters. Diphotons use unbinned category likelihoods; WW uses transverse-mass bins for 0/1 jet and an integrated 2-jet contribution. The full Table 6 combination also imports earlier 7 TeV channels, while the mass fit selects the four-lepton and diphoton channels only.

nodes.name: ATLAS response and background conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Use simulated signal acceptance and mass response with data calibration/control corrections; constrain reducible and WW/top backgrounds through the stated control regions and diphoton backgrounds through category-specific mass fits. Retain control-transfer and shared calibration dependence.

nodes.name: ATLAS selected opposite-flavor transverse mass
nodes.shortDescription: The 8 TeV opposite-flavor dilepton selection supplies the Figure 6 transverse-mass distribution. Table 5 separately reports 185,38,0 observed events in the 0-,1-,2-jet categories after its extra mass window; the search likelihood uses a different mT selection.

nodes.name: Atomic binding, spectroscopy and formation distinction
nodes.shortDescription: An electronic bound-state spectrum specifies possible atom states under a declared Hamiltonian. A prepared-atom spectroscopic response constrains transitions or energy differences. Formation is a further population-changing process requiring initial matter, radiation or collision conditions and competing capture, de-excitation and ionization rates. The selected cosmological model follows those electronic populations while keeping pre-existing nuclei; it is distinct from primordial nuclear synthesis and from the laboratory microwave-quenching preparation.

nodes.name: Correlated atomic-mass fit
nodes.shortDescription: Atomic masses and their differences are inferred from a jointly constrained comparison network. Uncertainty in D-H depends on the covariance as well as both marginal mass errors.

nodes.name: Scoped atomic binding and formation evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The selected hydrogen model, prepared-atom microwave spectroscopy and historical cosmological recombination calculation address different aspects of atomic structure and formation. The positive result is electronic binding with discrete levels and a source-reported neutralization history under stated conditions. A supplied nuclear charge and electron inventory delimit the model; the selected evidence does not establish all many-electron shell structures, every element identity or the substrate of all later material organization.

nodes.name: Helium line-response and metallicity extrapolation
nodes.shortDescription: Aver and colleagues reanalyze published hydrogen and helium emission lines in metal-poor extragalactic H II regions. He I 10830 infrared data are scaled to the optical data using the observed-to-theoretical Paschen-gamma ratio. The line model fits density, temperature, optical depth, reddening, underlying absorption, neutral-hydrogen fraction and helium abundance, retaining the weak [O III] temperature prior; screened object estimates are regressed to zero metallicity.

nodes.name: Selected zero-metallicity helium estimate
nodes.shortDescription: The helium regression for the 15 distinct qualifying H II regions reports a zero-metallicity intercept Y_P=0.2449 +/- 0.0040. Y_P is a helium mass fraction inferred from response-corrected emission-line abundances and a metallicity regression, not the helium number ratio or a direct measurement at the BBN epoch.

nodes.name: Bali conditional static-energy avoided crossing
nodes.shortDescription: The two-state fit gives an avoided crossing, with the lower energy approaching the two-static-light-meson threshold over the measured range. A quadratic gap fit reports r_c/a=15.00(8) and a*DeltaE_c=0.0217(9); physical-unit conversion and uncertainties retain their declared scale and ensemble.

nodes.name: Bali static string/two-meson correlators
nodes.shortDescription: The study estimates the string, two-meson and cross-channel Euclidean correlators in the shared two-flavor ensemble. The nonzero mixing channel and operator overlaps support a joint spectral analysis.

nodes.name: Bali conditional Euclidean mixing coupling
nodes.shortDescription: The fitted energy gap and mixing angle determine g=DeltaE*sin(2*theta)/2 in the chosen two-state basis. This energy-dimension coupling describes mixing and Euclidean relaxation; real-time evolution of the closed two-state model is oscillatory.

nodes.name: Bali Wilson-loop-only string-breaking null
nodes.shortDescription: At separations beyond the fitted string-breaking region, the Wilson-loop-only data at t<=9a show no visible departure toward the lower two-meson threshold. The full operator matrix is needed to resolve the reported spectrum.

nodes.name: Bali field and potential extraction
nodes.shortDescription: Form the vacuum-subtracted Wilson-loop/plaquette contrasts with local spatial averaging and time insertions nearest the Wilson-loop midpoint. Extrapolate electric and magnetic components separately in Euclidean T before combining them; integrated observables are integrated at fixed T before extrapolation. Excited-state contamination of a field insertion can decrease as exp[-Delta V(T/2-S)], more slowly than for the Wilson potential. Independently fit the same ensembles' Wilson-loop ratios to the static potential; its fitted tension fixes relative lattice scales and its differences enter the later geometric-width method.

nodes.name: Bali source-conditioned field profiles
nodes.shortDescription: The reported local contrasts show an elongated action-density distribution between fixed sources. Figure 12 compares R=20 at beta=2.5 with R=30 at beta=2.635, described by the authors as approximately 1.7 fm under their adopted scale; the plotted action normalization is adjusted between couplings. The selected spacing, volume and T comparisons support this finite-lattice profile extraction within their uncertainties. Energy and action contrasts are separate reported observables.

nodes.name: Bali pure-SU(2) flux ensembles
nodes.shortDescription: Simulate pure SU(2) Wilson gauge theory without sea quarks, with periodic boundaries and external static fundamental Q and Qbar. Table 1 specifies beta=2.5 on 16^4 and 32^4 sites, beta=2.635 on 48^3 x 64, and beta=2.74 on 32^4. The printed spacings are a=0.0826(5), 0.0826(14), 0.0541(2) and 0.0408(2) fm in that order. Field measurements number 8680, 2046, 248 and 670 respectively; Wilson-loop and vacuum-plaquette sample counts can differ. Spatial source smearing and time-link integration improve overlap and noise. With dimensionless fitted tension K=a^2 kappa, the adopted sqrt(kappa)=440 MeV supplies only an orientation for physical units.

nodes.name: Bali profile and width inference
nodes.shortDescription: For beta=2.5 and 2.635, compare Gaussian and dipole interpolations of the central action profile, direct cutoff-dependent moment integrals, and the geometric estimate delta_geom^2=gamma A/(pi h), where h is the central height and A the transverse profile integral. The geometric A uses the differential action sum rule, the same-ensemble potential differences and the adopted beta-function factor. The method assumes that aligned static differences sigma_R-sigma_(R-2) are localized near the center plane and that transverse shapes at different R differ by amplitude and length rescalings. For infinite-plane Gaussian and dipole profiles gamma is 1 and 2.

nodes.name: Bali conditional action-profile widths
nodes.shortDescription: For source separations above approximately 1 fm at beta=2.5 and 2.635, the reported geometric action rms estimate is a delta_geom approximately 0.52 fm sqrt(gamma). The authors' plausible-profile estimate spans approximately 0.5-0.75 fm, and the physical FWHM a rho plateaus at approximately 0.7 fm under their formulas. The data are compatible with a constant width and also with logarithmic broadening; the calculation does not select between them.

nodes.name: Bali two-flavor static-source computational context
nodes.shortDescription: Four-dimensional Euclidean SU(3) lattice gauge theory with two mass-degenerate Wilson sea quarks, external static sources and the I=0 string/two-meson sector. The 24^3 x 40 ensemble uses beta=5.6, kappa=0.1575 and r0/a=6.009(53); choosing r0=0.5 fm gives a approximately 0.083 fm. The sea-quark mass is slightly below the physical strange-quark mass.

nodes.name: Barnes kaon bubble-chamber acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Expose the BNL 80-inch hydrogen bubble chamber to a mass-separated 5 GeV/c K- beam. The report describes about 100000 pictures and roughly 10^6 feet of kaon tracks, partially analyzed for characteristic Omega decays; this admission concerns its one selected event.

nodes.name: Barnes reconstructed neutral cascade
nodes.shortDescription: Under the stated assignments the report finds a Lambda-compatible p+pi- mass of 1116 +/- 2 MeV/c^2, a two-photon mass of 135.1 +/- 1.5 MeV/c^2, and a neutral Xi-compatible mass of 1316 +/- 4 MeV/c^2. Shared vertex geometry and transverse balance support the proposed Xi0+pi- parent decay.

nodes.name: Barnes conditional Omega identification
nodes.shortDescription: The report conditionally identifies particle 3 with Omega- from Q=-1, inferred S=-3 and reconstructed mass 1686 +/- 12 MeV/c^2, with a production missing mass of 500 +/- 25 MeV/c^2 compatible with K0. The quoted event proper decay time is 0.7e-10 s; no spin/parity or ensemble-lifetime determination is supplied.

nodes.name: Barnes cascade reconstruction assumptions
nodes.shortDescription: Associate the fitted Lambda, two converted photons and the displaced neutral trajectory under Equation 1; use particle-mass hypotheses, transverse balance, production missing mass and alternative-channel tests to interpret the same event.

nodes.name: Barnes selected event track observations
nodes.shortDescription: The selected event has charged-track directions and momenta listed in Table I, gap-density particle-identification information, displaced vertices and two photon conversions shown in Figure 2. These measured inputs precede the neutral cascade and parent-mass interpretation.

nodes.name: First-order baryon-octet mass relation
nodes.shortDescription: Gell-Mann Equation 8.1 states (m_N+m_Xi)/2=(3*m_Lambda+m_Sigma)/4 to first order in unitary-symmetry violation for the baryon octet with common spin and parity. This is a supplied approximate mass relation, not exact equality of all measured masses.

nodes.name: Nuclear synthesis and atomic recombination boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Primordial nuclear synthesis changes light-nucleus composition. Later atomic recombination changes bound-electron and ionization populations of existing nuclei in an expanding radiation background. Formation of helium or hydrogen nuclei is therefore distinct from formation of neutral helium or hydrogen atoms. The selected atomic-recombination calculation supplies a separate electron-population model, not another nuclear-synthesis channel.

nodes.name: Primordial nucleosynthesis source boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Source card 2.0 is represented by a specified expanding nuclear network, selected absorption and helium-emission analyses, and conditional abundance comparisons. Spectra are not direct recordings of nuclear formation. Astrophysical primordial-abundance inferences depend on line response, chemical evolution and selection; comparison with BBN predictions additionally requires a supplied cosmological background and weak/nuclear inputs. The light-element comparison must retain the lithium discrepancy rather than asserting universal concordance.

nodes.name: Historical conditional light-element comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Pitrou Table VIII reports Y_P=0.24709 +/- 0.00017 and D/H=(2.459 +/- 0.036)*10^-5 for its selected BBN inputs, alongside the adopted helium and deuterium estimates represented separately here. It also predicts Li/H=(5.623 +/- 0.247)*10^-10 against an adopted stellar estimate 1.58(+0.35,-0.28)*10^-10. The selected deuterium and helium comparisons support the model conditionally; the lithium discrepancy prevents blanket concordance for all light elements.

nodes.name: Historical BBN prediction context
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Pitrou 2018 calculation evolves a homogeneous standard BBN network using its supplied expansion and plasma history, adopted baryon-density and neutron-lifetime inputs, weak-rate corrections and nuclear rates. Adopted historical inputs include Omega_b*h^2=0.022250 +/- 0.00016, tau_n=879.5 +/- 0.8 s and T_0=2.7255 +/- 0.0006 K from its Table X. The cosmological density input uses the stated Ade 2016/Planck 2015 analysis, not the separately represented Planck 2018 result. Section V.E assigns Table VIII to CMB-prior marginalization in addition to nuclear-rate and neutron-lifetime variation. Its quoted errors are source-reported one-standard-deviation uncertainties, not locally verified propagation. The table also lists adopted observed comparators; the calculation does not collect primordial spectra.

nodes.name: Beam neutron-decay count ratio
nodes.shortDescription: In the ideal corrected beam model, R_p=epsilon_p*N_n/tau and R_monitor=epsilon_0*v_0*N_n/L, so tau=L*epsilon_p*R_monitor/(epsilon_0*v_0*R_p). R_p counts detected proton-producing decays, and epsilon_0 is the monitor efficiency at the reference speed v_0.

nodes.name: Replayed beam calibration arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Equation 1 converts the printed monitor response to 3.109827...e-5. With the adopted zero drifts, the central efficiency-ratio rescaling gives 887.725... seconds, a +1.425... second shift. Diagonal quadrature of the five printed Table II entries gives 2.32379... seconds, rounding to 2.3.

nodes.name: Printed beam calibration arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Evaluate the Equation 1 thermal conversion, Equation 4 central lifetime rescaling with adopted zero drifts, and diagonal quadrature of the five rounded Table II uncertainty components.

nodes.name: Beane conditional bound-state interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Compare rest and moving systems across volumes, using the separately fitted single-baryon dispersion as a control. For an assumed two-body bound state at sufficiently large L, Equation 5 gives kappa(L)=kappa_0+6Z_psi^2 exp(-kappa_0 L)/L+..., with nonrelativistic kappa_0 approximately sqrt(M_B B). The authors find no statistically resolved volume dependence between the two largest boxes and adopt the average of the largest-volume rest and two boosted determinations as their infinite-volume estimate; they do not obtain a refined extrapolation by fitting Equation 5.

nodes.name: Beane flavor-symmetric nuclear ensembles
nodes.shortDescription: Use nf=3 degenerate dynamical quarks in SU(3) color gauge theory without electromagnetism, with tadpole-improved Luscher-Weisz gauge action and isotropic clover fermions. Table I specifies beta=6.1 and bare b*m_q=-0.2450 on 24^3 x 48, 32^3 x 48 and 48^3 x 64 lattices. The reported configuration counts are 3822, 3050 and 1905, with mean source counts per configuration 72, 48 and 54. The adopted Upsilon-spectrum spacing is b=0.1453(16) fm. The degenerate pseudoscalar mass is approximately 806 MeV, with common quark masses described as tuned near the physical strange mass.

nodes.name: Beane two-nucleon spectral extraction
nodes.shortDescription: Construct Gaussian-smeared quark sources and point/smeared sinks, baryon blocks projected to sink momentum, and multibaryon operators localized at one source point with upper Dirac components. The deuteron channel has I=0, J^P=1+ and flavor irrep 10bar; the dineutron channel has I=1, J^P=0+ and irrep 27. Fit effective-energy plateaus by correlated constant fits and correlators by exponential fits, using jackknife or bootstrap covariance. Vary accepted fit intervals to estimate fitting systematics. The finite-volume octet-baryon energies supply the shared threshold subtraction.

nodes.name: Beane conditional two-nucleon binding estimates
nodes.shortDescription: Table VII reports the original largest-volume rest/boost averages B_d=19.5(3.6)(3.1)(0.2) MeV and B_nn=15.9(2.7)(2.7)(0.2) MeV as estimates of infinite-volume binding at this flavor-symmetric parameter point. Their reported kappa_0 L values on the largest box are 6.3 and 5.7. These are the authors' conditional bound-state assignments, distinct from the finite-volume rest-frame shifts.

nodes.name: Beane finite-volume two-nucleon deficits
nodes.shortDescription: For P=0 and the volumes 24^3 x 48, 32^3 x 48 and 48^3 x 64 in that order, Tables V-VII report B_L=-DeltaE_L of 25.4(2.6)(4.7)(0.3), 22.5(2.3)(2.6)(0.2) and 19.7(3.1)(4.1)(0.2) MeV in the deuteron channel, and 17.8(1.7)(2.8)(0.2), 15.1(2.0)(2.0)(0.2) and 13.1(2.8)(4.3)(0.2) MeV in the dineutron channel. Parentheses give statistical, fitting systematic and scale errors respectively.

nodes.name: Belle tau-pair acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use 711 fb^-1 of Belle e+e- collisions at the Upsilon(4S) and 60 MeV below it, with asymmetric 3.5 and 8 GeV beams. The SVD1/SVD2 subsets have 157/554 fb^-1. Select six charged pion candidates with total charge zero, three per thrust hemisphere, rejecting reconstructed K0S, Lambda and pi0 candidates and applying the stated photon, thrust, momentum, pseudomass, vertex and direction-solution cuts, including closest-line separation dl<0.03 cm.

nodes.name: Belle reconstructed tau proper lengths
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports about 1.1 million selected data events. Figure 3 displays their reconstructed t=l/(beta*gamma) distribution in centimeters, with fitted signal-plus-background response and modeled background components. These are selected paired-decay candidates and reconstructed proper lengths, not direct clock readings or a background-free list of tau decays.

nodes.name: Belle tau-lifetime fit and calibration
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the reconstructed-length distribution with an exponential convolved with Equation 3 resolution plus fixed MC background shapes and normalizations. Float the signal normalization, exponential scale and five resolution parameters; fix asymmetry A=2.5 cm^-1. Calibrate the fitted scale with generated mean lengths 84, 87.11 and 90 micrometers. Apply the reported alignment, fixed-asymmetry, beam/radiation, fit-range, background and adopted-mass uncertainties before quoting the combined lifetime.

nodes.name: Belle charge-combined tau lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Belle reports mean c*tau=86.99 +/- 0.16 statistical +/- 0.10 systematic micrometers, equivalently tau=(290.17 +/- 0.53 statistical +/- 0.33 systematic) fs. This charge-combined mean lifetime is the result of the selected paired-three-pion sample and its calibrated response-convolution fit.

nodes.name: Belle tau-length reconstruction and response
nodes.shortDescription: For the paired tau->3pi nu hypothesis, neglect neutrino mass and initially ISR/FSR when solving two possible CM tau directions; use their mean vector, adopted beam energy and tau mass to boost to the lab. Fit each three-track vertex, approximate each tau path as straight and use the closest points of the two paths as production estimates. Reconstruct t=l/(beta*gamma), a length equal to c times proper time. Signal/background simulation and separate dimuon control data inform response and systematic treatment.

nodes.name: Finite benzene ring-center NICS with saturated control
nodes.shortDescription: Table1 reports ring-center NICS=-9.7 ppm for neutral D6h benzene and -2.2 ppm for saturated nonaromatic D3d cyclohexane in the selected GIAO-SCF/6-31+G* column. The distinct6-31G* column gives -11.5 and -2.1 ppm, respectively. The declared benzene response supplies a finite positive magnetic aromaticity-probe example, while the saturated control limits a sign-only classification.

nodes.name: Entropic hard-disk ordering and distinct transitions
nodes.shortDescription: The reported two-dimensional hard-disk calculations support first-order liquid-hexatic coexistence over approximately eta=0.700 to 0.716, using coexistence patterns, the equilibrium equation of state and interface scaling. At eta=0.718 the source finds exponential positional decay on a scale of about 100 disk radii and very slow orientational decay, interpreted as a single hexatic phase. Near eta=0.720 the positional correlations become approximately algebraic, near r^-1/3 over the resolved range, and the source identifies a continuous hexatic-solid transition. Thus this specified entropic model has ordered regimes and two distinct transition characters.

nodes.name: Hard-disk equilibrium sampling and correlation context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the reported constant-NV periodic hard-disk calculations with N=256^2, 512^2 and up to 1024^2 disks. The SEC event-chain algorithm moves in positive x or y directions, breaks detailed balance and preserves global balance. Interpret reported coexistence snapshots, the equilibrium equation of state and its Maxwell/interface analysis together with positional and bond-orientational correlations. Use the numerically located first-peak wave vector k_peak of the computed structure factor for positional correlations, rather than imposing the perfect triangular-lattice k_perf. Retain comparison of crystal/liquid initial conditions, autocorrelation and finite-size checks, and the supplement Gaussian sampling-error procedure.

nodes.name: Checked MAMI table identities and fit-census mismatch
nodes.shortDescription: The bound tables contain 1422 cross-section rows, 77 unconstrained plus four constrained Rosenbluth entries and 1000 spline evaluations. GE/(GM/mu_p) reproduces the tabulated normalized ratio within 1e-11. Nine Table IV rows admit their displayed reduced chi-square under rounding; the Friedrich-Walcher row does not.

nodes.name: Bound MAMI table verification
nodes.shortDescription: Parse the bound author tables under their distinct column conventions; check counts, shared-factor coverage, form-factor ratio identities and rounded Table IV arithmetic.

nodes.name: MAMI proton elastic-scattering acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Measure unpolarized electron scattering on liquid hydrogen at six beam energies with the three A1 spectrometers; extract acceptance-modeled ratios with the declared radiation, luminosity and normalization treatment.

nodes.name: MAMI-only fitted electric and magnetic form factors
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Mainz-only spline table gives GE, GM/mu_p and mu_p*GE/GM on 1000 Q^2 grid points from 0 to 0.998001 GeV^2, with separate pointwise bands. These are fitted elastic-response quantities conditional on shared normalization and the stated correction model.

nodes.name: MAMI-only Sachs form-factor fit
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the reused MAMI cross-section ratios with the published Mainz-only models and shared normalization parameters, retaining squared-form-factor response, scaled errors and correction assumptions.

nodes.name: MAMI extracted elastic cross-section ratios
nodes.shortDescription: The bound MAMI table contains 1422 cross-section ratios at six incident energies from 180 to 855 MeV, with acceptance-averaged Q^2 from 0.003839 to 0.977245 GeV^2. The ratios already use the spline normalization and scaled point errors.

nodes.name: MAMI dependent Rosenbluth separation
nodes.shortDescription: Reuse the spline-fit normalization and project the same acceptance-averaged cross sections to fixed Q^2 values before the epsilon-linear separation; retain unconstrained results and constrained alternatives separately.

nodes.name: MAMI dependent separated form factors
nodes.shortDescription: The bound Rosenbluth table reports 77 unconstrained GE/GM pairs over Q^2=0.0152-0.5524 GeV^2, plus four low-Q^2 GE alternatives constrained by GM/(mu_p*G_dipole)=1 or 1.05. The separation uses the same acquisition and spline-fit normalization.

nodes.name: Bethe approximate radiative-shift model
nodes.shortDescription: Bethe subtracts the free-electron electromagnetic mass contribution from the bound-electron self-energy. With an assumed cutoff K approximately m c^2, the nonrelativistic model estimates the hydrogen 2S shift as about 1040 MHz.

nodes.name: Binding-energy conversion inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Kessler converts the reciprocal recoil-corrected wavelength using 1.331025045(11)e-15 u per inverse meter or 1.239841870(54)e-6 eV per inverse meter. These are adopted 1999 conversion constants with uncertainties.

nodes.name: Bipartite quantum entanglement
nodes.shortDescription: Relative to H_A tensor H_B, a state is separable if rho = sum_i p_i rho_A_i tensor rho_B_i with p_i >= 0 and sum_i p_i = 1; otherwise it is entangled. For a pure state, separability reduces to factorization.

nodes.name: Bipartite quantum state
nodes.shortDescription: A finite bipartite quantum state is a positive, unit-trace density operator on a declared tensor product H_A tensor H_B. A product state has the form rho_A tensor rho_B.

nodes.name: SLAC 1969 corrected continuum cross sections
nodes.shortDescription: The report gives corrected d^2sigma/(dOmega dEprime) for W>=2 GeV at 6 and 10 degrees. Table I spans incident settings 7.000-17.696 GeV; its 6-degree and 10-degree columns use 10^-31 and 10^-32 cm^2/(sr GeV), respectively. Figure 1 separates pre-radiative spectra, the elastic tail and corrected spectra; Figure 2 shows the continuum changing much less with momentum transfer than the resonances. These are the companion data underlying the admitted Breidenbach interpretation.

nodes.name: SLAC 1969 response and radiative correction
nodes.shortDescription: For the existing SLAC electron-only acquisition, Bloom describes a 7 cm liquid-hydrogen target, beam-current monitors, a magnetic spectrometer and electron/pion discrimination. Correct dead time, tracking and identification efficiency, target-density changes, empty-target yields and positron-estimated backgrounds. Subtract the calculated elastic radiative tail, then unfold all spectra at each angle in two dimensions using the peaking approximation, interpolation and some extrapolation. SLAC and MIT analyses of the same data are averaged.

nodes.name: Borexino electron-decay search preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use 408 live days from January 2012 to May 2013 in the PC/PPO scintillator. The spectral selection uses a 75.5 t fiducial mass with R<3.02 m and |Z|<1.67 m. Count triggered PMTs in 230 ns; fit 62-220 hits, corresponding to 164-590 keV.

nodes.name: Borexino electron radiative-decay lifetime bound
nodes.shortDescription: Borexino reports tau(e- -> gamma + nu) >= 6.6e28 yr at 90% C.L., including systematic treatment. Its statistical-only result uses S=379 events, T=408 d, N_e=9.19e31 electrons in 278 t, and efficiency 0.264 in tau >= efficiency*N_e*T/S, giving the reported 7.2e28 yr bound.

nodes.name: Borexino constrained decay-limit inference
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the low-energy spectrum with constrained pp and other solar/background components, free light yield and resolution parameters, and a hypothetical photon contribution. Normalize probability profiles over nonnegative signal counts; integrate to the stated 90% level and combine profiles over correlated systematic variations.

nodes.name: Borexino electron-decay response model
nodes.shortDescription: Model a hypothetical 256 keV photon as a quenched 220 +/- 0.4 keV electron-equivalent response, using Birks quenching, a scaled-Poisson line shape and measured/simulated resolution inputs. Include data-driven synthetic pile-up. Simulation gives global photon efficiency 0.264, including the fiducial cut.

nodes.name: Borexino electron-decay search spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 1 reports the selected low-energy spectrum with radioactive, solar-neutrino and pile-up components. The hypothetical photon line is displayed at its 90% exclusion level; it is not an observed peak from electron decay.

nodes.name: Experiment-constrained nucleon component ratio
nodes.shortDescription: After additionally using the experimental neutron-proton mass difference, Borsanyi reports (M_n-M_p)_QCD/(M_n-M_p)_QED=-2.49+/-0.23 (statistical) +/-0.29 (systematic). This is a dimensionless, convention-dependent calibrated inference.

nodes.name: Physical-point isospin mass splittings
nodes.shortDescription: Table 1 reports total splittings in MeV with statistical then systematic uncertainties: n-p 1.51(16)(23); Sigma--Sigma+ 8.09(16)(11); Xi--Xi0 6.66(11)(09); D+-D0 4.68(10)(13); Xi_cc++-Xi_cc+ 2.16(11)(17); Coleman-Glashow combination Delta_N-Delta_Sigma+Delta_Xi 0.00(11)(06). The neutron-proton total is 1.51+/-0.16 (statistical) +/-0.23 (systematic) MeV.

nodes.name: Kaon finite-volume response
nodes.shortDescription: For the four enhanced-coupling volumes, Figure 1 reports chi^2/dof=0.86 for the neutral-kaon constant fit and 0.90 for the squared-mass-difference fit with a free 1/L^3 term. The leading 1/L and 1/L^2 terms alone do not describe all four mass-difference points.

nodes.name: Correlated lattice mass-difference fits
nodes.shortDescription: The paper extracts finite-lattice mass differences by fitting Euclidean correlators of isospin partners jointly. Ensemble fit-quality distributions and the selected time windows precede physical-point and cutoff extrapolations.

nodes.name: Convention-dependent isospin components
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected convention, Table 1 gives QCD and QED components in MeV, with statistical then systematic uncertainties: n-p 2.52(17)(24) and -1.00(07)(14); Sigma--Sigma+ 8.09(16)(11) and 0 by convention; Xi--Xi0 5.53(17)(17) and 1.14(16)(09); D+-D0 2.54(08)(10) and 2.14(11)(07); Xi_cc++-Xi_cc+ -2.53(11)(06) and 4.69(10)(17); Coleman-Glashow -0.00(13)(05) and 0.00(06)(02). Equation S38 gives the electromagnetic kaon squared-mass contribution -2250(80)(90) MeV^2.

nodes.name: Enhanced-coupling kaon volume scan
nodes.shortDescription: Four Table S4 ensembles at beta=3.2, bare e=1.00, a*m_u=-0.0859, a*m_d=-0.0792 and a*m_s=-0.0522: L^3*T=24^3*48, 32^3*64, 48^3*96 and 80^3*64. The rounded pion masses are 292, 290, 290 and 289 MeV. The common lattice spacing is about 0.102 fm; Figure 1 describes M_K0 as about 450 MeV.

nodes.name: Four-flavor isospin-breaking ensemble
nodes.shortDescription: Dynamical 1+1+1+1-flavor QCD+QED with tree-level Symanzik gluon action, clover-improved Wilson quarks, three HEX gluon-smearing steps and one APE photon-smearing step. The QED_L prescription, 27 neutral and 14 charged ensembles, four overall lattice spacings and declared mass/charge inputs define the production analysis.

nodes.name: Two-photon teleportation preparation
nodes.shortDescription: The BBO down-conversion source supplies 702.2 nm photon pairs. Calcite paths and polarization rotations prepare (|a1 a2>+|b1 b2>)/sqrt(2), with the input alpha|v>+beta|h> encoded in the polarization of Alice's resource photon. The stations are about 2.5 m apart; the coincidence window is 1.6 ns and runs last 10 s, typically yielding about 500 coincidences.

nodes.name: Conditional teleportation fringes
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 2 shows four outcome-conditioned coincidence curves versus Bob's analyzer angle for a 22.5 degree linear input, with maxima at 22.5, 67.5, -67.5 and -22.5 degrees as predicted by Equation 11. Figure 3 displays the corresponding verification for an elliptical input prepared with a 20 degree quarter-wave plate, using an outcome-dependent quarter-wave setting at Bob.

nodes.name: Three-state teleportation criterion
nodes.shortDescription: For linear inputs at 0, +120 and -120 degrees, each with prior probability 1/3, define S as I_parallel/(I_parallel+I_perpendicular), averaged with weights 1/3 over the inputs and 1/4 over the four Alice outcomes. Equations 1-3 and the Appendix bound S<=3/4 for single-copy measurement by Alice followed only by classical communication and state preparation by Bob. The verifier projects onto the corresponding prepared state after accounting for the outcome-dependent rotation.

nodes.name: Passive teleportation verification
nodes.shortDescription: Alice's path-polarization analyzer identifies four Bell-basis outcomes using a 50:50 beam splitter, polarizing beam splitters and four detector channels. Bob converts paths to polarization and sets the verification analyzer for each outcome according to Equation 11. The experiment uses passive outcome-dependent verification rather than active conditional correction. I_parallel and I_perpendicular are coincidences with the same Bob detector at orthogonal analyzer settings.

nodes.name: Three-state teleportation score
nodes.shortDescription: For the three equally weighted linear inputs and four equally weighted Bell outcomes, the source reports S=0.853 +/- 0.012, exceeding its classical-channel bound 3/4. This is the reported average projection score inferred from normalized conditional coincidences under the stated response and benchmark assumptions.

nodes.name: Calibrated diffraction wavelength
nodes.shortDescription: For the first-order angle used by Kessler, lambda_gamma=2*d220*(1-epsilon*p)*sin(theta), with d220 the vacuum spacing at 22.5 C and pressure p in atmospheres. The angle and crystal scale are separate inputs.

nodes.name: Conditional parallel-plate force coefficient
nodes.shortDescription: The main nine-point fit gives C_Cas=(2.34 +/- 0.34) x 10^-28 Hz^2 m^5 and K_C=(1.22 +/- 0.18) x 10^-27 N m^2 through K_C=epsilon0 C_Cas/(4 C_el). Agreement with ideal pressure is conditional on calibration and the declared fit.

nodes.name: Parallel-surface residual frequency shift
nodes.shortDescription: After electrostatic subtraction, the reported squared-frequency shift decreases toward smaller gaps. The readout is a force-gradient-dependent resonance shift, not a direct pressure sensor.

nodes.name: Parallel-surface frequency preparation
nodes.shortDescription: A chromium-coated silicon cantilever faces a rigid coated beam, overlapping 1.2 by 1.2 mm. Interferometry reads the torsional resonance; electrostatic sweeps calibrate gap and residual voltage.

nodes.name: Bulava N200 static-source ensemble
nodes.shortDescription: Use the N200 CLS ensemble with Nf=2+1 nonperturbatively O(a)-improved Wilson sea quarks, 128 x 48^3 sites, m_pi=280 MeV and m_K=460 MeV. Open temporal boundaries restrict measurements to the central half. Wilson loops on 1664 configurations are averaged into 104 bins aligned with the 104-configuration subset carrying light/strange propagators. The adopted spacing is a=0.06426(76) fm.

nodes.name: Bulava three-state mixing model
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the three extracted levels over 11<=r/a<=25 to eigenvalues of H(r)=[[V_hat0+sigma*r,g1,g2],[g1,E_hat1,0],[g2,0,E_hat2]], using an uncorrelated six-parameter fit. E_hat1, E_hat2, g1 and g2 are constant in r. Define r_c by V_hat0+sigma*r_c=E_hat1 and r_cs by V_hat0+sigma*r_cs=E_hat2; these are diagonal-branch crossing conventions.

nodes.name: Bulava light and strange screening spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: Figures 1-2 report the lowest three relative static energies V_n(r)-2E_B, n=0,1,2. They display light- and strange-channel avoided crossings; beyond the breaking region the ground level approaches the two-static-light threshold. The separately estimated two-static-strange threshold is 2E_Bs-2E_B=0.028(5)/a=85(16) MeV. Off-axis separations resolve the narrow strange-channel mixing region.

nodes.name: Bulava variational static-energy extraction
nodes.shortDescription: For external static Q and Qbar at fixed separation, combine a string interpolator, an I=0 two-static-light-meson interpolator and a two-static-strange-meson interpolator in the Sigma_g^+ sector after heavy-spin decoupling. Two string smearings (15 and 20 levels) make the variational matrix 4 x 4. HYP2 links and stochastic LapH quark propagators supply the correlators. With t0/a=5 and td/a=10, the fixed GEVP rotation gives C_hat_nn(t); correlated single-exponential fits to C_hat_nn(t)/C_B(t)^2 extract V_n(r)-2E_B.

nodes.name: Bulava conditional string-breaking scales
nodes.shortDescription: The three-state fit reports a*E_hat1=0.0019(2), a*E_hat2=0.0262(6), a*g1=0.0154(4), a*g2=0.0080(5), a^2*sigma=0.0229(3) and a*V_hat0=-0.434(5). Under its diagonal-crossing definition, r_c/a=19.053(82) and r_cs/a=20.114(87), converted to 1.224(15) fm and 1.293(16) fm using a=0.06426(76) fm.

nodes.name: Constrained bulk equilibrium, coexistence and phase-rule conditions
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected hydrostatic bulk thermodynamic framework, equilibrium criteria use allowed variations under explicit constraints: entropy is maximal at fixed total energy, or energy is minimal at fixed entropy. Write A=U-T*S and G=U-T*S+p*V; the relevant potential and stability comparison depend on what is held fixed. For phases in freely exchanging contact without gravity, electrical effects, solid distortion or capillary tension, equilibrium requires equal temperature, pressure and the potential of each freely exchangeable independently variable component. In this setting the intensive degrees of freedom obey f=C+2-N_ph, where C counts independent components and N_ph counts coexisting phases, not specimens.

nodes.name: Canonical gauge-invariant curvature mode
nodes.shortDescription: For scalar perturbations with spatial metric g_ij=-a^2[(1-2psi)delta_ij+2 partial_i partial_j E], define Hcal=a'/a=aH, Q=delta(phi)+(phi'/Hcal)psi, v=aQ, z=a phi'/Hcal=a dot(phi)/H, and R=psi+Hcal delta(phi)/phi'=v/z. Primes denote conformal-time derivatives. On an interval with H and dot(phi) nonzero, eliminating the linear lapse/shift constraints gives S2=(1/2)integral d_eta d^3x[(v')^2-(grad v)^2+(z''/z)v^2], up to boundary terms. A Fourier mode satisfies u_k''+[k^2-z''/z]u_k=0; its canonical momentum is pi_v=v'.

nodes.name: Capture photon and nuclear recoil
nodes.shortDescription: For capture by an approximately stationary proton, the binding energy includes the measured photon energy and the recoiling deuteron kinetic energy. The leading correction is E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2).

nodes.name: Material-dependent Casimir interaction
nodes.shortDescription: A Casimir interaction can be calculated from electromagnetic response and coupling to material sources. Ideal conducting boundaries are a limiting approximation; the external-source formulation does not require an independently measured absolute zero-point energy.

nodes.name: Geometry, response and force-observable boundary for Casimir claims
nodes.shortDescription: Specify geometry, separation, material response, temperature and the actual readout before comparing a Casimir model with an experiment. Ideal interaction energy per area, conjugate pressure, a curved-body force and a resonance shift sensitive to a force gradient are different quantities. Residual-force attribution additionally retains electrostatic calibration and subtraction. A measured conditional interaction does not uniquely identify an absolute vacuum energy or the original ontology of its parents.

nodes.name: Scoped material-boundary Casimir evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The existing corrected sphere-plane study supports an attractive residual force under its torsion-balance preparation and response assumptions. A separate parallel-surface study supports a conditional pressure coefficient inferred from a calibrated residual resonance-frequency shift. Together with the ideal-plate and material-response definitions, these provide bounded positive evidence for geometry- and material-conditioned electromagnetic interactions; they are not direct measurements of one universal vacuum substance, all force signs or a cross-level emergence law.

nodes.name: CDF top-width selected-event preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the full CDF II Run II proton-antiproton sample at sqrt(s)=1.96 TeV with integrated luminosity 8.7 fb^-1. Select one central electron or muon, missing transverse energy and at least four jets; separate zero, one and multiple b tags and tight/loose jet requirements into five exclusive categories.

nodes.name: CDF top-width likelihood and confidence construction
nodes.shortDescription: Fit correlated reconstructed-top and dijet masses with two-dimensional kernel densities and interpolation in width and jet-energy scale. Multiply five category likelihoods, constrain expected backgrounds and leave signal yields free. Use a nonnegative width estimator, simulated Neyman confidence bands with likelihood-ratio ordering and the reported Gaussian systematic treatment.

nodes.name: CDF top-width reconstruction and response
nodes.shortDescription: Apply calibrated jet response, neural-network energy corrections and secondary-vertex b tagging. Under the top-pair lepton+jets hypothesis choose the lowest-chi^2 jet assignment for the reconstructed top mass; a separate non-b dijet mass uses the pair closest to the adopted W mass. Simulated signal/background templates, auxiliary photon+jet resolution control and generator variations model their response.

nodes.name: CDF selected top-width categories
nodes.shortDescription: Table I reports 1627, 882, 997, 208 and 275 observed events in the 0-tag, 1-tagL, 1-tagT, 2-tagL and 2-tagT categories, respectively. These are selected signal-plus-background counts; the inference uses the corresponding reconstructed-event distributions rather than the five totals alone.

nodes.name: CDF conditional top-width interval
nodes.shortDescription: For input top mass 172.5 GeV/c^2, CDF reports best-fit estimator Gamma_meas=1.63 GeV, a two-sided 68% confidence interval 1.10<Gamma_top<4.05 GeV and a 95% confidence upper bound Gamma_top<6.38 GeV. Both intervals include the source statistical and systematic treatment.

nodes.name: Charged-fermion mass and Higgs coupling convention
nodes.shortDescription: For each supplied charged-fermion mass m_i in the declared mass basis, the tree-level term is -m_i*psi-bar_i*psi_i-(m_i/v)*H*psi-bar_i*psi_i. Defining y_i=sqrt(2)*m_i/v gives m_i=y_i*v/sqrt(2) and the one-Higgs coefficient y_i/sqrt(2)=m_i/v. This reparametrizes independent mass/Yukawa inputs; it does not calculate their numerical hierarchy.

nodes.name: Declared charged-matter electromagnetic regime
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the Maxwell-Dirac Lagrangian L=-F_mu_nu*F^mu_nu/4+psi_bar*(i*gamma^mu*D_mu-m)*psi, with F_mu_nu=partial_mu*A_nu-partial_nu*A_mu and D_mu=partial_mu+i*e*A_mu, in rationalized hbar=c=1 units. The current coupling is -e*psi_bar*gamma^mu*A_mu*psi. The declared Abelian gauge transformation acts jointly on A_mu and the charged spinor; it specifies an interacting model rather than deriving a material configuration.

nodes.name: CHSH local hidden-variable model
nodes.shortDescription: With binary outcomes, local responses and a hidden-variable distribution independent of measurement settings, S = E00 + E01 + E10 - E11 obeys |S| <= 2. Stochastic local responses are convex mixtures of deterministic ones.

nodes.name: CMS conditional strong-coupling extraction
nodes.shortDescription: The NNPDF2.1-based fit to R32 over Q=420-1390 GeV gives alpha_s(M_Z)=0.1148 +/- 0.0014 (experimental) +/- 0.0018 (PDF) +/- 0.0050 (theory), with chi^2/dof=22.0/20. The paper combines these uncertainties in quadrature to report 0.1148 +/- 0.0055.

nodes.name: CMS unfolded inclusive-jet ratio
nodes.shortDescription: CMS reports the ratio of inclusive three-jet to inclusive two-jet event yields, unfolded to stable-particle level, over Q=250-1390 GeV. R32 rises as third-jet phase space opens, forms a plateau around 600-1000 GeV and falls at higher Q.

nodes.name: CMS conditional running-coupling comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The three fitted scale regions give alpha_s(Q)=0.0936 +/- 0.0041 at 474 GeV, 0.0894 +/- 0.0031 at 664 GeV and 0.0889 +/- 0.0034 at 896 GeV. These total-uncertainty results, converted with the specified three-loop RGE, are reported as compatible with its scale dependence.

nodes.name: CMS fractionally charged search preparation
nodes.shortDescription: The search uses 5.0 fb^-1 of CMS pp collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV recorded in 2011. Single-muon triggering requires reconstructed pT>40 GeV and |eta|<2.1. Offline tracks matched to muon detectors require reconstructed pT>45 GeV, |eta|<1.5, track quality and isolation, at least six tracker ionization measurements including two pixel measurements, and collision-time/impact-parameter cuts.

nodes.name: CMS fractional-charge limit inference
nodes.shortDescription: Cosmic-ray control selections with inverted impact parameters predict 0.007 +/- 0.006 events. A scaled Z-peak control sample is fitted in zero-to-five low-ionization measurements using a generalized binomial form and extrapolated to the signal region, predicting 0.005 +/- 0.004 pp events. The reported total is 0.012 +/- 0.007. The paper uses CLs for 95% production-cross-section upper limits and compares them with the benchmark leading-order cross section to obtain mass exclusions.

nodes.name: CMS conditional fractional-charge limits
nodes.shortDescription: For the stated detector-stable spin-1/2 SU(3)c/SU(2)L-singlet benchmark, CMS reports 95% CLs cross-section upper limits over masses 100-600 GeV: 1.7-2.3 fb for |q|=2/3 and 14-5.4 fb for |q|=1/3. Comparing with its modified Drell-Yan prediction excludes benchmark masses below 310 GeV and 140 GeV, respectively, at the reported 95% confidence level.

nodes.name: CMS low-ionization signal response
nodes.shortDescription: The benchmark is pair-produced spin-1/2 particles with electric charges +/-e/3 or +/-2e/3, singlets under SU(3)c and SU(2)L, assumed not to decay within the detector. Modified Drell-Yan photon/Z production is simulated with PYTHIA 6.422, leading-order CTEQ6L1 parton distributions and GEANT4 detector response for masses 100-600 GeV. At least six retained tracker measurements with dE/dx<2 MeV/cm define the signal region.

nodes.name: CMS selected fractional-charge candidate count
nodes.shortDescription: CMS reports zero events in the signal region containing a selected track with at least six retained tracker measurements below 2 MeV/cm. Figure 2 also reports no search-sample track with five or more such measurements. This is the selected event count before a subtraction of the predicted 0.012 +/- 0.007 background.

nodes.name: CMS inclusive-jet ratio preparation
nodes.shortDescription: CMS 2011 proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV. The trigger samples have effective luminosities 0.15, 0.51 and 5.0 fb^-1 for HLT thresholds 190, 240 and 370 GeV. Particle-flow reconstruction and anti-kT R=0.7 define selected jets; both leading jets must have |y|<2.5 and selected jets require pT>150 GeV.

nodes.name: CMS 2016 tau-pair acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Select the 2016 CMS pp exposure at 13 TeV, 35.9 fb^-1, into tau_h tau_h, mu-tau_h, e-tau_h and e-mu final states with exclusive 0-jet, VBF and boosted categories; apply the stated triggers, object, isolation and charge selections.

nodes.name: CMS reported common-coupling compatibility
nodes.shortDescription: CMS Figure 22 reports contours compatible with the Standard Model point (kappa_V,kappa_f)=(1,1) under the authors' implemented model. This is a conditional interpretation of the same 2016 data with a common fermion modifier, not a separately measured tau Yukawa or a new acquisition.

nodes.name: CMS common-coupling scan conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Reuse the 2016 selections in the reported common kappa_V/kappa_f scan at mH=125.09 GeV, profile the nuisance parameters, and now include H-to-WW as signal. The cited CMS method and generic coupling framework delimit this interpretation without specifying a complete experiment-specific width/loop map.

nodes.name: CMS same-fit sensitive-bin summaries
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 18 regroups observed bins by the expected S/(S+B); Figure 19 displays S/(S+B)-weighted reconstructed-mass summaries of the same data and fitted components. In Table 4, the log10(S/(S+B))>-0.9 subset contains observed counts 11,54,91,207 for e-mu, e-tau_h, mu-tau_h and tau_h tau_h; expected component counts and totals remain reported post-fit quantities.

nodes.name: CMS original tau-rate likelihood
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the selected category bins and control regions jointly with a common H-to-tau-tau signal strength at the adopted mass 125.09 GeV. Profile yield/shape and template-bin nuisances with their stated correlations; treat H-to-WW as background for this rate and significance inference.

nodes.name: CMS 2016 tau-rate and local excess
nodes.shortDescription: For the 2016-only analysis at fixed mH=125.09 GeV, CMS reports mu=1.09 (+0.27/-0.26) relative to the Standard Model tau-pair rate, with local observed significance 4.9 and expected significance 4.7 standard deviations.

nodes.name: CMS tau response and control transfers
nodes.shortDescription: Apply simulated templates with data-constrained tau/object and missing-momentum response; use Drell–Yan, W+jets, QCD and top control regions with their stated transfer assumptions and shared nuisance constraints. Preserve the partial overlap of tau energy-scale calibration and search selections.

nodes.name: CMS selected tau-decay distributions
nodes.shortDescription: The selected data points in Figures 6–17 give channel/category reconstructed distributions for the 2016 exposure. The tau_h tau_h 0-jet input is one-dimensional; the remaining category inputs are two-dimensional. Simulated signal/background components and post-fit overlays are distinct from these observed bins.

nodes.name: Neutron mass and ILL calibration constraint
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA uses dimensionless eta_d=2.90430245(49)e-3 to connect neutron mass, recoil and d220(ILL). Because neutron mass occurs in no other observational equation, this datum does not independently constrain the ILL lattice spacing.

nodes.name: CODATA selected light-ion ratio inputs
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA D15-D18 use 0.503776367670(17), 1.0070527379117(85), 0.9992316600030(43) and 1.0073102639050(200), respectively. Their observational equations retain ionic charge factors, molecular binding and shared mass references.

nodes.name: Unresolved ILL calibration input identity
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA 2018 and 2022 label E13 as ILL/W04 minus one, -20(22)e-9. The cited Kessler tables assign the negative -20(9)e-9 comparison to WS1/NW04 and report different ILL comparisons. The physical identity of E13 has not been reconciled.

nodes.name: Shared carbon ionization inputs
nodes.shortDescription: CODATA Table XXVI correlates the carbon ionization inputs D8/D23, D8/D24 and D23/D24 by 0.9968, 1.0000 and 0.9968. The D15 and D16 equations share the C6+ denominator.

nodes.name: CODATA capture and lattice constraints
nodes.shortDescription: Trace the dimensionless capture input and published lattice comparisons through their observational equations, without reproducing the full adjustment.

nodes.name: CODATA light-ion mass constraints
nodes.shortDescription: Use the selected 2022 adjustment input ratios and observational equations, with explicit shared ionic references and theoretical binding inputs.

nodes.name: Conditional colloid crystal-fluid interface free energy
nodes.shortDescription: The source PMMA nuclei have ordered cores, disordered rough exteriors and a diffuse crystal-fluid interface. Using the small-subcritical-nucleus area fit with ellipsoidal areas, the source reports effective gamma approximately0.027*kB*T/a^2 across its samples; the Figure5 example at volume fraction0.445 gives0.026*kB*T/a^2. These are a general approximate summary and a specified sample fit, not competing independent measurements or a universal hard-sphere constant.

nodes.name: Scoped colloid pair interactions and evolving crystal-fluid interfaces
nodes.shortDescription: A dilute charged-sphere experiment supports a conditional screened repulsive isolated-pair potential. A separate concentrated PMMA experiment follows post-shear crystal nuclei and infers a rough crystal-fluid interfacial free energy under stated classification and statistical assumptions. These finite cases retain real colloidal interactions, kinetic structural evolution and interfaces without a universal stability, sharp-boundary, precursor-chain or supramolecular-growth theorem.

nodes.name: Preparation- and time-specific colloid stability and interface boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Specify the dispersed material, continuous medium, interaction model, preparation and observation time when describing colloid stability or an interface. Persistence over an observation window, a thermodynamic phase preference and a kinetic barrier to a particular change are different propositions. For the source spherical-crystallite approximation, DeltaG(r)=4*pi*r^2*gamma-(4*pi/3)*r^3*n*DeltaMu, where gamma is crystal-liquid interfacial free energy per area, n is crystallite particle-number density and DeltaMu is liquid-minus-solid chemical potential. The positive surface cost competes with a bulk growth term when DeltaMu>0.

nodes.name: Post-shear colloidal nucleus growth and critical range
nodes.shortDescription: In the source post-shear PMMA suspension, finite subcritical nuclei frequently shrink and larger nuclei can grow. For volume fraction0.47 the growth-minus-shrink probability changes sign across60<M<160 particles, giving a preparation- and classifier-dependent critical range. The source rc approximately6.2*a is a spherical-equivalent interpretation. Snapshots at volume fraction0.45 span20,43,66 and89 minutes after shear melting, illustrating finite kinetic evolution rather than permanent interface stabilization.

nodes.name: Conditional isolated-colloid screened pair repulsion
nodes.shortDescription: The source isolated-pair transition-matrix analysis reports a screened repulsive potential fitted with Zeff=1991+/-150 elementary-charge units and screening length kappa^-1=161+/-10 nm. It finds no statistically significant long-range attraction in its resolved preparation and separation range. These are conditional parameters and a finite negative bound, not the fully dissociated surface charge or an all-colloid exclusion of attraction.

nodes.name: Confinement criteria and their domains
nodes.shortDescription: Confinement is specified relative to a theory and observable. In an unscreened pure-gauge theory, asymptotic fundamental Wilson-loop area behavior defines a static string-tension criterion. With dynamical quarks, the reviewed Euclidean static-source spectra instead include mixing and screening by color-singlet meson pairs. The QCD interpretation of hadronic final states is a separate phenomenological statement, not an equivalent finite-loop test or a proof that separation energy grows without bound.

nodes.name: Hadronic evidence and confinement limits
nodes.shortDescription: The calibrated Durr light-hadron spectrum, TASSO charged-track jet interpretation and SLD reconstructed neutral-hadron yields are consistent with their stated QCD/hadronic descriptions. They test selected masses, event shapes and decay-reconstructed production observables under distinct assumptions. Together they delimit the phenomenological use of confinement; they do not form a single all-channel exclusion of free color or a derivation of nuclear and atomic stability.

nodes.name: Conjugation and criterion-specific aromaticity distinction
nodes.shortDescription: Conjugation describes specified orbital coupling across a molecular framework, including p-orbital interaction across an intervening sigma bond and qualifying lone-pair interactions. It can occur in linear systems such as butadiene. Aromaticity requires a stated cyclic-system criterion; a reference-defined energetic comparison, geometry descriptor and magnetic-response probe answer different questions. Cyclic connectivity, six active electrons or a delocalized representation alone are not a universal aromaticity classification.

nodes.name: Q1243+307 absorption observation context
nodes.shortDescription: Cooke and colleagues combine new and archived Keck HIRES observations of the low-metallicity absorber at z_abs=2.52564 toward Q1243+307. Echelle reduction and response characterization precede a joint analysis of three data sets. Eight neutral-deuterium Lyman-series lines and neutral-hydrogen absorption constrain the later column-density fit.

nodes.name: Selected neutral-deuterium absorption profiles
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Q1243+307 spectra contain eight D I absorption lines used together with H I absorption in the source analysis. These wavelength-dependent spectra are the measured input to the column-density model; they do not directly report a primordial abundance or observe BBN.

nodes.name: Absorption response and column-density inference
nodes.shortDescription: The alis chi-square model fits the three spectra jointly with absorption-component structure, continuum, zero level, relative velocities, instrumental response and blends. A common N(D I)/N(H I) is imposed across the selected components. The column ratio is then identified with elemental D/H under the explicitly stated ionization assumption.

nodes.name: Model-conditioned deuterium column ratio
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected z_abs=2.52564 absorber, the joint absorption-profile analysis reports log10[N(D I)/N(H I)]=-4.622 +/- 0.015. The source treats N(D I)/N(H I)=D/H under its ionization approximation. Quoted intervals are 68 percent confidence unless stated otherwise.

nodes.name: Seven-absorber primordial deuterium inference
nodes.shortDescription: The published precision sample combines the reanalyzed Q1243+307 system with six previously analyzed systems under a common analysis procedure. A weighted logarithmic mean and an intrinsic-scatter likelihood estimate the selected sample abundance, interpreted as primordial D/H. The same paper then uses a chosen BBN rate prescription for a separate baryon-density interpretation.

nodes.name: Seven-system primordial deuterium estimate
