nodes.shortDescription: The selected seven-system analysis reports log10(D/H)_P=-4.5974 +/- 0.0052, equivalently (D/H)_P=(2.527 +/- 0.030)*10^-5, at the reported 68 percent confidence level. The logarithmic and linear forms describe one pooled estimate, not independent measurements.

nodes.name: Dominant-mode stochastic classical approximation
nodes.shortDescription: In the reviewed large-squeezing, dominant-mode regime, neglect the subleading decaying solution and choose a time-independent phase so the retained f_k is real. The field can then be represented as y(k,eta) approximately f_k(eta)e(k), with time-independent Gaussian e, <e(k)e*(k')>=delta^3(k-k') and e(-k)=e*(k). Where |f_k|>0, with F=Im(conj(f_k) g_k) and g_k=i[f_k'-(a'/a)f_k], the limiting phase-space distribution is concentrated near p=(F/|f_k|^2)y. Random amplitudes then follow the specified classical mode evolution; this stronger approximation requires more than the equal-time Gaussian marginal.

nodes.name: Leading nonrelativistic Coulomb potential
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected leading nonrelativistic QED scattering-to-potential comparison, equal-sign charges of magnitude e give U(r)=+e^2/(4*pi*r), and opposite-sign charges give U(r)=-e^2/(4*pi*r), for r>0 in rationalized hbar=c=1 units. Feynman separately formulates an instantaneous Coulomb pair interaction and its relativistic perturbative extension; that amplitude is a model construction, not a detected population of exchanged photons.

nodes.name: Simultaneous coupled-ion frequency readout
nodes.shortDescription: Two ions in coupled magnetron orbits can share a simultaneous phase readout, but obtaining the free cyclotron ratio still requires the trap and interaction model.

nodes.name: Creutz conditional lattice scaling comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The fitted area coefficients show a crossover near beta=2 and a decrease compatible with the leading SU(2) asymptotic-freedom slope under fixed-string-tension renormalization. This is evidence within the finite pure-gauge model.

nodes.name: Creutz conditional string-tension fit
nodes.shortDescription: A constant-plus-perimeter-plus-area fit to finite square loops yields a dimensionless coefficient interpreted as a^2 K. Strong-coupling points require reduced fit assumptions, and above beta=2.5 the area contribution is not accurately resolved.

nodes.name: Creutz simulated square-loop expectations
nodes.shortDescription: The study reports square Wilson-loop expectations across bare couplings and lattice sizes. At beta=3, loops through side five appear stable against the tested size increase to 10^4 sites; larger loops show stronger finite-size effects.

nodes.name: Creutz pure SU(2) computational context
nodes.shortDescription: Pure SU(2) Wilson gauge fields without dynamical quarks on four-dimensional periodic Euclidean hypercubic lattices. Local heat-bath updates sample Z=integral dU exp(-beta S), S=sum[1-one half Tr U_plaquette], beta=4/e0^2. Runs compare random and ordered starts and lattice sizes up to 10^4 sites.

nodes.name: Crocker-Grier isolated-pair release context
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare the source dilute aqueous polystyrene-sulfate spheres of radius326 nm, monodisperse within1%, in a glass cell with3-4 micrometre gap, ion-exchange reservoirs and argon flushing to limit ionic contamination. Trap two isolated spheres initially1.5 or1.7 micrometres apart with dual optical tweezers, release when no other particles are nearby, and record796 pair trajectories. Use the source relative-coordinate projection,57 nm bins and a transition-time interval1/30 s; the source pools6502 initial/final separation samples to estimate a transition matrix.

nodes.name: Scoped spatial ordering and structural-transition evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The selected primary diffraction study supports finite icosahedral Al-Mn order that is not explained as a conventional periodic Bravais crystal or its multiple twins, together with protocol-dependent metastability. A separate periodic-box hard-disk study supplies a positive, purely entropic model of collective spatial ordering, first-order liquid-hexatic coexistence and a continuous hexatic-solid transition. These bounded cases support structural ordering and transition distinctions without a universal periodic-lattice requirement, universal critical behavior or a necessary ionic/dispersion/dipole precursor chain.

nodes.name: Conditional corrected Cs133 hyperfine coupling inference
nodes.shortDescription: The2024 published TableI and the actual2024 erratum report Cs1337d2D3/2 hyperfine coupling constants A=7.3547(8) MHz, B=-0.017(7) MHz and C=-0.3(4) kHz. A labels magnetic-dipole, B electric-quadrupole and C magnetic-octupole coupling in the selected state convention. C is consistent with zero at the printed uncertainty; the result does not resolve a precise nuclear magnetic octupole moment.

nodes.name: Corrected Cs1337d3/2 hyperfine spectral intervals
nodes.shortDescription: For Cs1337d2D3/2 excitation from6s1/2 F=3, the2024 erratum reports adjacent positive hyperfine intervals Fprime5-to4=36.760(9) MHz, Fprime4-to3=29.427(5) MHz and Fprime3-to2=22.073(5) MHz. The separate ground-F=4 column gives36.760(10),29.427(5) and22.071(5) MHz. These are source-reported corrected excited-state interval inferences from the optical spectra, with the source parenthesized uncertainties retained.

nodes.name: Specified-channel decay energy threshold
nodes.shortDescription: For an isolated particle at rest and declared asymptotically free final particles with positive on-shell energies, energy conservation requires initial rest energy at least the sum of final rest energies. A negative Q=(M-sum(mi))*c^2 excludes that final state; a nonnegative Q alone supplies no decay amplitude or lifetime.

nodes.name: Conditional heavy-field decoupling
nodes.shortDescription: For light-particle processes below the heavy production thresholds, a consistently matched EFT can omit the heavy field as an explicit low-energy degree of freedom while retaining its virtual effects in local coefficients and renormalized light parameters. In a controlled expansion with light scales E much smaller than M and non-growing dimensionless matching coefficients, higher-dimensional contributions are suppressed by powers of E/M. This conditional suppression does not erase heavy-field effects in the relevant or marginal sector.

nodes.name: Detmold heavy-mass state-identification analysis
nodes.shortDescription: The reported calculation uses a 24^3 x 48 lattice, a=0.145 fm, three degenerate clover flavors and a tree-level-improved Luscher-Weisz gauge action at pion mass approximately 800 MeV. It analyzes 16,368 configurations from 17 streams, bins 50 saved configurations for residual autocorrelation, and computes approximately 2.12 x 10^7 sparse-source propagators. A subset of gauge fields was also used in Beane2013. Zero-total-momentum dibaryon and local hexaquark operators probe I=1 A1+ and I=0 T1+ sectors. The source compares GEVP, symmetric/block Lanczos and asymmetric-correlator analyses of these related correlators.

nodes.name: Bare-deuteron energy calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Specify ground-state bare d -> free p+p+e-+electron-antineutrino, adopt the Rau joint adjusted proton/deuteron pair and CODATA 2018 electron and unit inputs, and evaluate the rest-energy excess with zero neutrino mass as the most permissive threshold.

nodes.name: Negative bare-deuteron beta-breakup energy
nodes.shortDescription: For the declared bare-deuteron channel, the local calculation gives Q0=(md-2mp-me)*c^2=-1.44223 MeV approximately. The printed-input rounding box remains negative, excluding this spontaneous final state under the stated kinematic conditions; the capture-derived neutron route cancels the shared binding input.

nodes.name: Mass-spectrometry input to capture inference
nodes.shortDescription: The printed 1994 atomic masses give D-H=1.0062767463 u. Kessler adopts Ar(2H)-Ar(1H)=1.00627674630(71) from that source for the neutron-mass calculation; its uncertainty is retained as an adopted input, not a reproduced covariance result.

nodes.name: CO+/N2+ drift-fit example
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 1 reports CO+/N2+ mass ratio 0.99959888760(8) from alternating frequency measurements with a sixth-order polynomial and robust estimation. This is an example within the twenty-comparison analysis.

nodes.name: 1994 fitted hydrogen-isotope masses
nodes.shortDescription: Table I reports neutral-atom masses H 1.0078250316(5) u and D 2.0141017779(5) u from the global fit after chemical and ionization corrections. Their covariance matters when forming D-H.

nodes.name: MIT twenty-comparison atomic-mass fit
nodes.shortDescription: Twenty pairwise comparisons use alternately trapped single ions in an 8.5 T field, axial rf SQUID detection and coupled radial-to-axial phase readout. Robust polynomial fits handle field drift. Corrected molecular-ion comparisons determine a global neutral-atom mass table with carbon-12 as reference.

nodes.name: Reconstructed dilepton invariant mass
nodes.shortDescription: Define the pair invariant mass by Mll^2 = (p_lplus+p_lminus)^2 for the assigned reconstructed lepton four-momenta, in c=1 units and the (+,-,-,-) metric. In the negligible daughter-mass limit this becomes 2 E1 E2 (1-cos(theta12)), where theta12 is the full three-dimensional opening angle. Detector calibration and any response or recoil constraint used to infer the four-momenta remain inputs.

nodes.name: Equilibrium dilute-electrolyte screened-potential model
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the selected equilibrium continuum-solvent ion-atmosphere model in its original electrostatic-cgs units. Let n_i be bulk ion-species number density, z_i signed valence, D the dimensionless solvent dielectric constant, kT thermal energy and e the positive charge magnitude. For electroneutral bulk sum_i(n_i*z_i)=0, the Boltzmann density n_i(r)=n_i*exp[-z_i*e*psi(r)/(kT)] gives, after weak-potential linearization, nabla^2*psi=kappa^2*psi outside the tagged source, with kappa^2=4*pi*e^2*sum_i(n_i*z_i^2)/(D*kT). In the dilute point-ion limiting model the tagged-charge mean potential is psi(r)=q*exp(-kappa*r)/(D*r). The screening length 1/kappa depends on composition, temperature and solvent response; it represents statistical ion-atmosphere structure rather than an ion-formation event.

nodes.name: Molecular orientation, alignment and dielectric boundary
nodes.shortDescription:
A coarse-grained molecular polarization P=n*

is a vector moment per unit volume, with SI units C/m^2. For a specified isotropic linear quasistatic medium, P=epsilon0*chi_e*E_macro and epsilon_r=1+chi_e. The replacement E_local=E_macro and chi_e=n*alpha/epsilon0 require a dilute independent-dipole approximation. The even alignment statistic has isotropic value 1/3 and does not determine the odd orientation statistic or a nonzero P.

nodes.name: Directional excitation interpretation boundary
nodes.shortDescription: A directional excitation claim must distinguish dispersion and envelope velocity, damping or attenuation, a localization criterion and intrinsic decay lifetime. They are different observables and require a specified model, state, environment, frame, held-fixed controls and directional comparison. The supplied free scalar propagation and photon polarization definitions establish no anisotropic environment or unequal directional persistence. No measured directional stability, localized transport bias or Level-0-to-field mechanism is admitted.

nodes.name: Dispersion, material response and measured-observable boundary
nodes.shortDescription: In this scope dispersion names the ground-state electric-response correlation contribution in the declared model. It is distinct from orientational interactions of supplied permanent dipoles and induction by an applied or static field, neither of which is estimated here. An atom-surface phase comparison additionally requires the particular material, channel geometry, atomic velocity and response model. A nonzero relative fringe phase can support an interaction model; it is not a direct measurement of microscopic fluctuating dipoles, a reconstructed dielectric function, a universal cohesion law or an isolated absolute vacuum energy.

nodes.name: Scoped ground-state dispersion and atom-surface evidence
nodes.shortDescription: A specified lowest-state electric-response model yields attractive nonretarded and retarded interaction-energy limits with distinct atom-pair and ideal atom-wall distance powers. A separate Na/silicon-nitride interferometer reports an arm-dependent relative phase and a conditional comparison with an adopted attractive nonretarded potential. These provide finite positive dispersion-related theory and interaction-sensitive evidence, with material, geometry, state and uncertainty limits retained. They do not directly observe transient dipoles or establish universal condensed-matter organization.

nodes.name: Fe-gluconate fitted spectral and relative vibrational response
nodes.shortDescription: The three-doublet analysis yields finite widths and distinct center shifts and quadrupole splittings under the stated spectral model. At 295 K its normalized area quantities a1,a2,a3 are 0.49,0.46,0.52 relative to 78 K. The model-derived effective Debye temperatures differ: Table 2 reports 377(9) K from CS1 and 204(4) K from a1. These results illustrate finite-temperature spectral and vibrational sensitivity, with fitted hyperfine/electronic-environment interpretation, rather than a natural-width measurement or absolute recoilless probability.

nodes.name: Finite-temperature Fe-57 transmission in amorphous Fe-gluconate
nodes.shortDescription: The selected dried Fe-gluconate specimen has a broad XRD pattern classified as amorphous, in contrast with the crystalline hydrated parent specimen. Fe-57 velocity-dependent transmission spectra show resonant attenuation at finite absorber temperatures across the reported 78-295 K study; Figure 2 displays 78 K and 268 K examples. This is a positive bound-solid Mossbauer case whose absorber is not reported to possess perfect periodic crystal order.

nodes.name: Amorphous Fe-gluconate diffraction and Fe-57 transmission context
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare the Fe-gluconate specimen by dissolving a crystalline sample in distilled water and drying at 50 degrees C in air; characterize the dried sample by Cu K-alpha X-ray diffraction. Record Fe-57 transmission spectra with a constant-acceleration drive and 1024 analyzer channels, using a room-temperature Co-57/Rh source supplying 14.4 keV gamma rays. The powdered absorber, reported as about 10 mg Fe per cm^2, is held between 78 and 295 K with reported temperature stability within plus/minus 0.1 K. Retain the source distinction between measured transmission and the subsequent thin-absorber spectral/model analysis.

nodes.name: Calibrated light-hadron mass spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: After the declared mass/scale inputs and correlated physical-mass, finite-volume and continuum treatment, the paper reports light-hadron masses compatible with its experimental comparison. The isospin-symmetric nucleon mass is 0.936 +/- 0.025 (statistical) +/- 0.022 (systematic) GeV with Xi normalization, or 0.953 +/- 0.029 +/- 0.019 GeV with Omega normalization, compared with 0.939 GeV. Table 1 entries below use GeV and statistical then systematic parentheses on the last digits: rho: comparison 0.775; Xi set 0.775(29)(13); Omega set 0.778(30)(33). K*: comparison 0.894; Xi set 0.906(14)(4); Omega set 0.907(15)(8). N: comparison 0.939; Xi set 0.936(25)(22); Omega set 0.953(29)(19). Lambda: comparison 1.116; Xi set 1.114(15)(5); Omega set 1.103(23)(10). Sigma: comparison 1.191; Xi set 1.169(18)(15); Omega set 1.157(25)(15). Xi: comparison 1.318; Xi set 1.318 (input); Omega set 1.317(16)(13). Delta: comparison 1.232; Xi set 1.248(97)(61); Omega set 1.234(82)(81). Sigma*: comparison 1.385; Xi set 1.427(46)(35); Omega set 1.404(38)(27). Xi*: comparison 1.533; Xi set 1.565(26)(15); Omega set 1.561(15)(15). Omega: comparison 1.672; Xi set 1.676(20)(15); Omega set 1.672 (input).

nodes.name: Finite-lattice hadron energy fits
nodes.shortDescription: Euclidean hadronic correlators yield effective-mass diagnostics and correlated single-mass fits across the reported bare parameters, volumes and fit windows. Gaussian source/sink profiles reduce the visible excited-state contamination in the illustrated pion and nucleon channels.

nodes.name: Unresolved lightest rho and Delta resonance masses
nodes.shortDescription: For rho and Delta at the lightest pion-mass point near a=0.085 fm, the lowest finite-volume energy is dominated by a two-particle state and depends too weakly on the resonance mass for a reliable extraction. Those two channel/point combinations are omitted from the resonance-mass analysis.

nodes.name: Two-plus-one-flavor light-hadron simulation
nodes.shortDescription: Two-plus-one-flavor SU(3) lattice QCD with degenerate up/down masses and a strange quark, without QED or isospin breaking. Tree-level Symanzik gauge and clover-improved Wilson fermion actions use six stout-link averaging levels. Three gauge couplings beta=3.3, 3.57 and 3.7 give spacings about 0.125, 0.085 and 0.065 fm; simulated pion masses reach 190 MeV.

nodes.name: Decay-channel population model versus beam loss
nodes.shortDescription: For the source constant-rate fit in one consistent time frame, parent disappearance obeys N_Pr(t)=N_Pr(0)*exp(-lambda_all*t), with lambda_all=lambda_EC+lambda_betaPlus+lambda_loss. Stable EC-daughter growth obeys N_Ce(t)=N_Pr(0)*lambda_EC/(lambda_all-lambda_loss)*[exp(-lambda_loss*t)-exp(-lambda_all*t)]+N_Ce(0)*exp(-lambda_loss*t). Loss includes residual-gas collisions and electron pickup in the cooler; it is not nuclear decay. The source Table I rates are in the ion rest frame, while Figure 2 times are laboratory times: for a constant Lorentz factor gamma, t_lab=gamma*t_rest and lambda_rest=gamma*lambda_lab.

nodes.name: Scoped effective-description construction
nodes.shortDescription: An effective description declares its retained fields, symmetries, operator basis, hierarchy of scales and target observables. Wilsonian elimination of short-distance modes, renormalized-parameter running with mu and the hard scale of a measurement are distinct operations or variables. Matching coefficients and boundary conditions are additional inputs to an RG equation. Approximate low-energy agreement retains heavy-field effects in parameters and higher operators; it does not remove microscopic causes or establish a physical-time process.

nodes.name: Scoped local effective-operator expansion
nodes.shortDescription: For specified light fields and realized Lorentz/internal symmetries in four spacetime dimensions, choose a local operator basis and write L_EFT=L_(d<=4)+sum_(d>4,i) C_i^(d)(mu) O_i^(d)/M^(d-4). Here d is operator mass dimension, M is the heavy scale and the displayed C_i are dimensionless. At light scales E and masses small compared with M, a declared perturbative power counting orders amplitudes in E/M and couplings. With bounded coefficients and controlled loop/logarithmic corrections, finitely many operators contribute at a chosen order.

nodes.name: Scoped atomic, molecular and optical evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed literature reports microwave-quenching resonances and an approximate level separation in metastable hydrogen, a corrected trapped-HD+ mass with a dependent molecular mass-closure comparison, and specimen-specific infrared reflectance and transmittance for window materials and an Au mirror. These supply distinct atomic, molecular and bulk optical constraints. They provide no common quantitative measurement of cross-scale formation, universal material stability or electromagnetic-only organization.

nodes.name: Electromagnetic material interpretation boundary
nodes.shortDescription: A scoped electromagnetic material regime comprises a declared charged-matter interaction model together with specified atomic, molecular or bulk preparations and their separate observables. Recurring use of the interaction framework does not itself identify a physical emergence stage. In the selected electroweak lepton model, the massless photon combination and e=g*g_prime/sqrt(g^2+g_prime^2) are conditional field and coupling definitions.

nodes.name: Free electromagnetic photon field
nodes.shortDescription: In Minkowski spacetime with hbar=c=1 and metric (+---), adopt the source-free Maxwell action S=-(1/4)integral d^4x F_mu_nu F^mu_nu, with F_mu_nu=partial_mu A_nu-partial_nu A_mu and A_mu identified with A_mu+partial_mu lambda under the stated boundary conditions. In this unbroken Abelian U(1) electromagnetic model there is no mass term. A constant gauge parameter leaves A_mu unchanged, giving its neutral transformation law in this model rather than a measured zero-charge result.

nodes.name: Electron anomaly conversion and finite arithmetic findings
nodes.shortDescription: The reported g/2 gives a_e=0.00115965218059 with the same absolute 1.3e-13 uncertainty. The six Table I components have square-sum 1.8102 and RSS 1.3454367 in 10^-13 units, compatible with the printed total 1.3 under display rounding. Synthetic frequency witnesses distinguish common-field cancellation from anomaly-scaled nonsimultaneous-field bias; the leading formula is evaluated only as supplied algebra.

nodes.name: Ideal electron anomaly/cyclotron frequency ratio
nodes.shortDescription: For common B, nu_c=e*B/(2*pi*m), nu_s=(g/2)*nu_c and nu_a=nu_s-nu_c, hence g/2=1+nu_a/nu_c. The free cyclotron frequency is distinct from measured trap-modified line centers; Fan uses the invariance relation and its controlled expansion before adding the cavity shift.

nodes.name: Signed electron moment, Bohr normalization and anomaly
nodes.shortDescription: For electron charge -e with e>0, mu_B=e*hbar/(2m)>0 and the spin operator relation is mu_vector=-g*mu_B*S_vector/hbar. Define a_e=g/2-1; the reported positive moment magnitude ratio is -mu/mu_B=g/2, with the signed spin projection kept explicit.

nodes.name: Finite electron-moment algebra procedure
nodes.shortDescription: Evaluate exact g/2-to-anomaly and signed-spin conversions, a synthetic common-field cancellation and nonsimultaneous-field counterexample, a supplied leading-formula substitution, and display-resolution compatibility of Table I quadrature.

nodes.name: Electronic-state sensitivity within a declared nuclear EC channel
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed primary experiment supports a finite electronic-state sensitivity of one nuclear channel: fitted orbital EC of stored H-like 140Pr58+ is faster than He-like 140Pr57+, while the measured beta+ partial rates agree within their reported errors. The Schottky acquisition, loss-corrected nuclear-rate inference and conditional hyperfine explanation remain separate roles within the same publication. This positive case constrains an occupancy-only story and does not extend to every nuclear decay or ordinary chemical environment.

nodes.name: Synthetic mass matrix and free-coupling identities
nodes.shortDescription: All three synthetic U(1) cases have the stated radial curvature and vector mass term. All three Weinberg matrices have zero determinant, the declared photon null direction and positive massive eigenvalue; the charged/neutral and electric-charge identities hold, while doubling the free electron coupling doubles its mass.

nodes.name: Synthetic scalar and gauge mass calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Choose three positive rational U(1) toy potentials V(rho)=kappa*(rho-a^2)^2/4, separately choose three Weinberg background/gauge/Yukawa tuples, and check the declared Hessian and quadratic identities exactly. None of these parameter choices is an experimental input.

nodes.name: Exponential ensemble survival
nodes.shortDescription: For a constant effective loss rate lambda, the modeled surviving population is N(t)=N(0)*exp(-lambda*t), with mean lifetime tau=1/lambda. Initial-population normalization and background corrections are separate measurement inputs.

nodes.name: External scattering-state boundary
nodes.shortDescription: External states specify the initial and final boundary of the scattering calculation. In the stated free plane-wave convention external electron momenta satisfy p^2=m^2, while external photons and source normalization require their own prescribed state factors. This definition does not assert general nonperturbative asymptotic completeness.

nodes.name: Reported cavity-mode frequency and quality-factor calibration
nodes.shortDescription: The three distinct calibration methods report mutually consistent mode information; the moment correction uses measured frequencies and Q values for 72 observed cavity modes. No complete 72-row numerical calibration table is bound here.

nodes.name: Distinct cavity-mode calibration preparations
nodes.shortDescription: Determine cavity mode frequencies and Q values through parametrically pumped electrons, one-electron first-excited-state lifetimes and high-excitation electron decay; retain these calibration preparations separately from the precision jump trials.

nodes.name: Calibration-conditioned cavity correction
nodes.shortDescription: The reported renormalized cavity calculation replaces ideal contributions for 72 modes with contributions using measured frequencies and Q values, and gives different Delta_g_cav/2 corrections at eleven magnetic fields as shown in Figure 4.

nodes.name: Fan 2022 electron moment in Bohr magnetons
nodes.shortDescription: The eleven-field corrected inference reports -mu/mu_B=g/2=1.00115965218059(13), with one-standard-deviation absolute uncertainty 1.3e-13 (about 0.13 ppt relative). The reported quantity is g/2; g and its absolute uncertainty are twice those values. This is the 2022 Northwestern determination published in 2023 and is not combined with the 2008 determination.

nodes.name: Conditional line-fit frequency estimates
nodes.shortDescription: The original thermal/Gaussian line analysis extracts f_bar_c and nu_bar_a and uses the axial-frequency measurement for Equation 5. Figure 3 illustrates the fits, while the rounded frequency scales do not supply all unrounded eleven-field estimates.

nodes.name: Single-electron measured transition and axial lines
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 3 reports cyclotron and anomaly transition-probability line shapes from alternating quantum-jump trials and an axial Johnson-noise dip. These measured responses precede the separate fitted-frequency record; they are not numerical free-frequency triples.

nodes.name: Line fitting, trap/cavity correction and moment inference
nodes.shortDescription: Fit thermal cyclotron line shapes convolved with Gaussian broadening and the nearly symmetric anomaly lines to extract f_bar_c and nu_bar_a; use the measured axial frequency, Equation 5 trap/relativistic terms, calibrated cavity-shift calculation and an eleven-field weighted combination.

nodes.name: Single-electron cryogenic Penning preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare one electron in a cryogenic cylindrical Penning trap, alternate cyclotron and anomaly quantum-jump trials, and observe spin/cyclotron state changes through axial-frequency shifts; record the axial noise dip separately.

nodes.name: Spontaneous polarization and demonstrated switching distinction
nodes.shortDescription: Distinguish a symmetry-allowed piezoelectric coupling, a spontaneous polarization state and demonstrated electric-field switching between stable polarization orientations. For the selected operational ferroelectric classification, the applied field must reversibly change the polarization state within the available breakdown and preparation window. A polarization-electric-field hysteresis loop alone is insufficient: integrated current can contain dielectric charging, conduction, charge injection and electret contributions. Retain stated non-switching controls and independent polarity-sensitive observations.

nodes.name: Fichtner AlScN prepared-capacitor switching context
nodes.shortDescription: Use reactive-sputtered c-axis-oriented polycrystalline Al1-xScxN on oxidized Si with an AlN/Pt bottom electrode and patterned Pt top electrodes. The source series uses x=0.27 with400 nm thickness, x=0.32,0.36,0.40 with600 nm, and x=0.43 with1 micrometre. Acquire bipolar current loops at711 Hz and non-switching unipolar controls at711 and411 Hz for the modified leakage correction. The selected x=0.36 direct transverse response uses4-point bending and16 mm^2 electrodes; polarization reversal uses a0.1 Hz unipolar sine waveform reaching-200 V over60 s. Separate switched/as-deposited regions from that wafer undergo electrode removal with50 nm overetch and polarity-selective wet etching. Use the stated2 ms pulse sequence with short-circuited retention intervals for the finite switching/non-switching comparison.

nodes.name: Field anisotropy interpretation boundary
nodes.shortDescription: A field-anisotropy assertion must identify a model, state or preparation, directional comparison, observable and transformation of the setup. Propagation, coupling, localization and response are different possible questions, not one interchangeable observable. The supplied free real scalar dispersion is an isotropic comparison within its assumptions; no anisotropic field regime, intrinsic vacuum axis or universal directional-admissibility law is admitted.

nodes.name: Stationary vacuum and unequal-time mode algebra
nodes.shortDescription: The ten declared mode maps preserve the formal canonical commutator, oscillator Hamiltonian and vacuum covariance; their derivatives satisfy the declared oscillator generator. Fifty composition and common-time-shift checks pass. For omega=2 and phase (3/5,4/5), <q(t)q(0)>=3/20-i/5 while <q(0)^2>=1/4 and [q(t),q(0)]=-2i/5. The adopted vacuum has <N>=0, <H>=1 and Var(H)=0. A squeeze preserves the commutator but changes the Hamiltonian and covariance; bare half-amplitude attenuation changes its commutator factor to 1/4.

nodes.name: Finite free-mode evolution preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt one free oscillator with unit mass, hbar=c=1, H=(p^2+omega^2*q^2)/2=omega*(N+1/2), [q,p]=i and a|0>=0. Check the coefficient map q(t)=c*q+s*p/omega, p(t)=-omega*s*q+c*p at omega=2 and 3/2 and phases (1,0),(0,1),(-1,0),(3/5,4/5),(-5/13,12/13). Use exact rational arithmetic and untruncated finite ladder words for vacuum moments.

nodes.name: Resonance inference from finite-volume energies
nodes.shortDescription: An elastic scattering model relates discrete finite-volume energies to an infinite-volume resonance mass and coupling. Mixing with two-particle states changes the relation between the lowest measured lattice energy and the resonance mass.

nodes.name: FSU corrected deuteron/proton ratio
nodes.shortDescription: Fink/Myers reports R=nu_c(H2+)/nu_c(D+)=m_D/m_H2(v=0,N=0)=0.999231660004(7)(7)(16)(19). Electron and molecular binding corrections give m_d/m_p=1.999007501274(38).

nodes.name: FSU ratio with adopted proton mass
nodes.shortDescription: Combining the FSU ratio with the Heiße 2019 proton mass gives m_d=2.013553212586(76) u. This absolute mass is conditional on the same proton input used in the LIONTRAP comparisons.

nodes.name: FSU H2+ and deuteron ratio
nodes.shortDescription: Store H2+ and D+ together in an 8.5 T trap, alternate the measured central ion, select seven ions with inferred vibrational v=0, and apply modeled rotational and instrumental corrections to 33 selected runs.

nodes.name: Conditional deuteron/proton mass ratio
nodes.shortDescription: Using the adopted state branch and H2+ binding correction, Fink/Myers reports m_d/m_p=1.999007501272(9). The two alternative state branches lower this result by 2.7 or 3.6 quoted standard uncertainties.

nodes.name: FSU drive and thermal controls
nodes.shortDescription: Vary drive time within a molecular state, extrapolate versus squared drive time, and estimate residual thermal imbalance from phase noise.

nodes.name: Driven and thermal frequency corrections
nodes.shortDescription: The 5 ms ratio receives a 29.5(1.4)e-12 driven-motion correction and a separate 2.9(2.9)e-12 thermal correction. The total reported systematic correction is 31.8(3.7)e-12.

nodes.name: State-conditional ground frequency ratio
nodes.shortDescription: For the adopted molecular-state branch, the corrected ratio is nu(H2+(0,0))/nu(D+)=0.9992316600030(21)(37)(43), with statistical, systematic and total uncertainties.

nodes.name: Proton mass inferred from direct deuteron input
nodes.shortDescription: Combining m_d/m_p=1.999007501272(9) with the direct Rau deuteron mass 2.013553212535(17) u gives the reported proton mass 1.007276466574(10) u.

nodes.name: Simultaneous FSU H2+/D+ acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare three H2+/D+ pairs in coupled magnetron orbits, cool each ion alternately, and measure both PnP phases simultaneously in the 8.5 T apparatus.

nodes.name: Three conditional molecular-state branches
nodes.shortDescription: The state analysis retains three R00(5 ms) branches: 0.9992316599712(21), 0.9992316599589(29) and 0.9992316599550(27). The highest branch is adopted conditionally; the other two remain possible.

nodes.name: FSU discrete molecular-state analysis
nodes.shortDescription: Group the same runs into eleven plateaus, fit allowed rovibrational assignments, and retain five uniquely assignable ratios within each of three branches.

nodes.name: Local fixed-point scaling classification
nodes.shortDescription: For the declared infrared flow F(g), a fixed point g_* satisfies F_i(g_*)=0. Near it, d(delta g_i)/d ell=B_ij delta g_j+O(delta g^2), where B_ij=partial F_i/partial g_j at g_*. For an admitted eigen-direction with real eigenvalue y_a, its linear scaling field obeys u_a(ell)=exp(y_a ell)u_a(0). A nonredundant local operator of full fixed-point scaling dimension Delta_a coupled homogeneously in d dimensions has y_a=d-Delta_a. With ell increasing toward the infrared, y_a>0 is relevant, y_a<0 irrelevant and y_a=0 linearly marginal.

nodes.name: Electric-charge residual modulo one
nodes.shortDescription: For a measured drop charge q=Q/e, define q_r=q-floor(q). The fractional residual tests departure from integer electric charge; q_c=q-nearest_integer(q) instead centers the individual integer peaks.

nodes.name: Free scalar Hamiltonian time evolution
nodes.shortDescription: For the specified free real scalar field, H=(1/2)*integral d^3x [pi^2+(grad phi)^2+m^2*phi^2] generates O_H(t)=exp(iHt)*O_S*exp(-iHt). With no explicit operator time dependence, dO_H/dt=i[H,O_H], so dphi/dt=pi and dpi/dt=(Laplacian-m^2)*phi. A positive-frequency mode evolves as a_p(t)=exp(-i*E_p*t)*a_p, E_p=sqrt(p^2+m^2)>0. These are evolution laws within an already specified quantum model.

nodes.name: Vacuum of a specified free field
nodes.shortDescription: In the chosen free-field Fock representation, a_p|0>=0 for every mode. The ground-state density operator is stationary under its time-independent Hamiltonian; the chosen number operator has expectation zero.

nodes.name: Free scalar envelope propagation
nodes.shortDescription: For the chosen free real scalar field in infinite homogeneous flat space, use hbar=c=1, m>0 and no material, external or boundary axis. The positive-frequency branch has E(k)=sqrt(k dot k+m^2). For an envelope narrowly concentrated around k0!=0, first-order dispersion and stationary phase give v_g(k0)=grad_k E|k0=k0/E(k0). A proper rotation R satisfies R^T R=I and det(R)=+1, giving v_g(Rk)=R v_g(k) and equal speed at fixed |k| and mass. E(-k)=E(k), while v_g(-k)=-v_g(k). Each free mode has |exp(-i E(k)t)|=1, and [N,H]=0 preserves the specified free Fock number sector. These are formal properties of this model, not an observed directional stability asymmetry.

nodes.name: Free real scalar field quantization
nodes.shortDescription: For the free real Klein-Gordon field, canonical commutators and a chosen vacuum define a Fock representation. Creation operators construct spin-zero bosonic states with E squared = p squared + m squared in natural units.

nodes.name: Neutron/mercury precession-magnitude ratio
nodes.shortDescription: In a common homogeneous static field, the positive neutron and 199Hg atomic precession-frequency ratio f_n/f_Hg equals |gamma_n|/|gamma_Hg|. Recovering that ratio from this experiment requires its stated field-sampling and frequency-shift corrections; the positive ratio alone carries no sign information.

nodes.name: Fundamental color-singlet tensor
nodes.shortDescription: For three fundamental SU(3) color indices, the normalized antisymmetric tensor epsilon_abc/sqrt(6) is invariant because U_ai*U_bj*U_ck*epsilon_ijk=det(U)*epsilon_abc and det(U)=1. A nontrivial center element acts as z or z^2 on one or two fundamental factors, excluding a singlet there. Three is therefore a restricted representation-theoretic minimum, not a measured particle population or sufficient formation condition.

nodes.name: Gaissmaier sodium bulk-energy calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the source PAW/VASP ground-state electronic calculation for supplied periodic Na bulk structures. The principal functional is PBE-GGA; BEEF-vdW provides a separate functional/ensemble comparison. The reported bulk settings include a 340 eV plane-wave cutoff, 0.15 inverse-Angstrom k-point mesh density, 0.2 eV Methfessel-Paxton smearing and a 1e-5 eV electronic convergence criterion. Uniformly expand/compress each unit cell and fit the stabilized-jellium equation of state to obtain an equilibrium and bulk modulus. Compare bulk energy per atom with an isolated neutral atom under the stated cohesive-energy convention.

nodes.name: Reported Na bcc cohesion and static equilibrium
nodes.shortDescription: For the supplied Na bcc branch, Table 1 reports PBE a0=4.19 Angstrom, E_coh=1.09 eV/atom and B0=7.96 GPa; BEEF-vdW gives a0=4.18 Angstrom, E_coh=1.15 eV/atom and B0=8.48 GPa. The BEEF cohesive-energy parenthesis 0.25 eV/atom represents the source functional-ensemble standard deviation. These are source computational outputs, not independently measured constants.

nodes.name: Gasser post-shear colloidal crystallization context
nodes.shortDescription: Use source PMMA spheres sterically stabilized with poly-12-hydroxystearic acid, radius a=1.26 micrometres and polydispersity below5%, in density- and index-matched decahydronaphthalene/cyclohexylbromide. Rhodamine dye imparts a small charge, so these are nearly hard spheres rather than an exact hard-sphere model. Shear melt the50 microlitre sample by magnetically agitating an embedded wire; acquire a58 by55 by20 cubic-micrometre confocal volume containing about4000 particles, at least8 and typically15 particle diameters from treated walls. Classify local order from particle centers with approximately0.04 micrometre accuracy.

nodes.name: Gauge-field structure and static-source evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed pure-SU(2) Wilson-loop and local field-profile calculations and the two-flavor and two-plus-one-flavor SU(3) static-energy calculations support different, source-conditioned gauge-field observables. The local profile adds spatial information that a potential fit alone does not determine; dynamical-quark screening concerns different theories and channels. Their bounded comparison supplies neither a single universal self-organizing mechanism nor a real-time formation or matter-stability law.

nodes.name: Scoped gauge-sector evidence comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The selected OPAL multijet fit constrains conditional color-factor ratios, while the historical UA1 W and Z analyses infer channel-dependent resonance masses. They test selected predictions of their adopted strong and electroweak descriptions. This comparison preserves those distinct response and model assumptions; it does not infer the Standard Model gauge/matter decomposition as a unique physical formation event.

nodes.name: Gauge-sector interpretation boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Gauge-sector differentiation denotes a chosen decomposition of a specified quantum field model by its gauge, matter and scalar transformation roles. It is a model description, not an observed event that partitions one undifferentiated field into permanent particle lineages. Representation labels, redundant field components and physical excitations require separate interpretation; distinct sectors remain coupled by the declared interactions.

nodes.name: Equal-time Gaussian cosmological-mode statistics
nodes.shortDescription: For the reviewed free real massless scalar on prescribed spatially flat FRW, set y=a phi and p=y'- (a'/a)y. Quadratic evolution of the supplied Gaussian vacuum preserves a Gaussian state. For one discrete nonzero Fourier pair k,-k, its independent complex amplitude y=y1+i y2 has equal-time density P(y1,y2)=exp[-|y|^2/|f_k|^2]/(pi |f_k|^2), with mean zero and <|y|^2>=|f_k|^2. This represents the commuting equal-time field-amplitude statistics; it does not by itself determine a classical trajectory or establish a quantum origin from an observed power spectrum.

nodes.name: Gaussian scalar engineering-dimension example
nodes.shortDescription: For the massless Gaussian scalar kinetic action S_*=(1/2)integral d^d x (partial phi)^2 with fixed kinetic normalization, x_prime=x/b and phi_prime(x_prime)=b^((d-2)/2)phi(b x_prime) keep that term invariant. Thus [phi]_engineering=(d-2)/2 and an operator containing n fields and r derivatives has engineering dimension Delta_eng=n(d-2)/2+r. In d=4 with phi->-phi symmetry, the monomials phi^2, phi^4 and phi^6 have dimensions 2, 4 and 6, giving engineering values y=2, 0 and -2 under the stated infrared convention.

nodes.name: Gluon fields
nodes.shortDescription: Gluon fields are the eight adjoint color components of the QCD gauge field, with spin-one gauge-boson excitations. The non-Abelian field strength gives gluon self-interactions.

nodes.name: Non-Abelian gluon self-coupling terms
nodes.shortDescription: For adjoint index A=1,...,8, set K^A_mu_nu=partial_mu A^A_nu-partial_nu A^A_mu and B^A_mu_nu=f^{ABC} A^B_mu A^C_nu. The reviewed PDG convention is F=K-g_s B, so L_g=-K.K/4+(g_s/2) K.B-(g_s^2/4) B.B, with Lorentz and adjoint indices contracted. The cubic and quartic terms generate three- and four-gluon vertices proportional to g_s and g_s^2. With [t^A,t^B]=i f^{ABC}t^C and Tr(t^A t^B)=T_R delta^{AB}, fundamental SU(3) has C_F=4/3, C_A=3 and T_R=1/2.

nodes.name: Specified ground-state atom-pair and ideal-wall dispersion limits
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected lowest-state, isotropic electric-dipole model of separated neutral atoms, the nonretarded interaction energy is U_AB(R)=-C6/R^6 with C6>0. At separations large compared with the relevant transition wavelengths the source result becomes U_AB(R)=-23*hbar*c*a_A(0)*a_B(0)/(4*pi*R^7). For an isotropic atom near a perfectly conducting plane the corresponding energy limits scale as -C3_ideal/z^3 and -3*hbar*c*a(0)/(8*pi*z^4). Here a denotes Gaussian/volume-normalized electric polarizability, explicitly distinct from the positive dimensionless fine-structure constant. These are different geometry-dependent energies under supplied atomic and field assumptions.

nodes.name: H1 inclusive e+p acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: H1 records 1996/97 e+p collisions with 27.6 GeV positrons and 820 GeV protons. The new inclusive neutral-current sample covers 1.5<=Q2<=150 GeV^2 and 3e-5<=x<=0.2. Standard samples have 4.5+13.4 pb^-1 and a dedicated low-Q2 run 1.8 pb^-1; effective exposure depends on the trigger, with smaller high-y subsets. Scattered-positron and hadronic measurements enter the stated event selection.

nodes.name: H1 reduced DIS cross sections
nodes.shortDescription: H1 reports corrected reduced cross sections in Tables 9-12 over 1.5<=Q2<=150 GeV^2 and 3e-5<=x<=0.2, with bin-dependent statistical, correlated and uncorrelated systematic errors. These are inclusive detector-corrected responses. The F2 values tabulated alongside them use the fitted longitudinal correction; the later gluon inference uses the reduced cross sections and their Q2 dependence.

nodes.name: H1 conditional NLO parton evolution
nodes.shortDescription: Fit reduced cross sections with NLO DGLAP evolution and coefficient functions in MSbar, using central mu_r^2=mu_f^2=Q2, input scale Q0^2=4 GeV^2, parameterized quark combinations and xg, and massive charm/beauty production with adopted on-shell masses 1.4/4.5 GeV. The standard H1-only gluon fit fixes alpha_s(MZ^2)=0.115 and uses 3.5<=Q2<=3000 GeV^2, including published high-Q2 H1 data from the same 1996/97 running. Equation 33 treats normalization and correlated-systematic nuisance parameters.

nodes.name: H1 low-x gluon distribution
nodes.shortDescription: The standard H1 NLO analysis constrains the momentum-weighted gluon distribution xg(x,Q2) for 3e-4<=x<=0.1. Its experimental uncertainty is about 5% at Q2=5 GeV^2 and about 3% at Q2=20 GeV^2. Figure 18 separately adds an alpha_s uncertainty borrowed from the joint H1+BCDMS analysis and then model uncertainty. This is a scheme- and model-conditioned distribution inferred mainly through scaling violations, not an observed free-gluon count.

nodes.name: H1 DIS reconstruction and corrections
nodes.shortDescription: Reconstruct kinematics with the electron or hadronic Sigma method, calibrate against control data, subtract photoproduction background and apply iterative bin, acceptance and radiative corrections using detector simulation. In the one-photon approximation, sigma_r=F2-y^2*FL/[1+(1-y)^2]. The published F2 extraction for y<=0.6 uses R=FL/(F2-FL) from a QCD fit; it is a derived response, not a separate acquired spectrum.

nodes.name: Hadron mass from a Euclidean correlator
nodes.shortDescription: A hadron mass is inferred from the Euclidean-time dependence of a correlation function with specified quantum numbers. Effective masses diagnose a fit regime; correlated single-mass cosh or sinh fits estimate the finite-lattice energy.

nodes.name: Supplied flavor weights and mass-spacing algebra
nodes.shortDescription: The supplied octet has eight states at seven distinct (I3,Y) positions; the decuplet has ten weights, with Omega at I=I3=0,Y=-2,S=-3,Q=-1. Ten symmetric flavor monomials match the decuplet weights, and nine synthetic mass-relation checks pass. The printed centers give two 147 MeV spacings and continuation 1679 MeV, compared only with the approximate 1680 MeV expectation.

nodes.name: Light-flavor and mass-relation calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Enumerate supplied light-baryon isospin/hypercharge weights and charges, compare degree-three symmetric flavor monomial weights, evaluate three synthetic positive-mass examples of the supplied octet relation, and compare the historical Figure 1 mass spacings.

nodes.name: Hadron mass inputs and scale setting
nodes.shortDescription: Dimensionless lattice results acquire a physical scale and a target quark-mass point through declared mass inputs. The reviewed calculation uses pion, kaon and Xi masses, with an alternative pion, kaon and Omega normalization.

nodes.name: Checked neutral-hadron table arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: The 44 displayed differential bins integrate centrally to 1.89787 K0/K0bar, 0.36454 Lambda/Lambdabar, 0.645525 K*0/K*0bar and 0.0980933 phi per decay. These do not exactly equal the displayed measured-range centers, but coherent display-rounding enclosures overlap the reported bins. Synthetic count corrections preserve the once-only branching efficiency and separate neutral-kaon factor two.

nodes.name: Finite neutral-hadron table arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Check the local transcription of 44 neutral-hadron bins, integrals of the displayed densities, coherent display-rounding bounds, and synthetic branching/efficiency and shared-normalization identities.

nodes.name: Inclusive identified-hadron yield
nodes.shortDescription: Define xp=2p/Ecm and the inclusive differential multiplicity (1/N)dn/dxp per hadronic Z0 decay. Integrating a differential multiplicity over xp gives a mean count, which may exceed one; it is not an event probability.

nodes.name: Two-dimensional hard-disk equilibrium model
nodes.shortDescription: The selected model contains N structureless disks of radius sigma in a two-dimensional periodic square of area V=L^2, with packing fraction eta=N*pi*sigma^2/V. Nonoverlapping configurations have zero potential energy and overlaps are forbidden. At fixed packing fraction its equilibrium phase behavior is independent of temperature, while pressure is proportional to temperature. Dense ordering can therefore be entropic without an attractive pair potential. Local sixfold bond orientation is Psi_k=average_l exp(6*i*phi_kl), with neighbors supplied by the stated construction, and sample orientation is Psi=N^-1*sum_k Psi_k.

nodes.name: Local-model test (2015)
nodes.shortDescription: With the declared fixed-n null, tau=0.0000108 and single-trial bound 0.75003240034992, the recomputed binomial upper tail is 0.039174643558790. The paper reports the rounded value 0.039; it is not a strict bound of 0.039.

nodes.name: Delft Bell-test preparation (2015)
nodes.shortDescription: Two NV spin qubits in diamond at 4 K, separated by 1280 m. Photon heralding, premeasurement validity filters and 3.7 microsecond binary spin readout define 245 Bell trials. Missing readout clicks give -1, not a discarded trial.

nodes.name: Spin correlations (2015)
nodes.shortDescription: Deposited event-table replay recovers 196 wins in 245 trials from 4746 exported rows; S=2.422499870 with conventional SD 0.203826598.

nodes.name: Local-model test (2016)
nodes.shortDescription: With the declared fixed-n null, tau=0.0000108 and single-trial bound 0.75003240034992, the recomputed binomial upper tail is 0.060727644566033. This run alone does not reject the specified null at 0.05.

nodes.name: Delft Bell-test preparation (2016)
nodes.shortDescription: Second run on the Delft apparatus, with 300 trials, changed heralding windows, psi-minus/psi-plus event tags, and QRNG bits combined with stored classical bits. The state tag changes which setting pair requires anticorrelation.

nodes.name: Spin correlations (2016)
nodes.shortDescription: Deposited event-table replay recovers 237 wins in 300 trials from 3918 exported rows; S=2.346430516 with conventional SD 0.184162420.

nodes.name: Herald-triggered optical counting
nodes.shortDescription: A two-photon-excited radiative cascade emits distinct frequencies nu_1 and nu_2. Detecting nu_1 triggers a gate for photomultipliers at the transmitted and reflected nu_2 outputs of a beam splitter. The intermediate lifetime is 4.7 ns; the selected gate is approximately 9 ns. The counters register gates, each output and joint output detections. This is a conditional detection preparation, not an ideal deterministic source in a single spatial mode.

nodes.name: Linearized U(1) scalar and vector example
nodes.shortDescription: For the Higgs1964 U(1) model with real fields and rho=phi1^2+phi2^2, choose (phi1,phi2)=(0,phi0), V'(phi0^2)=0 and V''(phi0^2)>0. The linearized radial and vector squared masses are 4*phi0^2*V''(phi0^2) and e^2*phi0^2. The shifted vector in Equation 3 contains the scalar-gradient term.

nodes.name: Single-doublet Higgs background and tree masses
nodes.shortDescription: Write rho=phi-dagger*phi and V=mu2*rho+(lambda_P^2/2)*rho^2 with mu2<0 and lambda_P>0. In unitary gauge choose phi=(0,(v+H)/sqrt(2)), v^2=-2*mu2/lambda_P^2. The tree-level relations are M_H^2=lambda_P^2*v^2, M_W=g*v/2, M_Z=sqrt(g^2+gprime^2)*v/2 and M_photon=0.

nodes.name: Conditional Higgs rate and coupling modifiers
nodes.shortDescription: For a single narrow resonance, sigma(i to H to f)=sigma_i*Gamma_f/Gamma_H. Relative to the same fixed-mass Standard Model reference, mu_if=(sigma_i/sigma_i_SM)*(Gamma_f/Gamma_f_SM)/(Gamma_H/Gamma_H_SM). The common-modifier benchmark groups vector couplings into kappa_V and fermion couplings into kappa_f under explicit loop, tensor-structure and total-width assumptions.

nodes.name: Evidence-based intra/intermolecular hydrogen-bond classification
nodes.shortDescription: Use an evidence-based hydrogen-bond classification for an attractive X-H...Y interaction with positively polarized H, X more electronegative than H and an electron-rich acceptor atom or group. Donor and acceptor may occur within one molecule or between molecules. Qualified structural, spectroscopic and theoretical diagnostics support classification; the definition itself is not an observed experiment.

nodes.name: Scoped hydrogen-bond definition, cold-dimer energy and model evidence
nodes.shortDescription: Hydrogen-bond classification can retain intra/intermolecular donor-acceptor interactions with qualified evidence criteria. In the finite positive cases reviewed, a prepared neutral water dimer has a measured fitted dissociation energy and an isolated-water model has directional equilibrium geometry and counteracting interaction-energy contributions. These distinct results support scoped hydrogen-bond description without a universal strength hierarchy, network-cooperativity requirement or necessary chemical/ionic/dispersion emergence chain.

nodes.name: Hydrogen-bond state, fragment and energy-convention boundary
nodes.shortDescription: A hydrogen-bond energy must specify the molecular system, electronic/rovibrational state, separated fragments and energy convention. For the neutral water dimer, D0 dissociation to water monomers differs from electronic well depth De, a frozen-fragment interaction energy, thermal dimerization enthalpy and covalent O-H bond cleavage. Intramolecular hydrogen-bond partners cannot generally be separated without changing the rest of the molecule.

nodes.name: Adopted hydrogen-isotope mass difference
nodes.shortDescription: The neutron-mass extraction adopts Ar(2H)-Ar(1H)=1.00627674630(71), a dimensionless relative atomic-mass difference, from the mass-spectrometry reference cited by Kessler.

nodes.name: Assigned Cs133 hyperfine reference and finite clock realization distinction
nodes.shortDescription: The SI second fixes the unperturbed Cs133 electronic-ground-state hyperfine transition frequency Delta_nu_Cs to exactly9,192,631,770 Hz, where Hz=s^-1. The selected standard transition connects ground2S1/2 F=4,mF=0 and F=3,mF=0. The definition refers to an isolated atom unperturbed by external fields, including ambient blackbody radiation. This exact assigned number is a normative unit definition; a finite apparatus realizes that reference through measurements, systematic corrections and nonzero uncertainty.

nodes.name: Scoped hyperfine spectral coupling and clock realization
nodes.shortDescription: A corrected Cs1337d3/2 optical-fluorescence study supplies finite nuclear-electronic hyperfine intervals and state-specific multipole coupling constants, while a distinct Cs/Rb ground-state fountain study supplies an actual corrected clock-frequency comparison. The SI exact Cs hyperfine reference is a separate definition. These retain measurable hyperfine structure, state sensitivity and clock operation under explicit preparation and inference limits, without universal splitting, parent-weight, population-threshold or independent-parameter claims.

nodes.name: Isotope- and state-specific hyperfine frequency parameters
nodes.shortDescription: For a declared isotope and electronic state, let I be nuclear spin, J total electronic angular momentum and F the coupled total angular momentum. Define K=F(F+1)-I(I+1)-J(J+1). With A expressed in frequency units, the first-order magnetic-dipole contribution relative to the state centroid is E_F/h=A*K/2; allowed higher-rank terms have separate state-specific constants, including the electric-quadrupole B term. In the selected Cs1337d2D3/2 assignment, J=3/2 and F=2,3,4,5 correspond to supplied I=7/2. The first-order electric-quadrupole term is absent within a J=1/2 electronic level; the Cs ground-state clock is not evidence that every hyperfine transition has a nonzero quadrupole contribution.

nodes.name: Ideal parallel-plate Casimir model
nodes.shortDescription: For parallel perfectly conducting plates, the regulated interaction energy per area is -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^3). The force per area conjugate to increasing separation is -pi^2 hbar c/(240 a^4), directed toward smaller separation.

nodes.name: ILL silicon spacing for capture recalibration
nodes.shortDescription: The two-path ILL calibration reports d220=192.0155721(64)e-12 m at 22.5 C and zero pressure. Its two path estimates are 192.0155735(56)e-12 m and 192.0155707(59)e-12 m.

nodes.name: Adjusted ILL2.5 lattice input
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Dewey author report adopts d220(ILL2.5)=1.920155822(96)e-10 m at 22.5 C in vacuum from the 1998 adjustment with an enlarged uncertainty; this supplies a recalculation of the existing capture data.

nodes.name: ILL2.5 lattice input for the 1999 analysis
nodes.shortDescription: The 1999 wavelength extraction adopts Table 3A d220(ILL2.5)=1.920155723(96)e-10 m in vacuum at 22.5 C, with the stated pressure correction for measurements in the reactor hall.

nodes.name: Inclusive decay widths and branching fractions
nodes.shortDescription: In the adopted inclusive weak-resonance decay convention, define Gamma_tot=sum_f Gamma_f over a complete, mutually exclusive channel partition and B_f=Gamma_f/Gamma_tot. The Gamma_f and Gamma_tot use the same energy-width and radiation convention; B_f is dimensionless. The LEP Z convention includes final-state QED/QCD corrections and nonfactorisable contributions so that its specified partial widths sum to its total width.

nodes.name: Inclusive electromagnetic DIS response
nodes.shortDescription: For unpolarized one-photon electron-nucleon scattering with negligible electron mass, use Q^2=4EEprime sin^2(theta/2)>0, nu=E-Eprime and x=Q^2/(2M nu). R=sigmaL/sigmaT=F2(1+4M^2*x^2/Q^2)/(2xF1)-1. The equivalent polarization convention is epsilon=[1+2(1+nu^2/Q^2)tan^2(theta/2)]^-1, Gamma=alpha*Eprime*(1/x-1)/[4*pi^2*M*E*(1-epsilon)], and Y=(d^2sigma/dOmega dEprime)/Gamma=sigmaT+epsilon*sigmaL. At fixed x,Q^2, the reduced-response intercept and slope determine R; nonzero intercept and a span in epsilon are required.

nodes.name: Internal propagator kernel
nodes.shortDescription: An internal line denotes a propagator kernel joining vertices in a specified perturbative amplitude. In the selected Fourier convention the photon includes (k^2+i0)^-1 and the electron an inverse Dirac operator. Vertex momentum conservation is imposed; loop four-momenta are integrated rather than individually restricted to a free mass shell.

nodes.name: Ion-to-atom mass conversion
nodes.shortDescription: A measured ionic mass-to-charge ratio is converted to a neutral-atom mass using charge state, electron mass, ionization and chemical binding energies, with neutral carbon-12 fixing the relative-mass scale.

nodes.name: Ion formation, binding and electrostatic interaction distinction
nodes.shortDescription: Changing the charge state of a selected atomic or molecular subsystem requires electron removal, attachment or redistribution under a specified channel and preparation. Donor-acceptor electron transfer is one possible process, distinct from direct above-threshold photoionization, electron-impact ionization and electric-field ionization of a prepared Rydberg state. These channel labels do not themselves supply a rate. Once charge states are specified, the leading vacuum Coulomb pair model distinguishes like-sign repulsion from opposite-sign attraction; a many-ion medium response is a further model. A bound-state energy, ion signal, formation rate and screened interaction are separate quantities.

nodes.name: Atomic and molecular ion charge-state convention
nodes.shortDescription: Define an atomic or molecular ion by nonzero net species charge q=z*e, with e>0 the positive elementary-charge magnitude and signed integer charge state z. Given supplied nuclear charge numbers Z_a and electron inventory N_e, z=sum_a(Z_a)-N_e is charge bookkeeping for the chosen isolated species. Positive z labels a cation and negative z an anion. In the stated two-center one-electron cases H2+ and HD+, two Z=1 nuclei and one electron give z=+1. Charge state, isotope composition, internal quantum state and preparation are different descriptors.

nodes.name: Scoped ion preparation and electrolyte interaction evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The selected literature supplies a prepared-H2 field-ionization ion readout, a stored charged HD+ mass/state preparation, calculated molecular-ion binding quantities and an equilibrium screened-electrolyte model. These retain real atomic/molecular ions and collective ionic interactions under different conditions. Ion production, persistence in a trap, bound-state energetics and statistical solution screening are not one common formation or maintenance experiment.

nodes.name: Hadron isospin mass differences
nodes.shortDescription: A mass splitting is a signed difference between specified isospin partners. Here Delta_N=M_n-M_p; isospin breaking is expanded to first order in the renormalized alpha and delta_m=m_d-m_u. It is distinct from an absolute hadron mass, decay width or lifetime.

nodes.name: Isotope kinetics and mechanism evidence boundary
nodes.shortDescription: An isotope-dependent infrared loss curve or reported first-order half-life is an observable under its stated preparation and detection conditions; a tunnelling mechanism additionally requires a specified reaction assignment and dynamical model. In this publication, temperature-limited dark kinetics, isotopologue comparison and a source calculation are combined in that interpretation. Deuterium non-decay without a stated observation window cannot supply a numerical deuterated half-life or k_H/k_D; a calculated lifetime is a separate model output.

nodes.name: KamLAND reactor acquisition and selection
nodes.shortDescription: Use the 766 ton-year exposure from 9 March 2002 to 11 January 2004, with 515.1 days of livetime after muon cuts. Require prompt energy 2.6-8.5 MeV, delayed energy 1.8-2.6 MeV, both vertices within 5.5 m, separation below 2 m and delay 0.5-1000 microseconds. Retain the PMT upgrade and reported 89.8 +/- 1.5% selection efficiency.

nodes.name: KamLAND normalized average survival estimate
nodes.shortDescription: From the same selected acquisition and the adopted reactor/background models, KamLAND reports average electron-antineutrino survival 0.658 +/- 0.044 statistical +/- 0.047 systematic. This is a period-averaged rate estimate, not an event-level probability measured at one baseline.

nodes.name: KamLAND selected-sample background estimate
nodes.shortDescription: The reported background above 2.6 MeV prompt energy is 17.8 +/- 7.3 events. Its central components are 2.69 +/- 0.02 accidental, 4.8 +/- 0.9 lithium/helium and 10.3 +/- 7.1 alpha-induced carbon-neutron events; the fast-neutron bound enters the uncertainty.

nodes.name: KamLAND-only oscillation likelihood
nodes.shortDescription: Use the same selected prompt spectrum and rate in the reported unbinned two-flavor maximum-likelihood analysis. Include reactor histories, detector response and background nuisance treatment: float the alpha-neutron component near 6 MeV, constrain the 2.6 and 4.4 MeV components and retain their stated energy-scale uncertainty. Keep the separate solar combination outside this result.

nodes.name: KamLAND-only rate-and-shape mass splitting
nodes.shortDescription: The KamLAND-only two-flavor rate-and-shape analysis reports Delta m^2=7.9(+0.6/-0.5)e-5 eV^2 and best-fit tan^2(theta)=0.46, with a large uncertainty on the mixing parameter. The fitted spectral distortion is interpreted within the declared propagation, flux, response and nuisance model.

nodes.name: KamLAND reactor response and backgrounds
nodes.shortDescription: Construct the no-oscillation reactor expectation from time-dependent reactor histories, fission-spectrum and cross-section inputs, 4.61e31 target protons, livetime and response. Use calibrations and auxiliary controls for the accidental, lithium/helium and alpha-induced carbon-neutron components; retain the reported uncertainty treatment separately from selected counts.

nodes.name: KamLAND selected prompt-energy sample
nodes.shortDescription: The full selection yields 258 candidate events. The official release lists their rounded prompt energies in MeV, including annihilation energy; these selected energies supply the measured spectrum used by the same-acquisition analyses.

nodes.name: KamLAND no-oscillation reactor expectation
nodes.shortDescription: The source predicts 365.2 +/- 23.7 systematic reactor antineutrino events above the 2.6 MeV prompt threshold in the absence of disappearance. This is the reactor signal expectation before adding background, conditioned on flux, cross section, calibration and selection inputs.

nodes.name: Deuteron binding energy with 1999 inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Equations 3, 5 and 7 report the recoil-corrected energy-equivalent wavelength 5.57340978(99)e-13 m, binding-energy mass equivalent 2.38817007(42)e-3 u and binding energy 2224566.14(41) eV.

nodes.name: Capture photon wavelength with 1999 inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Equation 1 reports lambda_gamma=5.57671299(99)e-13 m using the two-campaign angle, adopted ILL2.5 spacing and pressure correction. This is the emitted photon wavelength before recoil conversion.

nodes.name: Combined capture diffraction angle
nodes.shortDescription: The two-campaign final first-order angle is 0.083202194(14) degrees at 22.5 C, including the stated crystal-temperature and vertical-divergence uncertainty contributions.

nodes.name: Neutron mass inferred with 1999 inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Combining the adopted hydrogen-isotope mass difference with the binding-energy mass equivalent gives the reported neutron mass 1.00866491637(82) u. The binding-energy and mass-spectrometry uncertainty contributions are 0.42e-9 u and 0.71e-9 u.

nodes.name: Capture wavelength with adjusted lattice input
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Dewey author report Table VII reuses the Kessler measurement with adjusted lattice input: photon wavelength 5.57671328(99)e-13 m and recoil-corrected energy-equivalent wavelength 5.57341007(99)e-13 m. Its Table VIII binding-energy mass equivalent is 2.38816996(42)e-3 u.

nodes.name: 1995 capture diffraction angle
nodes.shortDescription: Table 2 gives 0.083202185(11) and 0.083202104(40) degrees for the 44- and 8-determination groups. The campaign estimate is 0.083202180(22) degrees after the stated uncertainty treatment.

nodes.name: GAMS4 capture campaign in 1995
nodes.shortDescription: February 1995 GAMS4 capture campaign at ILL: the common Kapton source and ILL2.5 silicon crystals, with 44 Bragg-angle determinations in (1,-2)/(1,2) and 8 in (2,-1)/(2,2). The March 6-7, 1995 optical-polygon calibration serves this campaign.

nodes.name: 1998 capture diffraction angle
nodes.shortDescription: Table 2 gives 0.083202197(12), 0.083202229(22) and 0.083202190(12) degrees for the 32-, 32- and 25-determination groups. The campaign estimate is 0.083202199(12) degrees.

nodes.name: GAMS4 capture campaign in 1998
nodes.shortDescription: March 1998 GAMS4 capture campaign at ILL: the common Kapton source and ILL2.5 silicon crystals, with 32 Bragg-angle determinations in (1,-2)/(1,2), 32 in (2,-1)/(2,2) and 25 in (1,-3)/(1,3). Calibrations on March 7-8, 25-26 and 29-30 and a humidity correction serve this campaign.

nodes.name: ILL silicon calibration analysis
nodes.shortDescription: Combine existing ILL transfer comparisons with revised W04/NW04 absolute references and WS1 comparisons, retaining two paths, empirical sample variability and the 22.5 C vacuum boundary.

nodes.name: KLOE radiative-decay acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the 427 pb^-1 KLOE sample collected in 2001-2002 near sqrt(s)=1.02 GeV. Select seven prompt calorimeter photons with an opposite-charge track vertex for the combined two eta-prime cascades, and seven photons without interaction-region tracks for the eta normalization cascade; impose the stated energy, timing, vertex and kinematic-fit selections.

nodes.name: KLOE conditional pseudoscalar mixing model
nodes.shortDescription: Use the same measured R_phi in the no-gluonium Equation 10: cot(phi_P)^2*[1-(m_s/m_bar)*(C_NS/C_S)*tan(phi_V)/sin(2phi_P)]^2*(p_eta-prime/p_eta)^3. Adopt the constituent-mass, overlap, vector-angle and phase-space inputs stated in the paper; keep the separate multi-source gluonium fit outside this inference.

nodes.name: KLOE no-gluonium pseudoscalar angle
nodes.shortDescription: Under the specified zero-gluonium model, the same R_phi gives phi_P=(41.4 +/-0.3 statistical +/-0.7 systematic +/-0.6 theoretical) degrees, corresponding to the reported octet-singlet angle theta_P=(-13.3 +/-0.3 +/-0.7 +/-0.6) degrees. This is a conditional same-acquisition interpretation.

nodes.name: KLOE radiative partial-rate ratio
nodes.shortDescription: After the Equation 7 response, daughter-branching and interference corrections, KLOE reports R_phi=BR(phi->eta-prime gamma)/BR(phi->eta gamma)=(4.77 +/-0.09 statistical +/-0.19 systematic)*10^-3.

nodes.name: KLOE cascade response and corrections
nodes.shortDescription: Estimate residual kaon backgrounds using simulation and the acquisition normalization; obtain branching-weighted signal efficiency 23.45% and reference efficiency 33.66%, plus FLS efficiencies 97% and 97.88% from control data. Equation 7 multiplies the subtracted yield ratio by inverse signal/reference efficiencies, FLS ratio, daughter-branching ratio and K_rho=0.95 +/-0.01.

nodes.name: KLOE selected radiative candidates
nodes.shortDescription: The selected eta-prime cascade sample contains 3750 candidates before residual background subtraction. The eta normalization selection contains 1665000 events. The reported energy and invariant-mass plots display detector-level responses with modeled components.

nodes.name: KLOE background-subtracted radiative yield
nodes.shortDescription: The residual background estimate 343 +/-43 is subtracted from 3750 candidates, giving N_eta-prime-gamma=3407 +/-61 statistical +/-43 systematic. The subtraction reuses the selected acquisition and treats background uncertainty as systematic.

nodes.name: Calculated H2+ ionization energy
nodes.shortDescription: Korobov Table V gives H2+ ground-state ionization energy 131058.1219937(6) cm^-1 under CODATA 2014 and spin-averaged conventions; (6) is the theoretical component only.

nodes.name: Calculated HD+ ionization energy
nodes.shortDescription: Korobov Table V gives spin-averaged HD+ ionization energy 131224.6841650(6) cm^-1. The final-digit uncertainty is theoretical and omits the separately discussed constant uncertainties.

nodes.name: H2+ ground-state binding calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Read the H2+ ground-state ionization calculation under the paper's spin and constant conventions; retain theoretical and constant uncertainties separately.

nodes.name: HD+ NRQED energy calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Calculate spin-averaged hydrogen molecular-ion energies with high-order NRQED corrections and stated approximations using CODATA 2014 inputs; quote theoretical uncertainty separately from constant uncertainties.

nodes.name: L3 normalized angular response
nodes.shortDescription: The analysis measures weighted four-bin angular fractions in seven 1993-1995 year/energy data sets after the stated detector corrections. Figure 1 displays the 1994 subset as ratios to the normal-running and no-running predictions: two theoretical denominators for the same subset, not independent measurements or absolute cross sections.

nodes.name: L3 conditional inverse-alpha difference
nodes.shortDescription: L3 interprets the same small-angle fit as alpha^-1(-2.1 GeV^2)-alpha^-1(-6.25 GeV^2)=0.78 +/- 0.26, with total experimental uncertainty. This is a conditional running-coupling difference, not an additional acquisition or two absolute coupling measurements.

nodes.name: L3 normalized running-coupling model
nodes.shortDescription: Use the corrected angular fractions and the multinomial shape likelihood of Equation 2 with modified BHLUMI 4.04. Equation 3 uses alpha(Q^2)=alpha(0)/(1-DeltaAlpha(Q^2)-S*(Q^2-Q0^2)), with Q0^2=-2.1 GeV^2, nominal running as the reference and unchanged timelike running.

nodes.name: L3 fitted spacelike deformation
nodes.shortDescription: The combined small-angle analysis reports S=(-3.6 +/- 2.7 statistical +/- 3.5 systematic)*10^-4 GeV^-2 in Equation 4. S is a fitted deformation of nominal spacelike running; zero slope does not mean a constant coupling.

nodes.name: L3 weighted small-angle acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Select L3 Bhabha events near the Z resonance in 1993-1995 with BGO energy thresholds of 0.8 and 0.4 times beam energy. Use silicon/BGO coordinates and the 32-54 mrad fiducial region with boundaries 32,35,40,46,54 mrad; enter four coordinates per event with weight 0.25. The retained sample is 6.7 million events, grouped into seven year/energy sets.

nodes.name: Computed water acceptor exchange and orientational reconfiguration
nodes.shortDescription: For the stated rigid-SPC/E liquid-water model, the reported trajectories and correlations support large, concerted OH reorientation with exchange of hydrogen-bond acceptors, together with a slower between-switch OO-frame contribution. The selected angular event takes about 250 fs; the forward completed-switch correlation gives 1.8 ps; the rank-two long-time orientational decay fitted directly from the MD trajectory is 2.0 ps. Table 1 gives 1.6 ps for the extended-jump-model rank-two prediction. These distinct results describe statistical reconfiguration under the declared simulation/event definitions, not directly measured molecule or cluster lifetimes.

nodes.name: SPC/E switch and orientational-correlation context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the stated rigid-SPC/E trajectory and geometric hydrogen-bond model to collect more than 16000 successful acceptor-switch events. Average paths centered on exchange, with the broader geometric bounds used for that selected ensemble. For the forward completed-switch correlation, use the source absorbing endpoint convention so subsequent back reaction or rupture does not contribute. Analyze orientational correlations over the ensemble of all OH bonds and fit their long-time components separately from the fast librational decay. Compare the original jump model and its extension including slower OO-frame reorientation as interpretations of this same simulation.

nodes.name: CLAS dual-target quasielastic preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Measure deuterium neutron/proton quasielastic coincidences at 2.6 and 4.2 GeV; use the simultaneous hydrogen target for detection-efficiency calibration and EC/TOF neutron detection with matched acceptance cuts.

nodes.name: CLAS conditional magnetic-response extraction
nodes.shortDescription: Interpret corrected deuterium ratios through Equation 1 with adopted proton and neutron electric responses, AV18/PWIA/Glauber nuclear corrections and a separate Fermi-motion acceptance correction; combine overlapping EC/TOF and energy settings.

nodes.name: CLAS combined neutron magnetic response
nodes.shortDescription: E111M1 releases 26 combined GMn/(mu_n*GD) values at Q2 centers 0.9848-4.7727 GeV2, with separate statistical and systematic error columns. These are original conditional inferences from corrected deuterium ratios, not free-neutron or magnetic-moment measurements.

nodes.name: Corrected deuterium neutron/proton ratios
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 1 reports the cut- and efficiency-treated quasielastic ratio R=sigma[d(e,e'n)p]/sigma[d(e,e'p)n] separately for 2.6 and 4.2 GeV, combining EC/TOF observations within each beam energy.

nodes.name: Conditional radiative interpretation of the level shift
nodes.shortDescription: The approximate measured separation is compatible with Bethe's 1040 MHz self-energy estimate under its subtraction and cutoff assumptions. Compatibility does not isolate vacuum polarization or validate full relativistic QED.

nodes.name: Microwave quenching resonances
nodes.shortDescription: Microwaves decrease the metastable-hydrogen detector current at field-dependent resonances; the experiment reports transitions across the 2.4-18.5 cm wavelength range.

nodes.name: Approximate hydrogen level separation
nodes.shortDescription: The comparison with Zeeman curves places hydrogen 2S1/2 about 1000 MHz above 2P1/2. This is the approximate 1947 result, with no fitted error bar supplied.

nodes.name: Hydrogen microwave preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Electron-impact preparation of a metastable hydrogen beam; microwave quenching at fixed frequency while magnetic field is varied; electron-ejection detection at a metal target.

nodes.name: Conditional sphere-plane Casimir comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The reported residual attraction agrees with the revised material-response calculation when the corrected radius is used. The accepted Au/Cu calculation removes the proposed need for a Cu-like contaminated coating as an explanation of their discrepancy.

nodes.name: Sphere-plane residual attraction
nodes.shortDescription: The torsion-balance readout retains an attractive force after the fitted electrostatic contribution is subtracted. The 216 sweeps are a selected dataset, not 216 independent replications.

nodes.name: Sphere-plane force preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Cu/Au-coated surfaces in a feedback torsion balance; relative separation from calibrated PZT motion and absolute separation from the electrostatic fit. The final dataset comprises 216 retained sweeps.

nodes.name: Quantum lattice continuum-limit prescription
nodes.shortDescription: To approach a quantum continuum description, reduce lattice spacing while adjusting bare parameters to hold specified physical quantities fixed. Creutz chooses fixed string tension; Wilson requires correlation lengths much larger than a.

nodes.name: Euclidean lattice gauge formulation
nodes.shortDescription: A lattice gauge theory assigns compact-group variables U_ij to oriented neighboring links, with U_ji=U_ij inverse. Gauge-invariant plaquette actions and invariant group integration define a regulated Euclidean path integral.

nodes.name: Leading strong-coupling surface expansion
nodes.shortDescription: In the SU(2) Wilson action convention beta=4/e0^2, the leading strong-coupling term for a simple planar fundamental contour tiled by N plaquettes is W(C) approximately (beta/4)^N. The corresponding leading area coefficient is a^2 K approximately -ln(beta/4).

nodes.name: Lee reported fractional-charge abundance limit
nodes.shortDescription: The authors report a 95% confidence upper limit of 1.17 x 10^-22 fractional-charge particles per nucleon in silicone oil for 0.18<=q_r<=0.82. The graph records the published limit with its unresolved normalization and material restrictions.

nodes.name: Lee selected-drop fractional-charge null
nodes.shortDescription: The final 70.1 mg silicone-oil sample shows integer electric-charge peaks and no accepted drop more than 0.15 e from the nearest integer. The result uses the stated cuts without background subtraction.

nodes.name: Lee silicone-oil electric-charge search context
nodes.shortDescription: A modified Millikan oil-drop experiment measures horizontal trajectories in an alternating electric field while upward air flow slows the drops.
