The final selected sample contains 70.1 mg of processed silicone oil in 16,807,644 drops with average diameter approximately 20.6 micrometers.

nodes.name: LEP-I Z scan acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL LEP-I electron-positron data accumulated mainly in 1990-1995 around the Z resonance. Peak and off-peak energy scans supply hadronic and charged-lepton samples; 1993 and 1995 use precision three-point scans. Reconstruct selected final states and the channel-specific angular observables with the declared detector acceptances.

nodes.name: Derived inclusive Z branching fractions
nodes.shortDescription: In Table 7.2 without lepton universality, the reported percentages are Bhad=69.967 +/- 0.093, Bee=3.3632 +/- 0.0042, Bmumu=3.3662 +/- 0.0066, Btautau=3.3696 +/- 0.0083 and Binvisible=19.934 +/- 0.098. Each visible fraction is its inclusive partial width divided by the common total width; the invisible fraction enforces the inclusive sum to one. These fractions and errors are dependent on the same fit and its correlations.

nodes.name: Correlated LEP-I Z combination
nodes.shortDescription: Combine four sets of nine pseudo-observables by the reported chi-square minimization using the 36-by-36 covariance. Preserve common beam-energy, luminosity, t-channel and QED/parametrization contributions, including the common theory term also added to diagonal blocks. Use the no-lepton-universality result and propagate its dependent parameter transformations to inclusive widths and fractions.

nodes.name: Individual LEP-I Z parameter fits
nodes.shortDescription: Table 2.4 reports four correlated nine-parameter fits: mZ, GammaZ, sigmaHad0, Re0, Rmu0, Rtau0 and three pole forward-backward asymmetries. The fitted total widths are ALEPH 2.4959 +/- 0.0043, DELPHI 2.4876 +/- 0.0041, L3 2.5025 +/- 0.0041 and OPAL 2.4948 +/- 0.0041 GeV. Their within-experiment matrices and shared uncertainties remain inputs to the combined result.

nodes.name: Combined LEP-I Z line shape
nodes.shortDescription: The no-lepton-universality branch of Table 2.13 reports mZ=91.1876 +/- 0.0021 GeV, GammaZ=2.4952 +/- 0.0023 GeV and sigmaHad0=41.541 +/- 0.037 nb. The width ratios are Re0=20.804 +/- 0.050, Rmu0=20.785 +/- 0.033 and Rtau0=20.764 +/- 0.045. These are correlated pseudo-observables in the declared running-width convention, including the three asymmetry parameters in the joint fit.

nodes.name: Derived inclusive Z partial widths
nodes.shortDescription: In Table 7.1 without lepton universality, the reported inclusive partial widths are GammaHad=1745.8 +/- 2.7, Gammaee=83.92 +/- 0.12, Gammamumu=83.99 +/- 0.18 and Gammatautau=84.08 +/- 0.22 MeV. GammaInvisible=497.4 +/- 2.5 MeV is the total-width residual after those visible components. These are parameter transformations of the same LEP-I fit, retaining their reported correlations.

nodes.name: LEP-I response and pseudo-observable extraction
nodes.shortDescription: Correct selected event rates for efficiency and backgrounds, normalize by small-angle Bhabha luminosity and extrapolate to declared idealized acceptances. Adopt the beam-energy model, its spread and correlations, t-channel electron contributions and QED radiation. TOPAZ0 4.4 and ZFITTER 6.23 relate cross-sections and asymmetries to each experiment's nine pseudo-observables; preserve the combination-specific calibration and program updates.

nodes.name: Selected LEP-I scan responses
nodes.shortDescription: The report describes roughly 200 cross-section and forward-backward-asymmetry measurements per experiment. Corrected channel rates vary across the scan energy, and Figure 2.3 displays selected hadronic cross-sections around the three principal energies. These detector- and luminosity-corrected observables precede the nine fitted pseudo-observables; the plotted combination bands are fitted summaries of the same data.

nodes.name: LEP W branching data preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the four experiments WW channel selections from 1997-2000 at 183-207 GeV. The report distinguishes ten four-fermion final states through jets, charged leptons and missing momentum; Table 5.1 specifies the exposure bins.

nodes.name: LEP W branching correlated fits
nodes.shortDescription: Combine experiment branching estimates with the full 12 by 12 covariance. Keep the fit without lepton universality separate from the fit with a common leptonic fraction and the sum-to-unity constraint; lepton-mass effects are neglected in the source treatment.

nodes.name: LEP W leptonic branching without universality
nodes.shortDescription: Without lepton universality, LEP reports B_e = 10.71 +/- 0.16%, B_mu = 10.63 +/- 0.15% and B_tau = 11.38 +/- 0.21%, with correlated total uncertainties.

nodes.name: LEP W branching response and signal convention
nodes.shortDescription: Relate selected channel yields to cross sections through luminosity, acceptance, signal efficiency and expected backgrounds. Retain the source CC03 diagrammatic WW signal convention, explicitly not gauge invariant by itself, and the shared detector and theory uncertainty categories.

nodes.name: LEP W branching with lepton universality
nodes.shortDescription: Assuming lepton universality and neglecting lepton-mass effects, LEP reports B_had = 67.41 +/- 0.18 statistical +/- 0.20 systematic percent and each B_l = 10.86 +/- 0.06 statistical +/- 0.07 systematic percent, with their sum constrained to one.

nodes.name: LEP combined W decay width
nodes.shortDescription: The LEP combination reports Gamma_W = 2.195 +/- 0.063 statistical +/- 0.055 systematic GeV, with total uncertainty 0.083 GeV, in its declared s-dependent Breit-Wigner convention.

nodes.name: LEP W width data preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the four experiments direct-reconstruction inputs from 1996-2000 at 172-209 GeV, primarily fully hadronic and semileptonic WW selections. Reconstructed jets, charged leptons and assigned missing momentum define the channel inputs.

nodes.name: LEP W width likelihood and combination
nodes.shortDescription: Fit mass estimators by experiment-specific reweighting or response convolution, varying m_W and Gamma_W independently for width extraction. Combine experiment, channel and period results with BLUE and shared systematics, using a relativistic Breit-Wigner propagator with s-dependent width.

nodes.name: LEP W width response and corrections
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt calibrated jet/lepton response, beam-energy constraints, radiative four-fermion signal and backgrounds, and hadronisation and final-state-interaction models. Kinematic mass estimators include response and unobserved-radiation corrections; the width analysis retains standard jet reconstruction.

nodes.name: Lepton charge, chirality and flavor labels
nodes.shortDescription: With e>0 the positron charge, the charged species e-, mu- and tau- have charge -e and their antiparticles have +e; the active neutrino fields are electrically neutral in the declared electroweak model. Left/right chirality labels field representation components; helicity is spin projected along momentum and is not the same label for a massive lepton. Charged-lepton mass-basis species and charged-current neutrino flavor labels must be distinguished from the neutrino propagation mass basis.

nodes.name: Lepton fields
nodes.shortDescription: Lepton fields are color singlets with spin one half. Their electroweak specification distinguishes left-handed doublets, charged right-handed singlets, charged leptons and neutrinos.

nodes.name: Ground-state light-baryon multiplets
nodes.shortDescription: For the stated spatially symmetric ground-state three-quark model, the spin-flavor 56 contains the J^P=1/2+ octet N,Lambda,Sigma,Xi and J^P=3/2+ decuplet Delta,Sigma*,Xi*,Omega. Their isospin rows contain 2+1+3+2 and 4+3+2+1 weights. Lambda and Sigma0 share (I3,Y)=(0,0) but have different isospin.

nodes.name: Light-flavor SU(3) convention
nodes.shortDescription: Use the approximate light-flavor SU(3) classification of u,d,s labels, distinct from local color SU(3). In this restricted sector Y=B+S and Q/e=I3+Y/2. The symmetry limit groups states with related quantum numbers; observed mass splittings do not disappear by a change of labels.

nodes.name: Light quark-antiquark flavor nonets
nodes.shortDescription: In the restricted u,d,s quark-antiquark model, 3 tensor 3bar decomposes as flavor 8 plus 1. The lightest L=0 pseudoscalar and vector assignments form separate nonets; spin/parity and physical state mixing remain part of their interpretation.

nodes.name: Declared linear homogeneous optical-propagation model
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected homogeneous isotropic linear medium, use the convention E(z,t)=Re[E0(omega)*exp(i*k(omega)*z-i*omega*t)] with k(omega)=omega*sqrt(epsilon(omega)*mu(omega)) in absolute SI constitutive units. Writing k=k_real+i*k_imag gives amplitude attenuation exp(-k_imag*z) and phase accumulation k_real*z. For the passive forward branch, k_imag>=0; the corresponding fixed-medium intensity attenuation coefficient is alpha_int=2*k_imag in m^-1. Nonlinear real propagation phase across a pulse bandwidth can produce dispersive waveform deformation, whereas a real phase linear in frequency supplies a delay. A wave number proportional to frequency at fixed speed is not by itself dispersive deformation. These phase effects are distinct from imaginary-part attenuation.

nodes.name: Carbon charge-state consistency
nodes.shortDescription: The 2019 C-12(6+)/C-12(3+) control agrees with its electronic-energy reference within 0.2 sigma at relative uncertainty 1.1e-10. Its doubled-voltage preparation tests a distinct charge-state comparison.

nodes.name: Carbon nuclear mass reference
nodes.shortDescription: For R=nu_c(C-12(6+))/nu_c(p), m_p=R*m_C/6 with m_C=12 u-6*m_e+sum(E_ion)/c^2. The nuclear reference retains its electronic-energy inputs and their stated uncertainty.

nodes.name: Published mass-correction boundaries
nodes.shortDescription: The 2019 proton correction budget reports a total 59.5(28.8) ppt. The displayed pair-specific terms, the total and the printed sign convention do not by themselves supply a reproducible global correction recipe.

nodes.name: Shared-data cyclotron-readout check
nodes.shortDescription: Using the same-cycle double-dip readout, the 2019 account reports R_DD=0.50377636768(3)(5) and m_p=1.00727646661(6)(10) u. Agreement with the PnA result is an internal comparison with about fourfold lower precision.

nodes.name: Proton-referenced oxygen mass
nodes.shortDescription: The reanalyzed oxygen campaign reports R_stat(O,p)=0.503936558242(17) and neutral m(O-16)=15.99491461937(54)(45)(51) u after corrections. The three uncertainties are statistical, systematic and the adopted proton-mass contribution.

nodes.name: Original LIONTRAP proton campaign
nodes.shortDescription: Single protons and C-12(6+) ions are alternated in a 5 mm-radius trap near 3.8 T and 4 K with separate axial detectors and common trapping voltages. Thirteen runs use three ion pairs. PnA and double-dip frequencies are acquired in each cycle; the original report fits excitation-dependent ratios and applies its stated corrections.

nodes.name: Original proton-mass result
nodes.shortDescription: The 2017 analysis reports R_stat=0.5037763676431(77), R_final=0.5037763676624(77)(146), and m_p=1.007276466583(15)(29) u. The uncertainties on the corrected result are statistical then systematic, on the final digits.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP carbon charge-state check
nodes.shortDescription: The reported C-12(6+)/C-12(3+) comparison doubles the precision-trap voltages to match the axial resonators. Its reference uses electron masses and electronic binding energies. Independent acquisition relative to the control described in 2017 is not established.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP same-cycle double-dip check
nodes.shortDescription: Double-dip cyclotron frequencies recorded in the same proton/carbon cycles are used instead of the PnA frequencies. The shared apparatus, ions, mass reference and corrections remain part of the comparison.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP oxygen data reanalysis
nodes.shortDescription: The oxygen campaign reported in 2017 compares O-16(8+) with a proton using a retuned axial resonator and the same measurement-cycle design. Revised temperature corrections and the reanalyzed proton mass enter the neutral-oxygen inference.

nodes.name: Reanalyzed proton-mass result
nodes.shortDescription: The 2019 reanalysis reports R_stat=0.5037763676401(81), R_cor=0.5037763676701(81)(144), and m_p=1.007276466598(16)(29) u. The mass shifts upward by 1.5e-11 u relative to the 2017 report of the same data.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP proton data reanalysis
nodes.shortDescription: The proton dataset reported in 2017 is reanalyzed with corrected temperature estimates and a measurement-program correction. A planar fit gives the zero-driven-excitation ratio, followed by the published systematic corrections. This is a revised analysis of the same acquisition, not a new independent experiment.

nodes.name: Static liquid pair structure and dynamic-correlation boundary
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected ambient-water structure analysis, the oxygen-oxygen pair-distribution function g_OO(r) describes a radial spatial correlation of oxygen positions. A distance-shell coordination is an integral of 4*pi*rho_O*r^2*g_OO(r) over stated radial bounds. It is distinct from a unique angular hydrogen-bond network, cluster identity or time correlation. In the selected dynamics model, C_n(t)=average P_n[u_OH(0) dot u_OH(t)] characterizes orientational decorrelation, while a completed hydrogen-bond partner exchange uses its own state definition and endpoint conditions. Static pair structure, orientational relaxation, exchange waiting time, angular-event duration and molecular persistence are different quantities.

nodes.name: Scoped liquid-water structure and dynamical-organization evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The selected ambient-water X-ray reanalysis supports finite ensemble-averaged radial oxygen shell structure under the reported conditions. A separate rigid-SPC/E simulation and jump/frame model supports a specified picture of hydrogen-bond acceptor exchange and orientational reconfiguration with distinct correlation time scales. Together these provide bounded positive structural and dynamical descriptions of a liquid, while retaining the distinction between measured-derived spatial correlations and computational trajectories. They establish neither universal self-organization, uniquely observed networks, obligatory crystal precursors nor necessary dispersion/hydrogen-bond/dipole fractions for all liquids.

nodes.name: Litvinov Pr140 charge-state storage and Schottky acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Produce 140Pr by fragmenting 152Sm projectiles at 508 MeV/u on a 1 g/cm^2 Be target, separate bare 59+, H-like 58+ and He-like 57+ charge states with the FRS, and inject them into the ESR under approximately 1e-11 mbar vacuum. Use stochastic and electron cooling near a stored-beam energy of 400 MeV/u, with an overall cooling time about 2 s. Record non-destructive time-resolved Schottky spectra: circulating ions induce pickup signals, Fourier spectra distinguish mass-to-charge peaks, and peak areas track stored populations. The example uses the 31st harmonic and averages each of 195 spectra over 10.5 s. Mechanical slits suppress feeding from other stored ions. Figure 2 time is laboratory time; the source uses gamma=1.43 to report rest-frame rates.

nodes.name: Reported charge-state-dependent Pr140 EC partial rates
nodes.shortDescription: The source Table I reports rest-frame partial constants in s^-1: bare 140Pr59+ lambda_betaPlus=0.00158(8), with no orbital-EC entry; H-like 140Pr58+ lambda_betaPlus=0.00161(10) and lambda_EC=0.00219(6); He-like 140Pr57+ lambda_betaPlus=0.00154(11) and lambda_EC=0.00147(7). The source EC ratio H-like/He-like is 1.49(8), despite reducing the bound-electron count from two to one. The beta+ values agree within their reported errors. The accompanying reported mean beam-loss constant is 0.0003(1) s^-1 and is not added to a nuclear partial rate as if it were another nuclear channel.

nodes.name: Conditional hyperfine interpretation of Pr140 EC enhancement
nodes.shortDescription: The source interprets the selected 140Pr nuclear-spin-1 to 140Ce spin-0 Gamow-Teller channel using H-like initial hyperfine F=1/2 or 3/2. In the allowed approximation only F=1/2 couples to the stated final nuclear-spin-0 plus neutrino-spin-1/2 state. With the source-assumed lower F=1/2 population, its statistical factor (2*I_i+1)/(2*F_i+1)=3/2 accounts for the enhanced H-like versus He-like EC rate. Thus electron occupancy alone is insufficient to specify the channel rate; nuclear/electronic angular momentum and state populations enter the interpretation.

nodes.name: Pr140/Ce140 Schottky intensity evolution
nodes.shortDescription: In the source Schottky sequence for H-like 140Pr58+, the assigned parent-frequency intensity decreases while the 140Ce58+ daughter intensity grows. The EC channel preserves ionic charge and gives an approximately 270 Hz frequency displacement at the 31st harmonic in the source example. These are mass-to-charge spectral assignments and time-dependent integrated intensities; nuclear partial decay constants require the separate population/loss fit.

nodes.name: Hybrid ground-state H2 dissociation energy
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports D0(H2)=36118.06962(37) cm^-1 for para-H2 X 1Sigma_g+ (v=0,N=0) relative to the separated H(1s)+H(1s) channel under its hyperfine conventions. The positive energy supplies a finite neutral-molecule binding result. It is a hybrid experimental/theoretical determination obtained through the ionization energy cycle; it is neither a directly scanned dissociation onset nor a measured energy release from a bond-forming event.

nodes.name: Assembled state-specific H2 ionization thresholds
nodes.shortDescription: The published interval assembly gives Ei(ortho-H2)=124357.23797(36) cm^-1 to the hyperfine center of the v+=0,N+=1 ionic level. Including the neutral N=1-to-0 interval 118.48684(10) cm^-1 and ionic N+=1-to-0 interval 58.2336751(1) cm^-1 gives Ei(para-H2)=124417.49113(37) cm^-1 for the ground-rovibrational neutral-to-ion threshold. The latter is an assembled threshold using the new optical measurement and the stated prior inputs.

nodes.name: Measured prepared-H2 EF-to-Rydberg interval
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports the ortho-H2 EF 1Sigma_g+ (v=0,N=1) to 54p1_1(0) interval as 25209.99756 +/- 0.00022 statistical +/- 0.00007 systematic cm^-1. The authors add these two final contributions linearly and quote 25209.99756(29) cm^-1. This calibrated state-labelled transition is the new measured interval; it is not by itself the ground-state ionization or dissociation energy.

nodes.name: Prepared H2 optical-transition acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the supplied supersonic H2 beam and two-step excitation: near-202 nm two-photon preparation from X 1Sigma_g+ (v=0,N=1) to EF 1Sigma_g+ (v=0,N=1), then near-397 nm excitation to the selected 54p1_1(0) Rydberg level. Delayed pulsed-field ionization yields detected H2+ signal versus frequency. Iodine references and a Fabry-Perot etalon calibrate the fundamental frequency; Gaussian fits and sixteen counterpropagating-beam pairs on four days determine line centers while cancelling the first-order Doppler offset. Amplifier, frequency-doubling, Stark and pressure contributions enter the source error budget.

nodes.name: H2+ readout after prepared-Rydberg field ionization
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected Liu H2 beam preparation, two-step laser excitation reaches Rydberg states below the specified ionic limit. A voltage pulse delayed by 150 ns after the 397 nm excitation ionizes and extracts H2+, which is detected by a microchannel plate. The resulting field-ionization spectrum records ion signal versus excitation wavenumber in arbitrary units. It supplies a positive source-specific ion-production/readout example; the ion signal is not itself the assembled ground-state ionization energy.

nodes.name: Local projective measurement marginals
nodes.shortDescription: For local projectors and the Born rule, sum_b tr[rho (P_a|x tensor Q_b|y)] = tr[rho (P_a|x tensor I)]. Thus the unconditioned marginal at A is independent of the chosen complete measurement at B.

nodes.name: Low-energy massive weak exchange
nodes.shortDescription: For the leading scalar denominator of a massive weak propagator, 1/(q^2-M_V^2)=-M_V^(-2)*[1+O(q^2/M_V^2)] when |q^2| is much smaller than M_V^2. With the declared charged-current normalization this yields the tree relation G_F/sqrt(2)=g^2/(8*M_W^2)=1/(2*v^2) for a local four-fermion approximation. Charged and neutral weak amplitudes retain their different currents; the contact description is distinct from a resonant production and decay process.

nodes.name: Marion Cs/Rb ground-state fountain comparison context
nodes.shortDescription: Use laser-cooled Cs133 and Rb87 atoms in their electronic ground states in the source fountain ensemble: Cs fountains FO1/FOM and a dual fountain DF operated alternately with Rb and Cs. Select mF=0 clock levels with microwave/laser pulses after0.3-0.6 s cooling and upward launch. Atoms undergo two Ramsey microwave interactions; fluorescence gives hyperfine-state populations and transition probability versus microwave detuning, and a digital servo locks the average microwave frequency. Microwave synthesizers share a100 MHz quartz signal phase-locked to one hydrogen-maser flywheel. Record overlapping fountain data within a few minutes to suppress shared-maser fluctuations, while keeping DF alternation and campaign-specific preparations.

nodes.name: Observational mass constraints
nodes.shortDescription: A mass adjustment relates measured frequency ratios to masses, binding energies and shared reference constants through explicit observational equations and covariance. Adjusted outputs do not supply additional independent acquisitions.

nodes.name: Replayed conditional mass arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Rounded historical inputs reproduce the reported Fink 2021 central mass ratio and direct-deuteron proton quotient; the two lower branch shifts are approximately -2.734 and -3.601 in units of the published 9e-12 mass-ratio uncertainty.

nodes.name: Conditional mass arithmetic replay
nodes.shortDescription: Convert the three printed frequency branches through the positive-binding mass balance and evaluate the printed direct-deuteron proton quotient.

nodes.name: Checked meson bookkeeping
nodes.shortDescription: Three rational matrix witnesses preserve scalar-plus-traceless reconstruction, idempotence and orthogonality. Nine q-qbar basis labels include three coincident zero-weight vectors. Three synthetic exposure cases recover the declared ratio only with the branch-weighted response and proper correction direction; Table 1 backgrounds sum 343 and 3750-343=3407.

nodes.name: Finite meson bookkeeping context
nodes.shortDescription: Check rational trace/traceless projectors and nine declared flavor weights; use an explicitly synthetic two-cascade response model to test efficiency, daughter-branching and common-exposure cancellation. Check only the printed 343 background sum and 3750-343=3407 subtraction.

nodes.name: Physical isoscalar meson mixing
nodes.shortDescription: The flavor-octet and singlet isoscalar basis vectors are (|u ubar>+|d dbar>-2|s sbar>)/sqrt(6) and (|u ubar>+|d dbar>+|s sbar>)/sqrt(3). Physical eta and eta-prime are rotated combinations, not exact octet/singlet labels. In the restricted flavor basis |eta>=cos(phi_P)*|q qbar>-sin(phi_P)*|s sbar> and |eta-prime>=sin(phi_P)*|q qbar>+cos(phi_P)*|s sbar>, with |q qbar>=(|u ubar>+|d dbar>)/sqrt(2) and theta_P=phi_P-arctan(sqrt(2)). Each ket labels a quark-antiquark basis state, not a subtraction or a complete observed particle population.

nodes.name: Metal cohesion relative to a declared neutral-atom reference
nodes.shortDescription: For the supplied periodic sodium calculation with N atoms per bulk unit cell, define positive cohesive energy per atom as E_coh=E_atom-E_bulk/N, relative to neutral isolated atoms computed with a compatible electronic method and reference. E_coh in eV/atom is a total-energy difference; the equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus come from a specified fitted energy-volume curve. Ground-state electronic cohesion, quasiparticle band energies and driven charge/heat transport are different quantities.

nodes.name: Metal spectral evidence and transport boundary
nodes.shortDescription: For the supplied sodium film, an ARPES map records photoelectron intensity versus binding energy and assigned crystal momentum. A near-Fermi-level intensity contour and a fitted occupied dispersion test a state-specific quasiparticle band description. Intensity, model-assisted momentum assignment, fitted bandwidth, comparison-dependent effective mass and macroscopic electrical/thermal transport remain distinct evidence roles; a spectral map is not a direct real-space electron-density image or a current measurement.

nodes.name: Metallic cohesion and electronic spectral evidence in declared sodium contexts
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed sources support two distinct finite metallic-sodium results: a supplied periodic electronic model predicts positive cohesion relative to neutral atoms, while a prepared sodium film has a near-Fermi photoemission contour and a source-inferred occupied quasiparticle band. Together these provide explicit energetic and spectral meanings for this selected metallic regime. Their agreement in material name does not turn band mobility into a measured cause of cohesion or supply conductivity, heat-flow and mechanical laws.

nodes.name: Molecular state, dissociation channel and formation distinction
nodes.shortDescription: A molecular binding statement must name the charge, isotope, internal state and separated-fragment channel. D0(H2) is the energy from its ground rovibrational level to two ground-state neutral hydrogen atoms; it differs from an electronic potential well depth and from total ionization to free nuclei and electrons. A measured transition between states of supplied H2 constrains an energy difference. It does not specify an association history, product yield, collision or radiation conditions, energy-disposal channel or molecular formation rate.

nodes.name: Molecular electric dipole and induced response
nodes.shortDescription: For a localized neutral molecular charge distribution in SI units, p=integral(rho(r)*r*d^3r) is an electric dipole moment in C m and does not depend on the coordinate origin. A state-specific body-fixed permanent moment can coexist with a zero laboratory vector average. Define electronic induced response at fixed state/geometry by delta p_i=alpha_ij*E_local,j to leading order; alpha_ij has SI units C m^2/V. Electronic deformation and field-dependent rotational orientation are separate contributions. A fixed dipole has field energy -p dot E; a reversible linear induced dipole has energy -(p dot E)/2.

nodes.name: Molecular-ion mass balance
nodes.shortDescription: A bound molecular-ion mass equals the masses of its free constituent nuclei and electrons minus positive binding energy divided by c^2. The energy must specify the electronic, vibrational, rotational and spin convention.

nodes.name: Scoped molecular dipole and polarization evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed sources support a selected KRb body-fixed moment with an explicit calibration correction, a distinct nitrogen pulse-driven angular response, and conditional molecular/ensemble definitions. These establish state- and preparation-specific dipolar response. The fixed-pair interaction and dilute constitutive law remain models; the selected experiments do not measure a collective dielectric curve, solvation structure, permanent field-free order or a universal emergence threshold.

nodes.name: Scoped molecular binding and spectroscopy evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The selected sources support finite molecular binding and discrete internal-state energy structure: a two-center electronic/nuclear model for one-electron molecular ions, a calibrated state-labelled optical interval in prepared H2, an assembled neutral ionization threshold and a hybrid dissociation energy relative to two hydrogen atoms. Existing H2+/HD+ theoretical ionization and HD+ mass records provide complementary state-conditional molecular-ion results. Isotope, charge, internal state and breakup channel identify each finite case; none of these prepared-molecule spectra or mass balances measures a universal molecular formation route.

nodes.name: Mooser reported proton magnetic moment
nodes.shortDescription: The 2014 author report gives statistical mu_p/mu_N=2.792847348(7) and corrected mu_p/mu_N=2.792847350(7)(6), with statistical then systematic uncertainty on the final digits. Its abstract combines these as 2.792847350(9).

nodes.name: Mooser double-trap moment campaign
nodes.shortDescription: Transport a cooled single proton between a strongly inhomogeneous analysis trap for spin identification and a precision trap for sideband/cyclotron measurements and spin drive. Fit the unbinned normalized spin-response resonance and correct its induced frequency biases.

nodes.name: Mossbauer spectral observable and vibrational-model boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Mossbauer transmission spectra record gamma attenuation as relative source/absorber velocity is varied. A fitted center shift, quadrupole splitting, linewidth and relative spectral area are inferred spectral parameters, distinct from a directly observed atomic geometry, absolute recoilless fraction or complete vibrational density of states. In the selected harmonic displacement convention, write f=exp(-k_gamma^2*mean(u_parallel^2)), where u_parallel is displacement projected along the gamma wave vector. In the selected Debye analysis, center shift contains isomer and second-order-Doppler contributions, while normalized thin-absorber area probes relative f. These two routes need not yield one identical effective Debye temperature.

nodes.name: Scoped bound-solid Mossbauer regime and evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The selected primary account and Fe-57 experiment support a finite Mossbauer regime: bound nuclear gamma transitions can contribute a zero-phonon resonant channel while conserving momentum, and finite-temperature transmission spectra provide model-dependent spectral and vibrational information. The observed amorphous absorber removes perfect periodic crystal order as a universal prerequisite. The declared source, nuclear transition, host, temperature, spectral model and inference limits determine the scope of this case.

nodes.name: Fermi coupling inferred from muon decay
nodes.shortDescription: Using the corrected muon-decay relation and assuming weak-interaction universality, the article infers G_F=1.1663788(7) x 10^-5 GeV^-2. The lifetime alone determines a muon-decay-specific coupling; universality is an additional assumption.

nodes.name: Positive-muon lifetime in R06
nodes.shortDescription: R06 lifetime: 2196979.9 ps with 2.5 ps statistical and 0.9 ps systematic uncertainties.

nodes.name: Positive-muon lifetime in R07
nodes.shortDescription: R07 lifetime: 2196981.2 ps with 3.7 ps statistical and 0.9 ps systematic uncertainties.

nodes.name: MuLan AK-3 preparation
nodes.shortDescription: R06 uses the AK-3 target, corrected positron-time histograms and the stated lifetime fit.

nodes.name: MuLan quartz preparation
nodes.shortDescription: R07 uses quartz, individual precession fits and the geometry-dependent relaxation analysis.

nodes.name: Combined positive-muon lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Combining R06 and R07 with the authors’ error matrix gives a positive-muon lifetime of 2196980.3 +/- 2.2 ps (1.0 ppm). The finite result contradicts an unrestricted assertion that all leptons are stable.

nodes.name: 1993 hydrogen-isotope masses
nodes.shortDescription: Table II(b) gives neutral-atom masses H 1.0078250317(7) u and D 2.0141017779(6) u after binding-energy corrections. The deuterium determination combines carbon comparisons using CD3+ and CD4+.

nodes.name: Nondoublet voltage-shift control
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 2 shows an approximately 3 ppb offset for N+ measured at its own PNP resonant voltage. The offset disappears at the stated precision when N+ evolves at the same 10 V setting as N2+ under the SOF protocol.

nodes.name: MIT unequal-voltage PNP control
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 2 measures N+ with the PNP method at its approximately 5 V resonant trap setting and compares it with common-voltage measurements at 10 V. The same diagnostic uses a 22.5 mV axial offset; an approximately 3 ppb shift remains for the unequal-voltage setting.

nodes.name: MIT common-voltage nondoublet measurements
nodes.shortDescription: The 8.5 T Penning trap at approximately 4.2 K measures single ions alternately. SOF stores the cyclotron phase difference in an amplitude under a common evolution voltage, then changes voltage for axial detection with a superconducting circuit (Q about 25000) and rf SQUID. Table II includes controls and carbon-referenced methane-ion comparisons.

nodes.name: Checked selected energies and vacuum phases
nodes.shortDescription: The 258 selected prompt energies span 2.61-7.95 MeV and sum to 1098.33 MeV; 61 entries are below 3.4 MeV prompt energy, consistently with the different neutrino-energy threshold. Printed background components sum to 17.79, and (258-17.8)/365.2=1201/1826 rounds to 0.658. Synthetic unitary witnesses preserve probability normalization, common-phase invariance and the two-flavor phase factor.

nodes.name: Neutrino oscillation evidence across preparations
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed KamLAND reactor disappearance, SNO active-flavor transformation, Super-Kamiokande atmospheric disappearance and OPERA accelerator tau-appearance results support flavor change compatible with their declared oscillation models across different preparations and responses. Their counts, fluxes, averaged probabilities and conditional fit parameters are distinct observables. This synthesis preserves those boundaries and supplies neither a pooled transition probability nor a new global fit.

nodes.name: Neutrino flavor and propagation bases
nodes.shortDescription: Use |nu_alpha>=sum_i U_alpha,i* |nu_i> for flavor states produced or detected through charged-current interactions. A closed two- or three-state unitary mixing model connects these labels to propagation mass eigenstates; the minimal massless Standard Model lepton classification alone does not supply neutrino masses.

nodes.name: Scoped neutrino mass and mixing evidence
nodes.shortDescription: KamLAND reactor spectral inference and the historical Super-Kamiokande atmospheric fit constrain their respective effective mass-squared differences and mixing amplitudes. SNO directly infers a joint non-electron active solar component; OPERA supports accelerator tau appearance and supplies a dependent full-mixing parameter comparison. These results support mass-induced flavor mixing within their stated models, while preserving distinct observables, preparations and inference assumptions.

nodes.name: Neutrino mass and mixing scope
nodes.shortDescription: The massive-neutrino description distinguishes charged-current flavor labels from propagation mass eigenstates and supplies a mixing matrix and mass-squared differences. Oscillation probabilities identify only restricted combinations under their preparation, propagation and response assumptions. Their structure requires an extension of the minimal massless-neutrino Standard Model, while its deeper mass-generation mechanism and parameter origin remain unspecified.

nodes.name: Neutrino mass-model boundary
nodes.shortDescription: With the usual fermion content, one Higgs doublet and no right-handed neutrino singlets, the minimal renormalizable Standard Model has no neutrino Dirac Yukawa term and leaves neutrinos massless. Formal extensions can add singlet neutrinos and Dirac masses, with total lepton number imposed to exclude Majorana terms, or allow lepton-number-violating Majorana masses. A dimension-five operator built from the lepton and Higgs doublets can instead generate a Majorana mass after electroweak symmetry breaking. These are alternative model constructions; flavor-oscillation evidence alone does not select one.

nodes.name: Coherent neutrino propagation in matter
nodes.shortDescription: For flavor amplitudes f, i*df/dx=H_f(x)*f with H_f=U diag(m_i^2) U-dagger/(2E)+diag(V_e(x),0,0), after removing a common identity term. For neutrinos V_e=sqrt(2)*G_F*n_e(x); for antineutrinos U is complex-conjugated and V_e changes sign. For neutrinos in neutral ordinary matter the active-sector neutral-current contribution is -G_F*n_n(x)/sqrt(2) times the identity and changes only a common phase; its sign also reverses for antineutrinos before removal.

nodes.name: Instantaneous matter mixing and adiabatic boundary
nodes.shortDescription: In the declared two-flavor approximation set A=2E*(V_e-V_x) and Delta_m=sqrt[(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)^2+(Delta*sin(2 theta))^2]. The eigenvalue gap is Delta_m/(2E), with cos(2 theta_m)=(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)/Delta_m and sin(2 theta_m)=Delta*sin(2 theta)/Delta_m. Nonzero mixing is maximal at A=Delta*cos(2 theta). An instantaneous eigenbasis has the additional connection -i*R-dagger*dR/dx; adiabatic following is an approximation that neglects its inter-state coupling relative to the gap.

nodes.name: Three-active-neutrino mixing parameterization
nodes.shortDescription: In a supplied closed unitary three-active-neutrino model, define U=R23 R13(delta) R12 P. Each real ij rotation acts on its plane with block [[cij,sij],[-sij,cij]] and as identity on the remaining direction, with cij=cos(thetaij) and sij=sin(thetaij); the 1-3 block is [[c13,s13 exp(-i delta)],[-s13 exp(i delta),c13]]. For generic three-mass mixing, charged-lepton and Dirac-neutrino rephasings leave three angles and one Dirac phase, with P=I. In the Majorana alternative use P=diag(exp(i eta1),exp(i eta2),1); these two extra column phases cancel from ordinary mass-induced flavor-oscillation probabilities.

nodes.name: Neutrino oscillation averaging
nodes.shortDescription: For a specified selected channel in a regime admitting a factored oscillation probability, define P_bar = integral dL dE w(L,E) P(L,E), with L>=0, E>0, w>=0 and integral w=1. The weight represents the stated source/baseline distribution and energy-dependent event response. Unresolved variation of the relative vacuum phase Delta m^2 L/(2E) can suppress the observed oscillatory pattern even when each production-propagation-detection contribution is coherent.

nodes.name: Neutrino production and detection coherence
nodes.shortDescription: Interfering neutrino mass alternatives must remain indistinguishable in the specified production and detection processes. In a declared apparatus frame, |Delta E_ik| << sigma_E and |Delta p_ik| << sigma_p describe a sufficient coherent regime within the reviewed localized-state treatment; the widths are intrinsic process uncertainties, not the beam energy spread or reconstructed-energy bin size.

nodes.name: Neutrino oscillation propagation scope
nodes.shortDescription: In the declared coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model, flavor-sensitive preparation and readout are related by interference between distinct mass propagation components. Their relative phases change transition probabilities as L/E varies; a probability is not a continuously measured sequence of flavor jumps. Oscillation is a conditional propagation phenomenon, not an additional bounded object or a universal property of every neutrino state.

nodes.name: Finite neutrino data and phase context
nodes.shortDescription: Bind the unchanged official data description and 258 prompt-energy rows; check their count, range and sum, printed background/survival arithmetic, and synthetic unitary two- and three-state vacuum phase identities in a declared convention. The executable owns only this finite calculation.

nodes.name: Astrophysical and cosmological transport boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Flavor evolution can affect the interpretation of an astrophysical neutrino signal, but a source-to-detector prediction also needs the emitted flavor composition and spectrum, propagation environment and flavor-dependent detector response. A prescribed coherent trajectory Hamiltonian alone does not supply collisional, absorptive, self-refracting or expanding-universe transport. This graph admits the propagation implication and explicitly excludes quantitative astrophysical transport and cosmological predictions from this reconstruction.

nodes.name: Coherent vacuum oscillation phase
nodes.shortDescription: In the coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum approximation with hbar=c=1, A_alpha-to-beta=sum_i U_beta,i exp[-i m_i^2 L/(2E)] U_alpha,i* and P=|A|^2. Antineutrinos replace U by U*. Relative phases use Delta m^2 L/(2E); the effective two-flavor survival probability is 1-sin^2(2 theta) sin^2[Delta m^2 L/(4E)]. A common mass-squared shift changes only a common phase.

nodes.name: Neutrino wave-packet overlap
nodes.shortDescription: For narrow, nondispersing vacuum packets, v_gi=p_i/E_i with E_i=sqrt(p_i^2+m_i^2). Interference involves the overlap of effective production/detection envelopes G_i(L-v_gi t). With v_g=(v_gi+v_gk)/2 and nonzero Delta v_g=|v_gi-v_gk|, l_coh approximately v_g sigma_x/Delta v_g is a separation scale: L << l_coh leaves that overlap unsuppressed, while substantial separation suppresses its interference term. The effective sigma_x includes both emission and detection coherence.

nodes.name: Finite neutron-response source and arithmetic findings
nodes.shortDescription: All 26 CLAS centers match the final-v2 vector figure within one plotting unit; the three Table III uncertainty decompositions reproduce their displayed totals. Literal GMn interpolation has a first-point central rounding mismatch but overlaps the reported GE display interval when gn rounding is retained. Two endpoint systematic errors remain inconsistent with the paper's stated relative range.

nodes.name: Finite neutron-response verification procedure
nodes.shortDescription: Check exact selected-source bytes and table census, final vector-plot identity, Table III quadrature and normalization arithmetic, and interpolation compatibility under printed rounding; preserve explicit discrepancy diagnostics.

nodes.name: Neutron mass from a nuclear mass balance
nodes.shortDescription: For nuclear rest masses, m_n=m_d-m_p+E_B(d)/c^2. Kessler implements the inference at the paper's precision with a hydrogen-isotope atomic-mass difference and the measured binding-energy mass equivalent.

nodes.name: Checked neutron-ratio correction and calibration arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: The 16 grouped table entries split into seven field-down and nine field-up cases. Subtracting the printed Table 1 shifts gives 3.8424583 and 3.8424562; the reported final error uses max(2.6,3.0)e-6. The adopted-reference product is 29.1647050759732 MHz/T, compatible with the displayed conditional result.

nodes.name: Printed neutron-ratio arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Check the 16 grouped run entries, printed directional correction arithmetic and the maximum-error rule; compare the adopted-reference product and explicitly conditional first-order uncertainty with the displayed result.

nodes.name: Neutron Sachs response and normalized electric/magnetic ratio
nodes.shortDescription: In the one-photon framework the unpolarized neutron response contains GE_n^2 and GM_n^2, while Riordan defines gn=mu_n*GE_n/GM_n for the polarized response. CLAS tabulates GM_n/(mu_n*GD), with GD=(1+Q2/(0.71 GeV2))^-2. These are different normalized quantities; gn is not the magnetic g factor.

nodes.name: Corrected selected-state KRb permanent moment
nodes.shortDescription: Ni et al. report B_Hz=1.1139(1) GHz and a body-fixed permanent-moment magnitude 0.566(17) D for 40K87Rb X1Sigma+ v=0, inferred from the N=0 Stark curve. The author thesis corrects the moment to 0.574(17) D after a plate-separation error. Use 1 D approximately 3.336e-30 C m. The N=2 curves test consistency within the same experiment.

nodes.name: Selected KRb dc Stark spectroscopy preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Supply optically trapped ultracold 40K87Rb molecules and use two-photon dark-resonance spectroscopy between weakly bound Feshbach and selected X1Sigma+ v=0 rotational states. Scan the external dc field over the reported approximately 0-2 kV/cm range using transparent plates outside a glass cell, and record resonance shifts relative to zero field. Rotational-state comparisons supply the rotational constant used in the singlet fit.

nodes.name: KRb singlet rotational Stark shifts
nodes.shortDescription: The selected KRb singlet v=0 N=0 resonance shifts downward with applied dc field, while the N=2 response splits by angular-momentum projection. The zero-field N=0/N=2 interval is reported as 6.6836(5) GHz. These are spectroscopic frequency differences, before identifying a body-fixed moment through a rotational model.

nodes.name: Nico beam acquisition and corrected analysis
nodes.shortDescription: Count released protons and downstream 6Li capture products in the June 2000-February 2001 acquisition, fit their rate ratio versus trap length, and apply the published background, transport and detector-loss corrections.

nodes.name: Published beam lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: The published Nico analysis reports 886.3+/-1.2 statistical +/-3.2 systematic seconds from the June 2000-February 2001 proton-counting beam acquisition.

nodes.name: Central thermal monitor response
nodes.shortDescription: The idealized monitor response epsilon_0(0,0) refers to a central pointlike beam at the 2200 m/s convention. Under inverse-velocity response, epsilon_0=epsilon_mono*lambda_0/lambda_mono before the stated spatial and finite-target normalization.

nodes.name: Finite-volume two-nucleon energy shift
nodes.shortDescription: At total momentum P=0 on a declared lattice, define DeltaE_X(L)=E_X(L)-2M_B(L), where E_X is the extracted energy in a specified two-nucleon channel and M_B is the rest energy of the degenerate octet baryon from the same theory and ensemble. Define the threshold deficit B_L=-DeltaE_X(L). The dimensionless lattice result b*DeltaE is converted to energy using the adopted lattice spacing; b is a length, not a baryon count.

nodes.name: Checked charge and color identities
nodes.shortDescription: The declared proton/neutron labels have charges +1/0 and baryon number 1; twelve pair insertions and two gluon insertions preserve their net labels while changing basis count. All 27 tensor components satisfy the determinant identity and the epsilon squared norm is 6. The first nonempty purely fundamental color-singlet tensor occurs at three factors within that restricted counting domain.

nodes.name: Declared charge and color algebra check
nodes.shortDescription: Use exact rational charge assignments and symbolic polynomials in nine independent matrix entries. Check pair/gluon charge preservation, the full epsilon determinant identity, its normalization and the center obstruction for one and two fundamental factors. No amplitudes or physical state probabilities are supplied.

nodes.name: Nucleon Fock-sector representation
nodes.shortDescription: In the specified light-front QCD framework, a proton eigenstate is expanded in quark-gluon Fock sectors with the same global quantum numbers, including uud and uudg sectors. The complete state sums amplitudes over sectors; restricting to a three-quark component is a truncation. Basis occupations, net flavor, color representation dimension and observed particles are different quantities.

nodes.name: Additional nucleon-ratio calibration
nodes.shortDescription: The reported nucleon QCD/QED component ratio supplements the lattice calculation with the experimental neutron-proton mass difference. This additional calibration input is separate from the primary mass and charge inputs used for the unconstrained isospin spectrum.

nodes.name: Nucleon valence quantum numbers
nodes.shortDescription: In the declared strong-interaction nucleon sectors, net flavor means quarks minus antiquarks: proton (N_u,N_d)=(2,1), neutron (1,2), with zero other net flavors. With B=sum_f N_f/3 and Q/e=sum_f q_f*N_f, these labels give B=1 and charges +1 and 0. Adding a same-flavor quark-antiquark pair or gluons preserves these additive labels without preserving total basis-particle count.

nodes.name: Ogi quartz resonance and mode-identification context
nodes.shortDescription: Use17 synthetic alpha-quartz specimens,15 from the source Z-growth regions and2 from X-growth regions, with source point group32 and dimensions about4.8 by5.2 by5.8 mm along the crystallographic axes. Measure free-vibration resonances on a needle-transducer tripod under approximately1 Pa vacuum at30 C, replacing each specimen between3 acquisitions. Use laser-Doppler displacement patterns for mode identification and72 identified resonance frequencies per specimen for a Rayleigh-Ritz inverse fit of6 elastic and2 piezoelectric coefficients. Supply the inherited fixed-strain dielectric ratios epsilon11/epsilon0=4.424 and epsilon33/epsilon0=4.632.

nodes.name: Historical Omega decuplet expectation
nodes.shortDescription: Keep the report's adopted missing decuplet slot separate from the selected event: I=0, Q=-1, S=-3, predicted J^P=3/2+ and mass about 1680 MeV/c^2. Figure 1 compares historical isomultiplet centers 1238,1385,1532 MeV/c^2 with that expectation.

nodes.name: Normalized one-photon wavepacket boundary
nodes.shortDescription: In the declared transverse-mode convention, let sum_r integral dPi_p |f_r(p)|^2=1 and sum_r integral dPi_p |p| |f_r(p)|^2 be finite. Define |1_f>=sum_r integral dPi_p f_r(p)a_r_dagger(p)|0>. The reviewed mode algebra gives unit norm and one quantum of N_0=sum_r integral dPi_p a_r_dagger(p)a_r(p). Free evolution replaces f_r(p) by exp(-i|p|t)f_r(p); it conserves N_0 within this supplied free Hamiltonian.

nodes.name: OPAL multijet acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use OPAL data within 3 GeV of the Z peak from 1991-1995: 4.1 million hadronic events before the additional selection, about 3.6 million retained, including about 250000 four-jet events. Require at least five accepted tracks and |cos(theta_thrust)|<0.9; combine matched tracks and calorimeter clusters. For angular observables use Durham y_cut=0.008 and each jet energy above 3 GeV.

nodes.name: OPAL corrected multijet distributions
nodes.shortDescription: Figures 1-2 report four normalized angular distributions (|cos(chi_BZ)|, |cos(Theta_NR)|, cos(Phi_KSW), cos(alpha_34)) and the Durham rates R4 and D2 after detector and hadronization correction to the declared parton-level convention. These six distributions come from the same selected OPAL sample; the 128-bin representation supplies 82 bins for the simultaneous fit.

nodes.name: OPAL jointly fitted color factors
nodes.shortDescription: OPAL reports C_A/C_F=2.25 +/- 0.08 statistical +/- 0.14 systematic and T_R/C_F=0.37 +/- 0.04 statistical +/- 0.06 systematic. With T_R=1/2, the same fit gives C_A=3.02 +/- 0.25 statistical +/- 0.49 systematic, C_F=1.34 +/- 0.13 statistical +/- 0.22 systematic and alpha_s(M_Z)=0.120 +/- 0.011 statistical +/- 0.020 systematic, compatible with the stated SU(3) expectations.

nodes.name: OPAL correlated color-factor fit
nodes.shortDescription: Fit eta=alpha_s*C_F/(2*pi), x=C_A/C_F and y=T_R/C_F simultaneously with MINUIT using 82 selected bins of six correlated observables. Use NLO O(alpha_s^3) four-jet angular predictions, NLO+NLL matched rates (R matching for R4, ln R matching for D2), five massless quark flavors and default mu/sqrt(s)=1. Convert the fitted ratios to C_A, C_F and alpha_s(M_Z) with the normalization T_R=1/2.

nodes.name: OPAL detector and hadronization correction
nodes.shortDescription: Correct each measured bin using C_det=H_MC/D_MC and C_had=P_MC/H_MC, so D_corr=C_det*C_had*D_meas. Use JETSET 7.4 matrix-element events with Lund fragmentation for four-jet angles and its parton shower for the jet rates, followed by OPAL detector simulation and the data selection.

nodes.name: OPERA accelerator beam and analyzed selection
nodes.shortDescription: Use the 2008–2012 CNGS exposure of 17.97e19 protons on target, with a predominantly muon-neutrino beam over 730 km and mean energy about 17 GeV. From target-fiducial interactions, analyze the first and second most probable bricks for 0-muon events and 1-muon events with p_mu<15 GeV/c under the stated timing, tracking and vertex procedures.

nodes.name: OPERA fully analyzed event sample
nodes.shortDescription: The reported exposure produces 19505 neutrino interactions in the target fiducial volume. Table I gives 5408 fully analyzed selected events: 1144 classified 0-muon and 4264 classified 1-muon with p_mu<15 GeV/c. These are the specified first/second-brick analysis samples.

nodes.name: OPERA reported accelerator tau appearance
nodes.shortDescription: The original channel-based tests report a one-sided significance of 5.1 standard deviations, with the Fisher-method background-fluctuation probability 1.1e-7; the profile-likelihood implementations also report 5.1. Under the stated beam, response and background model, the selected decay candidates support tau-neutrino appearance in the CNGS beam.

nodes.name: OPERA tau-decay candidate census
nodes.shortDescription: For tau-to-1h, tau-to-3h, tau-to-muon and tau-to-electron, Table III reports candidate counts 3,1,1,0, respectively, totaling five. This includes the new fifth event and four previously reported candidates from the same accelerator campaign.

nodes.name: OPERA conditional signal and background means
nodes.shortDescription: In the four-channel order, Table III gives signal expectations 0.52 +/-0.10, 0.73 +/-0.14, 0.61 +/-0.12, 0.78 +/-0.16, and background expectations 0.04 +/-0.01, 0.17 +/-0.03, 0.004 +/-0.001, 0.03 +/-0.01. Reported totals are 2.64 +/-0.53 signal and 0.25 +/-0.05 background, under the adopted response and nominal oscillation parameters.

nodes.name: OPERA fifth reconstructed tau-decay candidate
nodes.shortDescription: The 14 August 2012 event has a reconstructed 90 +/-2 mrad kink and flight length 960 +/-30 micrometers; the daughter undergoes a hadronic interaction. Its measured central kinematics satisfy the predefined tau-to-1h cuts, including daughter momentum 11(+14/-4) GeV/c and zdec=630 +/-30 micrometers. The stated secondary-vertex fragment and attached-photon searches find none.

nodes.name: OPERA original channel likelihood and interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Use four channel counts with independent Poisson means mu*s_i+beta_i and the Gaussian background factors of Equation 1. Compare Fisher-product and one-sided profile-likelihood statistics with their pseudoexperiment distributions for background-only mu=0. Use the same acquisition for nominal-signal compatibility and the full-mixing mass-squared interval.

nodes.name: OPERA same-data signal and mass-squared interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: The same analysis reports signal strength mu=1.8(+1.8/-1.1) at 90% confidence, compatible with nominal mu=1. Assuming full mixing, it reports Delta m23^2=3.3e-3 eV^2 with 90% interval [2.0,5.0]e-3 eV^2; the three stated interval methods give negligible differences.

nodes.name: OPERA reconstruction and expected-count conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Use emulsion vertex/track reconstruction, multiple-scattering momentum estimates and muon identification with the stated scanning and decay-selection response. Model signal and charm, hadronic-reinteraction and large-angle-muon-scattering backgrounds using the reported simulation and auxiliary checks, normalized to detected muon-neutrino interactions. Preserve the earlier method erratum.

nodes.name: Conditional optical anticorrelation criterion
nodes.shortDescription: The estimator is alpha=p_c/(p_t*p_r)=N_c*N_1/(N_t*N_r). For the same ensemble of gates, the tested semiclassical model uses a nonnegative gate-averaged incident intensity, fixed splitter/output efficiencies and the linear low-detection-probability response p_t=a_t*w*<i>, p_r=a_r*w*<i>, p_c=a_t*a_r*w^2*<i^2>. Cauchy-Schwarz gives alpha>=1. The published quantum cascade model instead gives alpha=[2*f(w)*N*w+(N*w)^2]/[f(w)+N*w]^2, including accidental cascades.

nodes.name: Optical-channel observable and inference boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Specify a channel input, medium, path/boundaries and receiver acceptance before interpreting transmitted optical flux. Separate a complex field transfer and its phase from an aggregate transmission measurement; separate intensity attenuation in m^-1 from dimensionless transmission and absorptance. Refractive redirection, absorption, angular redistribution, dispersion, diffraction and statistical coherence require their own stated variables and approximations rather than one universal medium-transformation label.

nodes.name: Optical gate and detector response
nodes.shortDescription: Time-to-amplitude converters and thresholds select output detections after a trigger; the two gates are superimposed within 0.1 ns and monitored by a third converter. The source excitation rate is stabilized within a few percent. Collection solid angle, optical transmission and detector efficiency enter the global efficiencies. In the published cascade model, f(w) combines 1-exp(-w/tau_s) with an angular-correlation factor, while N*w accounts for other cascades within the gate.

nodes.name: Scoped material optical-channel evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The existing IR-window experiment supplies a finite measured transmission response under its stated sample and collection conditions. A separately declared homogeneous linear field model makes attenuation and phase conventions explicit and distinguishes dispersive response from absorption. This supports a bounded optical-channel description while retaining the gap between aggregate flux and a uniquely identified bulk propagation, scattering, imaging or coherence operator.

nodes.name: Orbital electron capture and charge-state boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Orbital electron capture consumes a bound electron in a specified nuclear transition and emits an electron neutrino; in the selected 140Pr to 140Ce channel it converts a proton to a neutron, preserves mass number A=140 and lowers nuclear charge Z from 59 to 58. Initial bare 140Pr59+, hydrogenlike 140Pr58+ and heliumlike 140Pr57+ carry zero, one and two bound electrons respectively. EC removes one bound electron while lowering Z by one, so the daughter ionic charge remains the same. Changing the initial ionization state does not change which parent isotope is prepared; the subsequent nuclear decay does change the element.

nodes.name: Oscillation mass identifiability
nodes.shortDescription: In the leading coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model with hbar=c=1, hold U, L and E fixed. Replacing every m_i^2 by m_i^2+kappa multiplies A_alpha-to-beta by exp[-i kappa L/(2E)], leaving P=|A|^2 unchanged. This holds for shifts preserving m_i^2+kappa>=0 and (m_i^2+kappa)/E^2<<1. For three nonnegative squared masses, Delta21=m_2^2-m_1^2 and Delta31=m_3^2-m_1^2 both nonzero and unequal imply three pairwise distinct values; at most one can be zero, so at least two masses are nonzero.

nodes.name: Channel-specific partial lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: For a specified decay channel with branching fraction B, the partial decay rate is Gamma_channel=B/tau and its inverse is the partial lifetime tau/B. A search constrains that channel rate through exposure, signal efficiency and background.

nodes.name: Prepared PTFE out-of-plane radiometry context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the source ROSI under-illumination method: measure the entire incident-beam flux with the sample translated out, then the reflected flux in the selected viewing aperture with the sample in place. Normalize receiver/monitor signals and relative gain/sensitivity settings and apply finite-aperture/collection corrections. For the selected sintered PTFE scan use 550 nm illumination, incident azimuth180 degrees and incident polar angles70 to0 degrees; the actual viewing polar angle is45 degrees with azimuth90 or135 degrees. The white and gray targets have nominal vendor directional-hemispherical reflectances99 and10 percent, not prescribed constant bidirectional factors.

nodes.name: Source-reported finite benzene valence-bond energy lowering
nodes.shortDescription: Under the declared source model, W=Q+(sqrt(13)-1)*J_ex is approximately Q+2.6055*J_ex, while W_single=Q+1.5*J_ex for one Kekule function. Thus Delta W=W-W_single is approximately 1.1055*J_ex<0 for J_ex<0; the positive stabilization magnitude is -1.1055*J_ex. The source gives the unnormalized eigenfunction proportional to Psi_A+Psi_B+0.4341*(Psi_C+Psi_D+Psi_E). Table I also reports Q+2.4*J_ex for the two-Kekule restriction. These are positive finite results of the specified many-electron model and reference comparison.

nodes.name: Historical six-electron benzene calculation context
nodes.shortDescription: Supply a neutral planar six-carbon benzene framework with one active perpendicular p-like electron/orbital per carbon. Treat its six-electron spin-coupling problem with the two Kekule and three Dewar-type canonical functions. Omit in-plane/core contributions as common terms in the comparison, neglect the stated orbital overlap/exchange terms except equal nearest-neighbor exchange, and retain the nonorthogonal canonical-function secular matrix. Solve the five-function model for its stationary lowest energy and compare with restrictions to one or two Kekule functions using the same parameters. This records the source calculation, not a new solver execution.

nodes.name: Charge-aware cyclotron comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The free cyclotron frequency obeys omega_c^2=omega_plus^2+omega_z^2+omega_minus^2 in the stated Penning-trap treatment. A frequency ratio yields a mass-to-charge ratio, with charge state and magnetic-field drift handled explicitly.

nodes.name: Electrode image-charge correction
nodes.shortDescription: The ion induces charge on trap electrodes; the resulting field shifts the measured motion. A correction to the free cyclotron estimate must specify the field model, units and whether it maps ideal to measured or measured to ideal frequency.

nodes.name: Image-charge geometry model
nodes.shortDescription: A finite-element or semianalytical boundary-value model predicts the local image field for a specified electrode geometry. Geometry tolerances, fitted gradients and numerical convergence limit its frequency correction.

nodes.name: Magnetron image-charge control
nodes.shortDescription: Two separated radial pulses encode the magnetron phase in a classical motional amplitude. A changed electrostatic readout potential maps that amplitude to an axial-frequency shift; comparing single ions then constrains the image-charge contribution.

nodes.name: Driven-motion mass extrapolation
nodes.shortDescription: A phase-sensitive cyclotron comparison is extrapolated to zero deliberate excitation using a joint quadratic fit in the two species excitation strengths. Thermal-motion and apparatus corrections remain necessary.

nodes.name: Common-voltage SOF protocol
nodes.shortDescription: Two separated cyclotron pulses encode the frequency in a classical amplitude while the compared ions evolve under the same trap voltage. The voltage changes afterward to bring the axial mode into resonance for detection.

nodes.name: Reported arm-dependent Na atom-surface fringe phase
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports an approximately 0.3 rad relative fringe-phase displacement when G4 is inserted in one Na interferometer arm, with the sign reversed on inserting it in the other arm. The scale is described as about a 5 nm fringe displacement at 100 nm grating period. Nonzero fringe contrast remains for atoms transmitted through the supplied channels. This is an interaction-sensitive matter-wave phase observation, not a direct force trace or an event forming a molecular or ionic bond.

nodes.name: Conditional nonretarded Na/surface phase comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The source finds the sign of the arm-dependent phase consistent with an attractive Na/surface potential and reports approximate magnitude and slight velocity-trend agreement with its nonretarded prediction using adopted C3=3 meV*nm^3. This is a conditional comparison of the measured phase with a supplied finite-channel interaction model. It is not a newly fitted C3, a measurement of an atom-pair C6, a retarded-law test or an independent repetition of the phase acquisition.

nodes.name: Na/silicon-nitride relative-phase acquisition context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the reported oven-generated Na beam near 2 km/s, collimated by two 10 micrometer slits separated by 1 m, in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer made from three 100 nm-period silicon-nitride gratings. Insert an additional grating G4 with 50 nm-wide and 150 nm-long channels into either arm or out of the paths. Scan the third grating to read fringe phase and contrast; use the co-propagating optical interferometer for vibration compensation. Alternate test/control positions at 50 s intervals and subtract a fifth-order polynomial fit to control-phase drift. Keep the diffraction-order response and the separate statistical/systematic errors in the interpretation.

nodes.name: Perturbative QED amplitude convention
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected QED scattering construction, a perturbative amplitude combines the required terms for specified external states and interaction order before a transition probability is formed. Alternatives can interfere; for identical electrons the direct and exchanged two-electron amplitudes are antisymmetrized.

nodes.name: Scoped thermodynamic phase-regime organization
nodes.shortDescription: The selected literature supports a finite phase-regime organization in the specified hard-disk model: distinct liquid, hexatic and solid regimes, first-order coexistence and a continuous upper ordering transition under its declared density scan. Separate Al-Mn treatment observations support protocol-dependent metastability. Bulk equilibrium/coexistence conditions provide a formal interpretation boundary, while the reused ambient-water structure and dynamics records describe one liquid regime without measuring its transition boundaries. These cases support thermodynamic organization with stability and kinetic distinctions, rather than a universal material map or mandatory crystal-liquid-colloid ancestry.

nodes.name: Phase stability, criticality, kinetics and observable boundary
nodes.shortDescription: A phase-regime claim must specify its system, conserved composition, ensemble or contact constraints, control range and criterion for identifying phases. Local resistance to continuous perturbations is distinct from stability against formation of a different phase; kinetic persistence can occur without global thermodynamic stability. The selected Gibbs fluid critical endpoint is where two coexisting phases become indistinguishable, and is not a universal criterion for every continuous ordering transition. Finite-system coexistence/interface effects, structural correlations, annealing persistence and simulated molecular reorientation are different observables and inferences, rather than interchangeable phase-boundary measurements.

nodes.name: Scoped photon evidence comparison
nodes.shortDescription: The triggered optical coincidence summary and response-conditioned anticorrelation support nonclassical counting in one named preparation. Capture-photon wavelength and the corrected meson radiative ratio separately constrain their declared emission observables. This comparison preserves formal photon-state conventions, detector response and dependent analysis stages instead of treating them as one universal photon-property measurement.

nodes.name: Photon state and evidence scope
nodes.shortDescription: In the declared unbroken electromagnetic U(1) gauge model, constrained free Maxwell modes define two transverse bosonic photon polarizations, formal zero mass and neutral gauge-field transformation. A one-photon wavepacket additionally requires a specified free-state normalization and preparation boundary. Optical counting, radiation observables and internal electromagnetic mediation are distinct evidence and description roles.

nodes.name: Photon polarization state and response boundary
nodes.shortDescription: In the specified free Maxwell theory, fix an inertial frame, hbar=c=1 and nonzero momentum p. Locally choose a real transverse basis E(p)=(epsilon_1,epsilon_2), with E^T E=I and p^T E=0. For the existing one-photon wavepacket use dPi_p=d^3p/(2pi)^3 and f_r(p)=g(p)c_r(p), where c_dagger c=1 on the nonzero support of g, integral dPi_p |g|^2=1 and integral dPi_p |p| |g|^2 is finite. Its complex polarization vector is e(p)=E(p)c(p), so p dot e=0 and e_dagger e=1. Here e is a polarization amplitude, not the mean electric field, which vanishes in this one-photon number state. A passive real O(p) in SO(2) gives E'=E O, c'=O^T c and f'=O^T f in the transformed mode convention; transforming creation operators consistently preserves e and the one-photon state. An active polarization comparison instead fixes the basis and apparatus while varying relative coefficients. Both transverse modes have the same free frequency |p|; this model supplies no polarization-dependent propagation splitting or preferred vacuum axis.

nodes.name: PIENU stopped-pion acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Stop a 75 MeV/c positive-pion beam in the scintillator target. Use the stated positron triggers, extra-activity rejection and 60 mm tracking fiducial cut. The energy plot uses a 5-35 ns region; the low/high timing samples use their specified trigger streams and a 52 MeV split.

nodes.name: PIENU corrected inclusive pion ratio
nodes.shortDescription: After the published Table I corrections, PIENU reports R_e/mu=(1.2344 +/- 0.0023 statistical +/- 0.0019 systematic) x 10^-4 for the inclusive electronic-to-muonic pion partial-rate ratio.

nodes.name: PIENU acceptance and tail correction
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the Table I multiplicative factors to the raw fitted ratio: acceptance 0.9991 +/- 0.0003, tail 1.0316 +/- 0.0012 and other 1.0004 +/- 0.0008. Retain the empirical upper/lower tail construction and simulation dependence. A dedicated 70 MeV/c positron-beam sample in a simplified setup constrains the upper tail; 10-70 MeV/c positron-beam and stopped-muon controls constrain timing response. These auxiliary preparations supply response inputs rather than a new pion ratio.

nodes.name: PIENU simultaneous timing inference
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the low/high timing samples together with L1-L3 and H1-H6 components, a common fixed time origin and the declared nuisance treatment. Use -290 to 520 ns while excluding -19 to 4 ns; preserve the same acquisition and pre-unblinding choice of cuts and corrections.

nodes.name: PIENU ratio before acceptance and tail correction
nodes.shortDescription: The simultaneous timing fit reports R_raw=(1.1972 +/- 0.0022 statistical +/- 0.0005 systematic) x 10^-4, with chi-square per degree of freedom 1.02 for 673 degrees of freedom. It is a fitted same-acquisition intermediate result.

nodes.name: PIENU selected positron energy and time spectra
nodes.shortDescription: Figure 2 reports the selected calorimeter-energy distributions before and after background-suppression cuts. Figure 3 reports the low/high timing distributions separated at 52 MeV, with fitted component curves shown separately. These distinguish direct electronic-pion candidates from the pion-muon-positron chain within the declared response and background model.

nodes.name: Scoped piezoelectric response and demonstrated ferroelectric switching
nodes.shortDescription: The quartz study supplies a finite resonance-based piezoelectric tensor inference, while a separate oriented AlScN film study supports accessible polarization reversal through corrected electrical response and polarity-sensitive controls, with an effective transverse coefficient sign change. These retain actual electromechanical coupling and prepared ferroelectric states without equating symmetry compatibility, spontaneous polarization and demonstrated switching or asserting universal transition, memory or parent-population laws.

nodes.name: State- and boundary-specific piezoelectric tensor convention
nodes.shortDescription: For the declared isothermal uniform bulk linear response, the proper piezoelectric stress tensor is e_ijk=(partial D_i/partial strain_jk) at fixed E,T, equivalently -(partial stress_jk/partial E_i) at fixed strain,T. Its SI units are C/m^2. The piezoelectric strain tensor d relates strain to electric field at fixed stress,T or displacement D to stress at fixed E,T, with units m/V, equivalently C/N. Converting between e and d requires elastic compliance and matching tensor/shear conventions; they are not interchangeable numerical coefficients.

nodes.name: Checked PIENU printed ratio arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: The printed central correction gives 1.1972*0.9991*1.0316*1.0004=1.2344135596286528 in units of 10^-4, which rounds to the reported 1.2344. A positive-factor display-rounding box overlaps the reported display bin. Thirty-two synthetic efficiency/exposure witnesses preserve the ratio under common exposure, while unequal exposure does not cancel; distinct synthetic absolute branching allocations retain the same ratio.

nodes.name: Finite PIENU correction arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Check the printed PIENU Table I correction product and its display-rounding bounds. Use synthetic forward signal counts to test common-exposure and efficiency cancellation and demonstrate that a two-channel rate ratio alone does not identify absolute branching fractions.

nodes.name: Photon-inclusive pion partial-rate ratio
nodes.shortDescription: Define R_e/mu=Gamma(pi+ -> e+ nu(gamma))/Gamma(pi+ -> mu+ nu(gamma)), with associated radiative pion decays included in each partial rate. The dimensionless ratio compares two specified channels; a total decay rate is not measured by this ratio alone.

nodes.name: Planck selected angular-spectrum estimates
nodes.shortDescription: The reported data products are angular temperature and E-polarization spectrum estimates: Commander TT and SimAll EE for 2 <= ell <= 29, and Plik per-frequency half-mission TT, TE and EE cross-spectra at higher multipoles. The high-multipole union is TT 30-2508 and TE/EE 30-1996, with narrower pair-specific cuts. These response-conditioned angular correlations are distinct from a primordial curvature spectrum or an observed quantum-vacuum realization.

nodes.name: Planck selected CMB observation
nodes.shortDescription: The 2018 release reprocesses full-mission Planck intensity and linear-polarization maps. The selected high-multipole sample uses 100, 143 and 217 GHz HFI half-mission cross-spectra; low-E uses the 100 x 143 GHz full-mission polarization cross-spectrum, with low-temperature Commander estimates. The low-E cleaning uses 353 GHz dust templates and a 30 GHz synchrotron template at 100 GHz. This is selection from an existing sky observation, not a new 2018 experimental preparation.

nodes.name: Planck spectral response and foreground model
nodes.shortDescription: Commander jointly models low-temperature foregrounds and the CMB. SimAll uses foreground-cleaned 100 x 143 GHz quasi-QML polarization estimates and simulation-based probabilities. High-multipole Plik uses masked, beam-corrected half-mission cross-spectra with noise/covariance models and foreground, calibration, polarization-efficiency and temperature-to-polarization leakage treatment. Its covariance retains correlations between frequency pairs and TT, TE and EE using a fiducial model. Cross-spectra reduce additive noise bias only insofar as the split-map noises are uncorrelated.

nodes.name: Planck base-model primordial inference
nodes.shortDescription: The selected analysis assumes spatially flat base LambdaCDM with purely adiabatic scalar P_R(k)=A_s*(k/k_*)^(n_s-1), k_*=0.05 Mpc^-1. CAMB (August 2017) maps this prescribed initial spectrum and the adopted background, matter and thermal history to lensed CMB spectra; CosmoMC (July 2018) samples the six-parameter posterior. The base parameters are baryon and cold-dark-matter densities, theta_MC, tau, ln(10^10 A_s) and n_s, with flat base priors; the amplitude prior is 1.61 < ln(10^10 A_s) < 3.91. The adopted neutrino model has two massless states and one 0.06 eV state, BBN-predicted helium and the stated tanh reionization history. The likelihood multiplies Commander low-T, SimAll low-E and high-multipole Plik, exploring the allowed nuisance parameters jointly.

nodes.name: Planck conditional scalar amplitude and tilt
nodes.shortDescription: For TT,TE,EE+lowE in that base model, Planck reports n_s=0.9649 +/- 0.0044 and ln(10^10 A_s)=3.045 +/- 0.016, each as a marginalized 68 percent interval at k_*=0.05 Mpc^-1. These are the selected joint column of VI Table 2 and X Table 2, with the tilt also stated in X Equation 10. The amplitude and tilt are inferred primordial-spectrum parameters, conditional on the specified transfer model, likelihood and priors.

nodes.name: Specified fixed electric dipole pair interaction
nodes.shortDescription: For two specified, fixed electric dipoles separated by r much larger than their charge-distribution sizes, the leading electrostatic interaction is U=[p1 dot p2-3*(p1 dot r_hat)*(p2 dot r_hat)]/(4*pi*epsilon0*r^3). Its sign depends on orientation. This is a vacuum point-dipole approximation with moments in C m, distance in m and energy in J.

nodes.name: Sodium occupied quasiparticle-band inference
nodes.shortDescription: Fitting the same source ARPES data, shown over the reported 0.103-2.263 eV energy interval, to a finite-resolution spectral function with E(k)=W-gamma1*k^2-gamma2*k^4 gives the occupied bandwidth W=2.78 eV. Comparing with the supplied LDA bandwidth W_LDA=3.18 eV gives the source parabolic-band mass-renormalization estimate m*/m0=1.14. The inferred occupied quasiparticle bandwidth is not the cohesive energy per atom, and the LDA comparison is not a second independent experimental acquisition.

nodes.name: Potorochin sodium film ARPES preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Evaporate sodium onto cleaned W(110) held at 20 K, anneal the sample for 15 minutes at room temperature, then measure the approximately 15 nm Na(110) film at 20 K under a base pressure better than 6e-11 mbar. Use horizontally polarized 70 eV photons for the selected maps, the source Scienta R8000/R4000 analyzers at the respective beamlines, 30 meV energy resolution and 0.2 degree angular setting. The source uses photon-energy-dependent spectra to assign the measured normal-momentum plane near Gamma; the Fermi-level map integrates an approximately 0.015 eV energy window and is symmetrized about kx=0.

nodes.name: Sodium film energy-momentum and near-Fermi intensity
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Na(110) energy-momentum map shows a dispersing occupied intensity feature approaching the Fermi level.
