The source near-Fermi map is nearly circular in the assigned kx-ky plane, with reported ky Fermi wave vector about 0.91 inverse Angstrom. A separate photon-energy scan fitted in Appendix A yields an average about 0.88 inverse Angstrom and maximum near 69 eV photons; these are separate reported cuts/assignments, not a single exact universal radius.

nodes.name: Conditional primordial-spectrum and CMB compatibility
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE chain compares measured angular temperature/polarization statistics with a flat base-LambdaCDM transfer and likelihood model and infers its power-law scalar amplitude and tilt. The admitted quantum single-field construction is a conditional way to supply primordial curvature power with which such data can be compared. The parameter fit does not identify an inflaton potential, measure its initial quantum state, or uniquely prove inflationary quantum generation.

nodes.name: Conditional primordial curvature spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: Choose vhat(eta,x)=integral d^3k/(2pi)^3 [a_k u_k(eta) exp(i k.x)+h.c.], [a_k,a_q^dagger]=(2pi)^3 delta^3(k-q), a_k|0>=0, and u_k u_k*'-u_k* u_k'=i. In an early adiabatic regime with omega_k^2=k^2-z''/z>0, |omega_k'/omega_k^2|<<1 and k^2>>|z''/z|, choose u_k approximately exp(-ik eta)/sqrt(2k). With R(x)=integral d^3k/(2pi)^3 R_k exp(i k.x), define <R_k R_q>=(2pi)^3 delta^3(k+q)(2pi^2/k^3) P_R(k), so P_R=k^3|u_k/z|^2/(2pi^2). For the selected initial state and a slow-roll attractor with epsilon_H<<1 and |dot(epsilon_H)/(H epsilon_H)|<<1, the late growing-mode power is approximately [H^2/(8pi^2 epsilon_H M_pl^2)] evaluated at k=aH.

nodes.name: Specified primordial nuclear reaction network
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected homogeneous hot-expanding model, weak neutron/proton interconversion, expansion and thermodynamics set a reaction history for free nucleons and light nuclei. Abundances may be expressed per baryon as Y_i=n_i/n_b; a nuclear species balance has dilution dn_i/dt+3*H*n_i and a sum of reaction production and destruction terms. The deuterium photodissociation bottleneck delays effective light-nucleus assembly; nuclear reactions then produce deuterium, helium-3 and helium-4 and mass-seven species including beryllium-7, which later feeds lithium-7. These model equations require a supplied cosmological background, baryon density, weak rates, neutron lifetime and thermonuclear cross sections.

nodes.name: Conditional primordial-origin model
nodes.shortDescription: A primordial quantum-origin model supplies a curved cosmological background, field/gravity action, canonical scalar mode, initial state and validity regime. The admitted linear single-field construction predicts a conditional curvature two-point function, with restricted long-wave conservation and stochastic interpretation. Testing its primordial power against CMB statistics additionally requires a postinflationary transfer model, instrument/foreground response and cosmological likelihood. Compatibility of that chain is not a direct measurement of the assumed initial vacuum or a unique origin mechanism.

nodes.name: Entanglement with a projective local model
nodes.shortDescription: Werner constructs entangled mixed states on C^d tensor C^d, d >= 2, that admit a local hidden-variable model for all local projective measurements. Entanglement and Bell nonlocality are distinct conditions.

nodes.name: Replayed proton-decay bookkeeping
nodes.shortDescription: Printed phase exposures sum to 450.7 kton-years; phase-weighted efficiencies agree with the text within displayed precision, and rounding intervals admit the reported background totals. At fixed background mean 0.94, P(N>=1)=0.609372..., which rounds to the reported 60.9 percent.

nodes.name: Rounded proton-decay table arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Evaluate hand-transcribed phase exposure sums, weighted efficiencies, censored background rounding intervals and the fixed-mean Poisson probability of at least one event.

nodes.name: Checked proton-moment printed arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: The printed Schneider corrections sum to -133 ppt and their systematic uncertainty bounds sum linearly to 123 ppt. The quoted 75 and 34 final-digit errors combine quadratically to 82.3468... final-digit units, compatible with the abstract error 82. Central correction arithmetic does not exactly recover the final displayed digit, but conservative input-rounding bins overlap.

nodes.name: Spin-to-free-cyclotron frequency ratio
nodes.shortDescription: For the stated same-field proton measurement, g_p/2=nu_L/nu_c and nu_c^2=nu_plus^2+nu_z^2+nu_minus^2. The ideal frequency ratio connects spin response to the free cyclotron motion; finite-trap corrections remain preparation dependent.

nodes.name: Proton magnetic-moment unit convention
nodes.shortDescription: For the positive spin-1/2 proton, mu_N=e*hbar/(2*m_p) and mu_p/mu_N=g_p/2. In the Sachs convention, GM(0) equals this dimensionless moment in nuclear-magneton units; this specifies normalization without supplying a measured numerical value.

nodes.name: Printed proton-moment arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Evaluate formal free-frequency and same-clock identities, printed campaign counts, bias/correction directions, and rounded systematic/error sums without fitting experimental spectra.

nodes.name: Quantum chromodynamics field specification
nodes.shortDescription: QCD is the SU(3) color gauge sector with quark fields in the fundamental representation and gluon fields in the adjoint representation. Its Lagrangian specifies quark-gluon interactions and non-Abelian gluon self-interactions.

nodes.name: Gauge and fermion beta-function contributions
nodes.shortDescription: With d alpha_s/d ln(mu_R^2) = -b0 alpha_s^2 + O(alpha_s^3), b0=(11 C_A-4 n_f T_R)/(12 pi). For SU(3) fundamental Dirac quarks, C_A=3 and T_R=1/2, so b0=(33-2 n_f)/(12 pi). The gauge contribution and fermion contribution have opposite signs.

nodes.name: QCD effective flavor content and matching
nodes.shortDescription: A perturbative QCD coupling is specified for an effective theory with n_f light flavors. Couplings in theories with n_f and n_f+1 light flavors are related by threshold matching, with coefficients depending on the mass and renormalization prescriptions.

nodes.name: Specified QCD-to-nuclear-energy map
nodes.shortDescription: A QCD-to-nuclear-energy calculation declares its color gauge theory, quark-mass parameters, regulator, scale calibration, interpolating operators and energy-extraction procedure. Binding compares a specified nuclear channel with its compatible hadronic threshold, after state and volume inference. A calculation at one input point is a conditional result, not a measured derivative with respect to a renormalized quark mass or a complete prediction for bulk matter.

nodes.name: Conditional QCD and nuclear-energy evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The calibrated hadron spectra, convention-dependent isospin components, measured-input deuteron energetics and the new nonphysical-mass two-nucleon calculation address different stages of nuclear-energy reasoning. The latter reports finite-volume shifts and a conditional bound-state interpretation at one flavor-symmetric input point. State-identification limitations remain explicit. This finite evidence does not supply a controlled quark-mass sensitivity, ordinary-matter density, compressibility or an astrophysical equation of state.

nodes.name: QCD+QED mass and charge inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Charged-pion, charged/neutral-kaon and neutral-D masses fix the physical quark-mass point, the Omega mass sets the scale, and the electromagnetic input is alpha^-1=137.036. Experimental inputs and fitted extrapolations precede the reported isospin-splitting comparison.

nodes.name: Four-flavor QCD+QED hadron model
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed low-energy model includes dynamical up, down, strange and charm quarks with nondegenerate masses, gluons and photons. Quark charges are +2/3 for up/charm and -1/3 for down/strange in units of e; both strong and electromagnetic fields enter the Euclidean action.

nodes.name: QCD/QED separation convention
nodes.shortDescription: Separating an isospin splitting into strong and electromagnetic contributions requires a convention. Borsanyi adopts Delta_QED M_Sigma=0 at the reported precision, then infers the kaon electromagnetic squared-mass contribution and the other channel components.

nodes.name: QCD renormalization-scale dependence
nodes.shortDescription: The renormalized strong coupling alpha_s=g_s^2/(4 pi) depends on a specified renormalization scale mu_R and convention. Its renormalization-group equation describes changes of scale in a field-theory description.

nodes.name: QED effective coupling convention
nodes.shortDescription: In the L3 QED convention alpha(Q^2)=alpha(0)/(1-DeltaAlpha(Q^2)), where DeltaAlpha parameterizes vacuum-polarization corrections. The Bhabha analysis uses signed Q^2=t=-s*(1-cos(theta))/2<0 in the spacelike region; this alpha is the electromagnetic coupling, not alpha_s.

nodes.name: QED_L finite-volume prescription
nodes.shortDescription: QED_L removes photon modes with zero spatial momentum at every Euclidean time. Leading finite-volume mass terms scale as 1/L and 1/L^2 under the stated Ward-identity assumptions; composite-particle terms beyond those orders require additional treatment.

nodes.name: Quantum field theory framework
nodes.shortDescription: Quantum field theory specifies quantum fields, states and dynamics. A concrete model must choose its fields, symmetries, interactions and domain of application.

nodes.name: Quantum reaction effects within a declared experiment and model
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed primary publication supports a finite positive quantum-reaction case: cryogenic matrix-isolated trans-H-C-OH shows dark first-order infrared loss, with weak temperature dependence over the reported 11-20 K noble-gas points, a slower nitrogen host and qualitatively stable H-C-OD. The associated ground-singlet reaction-path/WKB calculation supplies a hydrogen-tunnelling interpretation and a source-predicted H/D lifetime contrast. Observation, mechanism inference and model prediction remain separate; the primary supplement is part of the same publication rather than a second confirmation.

nodes.name: Quark electromagnetic current
nodes.shortDescription: With e>0 the positron charge, define the quark contribution J_em,q^mu=sum_f Q_f*sum_a qbar_fa*gamma^mu*q_fa and L_em,q=-e*A_mu*J_em,q^mu. Here f labels the declared quark flavors, a is a contracted fundamental-color index, and Q_f is +2/3 for u,c,t or -1/3 for d,s,b. This electromagnetic vector current is flavor diagonal in the stated mass basis.

nodes.name: Quark fields
nodes.shortDescription: The Standard Model has six spin-one-half quark flavors. Up, charm and top carry charge +2e/3; down, strange and bottom carry -e/3. QCD quark fields transform in the three-dimensional fundamental color representation.

nodes.name: Quark mass prescription
nodes.shortDescription: A renormalized quark mass requires a prescription. The modified-minimal-subtraction mass mbar_q(mu_R) depends on the renormalization scale mu_R; the referenced summary table quotes u,d,s at 2 GeV and c,b at a scale equal to the respective running mass. A perturbative pole-mass prescription is distinct and has an ambiguity of order the QCD scale when related to observables.

nodes.name: Leading electromagnetic quark-parton response
nodes.shortDescription: For unpolarized electromagnetic DIS in the leading massless collinear spin-one-half quark-parton model, use Q2=-q^2>0, x=Q2/(2*P.q), and F2_gamma=x*sum_f Q_f^2*(q_f+qbar_f). The flavor distributions are evaluated at the stated scale; their sum includes quarks and antiquarks rather than net valence alone. In the negligible-target-mass limit the same model gives 2*x*F1_gamma=F2_gamma, hence FL_gamma=F2_gamma-2*x*F1_gamma=0.

nodes.name: Conditional quartz piezoelectric tensor inference
nodes.shortDescription: The source quartz resonance analysis reports averaged e11=0.151 C/m^2 and e14=-0.061 C/m^2 at30 C in its tensor/axis convention. TableI gives relative specimen standard deviations4.75 percent and17.8 percent, respectively. These conditional coupled-model coefficient estimates supply a finite piezoelectric example, not a newly measured spontaneous polarization or demonstrated ferroelectric switching.

nodes.name: Ideal qubit teleportation
nodes.shortDescription: For an unknown pure qubit initially independent of a shared singlet, Alice jointly measures the input and her resource qubit in the Bell basis. Each of four outcomes has probability 1/4. Two classical bits identify the outcome; Bob applies the corresponding identity or Pauli-equivalent rotation to recover the input state, up to a global phase. Averaging over the unreceived outcome gives Bob I/2, independent of the input.

nodes.name: Rahaman Cs133 optical-fluorescence hyperfine context
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare Cs133 vapor-cell Doppler-free two-photon excitation from6s1/2 F=3 or F=4 to7d2D3/2 Fprime=2,3,4,5 with a counterpropagating narrow-linewidth cw laser near767.8 nm. Scan the source AOM2 radio-frequency coordinate in a cat-eye double-pass geometry and record672.5 nm spontaneous fluorescence through a10 nm bandpass centered near670 nm. Stabilize the laser using a separate Cs-cell feedback and stabilize power at the measurement cell. The measurement cell is near135 C with two mu-metal shielding layers and residual field about2 mG; beam1/e^2 radius63+/-3 micrometres and a25 mm collection aperture about67 mm away delimit the observation. Vary theta between incident linear polarization and detection direction, including0+/-2,53+/-2 and90+/-2 degrees.

nodes.name: Recalibrated deuteron binding energy
nodes.shortDescription: Rescaling the existing capture wavelength with the revised ILL spacing yields photon wavelength 0.557671299(97)e-12 m and recoil-corrected binding energy 2224566.35(0.39) eV, or 0.00238817008(42) u.

nodes.name: Carbon ionic reference for the deuteron campaign
nodes.shortDescription: The 2020 deuteron and HD+ campaign converts cyclotron ratios with distinct C-12(6+) and C-12(4+) nuclear/electronic references and charge factors, using the stated CODATA 2018 inputs.

nodes.name: Direct corrected deuteron mass
nodes.shortDescription: AWG1 and AWG2 report zero-drive ratios 1.0070527378313(86) and 1.0070527378317(70), combined as 1.0070527378316(54). After corrections, R=1.0070527379117(54)(65)(85) and m_d=2.013553212535(11)(13)(17) u, with statistical, systematic and total uncertainties.

nodes.name: Bounded grouped-figure reconstruction
nodes.shortDescription: Weighted planes of 27 published grouped means give intercepts about 1.007052737831311, 1.007052737831752 and 1.007310263850385 for deuteron AWG1, deuteron AWG2 and HD+. Reconstructed residuals differ from the published values by less than 0.005 in ratio units of 1e-12.

nodes.name: Internal molecular mass closure
nodes.shortDescription: Using the 2019 proton input and direct deuteron mass, the molecular balance predicts m_HD=3.021378241576(37) u. Prediction minus direct HD+ measurement is 15(71) pu, where pu=1e-12 u.

nodes.name: Direct corrected HD+ mass
nodes.shortDescription: The HD+ comparison reports zero-drive ratio 1.007310263850(19), corrected ratio 1.007310263905(19)(8)(20), and m_HD=3.021378241561(56)(24)(61) u, with statistical, systematic and total uncertainties.

nodes.name: Jointly adjusted proton and deuteron masses
nodes.shortDescription: Including the FSU ratio gives m_p=1.007276466580(17) u and m_d=2.013553212537(16) u with correlation 0.26. These are outputs of the joint adjustment, not new direct acquisitions.

nodes.name: Locally adjusted nucleon masses
nodes.shortDescription: The local fit gives m_p=1.007276466595(29) u and m_d=2.013553212534(17) u with correlation -0.13; their adjusted ratio is m_d/m_p=1.999007501228(59).

nodes.name: Capture-constrained neutron mass
nodes.shortDescription: The joint proton/deuteron adjustment and recalibrated positive deuteron binding energy give m_n=m_d-m_p+E_B/c^2=1.00866491604(42) u. Its correlations with proton and deuteron are 0.03 and -0.03.

nodes.name: Rounded molecular and capture arithmetic
nodes.shortDescription: Using the unscaled Korobov HD+ ionization energy gives a molecular prediction-minus-direct difference about 14.731 pu. Rescaling the capture wavelength and adding deuteron recoil gives 2224566.3487 eV from the printed central inputs.

nodes.name: Deuteron AWG1 acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Pairs 1-2 of the four-pair LIONTRAP deuteron/C6+ campaign use the first excitation generator, alternating ions near 3.8 T and 4.2 K. A separate planar fit extrapolates the squared excitation strengths to zero drive.

nodes.name: Deuteron AWG2 acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Pairs 3-4 use a replacement excitation generator and their own excitation-plane fit, with the same LIONTRAP mass reference and corrected trap. The two generator groups share apparatus and systematic inputs.

nodes.name: Capture binding recalibration
nodes.shortDescription: Rescale the previously recalibrated capture wavelength by the revised ILL lattice spacing, then apply photon recoil and the stated mass-energy conversion. This analysis reuses the original Kessler capture data.

nodes.name: Published deuteron figure replay
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the named AWG1, AWG2 and HD+ publisher workbook panels as three weighted planes of grouped mean ratio versus squared radii, using 40-digit decimal arithmetic and independent diagonal errors. Check selected rounded mass and recoil arithmetic separately.

nodes.name: HD+ carbon comparison
nodes.shortDescription: One HD+/C4+ pair is compared for seven weeks with changed trap voltage to match axial frequencies. The ground rovibrational state is inferred from cryogenic storage and cooling; excitation and polarizability corrections remain.

nodes.name: Joint LIONTRAP and FSU adjustment
nodes.shortDescription: Add the independently acquired FSU deuteron/proton ratio to the LIONTRAP mass constraints. The quoted neutron mass additionally uses the recalibrated capture binding energy.

nodes.name: Local LIONTRAP mass adjustment
nodes.shortDescription: Fit the published 2019 proton mass, direct deuteron mass and HD+ molecular mass balance together, retaining common electronic, molecular and calibration inputs.

nodes.name: Finite Rb87 hyperfine clock-frequency comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Marion and colleagues report the2002 Rb87 electronic-ground-state hyperfine frequency relative to their average Cs133 fountain realizations as6,834,682,610.904324(4)(7) Hz. In the source convention the first parenthesis is1-sigma statistical uncertainty and the second is the separate systematic uncertainty including DF_Rb,DF_Cs and FOM. The1999 frequency6,834,682,610.904333 Hz is a conventional reference used in the comparison display, not the new2002 result or an exact SI defining constant.

nodes.name: State, zero-point energy and reaction-path tunnelling model
nodes.shortDescription: In the reviewed ground-singlet trans-H-C-OH to H2CO model, supply an electronic potential, an intrinsic reaction path, orthogonal vibrational modes and a declared initial vibrational energy. Zero-point energy changes vibrational state energies and energy-reference conventions; below-barrier transmission is a separate dynamical contribution estimated here by a reduced reaction-path Hamiltonian and WKB penetration. The reported 1220 cm^-1 reaction-mode wavenumber corresponds to zero-point energy h*c*nu_tilde/2 and barrier-attempt frequency c*nu_tilde, with consistent length units; a wavenumber is neither an energy nor a frequency in Hz by itself.

nodes.name: Reactor antineutrino coincidence readout
nodes.shortDescription: KamLAND identifies electron-antineutrino candidates through inverse beta decay, antinu_e+p->e-plus+n. The prompt positron kinetic plus annihilation signal is followed by neutron-capture light, normally a 2.2 MeV gamma from hydrogen. The approximate relation E_antineutrino=E_prompt+T_neutron+0.8 MeV uses neutron recoil kinetic energy and a rounded kinematic offset; energy response and delayed-coincidence selection remain explicit.

nodes.name: Bound-body recoil and zero-phonon nuclear transition
nodes.shortDescription: For a free nucleus of mass M, the leading nonrelativistic recoil energy is E_R=E_gamma^2/(2*M*c^2), displacing emission below and absorption above the nuclear transition energy. In the selected bound-solid oscillator account, a recoilless nuclear gamma event leaves the internal vibrational occupation state unchanged. Momentum is still transferred to the bound body; its whole-body translational recoil energy is negligibly small on the stated spectral scale. This zero-phonon channel is a fraction of events, not absence of binding vibrations, zero momentum transfer or a rule that every emitted gamma ray is resonant.

nodes.name: Regulated scalar vacuum region partition
nodes.shortDescription: Use hbar=c=1 and H=(1/2) integral d^3x [pi^2+|grad phi|^2]. Expand in real spherical harmonics and discretize radius at j*a, j=1,...,N, with phi_(l,m,N+1)=0 at L=(N+1)a. Equation 18 defines the radial oscillator couplings. The state is the pure Gaussian ground state, with Omega=sqrt(K) for each positive oscillator matrix K. Split each partial wave into inside sites j<=n and outside sites j>n, with R=(n+1/2)a.

nodes.name: Scale flow with declared infrared direction
nodes.shortDescription: After the shell step, use p_prime=b p, x_prime=x/b and a stated field normalization to restore the reference cutoff in dimensionless variables. Write the transformed action in dimensionless coupling coordinates g_i(ell), with ell=ln b and d g_i/d ell=F_i(g); increasing ell means a smaller physical cutoff Lambda_0 exp(-ell) and longer resolved lengths. Separately, a renormalized coupling g_R(mu) in a chosen subtraction scheme obeys mu d g_R/d mu=beta_R. The cutoff Lambda, subtraction scale mu and external physical momentum Q have distinct roles.

nodes.name: Reference-defined resonance energy and observable boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Define a resonance-model energy comparison only after fixing the Hamiltonian approximation, geometry/framework, active-electron space and restricted reference function. In this source rewrite the nearest-neighbor molecular exchange integral as J_ex=alpha_source<0, with units of energy; it is distinct from the positive dimensionless electromagnetic fine-structure constant alpha_EM=e^2/(4*pi). Compare the coupled-function energy W with the one-Kekule-function value W_single under the same Q and J_ex convention. W-W_single is a model-space energy difference, not an independently measured heat, a molecular dissociation energy, an energy released by switching drawings or an operational universal aromaticity criterion.

nodes.name: Energy-pole width and exponential proper lifetime
nodes.shortDescription: Define the energy-plane resonance pole by sqrt(s_R)=M_E-i*Gamma_E/2 with positive M_E and Gamma_E. In the isolated-resonance exponential approximation, P(t_proper)=exp(-Gamma_E*t_proper/hbar) and tau_proper=hbar/Gamma_E. For fixed Lorentz factor gamma, the corresponding laboratory survival is exp(-Gamma_E*t_lab/(gamma*hbar)). This convention separates an inferred decay timescale from the reported line-shape parametrization.

nodes.name: Scoped many-electron molecular resonance model evidence
nodes.shortDescription: A finite positive molecular-resonance result is supported by the specified six-electron benzene VB model: a coherent stationary combination of canonical functions lowers the model energy relative to the one-Kekule-function reference. The source assumptions and exchange parameter delimit the result. This treats resonance drawings as a representation of one state, with no observed interconversion or new molecule. General delocalized charge, conjugation, aromaticity, reactivity, optical and transport conclusions require additional identified models or measurements.

nodes.name: Method-defined ring-center NICS magnetic criterion
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected historical magnetic criterion, define ring-center NICS as the sign-reversed computed absolute magnetic shielding, in ppm, at the unweighted mean of the ring heavy-atom coordinates. The point has no observed nucleus. Specify the molecular geometry and quantum-chemical response method. The descriptor probes magnetic shielding under a chosen aromaticity convention; it is not a measured proton NMR shift, an energy or a direct observation of an electron circulating on a trajectory.

nodes.name: Hall A polarized-3He preparation
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare polarized electrons and a polarized 3He gas target with N2 admixture; measure coincidence helicity yields and beam/target polarizations, then form the reported charge- and polarization-normalized Ameas.

nodes.name: Measured polarized-3He helicity asymmetries
nodes.shortDescription: Table II reports Ameas=-0.136, -0.134 and -0.098 at acceptance-mean Q2=1.72, 2.48 and 3.41 GeV2, after the Equation 1 charge and beam/target polarization normalization. Corrected Aen endpoints are a separate computational outcome.

nodes.name: Corrected neutron-asymmetry endpoints
nodes.shortDescription: Table II reports Aen|exp=-0.188, -0.175 and -0.134 after the stated dilution and background treatment of the same three measured asymmetries. Its intermediate Aphys values are -0.148, -0.145 and -0.109. These are correction stages from the same data; the final endpoints are compared with GEA calculations in the ratio extraction.

nodes.name: Conditional neutron electric response
nodes.shortDescription: Using linearly interpolated Lachniet GMn, Table III reports GE_n=0.0236 +/- 0.0017(stat) +/- 0.0026(syst), 0.0208 +/- 0.0024 +/- 0.0019 and 0.0147 +/- 0.0020 +/- 0.0014 at Q2=1.72, 2.48 and 3.41 GeV2.

nodes.name: Polarized-3He correction and neutron-response extraction
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the declared target, accidental, inelastic and proton-background treatment, compare corrected neutron asymmetries with GEA/AV18 calculations, and convert the inferred normalized ratio to GE using external linearly interpolated CLAS GMn.

nodes.name: Inferred normalized neutron Sachs ratios
nodes.shortDescription: Table III reports gn=mu_n*GE_n/GM_n of 0.273 +/- 0.020(stat) +/- 0.030(syst), 0.412 +/- 0.048 +/- 0.036 and 0.496 +/- 0.067 +/- 0.046 at acceptance-mean Q2=1.72, 2.48 and 3.41 GeV2.

nodes.name: Cold water-dimer vibrational-predissociation measurement context
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare neutral water dimers in a pulsed supersonic expansion of about 2% H2O in He, with estimated rotational temperature 10 +/- 5 K. Excite the donor bound-OH band at 3602 cm^-1; state-selective 2+1 REMPI detects water fragments, while velocity-map images constrain translational distributions. Use IR-on/off signal discrimination, NO2 photodissociation calibration and reconstruction before fitting energy conservation. The estimated initial dimer internal energy is 5 +/- 5 cm^-1.

nodes.name: Finite non-Lambertian PTFE angular response
nodes.shortDescription: At550 nm the reported white and gray sintered-PTFE reflectance factors vary with the selected illumination/viewing geometry and depart from their constant Lambertian reference values, especially at large incident angles. For the gray target at90-degree viewing azimuth, using the nominal Lambertian value would produce a reported reference-value error exceeding30 percent. The source roughly estimates relative expanded uncertainties k=2 of1 percent for white and2 percent for gray in this scan; these are not universal instrument limits.

nodes.name: Molecular state inference
nodes.shortDescription: A vibrational or rotational ground-state assignment requires a preparation or readout model. Vibrational v=0 alone does not imply rotational N=0, and waiting for modeled cooling is not direct state certification.

nodes.name: Scope of QCD and QED running evidence
nodes.shortDescription: The reviewed CMS jet-ratio analysis supplies a correlated, theory/PDF-conditioned strong-coupling scale comparison. The reviewed L3 angular-shape analysis supplies a conditional electromagnetic running deformation and a dependent inverse-coupling difference. These are distinct observable/model chains. Their limited scale-dependence findings are compatible with the declared parameter-running descriptions; they do not directly measure Wilsonian mode elimination, establish fixed-point universality or validate every effective theory.

nodes.name: Sachs elastic proton form factors
nodes.shortDescription: For unpolarized elastic electron-proton scattering in the ultrarelativistic one-photon approximation, the reduced cross section is epsilon*GE(Q^2)^2+tau*GM(Q^2)^2, where tau=Q^2/(4*m_p^2). GE(0)=1 and GM(0)=mu_p specify reference normalization; the measured cross section does not determine signs by itself.

nodes.name: Isotropic free scalar dispersion
nodes.shortDescription: For the chosen free real scalar model in infinite flat space, use hbar=c=1, m>0 and the Fock vacuum. Its positive energy is E(k)=sqrt(k dot k+m^2). A proper spatial rotation R obeys R^T R=I and det(R)=+1, hence E(Rk)=E(k). Comparing nonzero wave vectors of fixed magnitude at fixed mass, state preparation and model gives an isotropic dispersion null. This is a formal prediction of the supplied model, not an observed anisotropic response.

nodes.name: Schleyer ring-center shielding computation context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the source neutral D6h benzene and saturated D3d cyclohexane geometries from Becke3LYP/6-31G*, as specified for these Table1 cases. Evaluate ring-center absolute magnetic shieldings with GIAO-SCF, taking the 6-31+G* column as the selected response basis. Reverse the shielding sign to report NICS in ppm. The source Gaussian94 calculation supplies a finite magnetic-response comparison; no new solver execution is performed.

nodes.name: Schneider corrected proton magnetic moment
nodes.shortDescription: The Science 2017 abstract reports mu_p/mu_N=2.79284734462+/-0.00000000082. The thesis identifies the same result as 2.79284734462(75)(34), with 68.3 percent statistical and separately stated systematic uncertainty, and total fractional precision 295 ppt.

nodes.name: Schneider 2016 acquisition and spin analysis
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare three single protons sequentially, infer initial/final spin states from analysis-trap axial series, and reconstruct free cyclotron frequencies during precision-trap Larmor excitation. Retain selection and shared noise-model assumptions in the reported statistical resonance estimate.

nodes.name: Schneider moment correction and uncertainty
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the signed preparation-specific corrections to the same campaign statistical center. Keep the linear systematic-bound aggregation separate from the reported statistical uncertainty and final total.

nodes.name: Schneider statistical moment estimate
nodes.shortDescription: The thesis reports the selected-campaign statistical estimate mu_p/mu_N=2.79284734500(75), before systematic correction, from 1264 selected ratios. The quoted 268 ppt statistical precision is a source inference, not an independently reproduced likelihood result.

nodes.name: Schreiner matrix isolation and dark infrared acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Generate hydroxymethylene by high-vacuum flash pyrolysis of glyoxylic acid at 1000 deg C and immediately co-condense the products with excess Ar, Kr, Xe or N2 on a cryogenic window. Unreacted precursor, CO2, formaldehyde and some CO are also present. Assign trans-H-C-OH and H-C-OD using infrared/UV observations and computed vibrational bands. For dark kinetics, shield external light and acquire infrared spectra every 30 min at the reported 11, 15 or 20 K settings, following the approximately 1050 and 1300 cm^-1 H-C-OH bands.

nodes.name: Matrix-specific hydroxymethylene dark decay
nodes.shortDescription: The source reports first-order H-C-OH loss and the following half-lives in hours: at 11 K Ar 1.8, Kr 2.0, Xe 2.3 and N2 7.0; at 15 K Ar 1.9; at 20 K Ar 1.7 and Kr 2.0. Other temperature/matrix entries in Supplementary Table 1 are explicitly not determined. H-C-OD infrared bands are reported unchanged for an unspecified extended observation period. The approximately two-hour summary applies to the reported noble-gas preparations, while the 11 K nitrogen matrix is slower by more than a factor of three.

nodes.name: Schreiner ground-singlet reaction-path calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Use the ground-electronic-singlet trans-H-C-OH to H2CO channel with AE-CCSD(T)/cc-pCVQZ stationary structures and focal-point energy corrections. Construct the intrinsic reaction path and orthogonal harmonic frequencies at AE-CCSD/cc-pCVTZ and refine path energies at AE-CCSD(T)/cc-pCVQZ. Apply a reduced reaction-path Hamiltonian with WKB transmission at the reaction-mode zero-point energy, using the 1220 cm^-1 reactant harmonic mode and its corresponding barrier-attempt frequency. The same procedure is applied to H-C-OD; an asymmetric Eckart calculation is a separate qualitative check.

nodes.name: Reported reaction-path tunnelling prediction
nodes.shortDescription: The source reduced reaction-path/WKB calculation predicts a near-0-K H-C-OH half-life of 122 min, reported as 2.0 h, and a H-C-OD half-life over 1200 yr. These are theoretical outputs. Figure 4 uses focal-point plus harmonic zero-point energies relative to CO+H2: trans reactant 54.2 and TS2 83.9 kcal/mol, with the displayed difference 29.7 kcal/mol; the trans anharmonic value is 54.0. A separate Eckart check uses a stated 31.60 kcal/mol barrier, -52.05 kcal/mol reaction energy and 2174i cm^-1 imaginary transition-state wavenumber. These printed model inputs have distinct conventions and are not merged into one experimental barrier.

nodes.name: Full-geometry image-charge prediction
nodes.shortDescription: For LIONTRAP at B0=3.764 T, the full-geometry calculation reports a cyclotron correction 475.4(2.1)(3.6) microhertz per charge state, with numerical and geometry uncertainties. The simplified calculations give 488.416(58) and 488.7(2.1); including electrode gaps changes the prediction.

nodes.name: Scoped image-charge comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Schuh Table I compares the extracted 2.291(126) mHz magnetron difference with 2.377(21) mHz from the geometry calculation. This supports the correction at roughly five-percent experimental precision, while the conversion to the distinct Table II experimental value remains unresolved.

nodes.name: Extracted image-charge difference
nodes.shortDescription: Subtracting the stated ideal, magnetic and tilt/ellipticity contributions gives an image-charge magnetron difference 2.291(61)(111) mHz, or 2.291(126) mHz with combined uncertainty, in Schuh Table I and Equation 23.

nodes.name: Measured magnetron difference
nodes.shortDescription: The dedicated image-charge experiment reports nu_minus(C-12(6+))-nu_minus(p)=393.258(61)(77) mHz after voltage correction. This includes the ideal-trap mass dependence and other apparatus shifts, not only the image-charge contribution.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP electrode-geometry calculation
nodes.shortDescription: COMSOL 5.2 finite-element electrostatics and a semianalytical expansion compare simplified electrode models and full LIONTRAP geometry. Field gradients are inferred from 21 ion positions; a long-cylinder reference and geometry perturbations estimate numerical and manufacturing uncertainty.

nodes.name: LIONTRAP dedicated magnetron experiment
nodes.shortDescription: Alternating single p and C-12(6+) ions undergo a Ramsey-like magnetron measurement with two 4.6 ms pulses and deformed-potential axial readout. The 120 cycles over 23 days use 20 or 40 s precision phase evolution. Voltage and tilt corrections enter the extracted image-charge difference.

nodes.name: Schwinger leading electron magnetic anomaly
nodes.shortDescription: The 1948 letter gives delta_mu/mu=e^2/(2*pi*hbar*c)=0.001162 in its Gaussian-unit convention. With alpha=e^2/(hbar*c) this is the positive leading correction a_e^(1)=alpha/(2*pi), or g/2=1+a_e^(1) at that order, using renormalized experimental mass and charge.

nodes.name: Finite-sphere screened repulsive pair model
nodes.shortDescription: For the source isolated identical spheres in the far-separation Debye-Huckel regime, use U(x)/(kB*T)=Zeff^2*lambdaB*[exp(kappa*a)/(1+kappa*a)]^2*exp(-kappa*x)/x. Here x is center-to-center separation, a is sphere radius, Zeff is effective charge in units of the positive elementary-charge magnitude, kappa is inverse screening length and lambdaB=e^2/(epsilon*kB*T) in the source electrostatic-cgs convention. This is a screened repulsive pair term, with finite-sphere amplitude and an effective charge that need not equal titratable charge.

nodes.name: Historical hydrogen recombination model context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the reported expanding-universe multilevel calculation with populations of 300 hydrogen atomic levels, free electrons and matter temperature, including capture/photoionization and bound-bound transitions. The displayed Figure 1 case adopts Omega_tot=1, Omega_B=0.05, H_0=50 km/s/Mpc, Y_P=0.24 and T_0=2.728 K. The approximate treatment evolves proton fraction x_p=n_p/n_H and helium ionization together with T_M, with x_e=n_e/n_H and supplied expansion and radiation temperature. Ground-state production is bottlenecked by resonance-photon trapping and proceeds through cosmological redshifting of Lyman-alpha photons and the slow 2s-to-1s two-photon channel; electron capture alone does not instantaneously make a persistent ground-state population.

nodes.name: Reported hydrogen neutralization history
nodes.shortDescription: For the supplied historical model, the reported population evolution builds neutral hydrogen as the universe expands and cools while leaving a residual free-electron population. Figure 1 compares the 300-level result with the effective three-level calculation; the source reports faster late hydrogen recombination and approximately 10 percent lower residual x_e than the earlier approximation. This is a computational formation-history comparison, not measured atom-production events or an independent experimental confirmation of the hydrogen spectrum.

nodes.name: Shalm photonic Bell acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Prepare nonmaximally polarization-entangled 1550 nm photon pairs by pulsed downconversion and distribute them to separate Alice/Bob stations. Each local 99.1 kHz trial records a setting and + for a detection in the accepted window or 0 otherwise. Settings combine phase-diffusion, photon-sampling and predetermined pseudorandom bits by XOR. The selected Classical XOR3 run lasted 30 minutes.

nodes.name: Shalm conditional photonic Bell test
nodes.shortDescription: For that five-pulse analysis, Table I reports nominal p=5.9e-9 and predictability-adjusted p=2.3e-7 using epsilon=0.003. These are conditional tail bounds against the specified local model; the adjusted result permits the declared limited setting predictability.

nodes.name: Shalm memory-robust Bell inference
nodes.shortDescription: Test P(++|ab)<=P(+0|ab')+P(0+|a'b)+P(++|a'b'). The statistic N_S counts ++ab among the first N_chi events in those four settings/outcome classes. A disjoint initial training segment estimates f and fixes N_chi=0.9*r*f for the remaining r trials. Per trial, epsilon bounds each maximum setting probability: max(P(a),P(a')) and max(P(b),P(b'))<=(1+epsilon)/2. Use the reported memory-robust binomial-tail bound, with success bound 1/2 for equiprobable choices or 1/2+epsilon/(1+epsilon^2) for bounded predictability.

nodes.name: Shalm detection and timing boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Local arrival windows and the timing/calibration model determine the accepted binary outcomes and spacelike-separation claim. Published system efficiencies are 74.7 +/- 0.3% and 75.6 +/- 0.3%; five-pulse timing margin is 38.3 +/- 3.7 ns. The analysis assumes outcomes are fixed at the time taggers and reliable measured positions/delays.

nodes.name: Shalm stopping-selected trial counts
nodes.shortDescription: For Classical XOR3 with pulses 4-8 aggregated, Table I reports 177358351 total trials through the selected stopping point, N_chi=12127 relevant events and N_S=6378 ++ab events. Supplement Table S-II retains all four outcomes, including 00, for each setting pair. These are stopping-selected counts from one recorded run.

nodes.name: Finite icosahedral Al-Mn order and reported metastability
nodes.shortDescription: For the selected rapidly cooled Al-Mn material, the source reports sharp electron diffraction with six fivefold, ten threefold and fifteen twofold axes of an icosahedral point group, with orientational correlation across finite grains up to about 2 micrometers. Dark-field imaging, small-volume convergent-beam diffraction and powder diffraction support the authors rejection of a conventional multiply twinned Bravais-lattice explanation. The icosahedral phase is metastable under the reported protocols: no detectable subsequent crystallization after 6 hours at 300 degrees C or 1 hour at 350 degrees C, and conversion to stable Al6Mn after 1 hour at 400 degrees C.

nodes.name: Al-Mn diffraction, imaging and annealing context
nodes.shortDescription: Use the reported rapidly cooled Al-Mn alloy specimens, especially Al-14 at.% Mn, and their finite grains up to about 2 micrometers. Rotate specimens to relate selected-area electron diffraction patterns to icosahedral axes. Keep dark-field imaging, convergent-beam microdiffraction and Cu K-alpha powder diffraction as reported complementary checks against a conventional multiple-twin explanation. Retain the separate morphology/segregation inference and the stated annealing durations when interpreting formation or metastability.

nodes.name: Silicon lattice calibration transfer
nodes.shortDescription: A relative Bragg-angle comparison transfers an absolute lattice-spacing reference to a specified silicon specimen under stated temperature, pressure, impurity and geometry conditions. Shared reference standards retain covariance.

nodes.name: Canonical scalar cosmological background
nodes.shortDescription: In hbar=c=1 units with signature (+---) and the curvature convention of Mukhanov Equation 1, take S=integral d^4x sqrt(-g)[-M_pl^2 R_4/2 + g^{mu nu} partial_mu phi partial_nu phi/2 - V(phi)], with reduced M_pl^2=(8 pi G)^(-1). The spatially flat background is ds^2=dt^2-a(t)^2 dx^2, dt=a d_eta. For homogeneous phi(t), H=dot(a)/a obeys 3 M_pl^2 H^2=dot(phi)^2/2+V, dot(H)=-dot(phi)^2/(2 M_pl^2), and ddot(phi)+3H dot(phi)+V_,phi=0. For H>0, epsilon_H=-dot(H)/H^2; epsilon_H<1 defines accelerated expansion and a decreasing comoving Hubble radius (aH)^(-1).

nodes.name: Ambient-water radial shell correlations and cutoff-dependent coordination
nodes.shortDescription: The common ambient-water X-ray reanalysis supports nonuniform radial oxygen-oxygen correlations, with recommended first-maximum position 2.80(1) angstrom and dimensionless height 2.57(5). The reported oxygen coordination is 4.3(1) when integrating 4*pi*rho_O*r^2*g_OO(r) from 2.4 to 3.30 angstrom. For the APS example it becomes 4.6(1) if the upper cutoff is 3.40 angstrom. This is finite statistical shell structure in the liquid, not a rigid lattice or a unique hydrogen-bond network.

nodes.name: Common ambient-water X-ray reanalysis context
nodes.shortDescription: Reanalyze the four reported ambient liquid-H2O X-ray datasets, APS, SPring-8, SSRL1 and SSRL2, with their stated temperatures between 22 and 26 degrees C. Keep the different high-energy/non-Compton-discriminating and lower-energy/analyzer approaches distinct. Use common scattering normalization and the specified quantum molecular form-factor input; subtract the literature O-H contribution in Q space, retain the small H-H approximation and sensitivity checks, and Fourier transform the isolated S_OO(Q) with the declared variable Lorch window and dataset-specific Q range. Retain the source separate statistical error, normalization/calibration limits and between-dataset comparison.

nodes.name: SLAC electron-proton measurement
nodes.shortDescription: The measured electron spectra and stated kinematics define the differential cross-section readout; Figure 1 uses a Mott normalization at fixed recoil mass.

nodes.name: Conditional structure-function scaling
nodes.shortDescription: Under transverse virtual-photon dominance, the extracted nu W2 approximately follows one curve in omega; the abstract states q^2>1 (GeV/c)^2 and omega>4. Figure 2 also explores q^2>0.5 and a separate low-q^2 spectrum. Longitudinal dominance does not give the same collapse.

nodes.name: Deep-inelastic electron spectrum
nodes.shortDescription: In the measured deep continuum, the inelastic differential/Mott ratio varies more slowly with q^2 than the plotted elastic/Mott comparator.

nodes.name: SLD 1993 three-jet acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the 1993 SLC Z0-resonance run recorded by SLD. Trigger on LAC electromagnetic energy above 12 GeV; select corrected clusters with nonzero electromagnetic energy and at least 100 MeV. Apply the stated cluster multiplicity, total-energy and energy-balance cuts, then JADE with y_c=0.02.

nodes.name: SLD conditional vector-gluon support
nodes.shortDescription: The normalized restricted-range shapes favor the specified vector QCD calculation over the scalar and tensor alternatives. For the Ellis-Karliner comparison, Table VII reports 18 bins and chi-squared values 19.5 (vector), 1684.0 (scalar) and 772.1 (tensor). These are the published comparison statistics, not locally reproduced fits.

nodes.name: SLD corrected three-jet shapes
nodes.shortDescription: Tables I-IV report normalized hadron-level distributions after detector/ISR correction. For example, Table IV gives density 1.700 +/- 0.035 statistical +/- 0.043 experimental systematic at cos(theta_EK)=0.875. Figures 4-7 further apply hadronization corrections to give parton-level estimates, with statistical and total systematic errors added in quadrature.

nodes.name: SLD restricted gluon-spin model comparison
nodes.shortDescription: Order jets by energy and compare normalized x_i=2E_i/sqrt(s) and Ellis-Karliner shapes with the specified massless leading-order vector QCD, scalar and Equation 6 tensor models. Restrict to 0.688<x1<0.976, x2<0.93, x3>0.09 and cos(theta_EK)<0.9, normalizing each prediction to the data in its selected range. Table VI separately compares QCD orders and showers.

nodes.name: SLD reconstructed three-jet shapes
nodes.shortDescription: About 51000 hadronic events pass the calorimeter selection; JADE at y_c=0.02 yields 22114 three-jet events. Figure 3 displays reconstructed x1, x2, x3 and cos(theta_EK) distributions with statistical-only error bars, alongside HERWIG 5.7 plus detector simulation.

nodes.name: SLD jet response and hadronization corrections
nodes.shortDescription: Weight cluster energies by the inverse simulated polar-angle response; rescale jet momenta to zero total three-momentum and adjust energies by Equations 10-12. Apply C_D=D_MC_hadron/D_MC_SLD from HERWIG 5.7 for detector, selection and ISR effects. Then apply C_H=D_MC_parton/D_MC_hadron, averaging JETSET 7.4 and HERWIG 5.7 and assigning the mean-to-extremum difference as a symmetric hadronization uncertainty.

nodes.name: SLD model-dependent momentum extrapolation
nodes.shortDescription: The same measured spectra are integrated with correlated systematic errors, then extrapolated over unmeasured xp using the mean accepted fraction from three specified fragmentation generators. The assigned absolute accepted-fraction uncertainty is 0.01 for K0 and Lambda and 0.015 for K*0 and phi.

nodes.name: SLD inclusive neutral-hadron reconstruction
nodes.shortDescription: SLD uses approximately 150000 hadronic events acquired in 1993-1995. The inclusive event selection retains 90213 events; CRID analyses additionally require detector readiness, leaving 79711. K0S and Lambda use displaced charged vertices; K*0 and phi use charged-pair mass fits with kaon identification. The event denominator is corrected for trigger and selection efficiency.

nodes.name: SLD extrapolated neutral-hadron totals
nodes.shortDescription: Table 16 reports all-flavor full-range totals per hadronic Z0 decay: K0/K0bar 2.01 +/- 0.08, Lambda/Lambdabar 0.395 +/- 0.022, K*0/K*0bar 0.707 +/- 0.041 and phi 0.105 +/- 0.008. The quoted errors combine experimental and model-extrapolation contributions.

nodes.name: SLD measured-range neutral-hadron yields
nodes.shortDescription: Tables 6-7 report corrected differential yields in 44 bins. Measured-range integrals per hadronic Z0 decay are K0/K0bar 1.90 +/- 0.02 +/- 0.07, Lambda/Lambdabar 0.37 +/- 0.01 +/- 0.02, K*0/K*0bar 0.647 +/- 0.022 +/- 0.029 and phi 0.0985 +/- 0.0046 +/- 0.0055, with statistical then systematic errors.

nodes.name: SNO pure-D2O acquisition and selection
nodes.shortDescription: Use the pure-D2O first-phase acquisition from 2 November 1999 to 28 May 2001, with 306.4 live days. Reconstruct effective kinetic energy, radius and solar angle from PMT times and hit patterns. Select Teff from 5 to 20 MeV and radius at most 550 cm; include the additional 250 ms veto after events with more than 60 hit PMTs.

nodes.name: SNO jointly inferred active-flavor components
nodes.shortDescription: The SNO-only direct joint analysis reports electron flux 1.76(+/-0.05 statistical)(+/-0.09 systematic) and non-electron active flux 3.41(+/-0.45 statistical)(+0.48/-0.45 systematic), in units of 10^6 cm^-2 s^-1. Under the stated response and B8-shape assumptions, the article reports the non-electron component 5.3 standard deviations above zero, supporting solar flavor transformation compatible with oscillations.

nodes.name: SNO accepted background estimates
nodes.shortDescription: Table I reports 78 +/- 12 accepted neutron-background events and 45(+18/-12) Cherenkov-background events. These estimates use the stated controls, production locations, response and simulation; they are not additional observed solar-neutrino counts.

nodes.name: SNO channel decomposition and normalization
nodes.shortDescription: Fit CC, ES and NC amplitudes by the reported extended maximum likelihood in Teff, cos(theta_sun) and (R/600 cm)^3. Use simulation templates for the standard B8 shape and centrally fixed background amplitudes from calibration. Repeat the decomposition with perturbed response templates for systematics; normalize channel rates using the stated electron-neutrino cross-section convention.

nodes.name: SNO response-normalized channel fluxes
nodes.shortDescription: In units of 10^6 cm^-2 s^-1, the channel-normalized results are CC 1.76(+0.06/-0.05 statistical)(+/-0.09 systematic), ES 2.39(+0.24/-0.23 statistical)(+/-0.12 systematic), and NC 5.09(+0.44/-0.43 statistical)(+0.46/-0.43 systematic). They use the adopted B8 shape and electron-neutrino cross sections for all three channel normalizations.

nodes.name: SNO fitted channel amplitudes
nodes.shortDescription: The three-channel extended likelihood reports CC 1967.7(+61.9/-60.9), ES 263.6(+26.4/-25.6) and NC 576.5(+49.5/-48.9) events. These are fitted channel-yield parameters; the quoted uncertainties here are statistical.

nodes.name: SNO direct joint active-flavor inference
nodes.shortDescription: Analyze the same selected sample and response model directly in electron and non-electron active-flux variables, assuming the standard B8 shape. Use the joint three-reaction information for the no-flavor-transformation null test. Retain note 13 and the source joint probability contours; this is the SNO-only inference before any external Super-Kamiokande solar-ES constraint.

nodes.name: SNO adopted calibration and response inputs
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the Cf-252 neutron calibration, N-16 energy calibration and simulation, nuclear cross sections and standard B8 spectral input. Use the separately described in-situ/ex-situ U/Th controls, deployed-source response and simulation to estimate accepted backgrounds. Retain 29.9 +/- 1.1 percent uniform-source neutron capture efficiency and 14.4 percent selected detection efficiency as different response quantities.

nodes.name: SNO selected Cherenkov events
nodes.shortDescription: The stated selection yields 2928 events in the reconstructed 5-20 MeV analysis region and fiducial radius at most 550 cm. Their energy, solar-direction and radial response is the shared input to the reported signal decompositions.

nodes.name: Adiabatic solar survival and source averaging
nodes.shortDescription: For the declared two-flavor solar model, adiabatic propagation to a vacuum endpoint and sufficient relative-phase averaging give P_ee(E,r)=cos^2(theta_m,p)*cos^2(theta)+sin^2(theta_m,p)*sin^2(theta)=[1+cos(2 theta_m,p)*cos(2 theta)]/2, with theta_m,p evaluated at production position r. For a source component s define a supplied nonnegative production density f_s(r|E), integral d^3r f_s=1, and a supplied nonnegative normalized energy-response weight w_s(E), integral dE w_s=1. The averaged survival is <P_ee>_s=integral dE w_s(E) integral d^3r f_s(r|E) P_ee(E,r). For a specified electron-flavor charged-current response, w_s is proportional to the unoscillated differential neutrino number flux dPhi_s/dE at the detector times its cross section and detection efficiency, with any selected-bin response included and the finite nonzero normalization divided out. Here dPhi_s/dE counts neutrinos per unit area, time and neutrino energy; the transported energy flux E*dPhi_s/dE would introduce an extra energy factor and is not the event weight.

nodes.name: Approximate solar electron-density input
nodes.shortDescription: Use the review's approximate radial solar electron density n_e(R)=n_e(0)*exp(-R/r0) for 0<=R<0.9 R_sun, with r0=R_sun/10.54 (quoted approximately as 6.6e7 m or 3.3e14 eV^-1). In the declared ordinary-matter convention V_e(R)=sqrt(2)*G_F*n_e(R) and A(R,E)=2E*V_e(R). A neutrino produced at radius R_p samples n_e(R_p), which is generally different from the central normalization n_e(0).

nodes.name: Solar neutrino CC, NC and ES response
nodes.shortDescription: In the stated solar-neutrino weak-response model, nu_e+d->p+p+e-minus is the charged-current channel, nu_x+d->p+n+nu_x is the neutral-current channel and nu_x+e-minus->nu_x+e-minus is elastic scattering. CC is electron-flavor sensitive; NC has equal sensitivity to the three active flavors; ES has reduced muon/tau sensitivity. Reconstructed Cherenkov observables distinguish statistical response templates, not individually labeled incoming flavors.

nodes.name: Source-conditioned gauge-field structure
nodes.shortDescription: Gauge-field structure here means spatial dependence of a specified gauge-invariant observable in a declared source-conditioned state or ensemble. Non-Abelian self-coupling specifies interaction terms; a Euclidean lattice formulation specifies an action, gauge group, regulator and sampling measure. The reviewed spatial profiles are vacuum-subtracted expectations of squared-field/action probes conditioned on external static sources, not a directly imaged gluon population or a measured autonomous self-organization process.

nodes.name: Specified spatial order, symmetry and finite-size boundary
nodes.shortDescription: Spatial ordering is specified here through diffraction, positional correlations, bond-orientational correlations, specimen size and preparation. Periodic Bravais-lattice translation is one possible ordering description; it is not imposed as a universal prerequisite for the finite icosahedral alloy evidence. In the selected two-dimensional hard-disk model, a solid has algebraically decaying positional correlations rather than nondecaying positional order, and the hexatic has short-range positional order with very slowly decaying orientational correlations. A finite ordered specimen, a thermodynamic phase assignment and a transition pathway are distinct claims.

nodes.name: Finite rigid-SPC/E water-reorientation model
nodes.shortDescription: The selected Laage-Hynes calculation uses 256 rigid SPC/E water molecules in a periodic cubic box, Ewald treatment of long-range forces and a 0.5 fs classical molecular-dynamics step. After 50 ps equilibration at 300 K and density 1 g/cm^3, it analyzes a 75 ps microcanonical trajectory. Hydrogen bonds are assigned by oxygen separation and OH-to-OO angular cutoffs of 3.5 angstrom and 30 degrees. For the ensemble around a successful acceptor switch, these bounds are extended to 4.0 angstrom and 50 degrees. This is a supplied finite classical force-field and event-selection model, rather than an observed trajectory of individual real molecules.

nodes.name: Srednicki regulated vacuum area entropy
nodes.shortDescription: Srednicki reports S approximately 0.30(R/a)^2 for N=60 and 1<=n<=30, proportional to sphere area A=4*pi*R^2. At fixed n<=N/2, the reported N=20,40,60 results agree within 0.5% in the worst case. The nonzero reduced entropy of this declared pure state means it does not factorize across the chosen inside/outside partition.

nodes.name: Srednicki Gaussian partial-trace calculation
nodes.shortDescription: Trace the inside oscillators from the pure ground-state density operator. For Omega blocks A,B,C, the reduced Gaussian has beta=B^T A^-1 B/2 and gamma=C-beta. Diagonalization gives mode parameters xi_i and S_l=sum_i[-log(1-xi_i)-xi_i*log(xi_i)/(1-xi_i)]. Sum S=sum_l(2l+1)S_l; the large-l expressions in Equations 20-21 control convergence in three spatial dimensions.

nodes.name: Standard Model field specification
nodes.shortDescription: The Standard Model specifies SU(3) color, SU(2) weak isospin and U(1) hypercharge gauge interactions, quark and lepton fields, and a scalar Higgs doublet. This is a particular quantum field theory.

nodes.name: Declared Standard Model sector decomposition
nodes.shortDescription: Adopt the local gauge algebra su(3)c plus su(2)L plus u(1)Y, conventionally written SU(3)c x SU(2)L x U(1)Y, with Q=T3+Y. For each of three generations, the pre-Higgs-background chiral assignments are Q_L=(u_L,dprime_L)~(3,2,1/6), u_R~(3,1,2/3), d_R~(3,1,-1/3), L_L=(nu_L,l_L)~(1,2,-1/2) and l_R~(1,1,-1). The single complex Higgs scalar is phi~(1,2,1/2). Each tuple gives the color representation, weak representation and declared hypercharge: 3 means the color fundamental, 2 the weak doublet and 1 a singlet. The gauge potentials are G_mu^a (a=1,...,8), W_mu^i (i=1,2,3) and B_mu, with couplings gs, g and gprime. This is a chosen interacting field specification; the scalar is a boson without being a gauge vector mediator.

nodes.name: Mass uncertainty conditional on molecular state
nodes.shortDescription: A mass result conditional on a discrete rovibrational assignment retains separate alternative assignments. The within-branch statistical uncertainty alone does not represent uncertainty over state identity.

nodes.name: Static string and two-meson operator basis
nodes.shortDescription: An I=0 correlation matrix combines a static quark-antiquark string operator Q and a static-light meson-antimeson operator B. Its off-diagonal entries permit mixing in the specified theory with dynamical quarks.

nodes.name: Specified one-electron hydrogen bound-state model
nodes.shortDescription: Choose a nonrelativistic electron of mass m_e in the Coulomb field of a supplied static point nucleus with charge +e. In rationalized hbar=c=1 units define alpha=e^2/(4*pi) and H=-nabla^2/(2*m_e)-alpha/r. Rewriting the selected primary result in these conventions gives E_n=-m_e*alpha^2/(2*n^2), n=1,2,..., relative to the separated-particle threshold. These are discrete negative bound energies with positive binding energy -E_n. The source describes regular spatial solutions with exponentially decreasing radial tails; the eigenfunctions are not classical electron orbits or compact hard-edged objects.

nodes.name: Static-source plaquette density contrast
nodes.shortDescription:
For a smeared traced Wilson source W(R,T) and an unsmeared normalized plaquette P_mu_nu=(1/2)Tr[ordered elementary plaquette link product], define C_mu_nu=/-

. The reference is the vacuum plaquette expectation. In the large-T projection and leading plaquette matching, E_R,i=(2 beta/a^4) C_i4 and B_R,i=-(2 beta/a^4) C_jk, with |epsilon_ijk|=1. These denote differences of color-contracted squared components between the static-source ground state and vacuum. Sum spatial components to define energy contrast epsilon_R=(E_R+B_R)/2 and action contrast sigma_R=(E_R-B_R)/2.

nodes.name: Static-source area-law criterion
nodes.shortDescription: For unscreened fundamental sources, an asymptotically linear potential has string-tension coefficient K. Its large-contour criterion is ln W(C)=-K A(C)+O(perimeter), with A=a^2 times the minimal plaquette count.

nodes.name: Stationary many-electron valence-bond representation
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected benzene model, five independent many-electron valence-bond functions describe different spin-pairing patterns on the same supplied framework: two Kekule functions A/B and three Dewar-type functions C/D/E. The stationary normal-state eigenfunction is a linear combination of these functions. This representation does not describe an observed sequence of bond drawings, a molecule hopping between five species or an incoherent mixture of isolable isomers. The canonical functions have nonzero overlaps; expansion coefficients are not by themselves probabilities or time fractions.

nodes.name: Conditional long-wavelength curvature evolution
nodes.shortDescription: Substituting v=zR in the canonical mode equation gives (z^2 R_k')'+k^2 z^2 R_k=0. At k=0 its two solutions are R=C1+C2 integral d_eta/z^2. For finite modes whose gradient term is negligible, this is a long-wavelength approximation on the regular single-field interval. R is approximately conserved only when the second contribution and gradient corrections are negligible. An attractor with a decaying second solution admits that limit; single-field dynamics or k/(aH)<<1 alone does not select it.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande atmospheric acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the reported 33.0 kiloton-year, 535-day exposure in the 22.5 kiloton fiducial volume, with reconstructed vertices more than 2 m from the inner photomultiplier wall. Separate fully contained (FC) from exiting, partially contained (PC) events; use single-ring FC electron-like and muon-like classifications and the stated visible-energy division.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande two-flavor fit context
nodes.shortDescription: Compare the same selected samples with weighted Monte Carlo in five zenith bins and seven momentum bins for each of two particle-type samples. Minimize the 70-bin chi-squared over the oscillation parameters and eight normalization/shape nuisance parameters in corrected Equations 2-4, with alpha free and the seven other nuisance penalties specified in Table II.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande event double ratios
nodes.shortDescription: For R=(mu/e)_data/(mu/e)_MC, Table I reports sub-GeV R=0.63 +/- 0.03 statistical +/- 0.05 systematic and multi-GeV R_FC+PC=0.65 +/- 0.05 statistical +/- 0.08 systematic. The multi-GeV mu-like count includes the partially contained sample.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande conditional atmospheric splitting
nodes.shortDescription: Within the physical two-flavor nu_mu-to-nu_tau model, the reported best fit is sin^2(2 theta)=1.0 and Delta m^2=2.2e-3 eV^2, with chi-squared 65.2 for 67 degrees of freedom. The reported 90% confidence region has sin^2(2 theta)>0.82 and 5e-4<Delta m^2<6e-3 eV^2. These are conditional fit results from the same selected atmospheric acquisition.

nodes.name: Atmospheric flux and Cherenkov response
nodes.shortDescription: Use the report's atmospheric-flux and full-detector Monte Carlo predictions with neutrino interactions, visible-energy response, ring classification and containment. Compare control and alternative-flux inputs; retain flavor contamination, geomagnetic effects and neutrino-lepton angular/energy correlations when interpreting selected ratios and zenith patterns.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande selected FC and PC samples
nodes.shortDescription: The report contains 4353 FC and 301 PC events. The FC single-ring samples used in the oscillation analysis contain 1231 electron-like and 1158 muon-like sub-GeV events, plus 290 electron-like and 230 muon-like multi-GeV events. All 301 PC candidates enter the mu-like class without a single-ring requirement.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande no-oscillation event prediction
nodes.shortDescription: Table I reports no-oscillation Monte Carlo expectations of 1049.1 electron-like and 1573.6 muon-like sub-GeV single-ring events, 236.0 electron-like and 295.7 muon-like multi-GeV single-ring events, and 371.6 PC events. These are predicted event means conditioned on the atmospheric flux and detector/interaction response.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande mu-like zenith asymmetry
nodes.shortDescription: The selected mu-like sample shows a zenith-dependent deficit while electron-like distributions are compatible with the no-oscillation expectation. For multi-GeV FC+PC mu-like events the paper reports A=(U-D)/(U+D)=-0.296 +/- 0.048 +/- 0.01, retaining its two quoted uncertainty components. The multi-GeV electron-like comparison is -0.036 +/- 0.067 +/- 0.02.

nodes.name: Scoped surface-reflection and angular-scattering evidence
nodes.shortDescription: Existing specified IR samples have an aggregate reflected-light response under their collection setup. The separate PTFE study supplies a finite angular example in which outgoing reflectance factors depend on the stated illumination and viewing geometry. Together with scoped radiometry, these support sample- and geometry-conditioned optical redistribution, while preserving the distinction between an integrated signal, an angular measurement and an unsolved inverse surface/scene problem.

nodes.name: Selected proton-decay search counts
nodes.shortDescription: The shared SK-I-IV search reports zero e+ pi0 candidates and one mu+ pi0 candidate, in the SK-IV conventional-volume upper-momentum region. No significant excess is found over the reported atmospheric-neutrino expectations of 0.59 and 0.94 events.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande partial-lifetime inference
nodes.shortDescription: Use the same selected data in the eight-region Bayesian rate construction, marginalizing the stated efficiency, exposure and background uncertainties before inverting each channel-rate bound.

nodes.name: Conditional proton partial-lifetime bounds
nodes.shortDescription: Under the published Bayesian selection and nuisance model, the reported 90 percent lower bounds are tau/B(p -> e+ pi0)>2.4e34 years and tau/B(p -> mu+ pi0)>1.6e34 years.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande signal and background model
nodes.shortDescription: Simulate free and oxygen-bound proton response and atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds under the paper nuclear, detector and interaction assumptions, with phase-specific exposure weighting.

nodes.name: Super-Kamiokande two-channel search
nodes.shortDescription: Apply the stated channel-specific Cherenkov, fiducial, kinematic and tagging selection to the shared April 1996-May 2018 SK-I-IV data, retaining detector phases and momentum regions.

nodes.name: TASSO charged-track measurement
nodes.shortDescription: The accepted charged-track momenta and specified shape definitions define the planar-event and three-jet readouts.

nodes.name: Hard-gluon interpretation of jet events
nodes.shortDescription: The report interprets the planar three-jet topology as evidence consistent with hard noncollinear gluon radiation in e+e- -> quark antiquark gluon, followed by fragmentation. The comparison excludes the specified collinear two-jet model; it does not determine all gluon properties or establish a free stable gluon.

nodes.name: Excess planar hadronic events
nodes.shortDescription: At high energy, A<0.04 and S>0.25 select 18 planar events versus 4.5 expected in the stated two-jet comparison and 4 in the randomization estimate. Selected events admit three-jet fits.

nodes.name: Three fitted hadronic jets
nodes.shortDescription: The selected coplanar events admit three-jet fits. Figure 6 displays two examples with three separated fitted axes and a two-jet comparator; the mean hadron transverse momentum relative to assigned jet axes is about 0.30 GeV/c in the 18 selected events.

nodes.name: Emulsion tau-neutrino appearance readout
nodes.shortDescription: The OPERA appearance readout identifies charged-current tau-neutrino interaction candidates through the topology and kinematics of the produced tau decay in an emulsion/lead detector. One-hadron, three-hadron, muon and electron decay selections are distinct channels with modeled backgrounds.

nodes.name: Tau-pair decay readout
nodes.shortDescription: In the CMS tau-pair selection, tau_h denotes a reconstructed hadronic tau decay; leptonic tau decays supply electron/muon candidates and missing neutrinos. Visible decay products and missing transverse momentum supply distinct visible-mass and SVFIT tau-pair mass observables.

nodes.name: Threshold matching and coefficient boundary data
nodes.shortDescription: In the selected continuum convention use dimensional regularization with modified minimal subtraction (MSbar). At a matching scale mu_t of order M, determine EFT coefficients by equating renormalized full-theory and EFT light-particle amplitudes through the chosen momentum and loop orders, with compatible external-field and infrared conventions. At loop order n, subtract EFT contributions containing the lower-order matched coefficients from the full result; their common infrared physics cancels in a consistent matching calculation. The resulting C_i(mu_t) are boundary data; RG evolution below the threshold does not determine them without those data. A finite tree example uses J^mu=bar(e) gamma^mu (1-gamma5) nu_e and O6=J_mu^dagger J^mu, with L_eff,CC=-(G_F/sqrt(2)) O6=-g^2 O6/(8 M_W^2). Match at mu_t of order M_W for light external fermions with m_light^2 and |q^2| much smaller than M_W^2, retaining this dimension-six contact operator at tree level.

nodes.name: Transverse action-profile width conventions
nodes.shortDescription: For a positive central action profile sigma_R(0,n_perp), a nonzero denominator and a declared transverse cutoff n_cut, define delta_cut^2=integral_0^n_cut dn n^3 sigma_R(0,n)/integral_0^n_cut dn n sigma_R(0,n). The physical cutoff radial rms is a delta_cut. Separately, let d denote the full-plane model rms parameter in the Gaussian and dipole profiles of Equations 59-60. Their full widths at half maximum are rho=2 d sqrt(ln 2) and rho=2 d sqrt(2^(1/3)-1), respectively; physical FWHM is a rho.

nodes.name: Transverse photon Fock construction
nodes.shortDescription: For nonzero three-momentum p, choose two real orthonormal transverse vectors epsilon_r(p), r=1,2, with p dot epsilon_r=0. Using dPi_p=d^3p/(2pi)^3, the free-field modes obey [a_r(p),a_s_dagger(q)]=(2pi)^3 delta_rs delta^3(p-q), with creation-creation and annihilation-annihilation commutators zero. Define a_r(p)|0>=0 and the normal-ordered Hamiltonian H_0=sum_r integral dPi_p |p| a_r_dagger(p)a_r(p). These are the two physical photon polarization modes of the selected free Maxwell field.

nodes.name: Conditional transverse two-body mass
nodes.shortDescription: For two effectively massless physical daughter four-momenta from a two-body decay, define mT^2 = 2 pT1 pT2 (1-cos(deltaPhi)); the exact parent invariant mass then obeys M >= mT. Replacing these quantities by reconstructed electron and missing transverse vectors defines an estimator under a single-invisible-daughter assignment. Response errors can make that estimator exceed the true mass, so the exact inequality is not an eventwise detector guarantee. The transverse recoil is the magnitude of the daughter transverse-vector sum; mT is not a fully reconstructed invariant mass.

nodes.name: Reported optical anticorrelation
nodes.shortDescription: The selected experiment reports alpha=0.18 +/- 0.06, below the stated semiclassical bound 1; Figure 2 error bars denote one standard deviation. For that setting the publication gives a classical expected coincidence count of at least 50 versus the 9 observed and reports a separation exceeding 13 standard deviations. A pulsed-diode control matched trigger and singles probabilities and satisfied the classical inequality. This supports nonclassical optical counting within the declared response assumptions.

nodes.name: Selected triggered coincidence counts
nodes.shortDescription: At the selected low-excitation setting, the paper reports 9 joint-output coincidences in approximately 5 hours. The gate rate N_1 is approximately 8800 s^-1, including a 300 s^-1 dark rate; the reflected singles rate N_r is approximately 5 s^-1 with dark rate 0.02 s^-1. N_t, N_r and N_c denote gated transmitted singles, reflected singles and coincidences, and the observed probabilities are p_t=N_t/N_1, p_r=N_r/N_1 and p_c=N_c/N_1.

nodes.name: Specified two-center one-electron molecular model
nodes.shortDescription: In the reviewed atomic-unit model, supply two nuclei with Z1=Z2=1 and one electron. The clamped-nuclei electronic Hamiltonian is H_el=p^2/(2*m)-1/r1-1/r2+1/R; its electronic energy E_el(R) enters the relative nuclear equation [-nabla_R^2/(2*mu_n)+E_el(R)]*chi=E0*chi. The electronic wavefunction and nuclear wavefunction are factorized for this adiabatic treatment. H2+ and HD+ differ in supplied nuclear masses. The two-center coordinate and coupled electronic/nuclear states specify a finite molecular-ion problem.

nodes.name: Unresolved heavy-mass two-nucleon state identification
nodes.shortDescription: The paired 2026 preprints leave the nature of the lowest I=1 and I=0 two-nucleon states at these heavy-mass action parameters unresolved without additional spectral assumptions. GEVP and Lanczos agree for the same correlator data, while different operator choices under N-state saturation yield inconsistent energy estimates; the wider two-sided bounds remain compatible. The authors find no positive I=1 bound-state evidence from those bounds, and the I=0 level is too near the bound-state threshold to settle its nature from this one volume. This does not exclude a missed bound state or validate the earlier binding assignment as consensus.

nodes.name: Two-state static-string mixing model
nodes.shortDescription: Within the two-state approximation, orthonormal string and two-meson basis states mix into energy states |1>=cos(theta)|Q>+sin(theta)|B> and |2>=-sin(theta)|Q>+cos(theta)|B>. A nonzero off-diagonal coupling can produce an avoided energy crossing.

nodes.name: UA1 1982 charged-boson search acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the 30-day November-December 1982 proton-antiproton run at sqrt(s)=540 GeV. The reported exposure is 18 nb^-1 after dead-time and instrumental corrections. Preserve the trigger and offline reconstruction stages preceding the electron and missing-energy searches.

nodes.name: UA1 selected electron and missing-energy candidates
nodes.shortDescription: The report displays six electron candidates A-F: five central-gondola events and endcap event B, with high transverse electron energy and associated imbalance. It restricts the final analysis to the five central events because B has possible asymmetric conversion and opposite muon activity. The separately labeled tau candidate is not another admitted electron-neutrino event.

nodes.name: UA1 conditional W mass interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Keep the source transverse lower-limit construction separate from mass fitting under W decay kinematics and standard V-A couplings. The chosen fit corrects the transverse W motion event by event and uses Drell-Yan predictions without additional smearing; the full-QCD-smearing spectrum fit is a same-data alternative. Retain the final five-central-event restriction.

nodes.name: UA1 reported W transverse lower limit
nodes.shortDescription: Under the stated event interpretation and source confidence construction, UA1 reports mW > 73 GeV/c^2 at 90 percent confidence level from the transverse-mass lower-bound method.

nodes.name: UA1 historical conditional W mass fit
nodes.shortDescription: The chosen event-by-event transverse-motion correction and unsmeared Drell-Yan fit reports mW = 81 +/- 5 GeV/c^2 with allowance for systematic errors. The same report obtains 74 +/- 4 GeV/c^2 from the electron spectrum with full QCD smearing; this alternative exposes production/recoil-model dependence rather than a second independent mass measurement.

nodes.name: UA1 W response and selection conditions
nodes.shortDescription: Use central tracking, electromagnetic shower shape, hadronic leakage, energy/momentum agreement and the described isolation and jet criteria to select electron candidates. Reconstruct transverse energy imbalance with the calorimeter and use muon/response checks and the reported background controls; preserve the distinct central-gondola and endcap responses.

nodes.name: UA1 overlapping search selections
nodes.shortDescription: The electron-first and missing-energy-first searches recover the same five central electron candidates. The missing-energy search also retains two events removed by the electron energy/momentum match, which the report discusses as compatible with tau hypotheses. Their appearance is not an independent replicated W sample or a confirmed tau-decay measurement.

nodes.name: UA1 derived transverse event quantities
nodes.shortDescription: Table 3 gives derived transverse mass and transverse recoil summaries for all six displayed A-F electron candidates from their reconstructed electron and missing-energy vectors. These event quantities provide inputs to the interpretation; the endcap candidate remains displayed despite its exclusion from the final central-event analysis.

nodes.name: UA1 1983 neutral-boson search acquisition
nodes.shortDescription: Use the four-week April-May 1983 proton-antiproton acquisition at sqrt(s)=540 GeV, with reported corrected exposure 55 nb^-1. Retain the electron, muon, jet and total-transverse-energy triggers and the express-line/offline selection used for the dilepton search.

nodes.name: UA1 constrained dimuon mass summary
nodes.shortDescription: For the one dimuon candidate, Section 5 reports a mass of 95.5 +/- 7.3 GeV/c^2. The source combines magnetic-deflection momenta with a solution using measured muon directions and calorimetric recoil under the no-neutrino assumption, as distinguished in Table 2.

nodes.name: UA1 historical electron-pair Z mass summary
nodes.shortDescription: The report combines its four electron-pair masses to give 95.2 +/- 2.5 GeV/c^2 and adopts that value in its neutral-boson interpretation. The result is retained with the source preliminary-calibration and uncorrected-radiation conventions; the number is not recomputed from rounded table centers.

nodes.name: UA1 original dilepton mass interpretation
nodes.shortDescription: Interpret the selected lepton pairs using the reported invariant-mass reconstruction and background evaluation. Combine the four electron-pair mass determinations as reported; for the dimuon retain the weighted magnetic and transverse-balance momenta conditional on no neutrino.
